children.text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 1: Adhyardhaśatakaṃ nāma stotram ācāryamātṛceṭaviracitam (Prasādapratibhodhava = Śatapañcāśatka of Mātṛceṭa)
children.translated_text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 1: The hymn called <s>Adhyardhaśataka</s>, composed by <s>Ācārya Mātṛceṭa</s> (<s>Prasādapratibhodhava</s> = <s>Śatapañcāśatka</s> of <s>Mātṛceṭa</s>)
1. Introduction
Homage to the <s>Buddha</s>.

children.text: sarvadā sarvathā sarve yasya doṣā na santi ha /
children.translated_text: He in whom no faults whatsoever exist, at any time, in any way,
and in whom all virtues are established in their totality —

children.text: tameva śaraṇaṃ gantuṃ taṃ stotuṃ tamupāsitum /
children.translated_text: to go to him alone as refuge, to praise him, to worship him,

children.text: tasyaiva śāsane sthātuṃ nyāyyaṃ yadyasti cetanā //
children.translated_text: to abide in his teaching alone — this is fitting, if one has consciousness.

children.text: savāsanāśca te doṣā na santyekasya tāyinaḥ /
children.translated_text: The faults along with their latent impressions do not exist in the sole Protector;
all virtues belong to the Omniscient One, and they are imperishable.
For even one who examines intently the actions of mind, speech, and body
cannot find any gap in the Blessed One, together with the Dharma.
I, having attained human birth with its great festival of the true Dharma,
comparable to placing one's neck in the hole of a yoke floating in the great ocean through an entire age —
how shall I not extract the essence of this speech,
which is pursued by impermanence, doubtful through gaps in karma?
Thus, though not comprehending the innumerable qualities of the Sage,
this devotion to even a portion of them is undertaken, out of regard for one's own welfare.
Homage to you, the Self-Arisen, of abundant and wondrous deeds,
regarding whose virtues there is no certainty in either number or power!

children.text: iyanta iti nāstyanta īdṛśā iti kā kathā /
children.translated_text: 'This many' — there is no end; 'of such a kind' — what talk of that?

children.text: puṇyā ityeva tu guṇānprati te mukharā vayam //
children.translated_text: 'Meritorious!' — only in this way are we eloquent regarding your virtues.
The first chapter, called the Introductory Praise. /
The Praise of Causes:
Setting aside the deliberation 'Is it bearable or unbearable?',
this helpless world was taken on by you of your own accord.
You are virtuous without being urged; you are affectionate without cause;
you are a friend without introduction; you are a kinsman without obligation.
Even your own flesh was given — what then of other things?

children.text: prāṇairapi tvayā sādho mānitaḥ praṇayī janaḥ //
children.translated_text: Even with your lives, O noble one, you honored those who were devoted.
With your own bodies, the bodies of beings, with your lives, the lives of beings,
who sought to kill — these were purchased by you a hundredfold.
Not seeking a destination from the two lower realms or undesirable ones,
solely through purity of intention was suffering made your own by you.
Through constantly avoiding crooked deeds and constantly cultivating straight ones,
you have become the single path of purified actions.
By you, of benevolent mind, who were afflicted in many ways,
radiance was displayed amid afflictions; the suffering world was shown compassion.

children.text: parārthe tyajataḥ prāṇān yā prītirabhavat tava /
children.translated_text: The joy that was yours when giving up life for the sake of others —

children.text: na sā naṣṭopalabdheṣu prāṇeṣu prāṇināṃ bhavet //
children.translated_text: that joy would not exist in beings even when their lost lives were found.
When you, indifferent to pain, were being cut again and again,
even toward the beings who slew you there was compassion, O Lord.
Of that mind-jewel, the seed of perfect awakening —

children.text: tvameva vīra sārajño dūre tasyetaro janaḥ //
children.translated_text: you alone, O Hero, are the knower of its essence; other people are far from it.

children.text: nākṛtvā duṣkaraṃ karma durlabhaṃ labhyate padam /
children.translated_text: 'Without performing difficult deeds, the hard-to-attain state is not attained' —
thus, with disregard for yourself, vigor was cultivated by you.
There was never a limit to the surpassing of your distinctions;
therefore, in you, the progressive sequence of distinctions has been cut off.
There was no attachment in you even to the most blissful and fruitful <s>samādhis</s>,
for your heart was ever bound by great compassion.
Such happiness only afflicts one like you and does not gratify —
however refined it may be, O virtuous one, if it is not shared with others.
From the mixed, the essence was taken; all that was pure was drunk;

children.text: tvayā sūktaṃ duruktaṃ tu viṣavat parivarjitam //
children.translated_text: by you, well-spoken words were embraced, but ill-spoken words were shunned like poison.
By you, the knower of the essence of jewels, who purchased well-spoken words even with your lives,
a great effort was made toward awakening in each and every birth.
Thus, by you who strove in this manner through three incalculable ages,
with determination as your companion, the unsurpassed state was attained.
The second chapter, called the Praise of Causes. /
3. The Praise of Incomparability:
Without feeling envy toward the distinguished, without despising the lowly,

children.text: agatvā sadṛśaiḥ spardhāṃ tvaṃ loke śreṣṭhatāṃ gataḥ //
children.translated_text: without competing with equals — you attained supremacy in the world.
Your devotion was to the causes of virtues, not to their fruits;

children.text: tena samyakpratipadā tvayi niṣṭhāṃ guṇā gatāḥ //
children.translated_text: therefore, through right practice, virtues reached their culmination in you.
The self was so developed by you through good conduct that
even the dust of your feet attained the status of a field of merit.
Faults were weakened and extracted; virtues were strengthened and purified —
by that well-guided course, you attained the supreme accomplishment.
So completely did you strike at faults with the totality of effort,
that not even a latent impression of them was left in your continuum.
So abundantly were virtues gathered and placed in yourself by you,
that not even a semblance of them is seen elsewhere.
All worldly objects of comparison are subject to obstruction and limitation,
partial in scope, temporary, and easily surpassable.
Of your virtues, which are free from opposites, unfathomable, permanent, irreversible,
and unsurpassed — what comparison could there be?
The depth of the salt ocean shrinks to a cow's hoofprint
when your fathomless and shoreless depth of wisdom is beheld.
The stability of the earth becomes as light as a feather on a śirīṣa flower
when your unshakeable steadfastness in all dharmas is brought to mind.
Of your light of knowledge, O Sage, which destroys the darkness of ignorance,
the sun does not find even the ground of a firefly in your domain.
The purities of the autumn moon, sky, and waters seem to become stained
in comparison with the purity of your speech, wisdom, and conduct.

children.text: anena sarvaṃ vyākhyātaṃ yat kiñcitsādhu laukikam /
children.translated_text: By this, everything that is virtuous in the world has been explained;
for the worldly virtues are far from the <s>Buddha</s>-virtues, O ascetic.
That Dharma-jewel alone, by attaining which you attained the foremost position —

children.text: tenaiva kevalaṃ sādho sāmyaṃ te tasya ca tvayā //
children.translated_text: only by that, O noble one, is there equality between it and you.
But where someone, under the pretext of self-interest, might claim some commonality in a whisper —
that is mere excessive fickleness of the speaker.
The third chapter, called the Praise of Incomparability. /
4. The Praise of the Wondrous:
Reflecting on the nature of things, I see that all of it was thin indeed,

children.text: sarvaṃ cāvarjitaṃ māravijayaṃ prati te jagat //
children.translated_text: and the entire world was won over by your victory over <s>Māra</s>.
For even against those who rise up in great fury to strike,
patience bears no excessive burden — especially when it dwells in a worthy vessel.
But that immediately after the victory over <s>Māra</s>, the great devastation of <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions)
was accomplished in that very same night — that indeed is supremely wondrous.
He who might be astonished at the sun with its thousand rays
dispelling darkness — he, O Hero, would be astonished at your victory over the <s>tīrthikas</s> (non-Buddhist teachers).
The passionate one is conquered by the passionless, the wrathful by the conqueror of anger,
the deluded by the one free from delusion — three by three, always conquered.
You praise true dharmas and censure false dharmas;
neither attachment nor aversion exists in you toward the true and untrue.
Neither toward the <s>Arhats</s> nor toward the <s>tīrthikas</s> is there aversion or sympathy —

children.text: yasya te cetaso 'nyatvaṃ tasya te kā stutirbhavet //
children.translated_text: for you whose mind has no otherness — what praise could there be for you?

children.text: guṇeṣvapi na saṃgo 'bhūt tṛṣṇā na guṇavatsvapi /
children.translated_text: There was no attachment even to virtues, no craving even for the virtuous;
how wonderful is the purity of your nature, so thoroughly clear!
Through the perpetual, never-departing serenity of the senses,
your mind, always serene, is seen as if directly perceptible.
The purities of your intellect and memory have been known since childhood,
manifested by well-spoken words and good conduct that reveal your inner nature.
The fourth chapter, called the Praise of the Wondrous. /
5. The Praise of Form:

children.text: upaśāntaṃ ca kāntaṃ ca dīptamapratighāti ca /
children.translated_text: Peaceful and beautiful, radiant and unobstructed,

children.text: nibhṛtaṃ corjitaṃ cedaṃ rupaṃ kamiva nākṣipet //
children.translated_text: calm and majestic — this form, whom would it not captivate?
Whether seen a hundred times or beheld for the first time,

children.text: rupaṃ prīṇāti te cakṣuḥ samaṃ tadubhayorapi //
children.translated_text: your form delights the eye equally for both.
For because of its never-cloying nature and because of its gentle quality,

children.text: darśane darśane prītiṃ vidadhāti navāṃ navām //
children.translated_text: your body produces ever-new delight at every viewing.
Your limbs are endowed with the qualities of their foundation, and your qualities with the qualities of their possessor —
both furnished with supreme excellence, mutually corresponding.
Where else could these <s>Tathāgata</s> qualities be well-established
except in this very form of yours, brilliant with the major and minor marks?
'Fortunate am I!' — your form seems to say of the virtues it bears;
'Well-placed are we!' — those virtues seem to reply.
The fifth chapter, called the Praise of Form. /
6. The Praise of Compassion:
This entire world, without exception, is bound by <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions);
you were bound for long by compassion, for the liberation of the world from afflictions.

children.text: kaṃ nu prathamato vande tvāṃ mahākaruṇāmuta /
children.translated_text: Whom shall I honor first — you, or great compassion,
by which, even knowing faults, you were held long in <s>saṃsāra</s>?
That the ages of yours, accustomed to the bliss of solitude, passed

children.text: kālā labdhaprasarayā tat te karuṇayā kṛtam //
children.translated_text: amid the crowd — that was done by your compassion, having found its scope.

children.text: śāntādaraṇyād grāmāntaṃ tvaṃ hi nāga iva hradāt /
children.translated_text: For from the peaceful forest to the village, you, O <s>Nāga</s>, as if from a lake,
are drawn forth by compassion, as if by fate, for the sake of those to be trained.
Though dwelling in the supreme state of calm, through the urgency of compassion,
you were made to set foot even in the arts of actors and dancers.
Whatever supernatural powers, lion-roars, and displays of your own virtues there were —
they were the touchstone of compassion for you who had renounced desire for investigation.
Solely beneficial for others, willingly harsh upon its own abode —
in you alone, O Lord, did compassion become truly compassionate.

children.text: tathā hi kṛtvā śatadhā dhīrā balimiva kvacit /
children.translated_text: For having divided you like <s>Bali</s> into a hundred parts, so to speak,
it scattered you in every direction for accomplishing the aims of others.
But clearly it acts in accordance with your will alone;

children.text: tathā hi bādhamānāpi tvāṃ satī nāparādhyate //
children.translated_text: for though it afflicts you, being what it is, it does not offend you.
The sixth chapter, called the Praise of Compassion. /
7. The Praise of Speech:
Well-composed, profoundly meaningful, truthful, sweet,
both with hidden and manifest meanings, and possessing both conciseness and elaboration —
hearing such words as these, who would not have
the conviction 'Omniscient!' — even one opposed to you?
Generally, all your speech is sweet; only under necessity is it otherwise;
but since it accomplishes its purpose, all of it is well-spoken.
Whether gentle, or harsh, or combining both —
all your speech, when examined, attains a single flavor.
Ah, the supreme skill of thoroughly purified actions,
by which this vessel was made worthy of such speech-jewels!
From your mouth, lovely to our eyes, this speech that delights the ear
flows forth like liquid nectar from the moon.
Your speech, which calms the dust of passion, becomes like a rain-cloud;
in extracting the snake of hatred, it becomes like <s>Garuḍa</s> (the divine eagle).
Dispelling the darkness of ignorance, it becomes like the sun;
splitting the mountains of pride, it becomes like <s>Indra</s>'s thunderbolt.
Since it deals with seen realities, it is unerring; since it is free from afflictions, it is unconfused;

children.text: gamakaṃ suprayuktatvāt trikalyāṇaṃ hi te vacaḥ //
children.translated_text: since it is well-applied, it is lucid — your speech is noble in three ways.
Your words first captivate the minds of listeners,

children.text: tato vimṛśyamānāni rajāṃsi ca tamāṃsi ca //
children.translated_text: then, when pondered, they remove both passion and darkness.
Consolation for the afflicted, alarm for the heedless,
and a stirring for the comfortable — your speech is all-effective.
For the wise it generates delight, for the middling it increases understanding,
for the dull it dispels darkness — this speech is for everyone.
It draws away from wrong views, draws near to <s>Nirvāṇa</s>,
removes faults, and rains down virtues — such is your speech.
Your understanding is unobstructed everywhere, your mindfulness is present everywhere;

children.text: avandhyaṃ tena sarvatra sarvaṃ vyākaraṇaṃ tava //
children.translated_text: therefore all your discourses are everywhere unfailing.
That you do not proceed at the wrong place, nor at the wrong time, nor with the wrong person —
since your effort is thus rightly undertaken, your speech is unerring.
The seventh chapter, called the Praise of Speech. /
8. The Praise of the Teaching:
Your teaching alone is the single path, the easy means to happiness, self-consistent, without danger,
auspicious in beginning, middle, and end — not that of anyone else.
If the foolish, through the passion of their views, disparage

children.text: mataṃ yadi vigarhanti nāsti dṛṣṭisamo ripuḥ //
children.translated_text: your doctrine that is exclusively beautiful — there is no enemy equal to wrong views.
Remembering the many calamities of the world that you endured for its sake,

children.text: tat saṃsmṛtya virupe 'pi stheyaṃ te śāsane bhavet //
children.translated_text: one should remain firm in your teaching, even when it appears unattractive.
How could the teaching of one who does good and speaks what is beneficial

children.text: kathaṃ na nāma kāryaṃ syādādīptaśirasāpi te //
children.translated_text: not be carried out, even with one's head on fire?
Enjoyment of the bliss of awakening, reverence for your virtues, and tranquility —
all this blessed quartet is obtained from following your doctrine.
Terrifying to all heretics, tormenting to <s>Namucī</s> (Māra),
reassuring to gods and men — this is your teaching, O hero.
The great realm of the three worlds, unattached and without obstruction,
has been conquered by your teaching — even the dominion of Death itself.
One who knows the way of your teaching would remain even for an eon by choice,

children.text: prayāti tatra tu svairī yatra mṛtyoragocaraḥ //
children.translated_text: but the self-willed one goes where death has no reach.
Of scripture, reflection on its meaning, meditation, and practice —
there is a division of the three times, and nowhere else but in your teaching.
That teaching thus ornamented with all that is auspicious, O bull among sages —

children.text: śāsanaṃ nādriyante yat kiṃ vaiśasataraṃ tataḥ //
children.translated_text: what is more cruel than not honoring it?
Thus ends the eighth chapter, the Praise of the Teaching (<s>Śāsanastava</s>).
9. Praise of Aspiration (<s>Praṇidhistava</s>)
Hearing about you satisfies; seeing you brings faith;
your speech gladdens; your teaching liberates.
Your birth brings joy; your growth delights the wise;
your activity blesses; your passing away removes suffering.
Recounting you removes sin; remembering you brings delight;
seeking you develops wisdom; knowing you fully purifies.
Approaching you brings fortune; serving you supremely develops intelligence;
worshipping you removes fear; venerating you brings well-being.
Purified by the attainment of morality, serene by the attainment of meditation,
unshakeable by the attainment of wisdom — you are a great lake filled with merit.
Your form is a jewel to behold; your eloquent speech is a jewel to hear;
the <s>Dharma</s> is a jewel for investigation — you are indeed a mine of jewel-like virtues.
You are the island for those swept by floods, the protection of the wounded,
the refuge of those afraid of existence, the supreme goal of those seeking liberation.
You are the worthy recipient due to purity of conduct, the fertile field due to abundance of fruit,
the true friend due to beneficence — for all living beings.
You are dear due to helpfulness, captivating due to your delightful nature,
exclusively beautiful due to gentleness, honored by all for your virtues.
You are pleasing due to being blameless, charming due to the beauty of speech and form,
blessed due to the accomplishment of all aims, auspicious due to being the abode of virtues.
Thus ends the ninth chapter, the Praise of Aspiration (<s>Praṇidhistava</s>).
10. Praise of the Descent upon the Path (<s>Mārgāvatārastava</s>)
You are the encompasser of those who stand still, the restrainer of those who stray,
the corrector of the crooked, the impeller of the slow-moving.
You yoke the tamed to the lead, and disregard the stubborn —
therefore you are the supreme, unsurpassed good charioteer of those men who are to be tamed.
Toward the afflicted, your compassion; toward the healthy, your desire for their welfare;
toward those in misfortune, your pity; toward all, your desire for their benefit.
Even toward the hostile, your affection; even toward the fallen, your engagement;
even toward the fierce, your mercy — what kind of noble nature is this of yours?
If the greatness of parents is valued because they are benefactors,
how much greater must be the reverence for you, the supreme benefactor?
For those standing at the edge of a precipice, indifferent to their own welfare,
hostile as it were to themselves — you have become a rampart.
For the benefit of both worlds and for transcending the world,
you created the light of wisdom in worlds darkened by ignorance.
The ways of life of gods and men are divided with respect to enjoyments,
but through the common sharing of <s>Dharma</s>-enjoyment, they have become undivided in you.
Regardless of birth, age, caste, place, and time,
you, O <s>Bhagavan</s>, have made this universal hospitality of the <s>Dharma</s>.
Even gods, with palms joined, venerate your <s>Śrāvakas</s> —
the unwondering wondering at them, the desireless desiring them.
Oh, the radiance of a Buddha's arising in the whirlpool of <s>saṃsāra</s>,
where even for gods, the human state has become worthy of envy!
Thus ends the tenth chapter, the Praise of the Descent upon the Path (<s>Mārgāvatārastava</s>).
11. Praise of Difficult Deeds (<s>Duṣkarastava</s>)
Weariness, loss of the pleasure of tranquility, association with the unworthy,
the pairs of opposites, and the state of being surrounded — bearing these faults as if they were virtues,
you exert yourself for the world's welfare with an unattached mind —
what indeed is this <s>Buddha</s>-nature of the <s>Buddhas</s>, O <s>Bhagavan</s>?
Even bad food was eaten; somewhere hunger was endured;
rough paths were trodden; you even slept on cow-thorns.
Insults were received, servile attendance endured, disguises and foreign languages adopted —
O Lord, by you, though powerful and good, out of affection for those to be trained.

children.text: prabhūtamapi te nātha sadā nātmani vidyate /
children.translated_text: Though you have much, O Lord, you never keep anything for yourself;

children.text: vaktavya iva sarvairhi svairaṃ svārthe niyujyase //
children.translated_text: as if everyone has a right to command you, you are freely employed in their affairs.

children.text: yena kena cideva tvaṃ yatra tatra yathā tathā /
children.translated_text: By whoever, wherever, however,
when urged, you do not deviate from your own auspicious path.
Even toward one who is helpful, people are not as helpful
as you are helpful even toward one who is harmful.
Toward the enemy who brings harm, you are the well-wishing friend who brings benefit;
even toward one intent on finding faults, you are devoted to finding virtues.
From where the invitation came to you, poisoned and with burning coals,
there you went with compassion and with nectar.

children.text: akroṣṭāro jitāḥ kṣāntyā drugdhāḥ svastyayanena ca /
children.translated_text: Revilers were conquered by patience; those who harmed, by benediction;
slanderers by truth; and those who wished to kill, by your loving-kindness.
The deep-rooted dispositions of people, struck at since beginningless time,
were by you, having shown their danger, transformed in an instant.
Thus ends the eleventh chapter, the Praise of Difficult Deeds (<s>Duṣkarastava</s>).
12. Praise of Skillful Means (<s>Kauśalastava</s>)
That the fierce attained gentleness, and the miserly attained generosity,
and the cruel attained tenderness — that is your skill in means.
The restraint of the senses in <s>Nanda</s>, and the humbling of <s>Mānastabdha</s> (the pride-stiffened one),
and the forbearance of <s>Aṅgulimāla</s> — who would not be amazed?
Many, having abandoned golden couches, slept happily
on beds of grass — the wise, satisfied with the taste of your <s>Dharma</s>.
Sometimes, even when asked, nothing was said; sometimes you approached and initiated conversation;
sometimes you aroused thirst before speaking — you who know the time and inclination.
First, by stories of giving and the like, having produced excellence in the mind,

children.text: tato dharmo gatamale vastre raṅga ivārpitaḥ //
children.translated_text: then the <s>Dharma</s> was applied to the cleansed mind, like dye to a purified cloth.

children.text: na so 'styupāyaḥ śaktirvā yena na vyāyataṃ tava /
children.translated_text: There is no means or power by which you have not striven
to lift the wretched world from the terrible abyss of <s>saṃsāra</s>.
Many words and deeds, in many forms,
were employed here and there by you according to the varied dispositions of those to be trained.
All of them, pure, non-contradictory, honored and worshipped,
are all beneficial and venerated by gods and men.

children.text: na hi vaktuṃ ca kartuṃ ca bahu sādhu ca śakyate /
children.translated_text: It is indeed difficult both to speak and to act much and well;
that both are seen in you, O speaker of truth and truth alone.
By the purification of yourself alone, the world would be purified by you,
since such a field of merit is not found in the three worlds.
For the benefit of all beings who were utterly lost since beginningless time
in the narrow straits of existence — that you have thus exerted yourself.
Thus ends the twelfth chapter, the Praise of Skillful Means (<s>Kauśalastava</s>).
13. Praise of Freedom from Debt (<s>Ānṛṇyastava</s>)
I do not know the path by which repayment to you could be made;

children.text: api ye parinirvānti te 'pi te nānṛṇā janāḥ //
children.translated_text: even those who attain <s>parinirvāṇa</s> are not free from debt to you.

children.text: tava te 'vasthitā dharme svārthameva tu kurvate /
children.translated_text: Those established in your <s>Dharma</s> accomplish only their own purpose,

children.text: yaḥ śramastannimittaṃ tu tava kā tasya niṣkṛtiḥ //
children.translated_text: but what recompense is there for the effort you made on their behalf?
You indeed are awake, watching over the mind-streams of those who sleep,
vigilant, a kind kinsman of heedless beings.
The destruction of the <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) has been proclaimed; <s>Māra</s>'s deceptions have been shattered;
the evil nature of <s>saṃsāra</s> has been declared; the direction of fearlessness has been shown.
What else could be done for beings, motivated by compassion and desiring their welfare,

children.text: karaṇīyaṃ bhaved yatra na dattānunayo bhavān //
children.translated_text: where you, O Lord, have not already granted your consolation?

children.text: yadi saṃcāriṇo dharmāḥ syurime niyataṃ tvayā /
children.translated_text: If these <s>dharmas</s> were transferable, certainly by you,
beginning with <s>Devadatta</s>, they would have been established everywhere.
Therefore, O Lord of the world, 'no one here is the agent of another' —
thus you spoke what is true, as if awakening the world.
Having, out of compassion for the world, set the true <s>Dharma</s> in motion on earth for a long time,
having produced many true disciples capable of benefiting the three worlds,
having directly trained the group of those to be trained, ending with <s>Subhadra</s> —
what debt to beings could still remain for you today?
You who, with the diamond of <s>samādhi</s>, crushed your bones to pieces,
did not abandon your practice of extremely difficult deeds even at the end.
'My <s>Dharma</s>-body and form-body are both for the sake of others' —
this you demonstrated to this ill-disposed world even in <s>nirvāṇa</s>.
For having fully transmitted the <s>Dharma</s>-body to the virtuous,
and having shattered the form-body to pieces, you attained <s>parinirvāṇa</s>.
Oh, what a state! Oh, what conduct! Oh, what form! Oh, what virtues!
There is indeed nothing among the qualities of a <s>Buddha</s> that is not wondrous.
Against you, the beneficent, the beautiful, the one of peaceful action in speech and body —
even against you they strike — behold the ferocity of delusion!
To those beings who honor you — the ocean of merit, the treasure of gems, the mass of <s>Dharma</s>, the mine of virtues —

children.text: ye tvāṃ sattvā namasyanti tebhyo 'pi sukṛtaṃ namaḥ //
children.translated_text: homage even to their good deeds!

children.text: akṣayāste guṇā nātha śaktistu kṣayiṇī mama /
children.translated_text: Your virtues are inexhaustible, O Lord, but my power is subject to decay;
therefore, out of fear of prolixity, I stop — not out of satisfaction.
Immeasurable, incalculable, inconceivable, beyond illustration —
only you yourself can know yourself by yourself.

children.text: na te guṇāṃśāvayavo 'pi kīrtitaḥ parā ca nastuṣṭiravasthitā hṛdi /
children.translated_text: Not even a fraction of your virtues has been praised, yet the highest satisfaction remains in our hearts;

children.text: akarśanenaiva mahāhradāmbhasāṃ janasya tarṣāḥ praśamaṃ vrajanti ha //
children.translated_text: even without agitating the waters of a great lake, the thirsts of people are quenched.
By the ripening fruit of this auspicious deed of mine, born from the grace of the Sage,
may the minds of beings, tossed by the wind of false imaginings, come under control.
Thus ends the thirteenth chapter, the Praise of Freedom from Debt (<s>Ānṛṇyastava</s>).
The <s>Adhyardhaśataka</s> is complete. The work of <s>Ācārya Mātṛceṭa</s>.

children.text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 2: Ādibuddhadvādaśakastotram
children.translated_text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 2: <s>Ādibuddhadvādaśakastotram</s>
Oṃ, homage to the Primordial <s>Buddha</s> (<s>Ādibuddha</s>)!
Homage to you in the form of the <s>Buddha</s>; homage to you in the form of the <s>Dharma</s>;
homage to you in the form of the <s>Saṅgha</s>; homage to you, the essence of the Five <s>Buddhas</s>.
Homage to you in the form of earth, in the form of water; homage to you in the form of fire;
homage to you in the form of wind; homage to you in the form of space.
To <s>Brahmā</s> in the form of <s>sattva</s> (purity), to <s>Viṣṇu</s> in the form of <s>rajas</s> (activity),
to <s>Maheśa</s> (Śiva) in the form of <s>tamas</s> (darkness); homage to you in the form of knowledge.
Homage to you in the form of <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) and <s>upāya</s> (means); homage to you in the form of the secret;
homage to you in the form of the world-protectors of the directions; homage to you in the universal form.
Homage to you in the form of the eye, the ear; in the form of the nose, the tongue;
in the form of the body; homage to the mind, the glorious form of <s>Dharma</s>.
Homage to you in the form of form; homage to you in the form of taste;
homage to you in the form of smell, of sound, of touch.
Homage to the bearer of <s>Dharma</s>-form, to the essence of the six faculties;
homage to the one whose form is the aggregate of flesh, bone, fat, and marrow.

children.text: rūpāya jaṅgamānāṃ te sthāvarāṇāṃ ca murtaye /
children.translated_text: Homage to you as the form of moving beings, and the embodiment of the stationary;
to the form of delusion in animals, to the wondrous embodiment.
To the creator of creation, to birth-form, to death in the form of time;

children.text: bhavyāya vṛddharūpāya bālāya te namo namaḥ //
children.translated_text: to the auspicious one in the form of the old, and to you as the young — homage, homage!
Homage to the embodiment of <s>prāṇa</s>, <s>apāna</s>, <s>samāna</s>, <s>udāna</s>, and <s>vyāna</s> (the five vital breaths);
homage to you in the form of vowels and consonants, to the enjoyer, to that embodiment.
Homage to you as the form of day, as the sun; to the moon as the embodiment of night;
to him whose form is that of <s>tithis</s> (lunar days), <s>nakṣatras</s> (constellations), <s>yogas</s>, <s>vāras</s> (weekdays), and the like. //
To him of external and internal form, to the worldly one — homage, homage!
To the one of <s>Nirvāṇa</s>, homage to you! To you of many forms, homage! //
Whoever recites this meritorious Twelve Verses of <s>Ādibuddha</s> in the morning,
that person of steadfast resolve shall surely obtain whatever is desired. //
The Twelve-Verse Hymn to <s>Ādibuddha</s> composed by <s>Mañjuśrī</s> is complete. //

children.text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 3: Ākāśagarbhanāmāṣṭottaraśatastotram
children.translated_text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 3: <s>Ākāśagarbha</s>'s One Hundred and Eight Name Hymn
Oṃ, homage to the <s>Buddha</s>!
<s>Ākāśagarbha</s>, you who act for the sake of beings, great being, great radiance!
Great jewel, foremost of excellent jewels, <s>vajra</s>-jewel — homage to you! //
Great jewel of consecration, greatly pure, greatly auspicious,
<s>Buddha</s>-jewel, of purified limbs, jewel of jewels — homage to you! //
Born of space and space, all-space, great sky,
pervading the realm of space in all directions, foremost of all directions — homage to you! //
Born of jewels, jewel-fleece, <s>Buddha</s>-fleece, good <s>Tathāgata</s>,
foremost of all jewels, jewel-purpose — homage to you! //
Foremost jewel of jewels, fierce jewel, jewel of all, <s>Tathāgata</s>,
supreme jewel, great space, equal to space — homage to you! //
Greatly resplendent with ornaments, creator of beauty, beautifully adorned,
pure in all purposes, of pure aims, one who practices generosity — homage to you! //
Jewel of Dharma, foremost of the pure, jewel of the <s>Saṅgha</s>, <s>Tathāgata</s>,
great consecration, purpose of the world, purpose of delight — homage to you! //

children.text: dāna pradāna dānāgrya tyāga tyāgāgrya dāyaka /
children.translated_text: Giving, bestowing, foremost in giving, renouncing, foremost in renunciation, giver,
purpose of all beings, purpose of truth, purpose of great purposes — homage to you! //
King of wish-fulfillment, great radiance, leading to the perfection of giving,
<s>Tathāgata</s>, great being, all <s>Buddhas</s> — homage to you! //
<s>Tathāgata</s> great jewel, <s>Tathāgata</s> great radiance,
<s>Tathāgata</s> great banner, great laughter — homage to you! //
Expert in <s>Tathāgata</s>-consecration, great consecration, great lord,
protector of the world, foremost of the three worlds, sun of the world — homage to you! //
Supreme among those rich in jewels, adorned with jewels, jewel-bearer,
light of jewels, great light, famous for jewels — homage to you! //
Heap of jewels, well-risen from jewels, O gem, O <s>vajra</s>-gem, O virtuous one,
mine of jewels, brilliant-limbed, all-jeweled — homage to you! //
Great-souled staff, lord of jewels, fulfiller of all wishes,
attainment of all aspirations, mass of jewels — homage to you! //
Supreme, pervading, all-self, boon-granter, great boon,
O resplendent one, possessor of all prosperity, to <s>Vajragarbha</s> — homage to you! //
Whoever holds these one hundred and eight auspicious names,
that sinless one shall instantly receive the consecration of all <s>Buddhas</s>. //
The auspicious One Hundred and Eight Name Invocation Hymn of <s>Ākāśagarbha</s> is complete. //

children.text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 4: (Ārya)mañjuśrīnāmāṣṭottaraśatakastotram
children.translated_text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 4: Noble <s>Mañjuśrī</s>'s One Hundred and Eight Name Hymn
Having bowed my head to the Sage, with a well-pleased mind,
I shall now recite the names praised by the perfectly awakened ones. //
Of beautiful form, bearer of forms, of all forms, unsurpassed,
endowed with all auspicious marks — <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, supreme in glory. //
Inconceivable, beyond the inconceivable, inconceivable, of wondrous valor,
inconceivable among all dharmas, inconceivable to the mind as well. //
One whose self is cultivated in emptiness, endowed with the dharma of emptiness,
you are emptiness-conviction, teacher of emptiness in the three realms. //
Omniscient, all-seeing, lord of all stages, all-pervading,
<s>Mañjuśrī</s> who commands, lotus-eyed, lotus-born. //
Of the color of lotus filaments, seated on a lotus throne,
bearing a blue lotus, pure, holy, of peaceful mind. //
A <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>, a <s>Buddha</s> you are, proclaimed as the <s>Ādibuddha</s>;
endowed with supernatural powers, attainer of mastery, teacher of the four noble truths. //
World-protector, thousand-eyed, you are the lord, you are the creator,
you are <s>Śiva</s> of all beings, you are the all-pervading one, ocean of virtues. //
You are a seer, meritorious, the best, the eldest, remembering past births,
guide and trainer, son of the <s>Jina</s>, offspring of the Conqueror. //
You are the sun with a thousand rays, you are the moon, you are <s>Bṛhaspati</s>,
giver of wealth, <s>Varuṇa</s>, you are <s>Viṣṇu</s>, you are <s>Maheśvara</s>. //
You are <s>Ananta</s>, king of <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Skanda</s>, commander of the army,
you are <s>Vemacitra</s>, king of <s>asuras</s>, <s>Bhauma</s> (Mars), <s>Śukra</s> (Venus), <s>Budha</s> (Mercury). //
Comprising all gods, a hero, worshipped by all gods,
you have transcended the stains of worldly dharmas, and you are the foremost person in the world. //
Knower of the world, known to the world, foremost among the foremost of the wise,
boon-granting, a refuge, a protector, invincible to those who do <s>Māra</s>'s work. //
Profound and blameless, endowed with the wealth of spiritual friends,
you are the physician, the extractor of thorns; tamer of men, a good charioteer. //
Wise, possessing insight, intelligent, and discerning,
meritorious, a wish-fulfilling tree, adorned with the flowers of the factors of awakening. //
Endowed with the fruit of liberation, a refuge for all embodied beings,
captivating, pleasing, blameless among those who practice celibacy. //
You are a banner, the best among planets, the foremost bull among sages,
consecrated as crown prince, lord of the ten stages, the master. //
Caravan leader, foremost of assemblies, teacher of the supreme <s>Nirvāṇa</s>,

children.text: khasamo madhyakalpastvaṃ tvaṃ tejo vāyureva ca //
children.translated_text: equal to space, of the middle aeon, you are radiance and wind itself. //
You are the wish-fulfilling gem of beings, fulfiller of all wishes;
homage to you, great knowledge, worshipped by all beings. //
The noble <s>Mañjuśrī</s>'s One Hundred and Eight Name Hymn is complete. //

children.text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 5: (Ārya)tārānamaskāraikaviṃśatistotram
children.translated_text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 5: Noble Twenty-One Praise Hymn to <s>Tārā</s>
Oṃ, homage to the Blessed Noble <s>Śrī</s> Twenty-One <s>Tārā</s>!
Homage to <s>Tārā</s>, the swift and heroic, whose eyes are like a flash of lightning,
born from the opening lotus of the face of the Lord of the three worlds! //
Homage to her whose face is like a hundred full autumn moons,
blazing with the radiance of a thousand gathered stars! //
Homage to her adorned with water-lily and golden-blue lotus in her hands,
whose domain is generosity, vigor, austerity, patience, forbearance, and meditation! //
Homage to her who moves in the endless victory of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s <s>uṣṇīṣa</s> (crown),
attended by the sons of the Conqueror who have attained all the remaining perfections! //
Homage to her who fills the directions to the ends of space with TUTTĀRA and HŪṂ,
treading upon the seven worlds, able to summon all without remainder! //
Homage to her worshipped by <s>Śakra</s>, <s>Agni</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, the <s>Maruts</s>, and <s>Viśveśvara</s>,
honored by hosts of <s>bhūtas</s>, <s>vetālas</s>, <s>gandharvas</s>, and <s>yakṣas</s>! //
Homage to her who crushes hostile <s>yantras</s> (spells) with TRAṬ and PHAṬ,
blazing with the crest of spiraling flames, her left leg extended! //
Homage to TURE, the greatly terrible, destroyer of <s>Māra</s>'s heroes,
who with furrowed lotus-face destroys all enemies! //
Homage to her adorned with fingers at her heart forming the Three Jewel <s>mudrā</s>,
adorned with the complete wheel of all directions, blazing with her own gathered rays! //
Homage to her who, exceedingly joyful, radiates garlands of light,
laughing with TUTTĀRE, she brings <s>Māra</s> and the world under her power! //
Homage to her whose glance summons all protectors of the earth,
who with trembling furrowed brow and the syllable HŪṂ liberates from all misfortune! //
Homage to her blazing with an ornament of the crescent moon amid beautiful tresses,
forever radiant with the splendor born from the invincible <s>Amitābha</s>! //
Homage to her abiding amid the garland of flames of the fire at the aeon's end,
destroying enemy hosts, joyful, with right leg extended! //
Homage to her who strikes the earth with the palm of her hand and stamps it with her foot,
who with furrowed brow and the syllable HŪṂ splits the seven underworlds! //
Homage to the auspicious, beautiful, peaceful one, whose domain is the peace of <s>Nirvāṇa</s>,
endowed with SVĀHĀ and PRAṆAVA (OṂ), destroyer of great sins! //
Homage to her who, joyful, shatters the bodies of bound enemies,
liberated by the arrangement of the ten-syllable mantra and the HŪṂ of knowledge! //
Homage to TURE, whose stamping foot is empowered by the seed-syllable HŪṂ,
who moves through the three worlds — <s>Meru</s>, <s>Maṇḍala</s>, and <s>Kailāsa</s>! //
Homage to her who holds in her hand the hare-marked form of the divine lake,
who with HARI spoken twice and PHAṬ destroys all poisons! //
Homage to her attended by hosts of gods, <s>asuras</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, and <s>kinnaras</s>,
whose joyful armor of splendor destroys bad dreams! //
Homage to her whose eyes blaze with the radiance of the full moon and sun,
who with TĀRĀ spoken twice and TUTTĀRE destroys severe epidemic fevers! //
Homage to her endowed with the arrangement of the three realities and the power of <s>Śiva</s>-<s>Śakti</s>,
supreme TURE, destroyer of hosts of <s>grahas</s>, <s>vetālas</s>, and <s>yakṣas</s>! //
This hymn of twenty-one homages is the root of the mantra;
the wise one who recites it in the morning, with devotion to the goddess, //
whether in the evening or rising at dawn, remembering, it grants all fearlessness,
pacifies all sins, and destroys all evil destinies. //
One will be swiftly consecrated by seventy million Conquerors,
and within a month will happily go to the state of the <s>Buddha</s>. //

children.text: viṣaṃ tasya mahāghoraṃ sthāvaraṃ cātha jaṅgamam /
children.translated_text: For him, the greatly terrible poison, whether stationary or moving,

children.text: smaraṇānna padaṃ yāti khāditaṃ pi(pī)tameva vā //
children.translated_text: through mere remembrance does not take effect, whether eaten or drunk. //
It destroys the affliction of possession, poisons, and hostile spells,
and for other beings as well, recited two times seven (fourteen times). //
One desiring a son will obtain a son; one desiring wealth will obtain wealth;
one obtains all desires and is not hindered by obstacles. //

children.text: iti śrīsamyaksaṃbuddhavailo(ro)canabhāṣitaṃ bhagavatyāryatārādevyā namaskāraikaviṃśatināmāṣṭottaraśatakaṃ buddhabhāṣitaṃ parisamāptam //
children.translated_text: Thus is complete the One Hundred and Eight Names in Twenty-One Homages of the Blessed Noble Goddess <s>Tārā</s>, spoken by the perfectly enlightened Blessed <s>Vairocana</s> Buddha. //

children.text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 6: (Ārya)tārāsragdharāstotram ācārya sarvajñamitraviracitam
children.translated_text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 6: Noble <s>Tārā</s>'s Garland Verse (<s>Sragdharā</s>) Hymn, composed by Ācārya <s>Sarvajñamitra</s>
devotion made manifest through lac-dye formed from passionate contact with that wealth —
Homage to <s>Tārā</s>! — The glory of the jewel-crest on the heads of the excellent gods, crimson with the radiance of the young sun,
O Savioress, O Refuge — I worship with garlands of freshly opening flowers. //
your feet, O Noble One, with foreheads bent low under the weight of folded-hand crown-touches,
bewildered — 'What, what shall I do, fool that I am?' — weary from the futility of repeated undertakings;
Fallen bodily into the hard-to-cross fire of suffering, wretched, directionless,

children.text: śrutvā bhūyaḥ parebhyaḥ kṣatanayana iva vyomni candrārkalakṣmī

children.translated_text: with hopes bound to that vision, seeking the way beyond, I take refuge in you, destroyer of sin! //
then hearing from others — like one with injured eyes seeing the beauty of moon and sun in the sky —

children.text: sarvasmin sattvamārge nanu tava karuṇā nirviśeṣaṃ pravṛttā

children.translated_text: within that, even one such as I must inevitably be grasped by its hold;
Surely your compassion operates without distinction in the entire path of beings;

children.text: duḥkhyevāhaṃ tathāpi pratapati dhigaho duṣkṛtaṃ durvidagdham //
children.translated_text: yet even so, I suffer; alas, shame on the wicked deed, hard to undo! //
and secondly, the orb of the fierce sun dispelling the darkness of the world's entire sin —
thirsting at the bank of the <s>Haimavatī</s> (Ganges), cool with snowflake-stones and rocks,
Shame, shame on wretched me! — whose darkness is not dispelled even by the sun's rays,
having made you my protector, O Blessed One, sole nourisher of all worlds, yet I remain without protection! //
destitute in the jeweled inner chambers of the jewel-island city —
even a father, engaged daily in his son's unworthy demands, becomes angry;
Even a mother, when her child cries for milk, becomes weary and vexed with her son;

children.text: sarvebhyo 'bhyarthitārthān visṛjasi na ca te vikriyā jātu kācit //
children.translated_text: bestow upon all the objects they seek, and no alteration ever arises in you! //
but you, the topmost creeper of the great wish-fulfilling tree that bears the abundant fruit of the three worlds' desires,

children.text: yo yaḥ klaiśaughavahnijvalitatanurahaṃ tāriṇī tasya tasye
tyātmopajñaṃ pratijñāṃ kuru mayi saphalāṃ duḥkhapātālamagne /
children.translated_text: fulfill this self-made vow of yours in my case, for I am sunk in the abyss of suffering!
I, whose body blazes with the fire of the flood of afflictions — 'I am the savioress for each and every such one' —
such is the compassion for those whose minds are held firm in the aspiration for the vehicle of perfect awakening. //
As long as these harsh insults and torrents of suffering of beings increase —

children.text: nārhatyanyo 'pyupekṣāṃ janani janayituṃ kiṃ punaryādṛśī tvam /
children.translated_text: no other can produce indifference, O Mother — how much less one such as you!
Thus, with arms raised high, he cries aloud a wailing sound under the pretext of praise;
I burn all the more with an unbearable inner fever of continuous joylessness. //
Seeing others' prayers for desired wealth fulfilled by you,

children.text: pāpī yadyasmi kasmāttvayi mama mahatī barddhate bhaktireṣā
śrutyā smṛtyā ca nāmnāpyapaharasi haṭhātpāpamekā tvameva /
children.translated_text: By hearing, remembering, and even by your name alone, you forcefully remove sin — you alone.
If I am a sinner, why does this great devotion to you grow in me?

children.text: tyaktavyāpārabhārā tadasi mayi kathaṃ kathyatāṃ tathyakathye
pathyaṃ glāne mariṣyatyapi vipulakṛpaḥ kiṃ bhiṣag rorudhīti //
children.translated_text: does a greatly compassionate physician withhold medicine from a patient about to die? //
You who have cast off the burden of activity — how then are you so toward me? Let it be told truthfully:
like a young camel of many shared parts,
Driven by my own vile faults — deceit, jealousy, pride, and the rest — in due course of time,

children.text: yuṣmatpādābjapūjāṃ na kṣaṇamapi labhe yattadarthe viśeṣā

children.translated_text: composition of words and syllables, wretched with poverty, be of unfailing desire for me! //
I do not obtain even a moment's worship of your lotus-feet; to that end, may this special
whose shores are hurled up in turbulence with terrible crashing, splitting, bursting great laughter —
From the ocean whose waves roll wildly with water churned by winds roaring at the end of an age,
freely cross to the shore at once, O Goddess, through being devoted to your praise! //
those who are drowning, their boats shattered, feebly motionless with piteous cries and wailing,
with sparks creeping across the expanse of sky-homes born from the wombs of clouds confused with smoke —
Those whose beds rest in houses of flame — terrible blazing fires of swiftly spreading conflagration,
are supported in an instant by the swiftness of rain-clouds brilliant with flashing lightning! //
with their cupped palms of homage bound to you, their crowns joined in prayer, their supplications uttered with choked voice,
summoned by its trumpeting, with garlands dangling from its flanks dripping with must-water,
Of an elephant maddened by rut, whose rage-fire is kindled by the challenging roar of a rival elephant
and sits rejoicing on the peak of a broad mountain summit! //

flees in terror, turning away, upon hearing words anointed with meaning from a hymn composed in your honor! //
raging, coming near from nearby, with terrible fangs bared in his gaping mouth,

One whose hair is cruelly pulled by fierce soldiers of an angry platoon, frightened by the master's frown,

children.text: kṣuttṛṭkṣāmopakaṇṭhastyajati sa sapadi vyāpadaṃ tāṃ durantāṃ

when hemmed in by powerful enemies of mighty arm-strength in the time of battle,

through devotion to the practice of the excellent remedy-pill of worship at your feet,
from poverty of learning —
One whose scriptural begging-bowl has rested with teachers, who has become mute in learned assemblies
even he, through the power of devotion to you, captures the lion-throne of debaters in royal assemblies! //
attaining lordship of speech adorned with all ornaments and wealth,
crushing lice, begging at others' doors with a skull-bowl seeking nourishment —
One gray with dust from sleeping on the ground, his body displayed in tattered rags at the hip,
fanned by chowries of lovely young women, with a single parasol raised above the dense tusks of maddened elephants! //
having worshipped you with determination, he holds a beautiful broad earth
not obtaining wealth — the auspicious fruit of merit accumulated in former births —
Those exhausted by the various means of service, labor, craft, entreaty, exchange, and stratagem,
the destitute obtain heaps of refined gold, inexhaustible treasuries! //
having entreated you, O Mother of the wretched, who surpass fate, for wealth,
shunned from afar by his own people, sons, friends, and kinsmen for his selfishness —
One ashamed at loss of livelihood, scolded by his wife in torn garments,

children.text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 7: (Ārya)tārāṣṭottaraśatanāmastotram
children.translated_text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 7: The Hymn of 108 Names of Noble <s>Tārā</s>
Oṃ! Homage to glorious Noble <s>Tārā</s>!
In the glorious, delightful <s>Potalaka</s>, brilliant with various minerals,
filled with various trees and creepers, resounding with various birds,
echoing with the sounds of various waterfalls, teeming with various animals,
perfumed on all sides by various kinds of flowers,
endowed with various heart-pleasing fruits, with the singing sounds of bees,
with <s>kinnaras</s> singing sweetly, crowded with maddened elephants,
resounding with hosts of <s>siddhas</s>, <s>vidyādharas</s>, and <s>gandharvas</s>,
constantly well-attended by sages free from passion,
and by other hosts of <s>bodhisattvas</s>, lords of the ten stages,
by deities such as Noble <s>Tārā</s>, and by thousands of <s>vidyā</s>-queens,
and surrounded by other hosts of wrathful kings such as <s>Hayagrīva</s> —
the Blessed <s>Avalokita</s> (Avalokiteśvara), devoted to the welfare of all beings,
the glorious one, seated on a lotus-womb throne, then spoke.

children.text: mahatā tapasā yukto maitryā ca kṛpayānvitaḥ //
children.translated_text: Endowed with great austerity, with loving-kindness and compassion,

children.text: dharmaṃ dideśa tasyāṃ ca mahatyāṃ devaparṣadi /
children.translated_text: he taught the Dharma in that great assembly of gods.
Then <s>Vajrapāṇi</s> of great strength, having arrived there,
endowed with supreme compassion, questioned <s>Avalokita</s>:
'In a place teeming with robbers, serpents, fierce lions, elephants, and tigers —
These beings, O sage, are sinking, drowned in the ocean of <s>saṃsāra</s>,
bound by the fetters of worldly existence, made of passion, hatred, and darkness.

children.text: mucyante yena sattvāste tanme brūhi mahāmune /
children.translated_text: Tell me, O great sage, that by which those beings are liberated.
Thus addressed, the Lord of the World, the glorious <s>Avalokita</s>,
spoke sweet words, awakening <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>:
'Listen, O <s>Guhyaka</s> lord <s>Indra</s>, to the saving hymn of <s>Amitābha</s>,
born from the power of his vow, my command, the Mother of the World,
endowed with great compassion, raised for the deliverance of the universe.
Resembling the risen sun, with a face radiant as the full moon,
this <s>Tārā</s> illuminates gods, <s>asuras</s>, and humans.',

children.text: kampayantīṃ ca trīn lokān trāsayantīṃ yakṣarākṣasān /
children.translated_text: She who shakes the three worlds and terrifies <s>yakṣas</s> and <s>rākṣasas</s>,

children.text: nīlotpalakarāṃ devīṃ mā bhairmā bhairiti bruvan //
children.translated_text: the goddess holding a blue lotus, saying 'Fear not, fear not!'
'For the protection of the world, I have been produced by the <s>Jinas</s> (Victorious Ones).
In wilderness, in the clash of weapons, amidst manifold terrors,
by the mere remembrance of my names, I always protect beings.
I shall ferry beings across the great ocean of manifold fears.

children.text: tena tāreti māṃ loke gāyanti munipuṃgavāḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, the chief of sages sing of me in the world as <s>Tārā</s> (the Saviouress).'
Then, with palms joined, with reverence and awe,
he made her blaze in the sky and spoke these words:
'Recite the hundred-and-eight names that were formerly proclaimed
by the lords of the ten stages, the greatly powerful <s>Bodhisattvas</s>.',
'They remove all sins, are meritorious, auspicious, and fame-increasing,
bestow wealth and grain, and promote health and nourishment.
They generate long life and health, and bring happiness to all beings,
establish the glory of <s>Lakṣmī</s>, and promote the welfare of all beings.
Relying on loving-kindness toward all beings, recite them, O great sage.'
Thus addressed, the Lord of the World, the smiling <s>Avalokita</s>,
having surveyed all the directions with a gaze suffused with loving-kindness,
raising his right hand, adorned with auspicious marks,
the greatly wise one spoke to him: 'Excellent! Excellent! O great ascetic!
Hear these names, O greatly fortunate one, O sole cherisher of all beings,
by reciting which, mortals shall become prosperous and lords of wealth,
freed from all diseases, endowed with all sovereignty and virtues.
Those burned by untimely death, having departed, go to <s>Sukhāvatī</s> (the Pure Land).
I shall now declare them — O assemblies of gods, listen to me!
Rejoice in this, and you shall become perfectly blissful.'

These one hundred and eight names that I have recited

They bring good fortune and enjoyment, and destroy all sins,
pacify all diseases, and bring happiness to all beings.
One who, being wise and pure, recites them three times daily in a clean place,
will, in no long time, obtain the glory of sovereignty.

children.translated_text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 8: The Praise of Noble <s>Tārā</s>, composed by Ācārya <s>Candradāsa</s>.
Homage to <s>Tārā</s>!
whose feet-moons are kissed and anointed by the abundant spread of copious flame-tips —
With a cluster of beautiful rays from the crest-jewel of the lovely wheel of bliss,
I compose, O Goddess, a hymn of praise as a fitting offering to you.
O one whose compassionate eyes are turned sideways with startled concern, even toward the world of moving and unmoving things,
guarding the vast expanse of blood-curtains — those forest-plunderers,
Those whose nails, with hard tips, tear open the flanks of elephant foreheads, causing terrible gashes,
when devoted to you, instantly lose even their blunted strength of ferocity.
fierce with terrifying laughter, their manes standing erect, formidable like hollowed banks on cliff-slopes — those lions,
with buzzing swarms of bees creating a dense clamor, sporting in graceful play,
With flowing rut-water dripping from their great dark cheek-surfaces, staggering and bewildered,
elephants do not move on the path, steady as mountain ranges, when charmed by your name.
with the fragrant powder on their bodies blown up by the wind of their flapping ear-fans —
terrifying the quarters with the cries 'Alas! Alas!' of the city-women whose homes are being destroyed,
With masses of flame-tips leaping up from the force of wind-blows,
fire, even raging greatly, goes to rest through devotion and homage to you.

children.text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 9: Aṣṭamātṛkāstotram
children.translated_text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 9: Hymn to the Eight Mothers (<s>Aṣṭamātṛkā Stotra</s>).
<s>Oṃ</s> Homage to the glorious <s>Vighneśvara</s> and the Eight Mothers!
O <s>Vighneśvara</s>, great hero, of the form of <s>Siddhi</s>, for the sake of prosperity,
destroyer of obstacles, O god, to <s>Gaṇeśa</s> I bow.
In the east, the goddess <s>Brahmāṇī</s>, seated upon a swan —
a goddess of yellow luster — to <s>Śrī Brahmāṇī</s>, homage to you!
In the south, <s>Śrī Vārāhī</s>, seated upon a buffalo —
red in color, holding a goad — to <s>Śrī Vārāhī</s>, homage to you!
In the west, the goddess <s>Indrāṇī</s>, seated upon an elephant —
saffron-hued, holding a <s>vajra</s> — to <s>Śrī Indrāṇī</s>, homage to you!
In the north, the goddess <s>Māheśvarī</s>, seated upon a bull —
a goddess of white luster — to <s>Māheśvarī</s>, homage to you!
In the southeast, young <s>Kaumārī</s>, filling with the beauty of a peacock —
red in color, holding a spear — to <s>Śrī Kaumārī</s>, homage to you!
In the southwest, the goddess <s>Vaiṣṇavī</s>, dark-hued, seated upon <s>Garuḍa</s> —
bearing conch and discus — to <s>Nārāyaṇī</s>, homage to you!
In the northwest, the goddess <s>Cāmuṇḍā</s>, seated upon a lion —
bearing the form of the syllable <s>ka</s>, holding a sword — to her I bow.
In the northeast, the goddess <s>Caṇḍikā</s>, smoke-colored and blazing —
bearing a cleaver and a skull — to <s>Mahālakṣmī</s>, homage to you!
To the goddesses established in eight seats, dwelling in eight trees,
united with eight <s>Bhairavas</s> — to the Eight Mothers, I bow.
The Sun, the Moon, Mars (Son of Earth), Mercury, the Guru of gods and <s>asuras</s> (Jupiter),

children.text: śaniśca rāhuḥ ketuśca yamāya ca namo namaḥ //
children.translated_text: Saturn, <s>Rāhu</s>, and <s>Ketu</s> — and to <s>Yama</s>, homage, homage!
The Hymn to the <s>Śrī Aṣṭamātṛkā</s> (Eight Mothers) is complete.

children.text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 10: Avadhānastotram (vandanāstavaṃ vā)
children.translated_text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 10: <s>Avadhāna Stotra</s> (or <s>Vandanā Stava</s>).
<s>Oṃ</s> Homage to the Lord of the World!
You are worshipped by the hosts of <s>nāgas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, and worldly beings; to you who are venerated by <s>gandharvas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, and sages,
who are adorned with the thirty-two excellent primary marks — I always bow my head to you, the compassionate one.
To you whose body is equal in radiance to tens of millions of young suns, who at the summit is beheld wearing the crest of the <s>Sugata</s>,

children.text: śubhrāṃśumaulitilakāya jaṭadharāya nityaṃ namāmi śirasā karuṇāmayāya //
children.translated_text: who has the tilaka of a bright-rayed diadem, who bears matted locks — I always bow my head to you, the compassionate one.
To you who are seated on a lotus throne with lotus-hands, who are splendidly adorned with a sacred thread of the serpent-king,
who are brilliantly decorated with necklaces of gems and gold — I always bow my head to you, the compassionate one.
To you who ferry across the ocean of existence with its arising and destruction, who liberate those in evil states difficult to escape,

children.text: rāgādidoṣaparimukta sunirmalāya nityaṃ namāmi śirasā karuṇāmayāya //
children.translated_text: who are spotlessly pure, freed from the faults of passion and the rest — I always bow my head to you, the compassionate one.
To you who dwell in the four <s>brahmavihāras</s> (divine abodes) beginning with <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness), who nourish all beings with streams of nectar,
who rend apart the faults born of the darkness of delusion — I always bow my head to you, the compassionate one.
To you who grant liberation from the chain of the lineage of <s>daitya</s>-lords, who are resolved and swift in benefiting beings,
whose teaching is filled with omniscient knowledge — I always bow my head to you, the compassionate one.
To you who purify the path of the eighteen hells, who dispel the dense darkness of ignorance,
who grant liberation through the single eye of knowledge — I always bow my head to you, the compassionate one.
You, O <s>Lokanātha</s> (Lord of the World), Lord of the universe, the great giver, who shatter the cage of poverty and suffering —
to you whose pair of lotus-feet are venerated — I always bow my head to you, the compassionate one.
I praise you, whose nature is <s>tathatā</s> (suchness), with the radiance of the orb of the sun, whose power is immaculate and supremely fruit-giving,

children.text: cintāmaṇiṃ susadṛśaṃ tvatidurbhago 'haṃ nityaṃ namāmi śirasā karuṇāmayāya //
children.translated_text: who resembles a <s>cintāmaṇi</s> (wish-fulfilling gem) — I who am most unfortunate always bow my head to you, the compassionate one.
With devotion, with my ten fingertips joined above my head, prostrating with the eight limbs before your lotus feet —

children.text: duḥkhārṇave patitamuddhara māṃ kṛpālo nityaṃ namāmi śirasā karuṇāmayāya //
children.translated_text: lift me who have fallen into the ocean of suffering, O compassionate one! I always bow my head to you, the compassionate one.
On the seventh-eighth day of the bright fortnight of <s>Mādhava</s> (spring month), under the <s>Punarvasu</s> constellation combined with <s>Tārā</s>, on Friday —

children.text: śrīkrauṃcadāraṇatithau ca stutiṃ karomi me dehi vāñchitaphalaṃ bhuvanaikanātha //
children.translated_text: on the day of the splitting of <s>Krauñca</s>, I compose this praise; grant me the desired fruit, O sole Lord of the world!
Those who recite this, which is greatly meritorious, sacred, and destructive of sins,
will attain the fulfillment of all desires and purposes, and will go to <s>Sukhāvatī</s> (the Pure Land).
The <s>Avadhānastotra</s> of the glorious noble Lord <s>Avalokiteśvara</s> is complete.

children.text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 11: Avalokiteśvarahayagrīvadhāraṇī
children.translated_text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 11: <s>Avalokiteśvarahayagrīvadhāraṇī</s>

children.text: namo ratnatrayāya / nama āryāvalokiteśvarāya bodhisattvāya mahāsattvāya mahākāruṇikāya / namaḥ sarvasattvavyasanaghātine / namaḥ sarvasattvavyasanāvahāriṇe / namaḥ sarvasattvabhayottāraṇāya / namaḥ sarvabhavapraśamanakarāya / namaḥ sarvasattvabodhicikitsaṃkarāya / namaḥ sarvabandhanacchedanaparāya / namaḥ sarvaduḥkhapramokṣaṇakarāya / namaḥ sarvāndhakāravidhamanakarāya / namaḥ sarvavidyārājavaśaprāptaye mahāyogayogīśvarāya /
children.translated_text: Homage to the Three Jewels! Homage to the noble <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, <s>Bodhisattva</s>, <s>Mahāsattva</s>, the greatly compassionate one! Homage to the destroyer of all beings' misfortunes! Homage to the remover of all beings' calamities! Homage to the deliverer from all beings' fears! Homage to the one who pacifies all states of existence! Homage to the one who applies the healing of awakening to all beings! Homage to the one devoted to cutting all bonds! Homage to the one who liberates from all suffering! Homage to the one who dispels all darkness! Homage for the attainment of mastery over all <s>vidyā</s>-kings, to the Lord of great <s>yoga</s> and <s>yogins</s>!

children.text: tasmai namaskṛtvā idamāryāvalokiteśvaramukhodgīrṇam / ṛṣividadādevanāgayakṣarākṣasaśakrabrahmalokapālaviṣṇumaheśvaranārāyaṇaskandakuberāsurendramātṛgaṇa namaskṛtaṃ vajrakṣuramahīyaṃ hayagrīvabrahmaparamahṛdayamāvartayiṣyāmi / aprameyārthasādhakam asahyaṃ sarvabhūtānāṃ sarvavighnavināśakam / amoghaṃ sarvakarmaṇāṃ viṣāṇāñca vināyanam / tad yathā
children.translated_text: Having paid homage to him, I shall recite this supreme heart-<s>mantra</s> of <s>Hayagrīva</s> (Horse-necked one), the diamond-razor, uttered from the mouth of the noble <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, honored by <s>ṛṣis</s>, <s>vidyādharas</s>, <s>devas</s>, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>rākṣasas</s>, <s>Śakra</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Lokapālas</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Maheśvara</s>, <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, <s>Skanda</s>, <s>Kubera</s>, <s>Asurendra</s>, and the host of <s>Mātṛs</s>. It accomplishes immeasurable purposes, is irresistible to all beings, destroys all obstacles, is unfailing in all actions, and subdues poisons. Thus:

children.text: om tarula tarula vitarula vitarula sarvaviṣaghātaka sarvabhūtavidrāvaka jvalitānalavisphuliṅgāṭṭahāsa kesarātopāpravitakāya vajrakṣuranirgatita calitavasudhātala bajrodaśvasata hāsitamarutakṣatipraśamanakara paraduṣṭavighnān saṃbhakṣaṇakara svavidyopadeśakara paramaśāntikara buddha buddha bodhayāmiti /
children.translated_text: Oṃ <s>tarula tarula vitarula vitarula sarvaviṣaghātaka sarvabhūtavidrāvaka jvalitānalavisphuliṅgāṭṭahāsa kesarātopāpravitakāya vajrakṣuranirgatita calitavasudhātala vajrodaśvasata hāsitamarutakṣatipraśamanakara paraduṣṭavighnān saṃbhakṣaṇakara svavidyopadeśakara paramaśāntikara buddha buddha bodhayāmiti</s>.

children.text: bhagavan hayagrīva sarvavidyāhṛdayamāvartayiṣyāmi / khāda khāda mahāraudramantreṇa / rakṣa rakṣa ātmasvahitān mantreṇa / sidhya sidhya sarvakarmasu me siddhe dehi dehi / āveśa āveśa praveśa praveśa sarvagraheṣu apratihata / dhuna dhuna vidhuna vidhuna matha matha pramatha pramatha sarvavaropagrama / kṛtakakhordo / durlaṅghita mūṣika / viṣakara viṣadraṃṣṭra viṣacūrṇayo abhicāraviṣakaraṇa / sidhya añjana cakṣurmohana / cittavikṣobhaṇakara / nityāparaprekṣaṇa trāsaya trāsaya mahābodhisattva ṛddhadaṃṣṭraṇena sarvabhayebhyaḥ sattvānāṃ rakṣa rakṣa / mama buddhadharmasaṃghānujñātaṃ me karma śīghraṃ kuru kuru phaṭ / hayagrīvāya phaṭ / bajrakṣurāya phaṭ / vajradaṃṣṭrotkaṭabhayabhairavāya phaṭ / paramantraṇanāśanakarāya phaṭ / paraduṣṭavighnān saṃbhakṣaṇakarāya phaṭ / sarvagrahotsādanakarāya phaṭ / sarvagraheṣu
children.translated_text: O <s>Bhagavan Hayagrīva</s>, I shall recite the heart of all <s>vidyās</s>! Devour, devour, with the great fierce <s>mantra</s>! Protect, protect the self and beneficent ones with the <s>mantra</s>! Succeed, succeed in all my deeds! Give, give! Enter, enter, penetrate, penetrate all seizures unobstructed! Shake, shake, agitate, agitate, churn, churn, crush, crush all hostile assemblies! One of accomplished fury! Insurmountable mouse! Poison-maker, poison-fanged, poison-powder, sorcery-poison-doer! Succeed, O collyrium! Eye-deluder! Mind-agitator! Ever-watchful one! Terrify, terrify, O great <s>Bodhisattva</s>, with mighty fangs, protect, protect beings from all fears! Authorized by the <s>Buddha</s>, <s>Dharma</s>, and <s>Saṅgha</s>, quickly accomplish my deed! <s>Phaṭ</s>! To <s>Hayagrīva</s>, <s>phaṭ</s>! To the diamond-razor, <s>phaṭ</s>! To the terrifyingly fierce one with adamantine protruding fangs, <s>phaṭ</s>! To the destroyer of hostile <s>mantras</s>, <s>phaṭ</s>! To the devourer of hostile evil obstacles, <s>phaṭ</s>! To the annihilator of all seizures, <s>phaṭ</s>! To the one

children.text: apratihatāya phaṭ / paṭalamukhāya phaṭ / ye kecit mama ahiteṣiṇaḥ kāye kramanti mantrayaṇa yamanti juhvānati kākhordaṃ kurvanti / tena sarveṇābhimukhena vākrīhāya phaṭ / namaḥ sarvaduṣṭagrahotsādanāya hayagrīvāya sidhyantu mantrapadaiḥ svāhā / om amitodbhavāya huṃ phaṭ phaṭ svāhā / om namo hayāya svāhā / om namo viśvamūrtaye svāhā / namaḥ sarvasattvānāṃ sidhyantu mantrapadāya svāhā //
children.translated_text: unobstructed among all seizures, <s>phaṭ</s>! To the one of the <s>paṭala</s>-face, <s>phaṭ</s>! Whatever ill-wishers against me who approach my body, who enchant with <s>mantras</s>, who summon <s>Yama</s>, who make offerings, who perform sorcery — against all of them, turning them face to face, <s>phaṭ</s>! Homage to the annihilator of all evil seizures, <s>Hayagrīva</s>! May the <s>mantra</s>-words succeed! <s>Svāhā</s>! Oṃ, to the one born of <s>Amita</s>, <s>huṃ phaṭ phaṭ svāhā</s>! Oṃ, homage to <s>Haya</s> (the Horse), <s>svāhā</s>! Oṃ, homage to the one of universal form, <s>svāhā</s>! Homage! May the <s>mantra</s>-words succeed for all beings! <s>Svāhā</s>!

children.text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 12: Avalokiteśvarāṣṭakastotram
children.translated_text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 12: <s>Avalokiteśvarāṣṭakastotram</s>
Oṃ, homage to <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>!

children.text: stutvā guṇairanupamairanubindupātraṃ stotraṃ mayā kṛtamidaṃ jaḍavāliśena /
children.translated_text: Having praised with incomparable virtues the vessel worthy of each drop — this hymn has been composed by me, the dull and foolish one;

children.text: lokeśvaraṃ guṇanidhiṃ guṇasāgaraṃ ca nityaṃ namāmi śirasāñjalisaṃpuṭena //
children.translated_text: I always bow my head with palms joined to the Lord of the World, the treasure of virtues, the ocean of virtues.

children.text: prāṇeṣu yan sravati yena rasāmbupārān kṣuttṛṣṇaduḥkhaparipīḍitasarvasattvān /
children.translated_text: He by whom life-breath flows through beings, by whom the waters of nectar flow — for all beings afflicted by the suffering of hunger and thirst —

children.text: evaṃvidhaṃ jagadidaṃ paripālanāya tasmai namo 'stu satataṃ hi yathārthanāmne //
children.translated_text: for the protection of this world in such a manner — to him whose name is true to its meaning, constant homage!
Of a color like excellent saffron-anointed reddish marks, with bodily beauty adorned by the thirty-two marks,

children.text: sarveṣu yasya karuṇāmayavatsalatvaṃ tasmai namāmi bhavate karuṇāmayāya //
children.translated_text: he whose compassionate affection is toward all — I bow to you, the compassionate one.
O one skilled in destroying the great abode of the ocean of <s>saṃsāra</s>, you alone are the refuge on earth, the sole Lord;

children.text: kenāpi tvadguṇagaṇā gaṇane na śakyāstaṃ lokanāthamavalokitanāmasaṃjñam //
children.translated_text: your multitudes of virtues cannot be counted by anyone — that Lord of the World, known by the name <s>Avalokita</s>.
Of divine form adorned with various ornaments, the Lord of the World with matted hair decorated with a crescent moon,

children.text: vāme ca maṇḍaladharaṃ varadaṃ ca savye tvāṃ lokanātha śaraṇaṃ pravrajāmi nityam //
children.translated_text: holding a disc in the left hand and the boon-granting gesture in the right — to you, O Lord of the World, I always go for refuge.
Surrounded by <s>Brahmā</s> and others, by hosts of gods and <s>siddhas</s>, <s>gandharvas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, great <s>uragas</s>, <s>nāgas</s>, and <s>yakṣas</s> —

children.text: nāthasya yasya bhavataścaraṇāmbujaṃ ca taṃ lokanāthacaraṇaṃ śaraṇaṃ vrajāmi //
children.translated_text: the lotus-feet of that Lord of yours — I go for refuge to the feet of the Lord of the World.
By <s>bhūtas</s>, <s>piśācas</s>, <s>garuḍas</s>, <s>uragas</s>, <s>rākṣasīs</s>, <s>kumbhāṇḍas</s>, <s>pūtanas</s>, great <s>hallakas</s>, kings of kings,

children.text: vaiśvānarāsuraśataiḥ parivārabhūtaṃ taṃ lokanāthacaraṇaṃ śaraṇaṃ gato 'smi //
children.translated_text: <s>Vaiśvānara</s>, and hundreds of <s>asuras</s> — surrounded as retinue — I have gone for refuge to the feet of that Lord of the World.
The ocean is not dried up by the rays of the sun; likewise your ocean of virtues is not exhausted by hundreds of great poets;
O Lord of the World, you who are the repository of celebrated fame — the treasure of virtues of the ocean of virtues is not depleted.

children.text: ślokāṣṭakaṃ pratidinaṃ khalu ye paṭhanti te prāpnuvanti sahasā dhanaputramokṣān /
children.translated_text: Those who recite this eight-verse hymn daily — they quickly obtain wealth, sons, and liberation;

children.text: kuṣṭhādiroganikaraṃ kṣamatāṃ prayāti vandāmahe ca nitarāṃ tava pādayugme //
children.translated_text: the multitude of diseases beginning with leprosy comes to an end — we venerate your pair of feet exceedingly.
The eight-verse hymn of the noble, glorious <s>Avalokiteśvara</s> is complete.

children.text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 13: Avalokiteśvarastavaḥ candrakāntābhikṣuṇīkṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 13: Praise of <s>Avalokiteśvara</s> composed by the nun <s>Candrakāntā</s>
Oṃ, homage to <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>!
The world-teacher venerated by the three realms, the supreme <s>Brahmā</s> praised by the lord of the immortals,
the best of sage-kings, the one who brings radiant perfection — I bow to the one who bears the name <s>Avalokita</s>.
Of beautiful form like a son of the <s>Sugata</s>, with an excellent body adorned with many marks,
wearing <s>Amitābha Tathāgata</s> on the crown, with the left hand adorned by a golden lotus.
With curling, pure, tawny-brown matted locks, with a full face shining like the disc of the moon,
with beautiful wide lotus-eyes, with a pair of cheeks pale-white like a piece of snow.
With lips surpassing the beauty of a lotus-navel, with a voice like the rumbling of an autumn cloud,
with a pair of arms adorned with many gems, with palms soft and green like tender grass.
With the left side of the body wrapped in a deer-skin, with beautiful earrings adorning the swinging ear-lobes,
with a spotless navel-region like the center of a lotus, with an excellent golden girdle adorned with gems.
Wearing beautiful, colorful garments wrapped at the waist, one who has crossed the great ocean of the <s>Jina</s>'s awakening,
who has obtained boons earned through much merit, who destroys fever and disease, who produces much happiness.
Who brings auspicious peace, who creates in the three existences, who is praised by the moving and the sky-moving,
who has conquered <s>Māra</s>'s forces through various means, who accomplishes the ultimate meaning of the ten <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections).
Devoted to the seclusion of the fourfold <s>vihāra</s>, who produces the awakening of non-dual <s>tathatā</s> (suchness),
with a pair of feet resounding with jeweled anklets, with a gait slow and stately like an elephant or a swan.
Who has attained steadfastness through the full great nectar, whose constant course is in the milk-ocean,
who delights in dwelling at <s>Śrī Potalaka</s>, of compassionate nature, with spotless, beautiful eyes.
The praise of the glorious noble Lord <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, composed by the nun <s>Candrakāntā</s>, is complete.

children.text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 14: Avalokiteśvarastotram carapatipādaviracitam
children.translated_text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 14: Praise of <s>Avalokiteśvara</s> composed by <s>Carapati</s>
Oṃ, homage to <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>!
Whose feet are praised by gods, men, and <s>asuras</s>; who has overcome birth, old age, disease, and death;

children.text: lokeśa tvaṃ māmaśaraṇyaṃ rakṣa kṛpālo kuru kāruṇyam //
children.translated_text: O Lord of the World, protect me who am without refuge! O compassionate one, show mercy!
I am sunk in the midst of the ocean of <s>saṃsāra</s>, broken by the great waves of the <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions);

children.text: māmavadhāraya mā viruvantaṃ trāhi mahākṛpa naumi bhavantam //
children.translated_text: support me, do not let me cry out! Save me, O greatly compassionate one! I bow to you.
My eyes are afflicted by the darkness of craving; my limbs tremble with the great fear of death;

children.text: pālaya bhagavannavalokaya māṃ yāvadavīciṃ yāmi na viṣamām //
children.translated_text: protect me, O <s>Bhagavan</s>, look upon me, so that I do not go to the terrible <s>Avīci</s> (hell).
I have constantly seized the wives of others; I have killed thousands of living beings unknowingly;

children.text: nātha mayā kṛtapāpamaśeṣaṃ nāśaya saṃprati kāyikadoṣam //
children.translated_text: O Lord, I have committed boundless sin — now destroy my bodily faults!
Whatever untruth I have constantly spoken to the world for the sake of livelihood and honor —
O <s>Lokeśvara</s>, pacify all of that verbal karma leading to hell, long practiced.
Whatever harmful thoughts toward beings, whatever evil deeds of men I myself have approved —

children.text: adhunā tanmama mānasapāpaṃ sphoṭaya nātha karomi vilāpam //
children.translated_text: now destroy that mental sin of mine, O Lord! I make lamentation.
Of the births of gods, men, and <s>asuras</s>, of the destinies of animals, hell-beings, and hungry ghosts —

children.text: sattvā ye nivasanti sadārtā rakṣasi tāniti tava mayi vārtā //
children.translated_text: the beings who always dwell in suffering — the report of you is that you protect them.

children.text: tena mamopari sṛja kāruṇyaṃ vīkṣya śarīragataṃ tāruṇyam /
children.translated_text: Therefore, pour compassion upon me, beholding the youth dwelling in my body;

children.text: iti śṛṇu bhagavan bhavati bhaṇāmi yāvannarakaṃ naiva viśāmi //
children.translated_text: thus hear, O <s>Bhagavan</s>, I declare: may I never enter hell!

children.text: kiṃ copetya karoṣi parārthaṃ muñcasi bhagavan māmakṛtārtham /
children.translated_text: Why do you come and act for others' benefit, O <s>Bhagavan</s>, while releasing me unfulfilled?

children.text: athavā prekṣya kṛpā tava puṇyaṃ janayasi dṛṣṭaṃ kathamavipannam //
children.translated_text: Or rather, seeing compassion, do you generate merit — how is what is seen not in vain? //

children.text: smaraṇenāpi bhavasi parituṣṭaḥ kṣipasi ca kaluṣaṃ kimiti na dṛṣṭaḥ /
children.translated_text: Even by remembrance you are pleased, and you cast away impurity — why then are you not seen?

children.text: yasmād bhagavan parahitadakṣa kṣepaṃ mā kuru māmiha rakṣa //
children.translated_text: Since, O Blessed One, you are skilled in helping others, do not reject me — protect me here! //
Elephants, horses, sons, wives, untroubled kingdom, wondrous dwellings,
bones, skulls, blood, flesh, and all — endlessly given to those who sought from you. //
The <s>siddhi</s> of collyrium, magical sandals, accomplished herbs, purification of gems and mantras,

children.text: siddhayati yakṣastrīpuraveśaḥ tuṣyasi yasya tvaṃ lokeśa //
children.translated_text: entry into the city of <s>yakṣa</s>-women — all these are attained by one with whom you, O Lord of the World, are pleased. //
Those who are deprived of hands, feet, and eyes, afflicted by various diseases and great fears —

children.text: te tvayi tuṣṭe puṣṭaśarīrā vilasantyarujo guṇagambhīrāḥ //
children.translated_text: when you are pleased, they become full-bodied, sporting free from disease, deep in virtues. //

children.text: garalaṃ vyādhirgrahaḍākinyaḥ śāntiṃ yānti sadā yoginyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Poisons, diseases, <s>grahas</s> (possessing spirits), and <s>ḍākinīs</s> are always pacified, as are <s>yoginīs</s>;

children.text: sarati na tasya puro yamadūtaḥ proto yasya ca tvaṃ jinabhūtaḥ //
children.translated_text: the messenger of <s>Yama</s> does not approach before him who has you, O embodiment of the <s>Jina</s>, as protector. //

children.text: iti lokeśvara kiṃ kriyamāṇaṃ muñcasi bhagavan māmatrāṇam /
children.translated_text: Thus, O Lord of the World, what are you doing? Will you release me, O Blessed One, without protection?
I cry out daily with uplifted hands — destroy the fear in my agitated voice! //
Whatever sin has been committed by me with a mind distracted by sense-objects and restless senses,

children.text: nītaṃ janma mayā 'smin sakalaṃ jaṭharanimittaṃ bhramatā vikalam //
