children.translated_text: this entire birth has been led by me wandering confused, for the sake of the belly alone. //

children.text: tatkuru saṃprati mama lokeśa praṇato vividhāñjalirahameṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore act now for me, O Lord of the World! I am this one, bowing with various joined palms,

children.text: yenābhuktvāpāyikadoṣaṃ sugatiṃ bhavato yāmi na mokṣam //
children.translated_text: so that, without experiencing the faults of the lower realms, I may go to a good destiny from your presence — not yet to liberation. //
You are the cause of destroying delusion and hatred, you are the bridge across the great ocean of <s>saṃsāra</s>,
you are the one who raises the arm of the fallen and frightened, you are the <s>Rāhu</s> (eclipse) of the moon of heavy sin. //
You are the one who has taught the unsurpassed truth of the <s>Sugata</s>, you are the protector of many suffering beings,
you are the conqueror of the unconquerable <s>Manmatha</s> (Kāma) and <s>Māra</s>, you are the one who has crossed to the far shore of the ocean of existence. //
You are the body that cuts through all tethers, you are the one who has perfected the good body for the world,
O Blessed One, you are the ocean of incomparable compassion, you are known to people as the kinsman without cause. //
You are the one who playfully shatters the divisions of <s>karma</s>, you are the one attached to the domain of benefiting others,
you are the one whose mind is absorbed in divine meditation, you are the one whose heart is shared with all supplicants. //

children.text: paramapakurvaṃnnapi karuṇāvān mayi paritoṣaṃ na karoṣi bhavān /
children.translated_text: Though you do the utmost for the supreme, O compassionate one, you do not bring satisfaction in my case;
how, bitten by the great serpent of delusion, is this body of sense-objects, unwholesome, fallen? //

children.text: sakalajanārthaṃ prati yā karuṇā sā kiṃ bhavato niyataspharaṇā /
children.translated_text: Is your compassion toward all people of fixed reach?

children.text: yena na rakṣasi kilviṣavantaṃ bhavataḥ purato māṃ viruvantam //
children.translated_text: For you do not protect me, a sinner, crying before you! //

children.text: nātha kṛpā te vyomaviśālā sattveṣu hi yathāmbudadhārā /
children.translated_text: O Lord, your compassion is vast as the sky, toward beings like the flow of rain-clouds,
flowing ceaselessly, constantly, to land, water, low and high, in all places without remainder. //
By whatever merit arises from this remembrance of the Blessed One, may this world be unharmed;
may it attain residence at the glorious <s>Potalaka</s> mountain and produce beautiful, various delights. //
The hymn composed by the wandering master at the feet of the glorious noble lord <s>Avalokiteśvara</s> is complete. //

children.text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 15: Avalokiteśvarastotram vāsukināgarājakṛtam
children.translated_text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 15: Hymn to <s>Avalokiteśvara</s> composed by the <s>Nāga</s> king <s>Vāsuki</s>
Oṃ, homage to <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>!
Bearing matted locks, with gentle, expansive eyes, whose face is like an ever-radiant moon,
whose lotus-feet are worshipped by gods and <s>asuras</s> — I bow to the lord born of the jewel-lotus. //
Whose divine eyes are wide as lotus petals, whose pure vision purifies wrong views,
whose compassion-nectar moistens — the sole eye of the world — I bow to the lord born of the jewel-lotus. //
Blazing more than half-moon necklaces and snow, with polished, spotless, swaying earrings on the cheeks,
crowded with millions of garlands of rays — I bow to the lord born of the jewel-lotus. //
Awakened on the path of Dharma, of the Dharma-realm, with a thousand arms, or two, four, or six arms,
with arms infinite as the space-element — I bow to the lord born of the jewel-lotus. //
Born from the churning of the ocean of skillful means and wisdom, born for the sake of protecting the three realms,
crowned among the lords of conquerors, born from the essence of the <s>Jina</s> — I bow to the lord born of the jewel-lotus. //
Standing upon a lotus, the lord, lotus in hand, bearing matted locks —
I honor the noble <s>Avalokita</s>, the compassionate one toward all beings. //
The hymn to noble <s>Avalokiteśvara</s> composed by the <s>Nāga</s> king <s>Śrī Vāsuki</s> is complete. //

children.text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 16: Avalokiteśvarāṣṭottaraśatanāmastotram
children.translated_text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 16: The One Hundred and Eight Name Hymn of <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>
Oṃ, homage to <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>!
<s>Padmasattva</s>, great lotus, Lord of the World, great lord,
Lord <s>Avalokita</s>, foremost in resolve, <s>Vajradharma</s> — homage to you! //
Dharma-king, greatly pure, king of beings, of great wisdom,
lotus-souled, great lotus, lord of the lotus — homage to you! //
Lotus-born, of lovely lotus-radiance, lotus-pure, great purifier,
<s>vajra</s>-lotus, beautifully lotus-marked, lotus of lotuses — homage to you! //
Great universe, great radiance, great body, great likeness,
greatly resolute, great hero, great valor — homage to you! //
Intent on beings, <s>Mahāyāna</s>, great yoga, grandfather,

children.text: śambhu śaṅkara śuddhārtha buddhapadma namo 'stu te //
children.translated_text: <s>Śambhu</s>, <s>Śaṅkara</s>, of pure purpose, <s>Buddha</s>-lotus — homage to you! //
Truth of Dharma-reality, true Dharma, pure Dharma, maker of good Dharma,
great Dharma, foremost of good Dharma, Dharma-wheel — homage to you! //
<s>Buddha</s>-being, foremost of good beings, Dharma-being, upholder of good beings,
supreme being, knower of good beings, being of beings — homage to you! //
Lord <s>Avalokita</s>, foremost protector, great protector, the seen one,
light of light, purpose of the world, lord of the world — homage to you! //
Imperishable syllable of the world, great imperishable, foremost of syllables, likened to the syllable,
imperishable, all-eyed, wheel of syllables — homage to you! //
Lotus-handed, great-handed, consoler, giver,
<s>Buddha</s>-dharma, great <s>Buddha</s>, <s>Buddha</s>-souled — homage to you! //
<s>Buddha</s>-form, great form, <s>vajra</s>-form, knower of beautiful forms,
light of Dharma, foremost of radiance, light of the world — homage to you! //
Lord of <s>Padmaśrī</s>, foremost protector, lord of <s>Dharmaśrī</s>, possessing a protector,
<s>Brahma</s>-lord, great <s>Brahma</s>, son of <s>Brahma</s> — homage to you! //
Lamp, foremost lamp, fierce lamp, light of lamps, good illuminator,
lord of lamps, great lamp, <s>Buddha</s>-lamp — homage to you! //
Consecrated by the <s>Buddha</s>, foremost among <s>Buddhas</s>, son of the <s>Buddha</s>, greatly wise,
foremost in <s>Buddha</s>-consecration of the crown, <s>Buddha</s> of <s>Buddhas</s> — homage to you! //
<s>Buddha</s>-eye, great eye, Dharma-eye, great vision,
the very essence of <s>samādhi</s>-knowledge, <s>vajra</s>-eyed — homage to you! //
Thus, whoever wholeheartedly meditates upon or praises
these one hundred and eight secondary names of yours shall attain lordship over the world. //
The One Hundred and Eight Name Invocation Hymn of Noble <s>Avalokiteśvara</s> is complete. //

children.text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 17: Bhadracarīpraṇidhānastotram
children.translated_text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 17: The Aspiration Prayer of Good Conduct (<s>Bhadracarīpraṇidhāna</s> Hymn)

children.text: atha khalu samantabhadro bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ evameva lokadhātuparamparānabhilāpyānabhilāpya buddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamān kalpān kalpaprasarānabhidyotyamāno bhūyasyā mātrayā gāthābhigītena praṇidhānamakārṣīt -
children.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Samantabhadra</s>, illuminating aeons equaling the atoms of <s>Buddha</s>-fields in successive world-systems beyond expression, to a greater degree made this aspiration in sung verses:

children.text: yāvata keci daśaddiśi loke sarvatriyadhvagatā narasiṃhāḥ /
children.translated_text: However many lion-among-men there are in the ten directions of the world, those gone through the three times —

children.text: tānahu vandami sarvi aśeṣān kāyatu vāca manena prasannaḥ //
children.translated_text: I venerate them all, every one, with body, speech, and mind, joyfully. //
With bodies as numerous as the dust-motes of the fields, I make prostrations to all the conquerors,
facing all the <s>Jinas</s> with my mind, by the power of the <s>Bhadracarī</s> aspiration. //
Upon each dust-mote, <s>Buddhas</s> as numerous as dust-motes, seated amid the sons of the <s>Buddha</s> —
thus I trust that the entire <s>dharmadhātu</s> is completely filled with conquerors. //
In them, with inexhaustible oceans of praise, with sounds from oceans of every voice and limb,

children.text: sarvajināna guṇān bhaṇamānastān sugatān stavamī ahu sarvān //
children.translated_text: proclaiming the virtues of all the conquerors — I praise all those <s>Sugatas</s>. //
With the finest flowers, the finest garlands, music, ointments, and the finest parasols,

children.text: dīpavarebhi ca dhūpavarebhiḥ pūjana teṣa jināna karomi //
children.translated_text: the finest lamps and the finest incense — I make offerings to those conquerors. //
With the finest garments, the finest fragrances, and packets of powders equal to <s>Meru</s>,
with the finest of all excellent arrangements — I make offerings to those conquerors. //

children.text: yā ca anuttarapūja udārā tānadhimucyami sarvajinānām /
children.translated_text: Whatever unsurpassed, exalted offerings there are — I trust in them for all the conquerors;
by the power of faith in good conduct, I venerate and make offerings to all the <s>Jinas</s>. //

children.text: yacca kṛtaṃ mayi pāpu bhaveyyā rāgatu dveṣatu mohavaśena /
children.translated_text: Whatever sin may have been committed by me, through the power of passion, hatred, or delusion,

children.text: kāyatu vāca manena tathaiva taṃ pratideśayamī ahu sarvam //
children.translated_text: whether by body, speech, or mind — I confess it all. //

children.text: yacca daśaddiśi puṇya jagasya śaikṣa aśaikṣapratyekajinānām /
children.translated_text: Whatever merit there is of the world in the ten directions, of learners, non-learners, and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>,

children.text: buddhasutānatha sarvajinānāṃ taṃ anumodayamī ahu sarvam //
children.translated_text: and of the sons of the <s>Buddha</s> and all the conquerors — I rejoice in it all. //

children.text: ye ca daśaddiśi lokapradīpā bodhivibuddha asaṃgataprāptāḥ /
children.translated_text: Those who are lamps of the world in the ten directions, who have awakened to <s>bodhi</s> and attained non-attachment —

children.text: tānahu sarvi adhyeṣami nāthān cakru anuttaru vartanatāyai //
children.translated_text: I beseech all those lords to turn the unsurpassed wheel. //
And those who wish to display <s>Nirvāṇa</s> — I entreat them with joined palms:
remain for aeons equal to the dust of the fields, for the benefit and happiness of all the world! //
In worship, offering, confession,

children.text: yacca śubhaṃ mayi saṃcitu kiṃcidbodhayi nāmayamī ahu sarvam //
children.translated_text: rejoicing, entreaty, and supplication — whatever little good has been accumulated by me, I dedicate it all to awakening. //

children.text: pūjita bhontu atītaka buddhā ye ca dhriyanti daśaddiśi loke /
children.translated_text: May the <s>Buddhas</s> of the past be honored, and those who abide in the worlds of the ten directions,

children.text: ye ca anāgata te laghu bhontu pūrṇamanoratha bodhivibuddhāḥ //
children.translated_text: and those of the future — may they quickly become fully awakened with fulfilled aspirations! //

children.text: yāvata keci daśaddiśi kṣetrāste pariśuddha bhavantu udārāḥ /
children.translated_text: However many fields there are in the ten directions — may they become pure and exalted,
filled with conquerors who have gone to the king of <s>bodhi</s>-trees, and with sons of the <s>Buddha</s>! //

children.text: yāvata keci daśaddiśi sattvāste sukhitā sada bhontu arogāḥ /
children.translated_text: However many beings there are in the ten directions — may they always be happy and free from illness;

children.text: sarvajagasya ca dharmiku artho bhontu pradakṣiṇu ṛdhyatu āśāḥ //
children.translated_text: may the Dharma-purpose of the entire world be auspicious, and may their wishes prosper! //

children.text: bodhicariṃ ca ahaṃ caramāṇo bhavi jātismaru sarvagatīṣu /
children.translated_text: And as I practice the conduct of awakening, may I remember my births in all destinies;

children.text: sarvasu janmasu cyutyupapattī pravrajito ahu nityu bhaveyyā //
children.translated_text: in all births, in death and rebirth, may I always be a renunciant! //
Following the example of all the conquerors, fulfilling the conduct of good practice,
may I always practice moral conduct, stainless, pure, unbroken, and unsplit! //
In the languages of gods, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>kumbhāṇḍas</s>, and humans,

children.text: yāni ca sarvarutāni jagasya sarvaruteṣvahu deśayi dharmam //
children.translated_text: and in whatever languages there are in the world — in all languages may I teach the Dharma! //

children.text: ye khalu pāramitāsvabhiyukto bodhiyi cittu na jātu vimuhyet /
children.translated_text: For one who is devoted to the perfections, may the mind of awakening never be confused;

children.text: ye 'pi ca pāpaka āvaraṇāyāsteṣu parikṣayu bhotu aśeṣam //
children.translated_text: and as for the sins that are obstructions — may they be entirely exhausted! //

children.text: karmatu kleśatu mārapathāto lokagatīṣu vimuktu careyam /
children.translated_text: From <s>karma</s>, afflictions, and the paths of <s>Māra</s>, may I move liberated in the destinies of the world,

children.text: padma yathā salilena aliptaḥ sūryaśaśī gaganeva asaktaḥ //
children.translated_text: as a lotus is unstained by water, as the sun and moon are unattached in the sky! //

children.text: sarvi apāyadukhāṃ praśamanto sarvajagat sukhi sthāpayamānaḥ /
children.translated_text: Pacifying all the sufferings of the lower realms, establishing all the world in happiness,

children.text: sarvajagasya hitāya careyaṃ yāvata kṣetrapathā diśatāsu //
children.translated_text: may I practice for the benefit of all the world, in as many realms as there are in the directions! //
Following the conduct of beings, fulfilling the conduct of awakening,

children.text: bhadracariṃ ca prabhāvayamānaḥ sarvi anāgatakalpa careyam //
children.translated_text: manifesting good conduct — may I practice throughout all future aeons! //

children.text: ye ca sabhāgata mama caryāye tebhi samāgamu nityu bhaveyyā /
children.translated_text: And those who share the same conduct as mine — may I always be gathered with them;

children.text: kāyatu vācatu cetanato cā ekacari praṇidhāna careyam //
children.translated_text: in body, speech, and intention — may I practice the aspiration of unified conduct! //

children.text: ye 'pi ca mitrā mama hitakāmā bhadracarīya nidarśayitāraḥ /
children.translated_text: And those friends who desire my benefit, who reveal the good conduct —

children.text: tebhi samāgamu nityu bhaveyyā tāṃśca ahaṃ na virāgayi jātu //
children.translated_text: may I always be gathered with them, and may I never displease them! //

children.text: saṃmukha nityamahaṃ jina paśye buddhasutebhi parīvṛtu nāthān /
children.translated_text: May I always see the conquerors face to face, the lords surrounded by the sons of the <s>Buddha</s>;

children.text: teṣu ca pūja kareyu udārāṃ sarvi anāgatakalpamakhinnaḥ //
children.translated_text: and may I make exalted offerings to them, throughout all future aeons, unwearied! //
Upholding the true Dharma of the conquerors, illuminating the conduct of awakening,

children.text: bhadracariṃ ca viśodhayamānaḥ sarvi anāgatakalpa careyam //
children.translated_text: purifying good conduct — may I practice throughout all future aeons! //

children.text: sarvabhaveṣu ca saṃcaramāṇaḥ puṇyatu jñānatu akṣayaprāptaḥ /
children.translated_text: And wandering through all existences, having obtained inexhaustible merit and knowledge,
through wisdom, skillful means, concentration, and liberation — may I become an inexhaustible treasury of all virtues in existence.

children.text: ekarajāgri rajopamakṣetrā tatra ca kṣetri acintiyabuddhān /
children.translated_text: In a single atom of dust, in fields equal to atoms, I would behold inconceivable Buddhas there,

children.text: buddhasutāna niṣaṇṇaku madhye paśyiya bodhicariṃ caramāṇaḥ //
children.translated_text: seated amidst the sons of the Buddhas, practicing the conduct of awakening.
Thus, without remainder, in all directions, in realms traversing the three times,
I would enter oceans of Buddhas, oceans of realms, and oceans of eons of spiritual practice.
Through the ocean of sounds of a single syllable, I would enter the purity of voice of all the <s>Jinas</s>,
the sounds according to the aspirations of all the <s>Jinas</s> — I would always enter the eloquence of the Buddhas.
And in those inexhaustible utterances of the <s>Jinas</s> gone through the three times,
as they turn the wheel of the teaching — through the power of understanding, I would enter them.
In a single instant, I would enter all future eons;

children.text: ye 'pi ca kalpa triyadhvapramāṇāstān kṣaṇakoṭipraviṣṭa careyam //
children.translated_text: and those eons spanning the three times — I would traverse them, having entered billions of instants.

children.text: ye ca triyadhvagatā narasiṃhāstānahu paśyiya ekakṣaṇena /
children.translated_text: And those Lion-among-Men gone through the three times — I would behold them in a single instant;

children.text: teṣu ca gocarimotari nityaṃ māyagatena vimokṣabalena //
children.translated_text: and I would always enter their domain, through the liberating power of illusion-like practice.
And those excellent array-realms of the three times — I would produce them on a single atom;
thus, without remainder, in all directions, I would enter the array-realms of the <s>Jinas</s>.

children.text: ye ca anāgata lokapradīpāsteṣu vibudhyana cakrapravṛttim /
children.translated_text: And those future Lamps of the World — their awakening, the turning of the wheel,

children.text: nirvṛtidarśananiṣṭha praśāntiṃ sarvi ahaṃ upasaṃkrami nāthān //
children.translated_text: the display of <s>Nirvāṇa</s>, the peace of cessation — I would approach all those Protectors.
Through the power of miraculous ability, with universal swiftness; through the power of knowledge, with universal scope;
through the power of practice, with universal virtue; through the power of loving-kindness, pervading everywhere;
through the power of merit, universally auspicious; through the power of knowledge, proceeding without attachment;
through the powers of wisdom, skillful means, and concentration — I would gather the power of awakening.
Purifying the power of <s>karma</s>, crushing the power of afflictions,

children.text: mārabalaṃ abalaṃ karamāṇaḥ pūrayi bhadracarībala sarvān //
children.translated_text: rendering the power of <s>Māra</s> powerless — I would fulfill all the powers of the Excellent Conduct.
Purifying the ocean of realms, liberating the ocean of beings,
perceiving the ocean of Dharma, diving into the ocean of knowledge,
purifying the ocean of practice, fulfilling the ocean of vows,
worshipping the ocean of Buddhas — I would practice untiringly through the ocean of eons.
And the special vows of awakening-conduct of the <s>Jinas</s> gone through the three times —

children.text: tānahu pūrayi sarvi aśeṣāt bhadracarīya bibudhyiya bodhim //
children.translated_text: all those I would fulfill without remainder; through the Excellent Conduct, I would awaken to <s>bodhi</s>.

children.text: jyeṣṭhaku yaḥ sutu sarvajinānāṃ yasya ca nāma samantatabhadraḥ /
children.translated_text: He who is the eldest son of all the <s>Jinas</s>, whose name is <s>Samantabhadra</s> —

children.text: tasya vidusya sabhāgacarīye nāmayamī kuśalaṃ imu sarvam //
children.translated_text: to the practice in accord with that wise one, I dedicate all this merit.
Purity of body, speech, and mind, purity of conduct, and purity of realm —

children.text: yādṛśanāmana bhadravidusya tādṛśa bhotu samaṃ mama tena //
children.translated_text: such as is the dedication of the wise <s>Bhadra</s> (Samantabhadra), may mine become equal to his.
For the universally excellent conduct of <s>Bhadra</s>, I would practice the aspiration of <s>Mañjuśrī</s>;

children.text: sarvi anāgata kalpamakhinnaḥ pūrayi tāṃ kriya sarvi aśeṣām //
children.translated_text: untiring through all future eons, I would fulfill all those deeds without remainder.

children.text: no ca pramāṇu bhaveyya carīye no ca pramāṇu bhaveyya guṇānām /
children.translated_text: May there be no measure to my practice, may there be no measure to my virtues;

children.text: apramāṇu cariyāya sthihitvā jānami sarvi vikurvitu teṣām //
children.translated_text: abiding in immeasurable practice, I would know all their miraculous displays.

children.text: yāvata niṣṭha nabhasya bhaveyyā sattva aśeṣata niṣṭha tathaiva /
children.translated_text: As long as space has an end, and beings without remainder have an end likewise,

children.text: karmatu kleśatu yāvata niṣṭhā tāvata niṣṭha mama praṇidhānam //
children.translated_text: as long as <s>karma</s> and afflictions have an end — that long is my aspiration without end.

children.text: ye ca daśaddiśi kṣetra anantā ratnaalaṃkṛtu dadyu jinānām /
children.translated_text: Those who in the ten directions offer to the <s>Jinas</s> infinite realms adorned with jewels,

children.text: divya ca mānuṣa saukhyaviśiṣṭāṃ kṣetrarajopama kalpa dadeyam //
children.translated_text: and the choicest divine and human happiness, for eons equal to atoms of realms —
yet one who, hearing this King of Dedications, generates faith even once,
aspiring to the supreme <s>bodhi</s> — this merit would be foremost and superior.

children.text: varjita tena bhavanti apāyā varjita tena bhavanti kumitrāḥ /
children.translated_text: By that, the lower realms are avoided; by that, evil friends are avoided.

children.text: kṣipru sa paśyati taṃ amitābhaṃ yasyimu bhadracari praṇidhānam //
children.translated_text: Quickly that one sees <s>Amitābha</s> — one who has this Aspiration of Excellent Conduct.

children.text: lābha sulabdha sajīvitu teṣāṃ svāgata te imu mānuṣajanma /
children.translated_text: Well-gained is their livelihood; welcome is this human birth for them.

children.text: yādṛśu so hi samantatabhadraste 'pi tathā nacireṇa bhavanti //
children.translated_text: Just as <s>Samantabhadra</s> himself is — they too shall become such, in no long time.

children.text: pāpaka pañca anantariyāṇi yena ajñānavaśena kṛtāni /
children.translated_text: The five heinous sins of immediate retribution, committed through the power of ignorance —

children.text: so imu bhadracariṃ bhaṇamānaḥ kṣipru parikṣayu neti aśeṣam //
children.translated_text: one who recites this Excellent Conduct quickly exhausts them completely without remainder.

children.text: jñānatu rūpatu lakṣaṇataśca varṇatu gotratu bhotirūpetaḥ /
children.translated_text: Endowed with knowledge, form, marks, complexion, and lineage,
unassailable by hosts of <s>tīrthikas</s> and <s>Māra</s> — that one is worshipped in all three worlds.

children.text: kṣipru sa gacchati bodhidrumendraṃ gatva niṣīdati sattvahitāya /
children.translated_text: Quickly that one goes to the supreme <s>Bodhi</s>-tree; having gone, one sits for the welfare of beings;

children.text: buddhyati bodhi pravartayi cakraṃ dharṣati māru sasainyaku sarvam //
children.translated_text: one awakens to <s>bodhi</s>, turns the wheel of Dharma, and conquers <s>Māra</s> with all his armies.

children.text: yo imu bhadracaripraṇidhānaṃ dhārayi vācayi deśayito vā /
children.translated_text: Whoever holds, recites, or teaches this Aspiration of Excellent Conduct —

children.text: buddhavijānati yo 'tra vipāko bodhi viśiṣṭa ma kāṅkṣa janetha //
children.translated_text: the Buddha alone knows what the ripening is here; do not doubt that <s>bodhi</s> is supreme.

children.text: mañjuśirī yatha jānati śūraḥ so ca samantatabhadra tathaiva /
children.translated_text: Just as the hero <s>Mañjuśrī</s> knows, and <s>Samantabhadra</s> likewise —

children.text: teṣu ahaṃ anuśikṣayamāṇo nāmayamī kuśalaṃ imu sarvam //
children.translated_text: training in accord with them, I dedicate all this merit.
By whatever supreme dedication has been praised by the <s>Jinas</s> gone through the three times —

children.text: tāya ahaṃ kuśalaṃ imu sarvaṃ nāmayamī vara bhadracarīye //
children.translated_text: by that I dedicate all this merit to the excellent Conduct of <s>Bhadra</s>.

children.text: kālakriyāṃ ca ahaṃ karamāṇo āvaraṇān vinivartiya sarvān /
children.translated_text: And when I am making my time of death, having removed all obscurations,

children.text: saṃmukha paśyiya taṃ amitābhaṃ taṃ ca sukhāvatikṣetra vrajeyam //
children.translated_text: may I see <s>Amitābha</s> face to face, and may I go to the realm of <s>Sukhāvatī</s>.

children.text: tatra gatasya imi praṇidhānā āmukhi sarvi bhaveyyu samagrā /
children.translated_text: Having gone there, may all these aspirations become complete, face to face;

children.text: tāṃśca ahaṃ paripūrya aśeṣān sattvahitaṃ kariyāvata loke //
children.translated_text: and having fulfilled them all without remainder, may I work for the welfare of beings as long as the world exists.

children.text: tahi jinamaṃḍali śobhaniramye padmavare rūcire upapannaḥ /
children.translated_text: Born there in the beautiful, delightful <s>Jina</s>-maṇḍala, upon a supreme, lovely lotus,

children.text: vyākaraṇaṃ ahu tatra labheyyā saṃmukhato amitābhajinasya //
children.translated_text: may I receive a prophecy there, face to face, from the <s>Jina</s> <s>Amitābha</s>.

children.text: vyākaraṇaṃ pratilabhya ca tasmin nirmita koṭiśatebhiranekaiḥ /
children.translated_text: And having received that prophecy, with billions of emanations,

children.text: sattvahitāni bahūnyahu kuryāṃ dikṣu daśasvapi buddhibalena //
children.translated_text: may I accomplish many benefits for beings in the ten directions, through the power of understanding.

children.text: bhadracaripraṇidhāna paṭhitvā yatkuśalaṃ mayi saṃcitu kiṃcit /
children.translated_text: Having recited the Aspiration of Excellent Conduct, whatever merit has accumulated in me,

children.text: ekakṣaṇena samṛdhyatu sarvaṃ tena jagasya śubhaṃ praṇidhānam //
children.translated_text: may it all be accomplished in a single instant — that auspicious aspiration for the world.
The infinite, supremely distinguished merit obtained through the dedication of Excellent Conduct —
by that, may the world, drowning in the flood of calamities, go to the supreme city of <s>Amitābha</s>.
The Śrī <s>Bhadracarīpraṇidhāna</s> Stotra is complete.

children.text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 18: Bhaktiśatakam mahāpaṇḍita-rāmacandrabhāratīviracitam
children.translated_text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 18: <s>Bhaktiśataka</s>, composed by the great <s>paṇḍita</s> <s>Rāmacandra Bhāratī</s>.
Homage to that Blessed One, the Worthy One, the Perfectly Awakened One.

children.text: yasmin rāgalavo 'pi naiva na punardveṣo na mohastathā /
children.translated_text: in whom there is not even a trace of passion, nor again aversion, nor delusion,
He whose knowledge encompasses all things, whose speech is faultless,

children.text: buddho vā giriśo 'thavā sa bhagavān tasmai namaskurmahe //
children.translated_text: whether he is the Buddha or <s>Giriśa</s> (Śiva), to that Blessed One we bow.
whose causeless, immense sweetness of compassion bestows happiness on infinite beings —

children.text: devaḥ śambhurna vairī harirapi na ripuḥ kevalī no sapatno
nodāsīnaḥ svayambhurna ca punarapare te pare vāsavādyāḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Svayambhū</s> (Brahmā) is not indifferent; and neither the others — <s>Indra</s> and the rest, those supreme gods.
<s>Śambhu</s> is not an enemy; <s>Hari</s> too is not a foe; the <s>Jina</s> (Jain teacher) is not a rival;

children.text: śāstā buddho na bandhurjagati na janako naikagotraikajātiḥ
kintveṣāṃ vītarāgo bhavati sakalavid yaḥ sudhībhiḥ sa sevyaḥ //
children.translated_text: Rather, among these, whoever is free from passion and omniscient — the wise should resort to him.
The Teacher, the Buddha, is not a kinsman in the world, nor a parent, nor of a single clan or birth.
<s>Viṣṇu</s>, through excess of passion — <s>Pārvatī</s> was held upon his own body by <s>Śaṅkara</s>.
<s>Brahmā</s> is overwhelmed by ignorance and embraced by unfathomable great <s>māyā</s>;

children.text: vītāvidyo vimāyo jagati sa bhagavān vītarāgo munīndraḥ
kaḥ sevyo buddhimadbhirvadata vadata me bhrātarasteṣu muktyai //
children.translated_text: Who should be resorted to by the wise? Speak, speak to me, O brothers — among these, for the sake of liberation!
Free from ignorance, free from illusion, free from passion in the world — the Blessed One, Lord of Sages.

children.text: brāhmaṃ vaiṣṇavamaiśvarañca bahudhā labdhvā padaṃ hetutaiḥ (taḥ) saṃsāre vata saṃsaranti punarapyekāntaduḥkhāspade /
children.translated_text: Having obtained the station of <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and <s>Īśvara</s> by various causes, they still wander in <s>saṃsāra</s>, alas, an abode of absolute suffering.

What use are those stations for embodied beings — stations dense with lower realms, with beginning and end? Therefore, the eternal Buddhist station, without beginning, middle, or end, should be sought.
without desire, without appearance, the seed of boundless compassion, ageless,
Of the nature of consciousness, subtle, omnipresent, pure, without form,

children.text: jitānaṅgaiḥ sevyaṃ bhavatu mama tadvastu śaraṇam //
children.translated_text: resorted to by those who have conquered <s>Kāma</s> — may that Reality be my refuge.
all-knowing, free from all conditions, bestowing immortality through sovereignty —
surpassing the world in majesty, with abundant compassion,
Smaller than the smallest, with a mind unobstructed by afflictions, infinite; greater than the greatest,
two-eyed yet eyeless, with qualities yet qualityless — that is my refuge.
two-armed yet armless, two-footed yet footless, three-faced,
to be resorted to by the good, having rightly realized the truth, of equanimous mind,
Always blissful, truthful, with a tender heart, an abode of good speech,

children.text: sadīyaṃ sarvīyaṃ bhavatu mama tad vastu śaraṇam //
children.translated_text: one's own and everyone's — may that Reality be my refuge.
self-accomplished yet to be accomplished, granting all fruits, of gentle countenance,
of radiant fortune, free from enjoyments, of great valor, conqueror of desire,
Self-existent, possessing supernormal knowledge, removing the fear of existence, fearless,
may this Reality bestow abundant, world-surpassing joy upon beings.
of four paths, of pure nature, and non-agent —

children.text: kvacinnīlaṃ pītaṃ kvacidapi ca raktaṃ kvacidap

children.translated_text: somewhere of moonlike luster, and somewhere of <s>māñjiṣṭha</s> (madder) beauty,
Somewhere blue, somewhere yellow, somewhere red,
bearing above the six-fold crest of flames — that Reality is my refuge.
somewhere self-luminous, transcending the mixture of colors —
of three vehicles, of three wisdoms, refuge of the three worlds, of triple speech,
Invincible by others, of luster like <s>Jāmbūnada</s> gold, the Triple Refuge,
established in meditation, with feet set in <s>siddhāsana</s> — that Reality is my refuge.
a vessel of compassion, with a gentle smile, wearing a reddish-orange true robe,
repeatedly with compassion to the hosts of gods and humans,
Serene, with a pair of eyes like full-blown blue lotuses, expounding the <s>Tripiṭaka</s>

children.text: dṛśāṃ navyātithyaṃ bhavatu mama tad vastu śaraṇam //
children.translated_text: ever new hospitality for the eyes — may that Reality be my refuge.
supremely peaceful, equal toward gold, stone, silver, and clods of earth —
I follow the Dharma as refuge, foremost in freedom from passion.
I go to the Buddha as refuge, the foremost — well indeed, always!
I go again to the Triple Refuge, two or three times.
I go to the <s>Saṃgha</s> as refuge, the foremost of assemblies.

children.text: punarapi śaraṇaṃ vrajāmi buddhaṃ punarapi lokaguruṃ guruṃ karomi /
children.translated_text: Again I take refuge in the Buddha; again I make the World-Teacher my guru;

children.text: punarapi kathayāmi naumi vande, tvayi mama gautama naiva tṛptirāste //
children.translated_text: again I speak, I bow, I salute — O <s>Gautama</s>, in you my satiation never rests.
Having examined the three worlds more than once, I have resorted to the dust of the lotuses of your feet.

children.text: śaraṇamayamayañca daivatamme gatiraparā mama nāsti nāsti nāsti //
children.translated_text: This is my refuge, this is my deity; I have no other recourse — none, none, none!
To the one who proclaims 'All is impermanent, suffering, and without self' —

children.text: namo buddhāya dharmāya saṅghāya ca namo namaḥ //
children.translated_text: homage to the Buddha, to the Dharma, and to the <s>Saṃgha</s>, homage, homage!

children.text: bho vītarāga bhagavaṃstava pādameva vande munīndra muhurevamimaṃ pravande /
children.translated_text: O Passion-Free One, O Blessed One, I bow to your feet alone, O Lord of Sages, I bow again and again, I repeatedly prostrate.

children.text: bhūyaḥ punaḥ punarimaṃ parataḥ parastāt pārśvadvayorupari dikṣu vidikṣu vande //
children.translated_text: Again, again, and again, beyond and further beyond, on both sides, above, in the directions and intermediate directions, I bow.

children.text: gatamiha bhavatā pathā ca yena sthitamapi yatra ca yatra vā niṣaṇṇam /
children.translated_text: Wherever you walked on this path, wherever you stood, wherever you sat,

children.text: śayitamapi munīndra yatra yogāt tadapi śataṃ praṇamāmi puṇyatīrtham //
children.translated_text: wherever you lay down, O Lord of Sages, through practice — even that I bow to a hundred times, that holy ground of merit.

children.text: samajani bhagavān svayaṃ sma yasmin sakalamabodhi ca yatra dharmacakram /
children.translated_text: Where the Blessed One himself was born, where he fully awakened, where the Dharma-wheel
was most brilliantly illumined, where nectar was poured — even that I bow to.
O Royal Swan of the lotus-lake of the omniscient-wheel, of a beauty like jasmine and moon,
worshipped by the hosts of gods, companion of the Dharma-wheel, O <s>Pārijāta</s>-tree of mankind — I bow with devotion to the stainless Śrī Tooth-Relic.
Upon the peak of the golden mountain of <s>Trikūṭa</s>, on the summit of the <s>Cakravāla</s> world-encircling mountains, above the <s>Nāga</s>-realm,
I bow with my head to the supreme <s>Jina</s>-<s>caitya</s>, the imperishable relic-image set at the root of the <s>Bodhi</s>-tree.
With a golden pedestal encircled by a ring, a jewel pathway within, the root sparkling with a <s>vajra</s>-seat — the supreme <s>Bodhi</s>-tree of <s>Indra</s> —

children.text: yaṃ prāpya māravijayānupadaṃ prapede sarvajñatāṃ sa bhagavān tamahaṃ namāmi //
children.translated_text: Having attained which, immediately after the victory over <s>Māra</s>, he reached omniscience — to that Blessed One I bow! //

children.text: mūrddhan buddhaṃ nama tvaṃ śravaṇa śṛṇu sadā dharmamadvaidhavādi
proktaṃ sarvatra rūpaṃ nayana nirupamaṃ paśya jighrāṅaghripadmam /
children.translated_text: O eye, behold everywhere the incomparable form! O nose, smell the lotus-feet
O head, bow to the <s>Buddha</s>! O ear, always hear the Dharma that speaks non-duality!

children.text: ghrāṇa tvaṃ cārkabandhoḥ stuhi sakhi rasane śrīghanaṃ pūjayethāḥ
siddhaṃ pāṇe vrajāṅghre jinasadanamadasmadguṇaṃ citta cintya //
children.translated_text: O accomplished one, O foot, go to the abode of the <s>Jina</s>! O mind, contemplate this our virtue! //
of the kinsman of the sun! O friend tongue, praise him! O hand, worship the mass of glory!
beginning today I give my self to this, which destroys the fear of the three existences.
The <s>Buddha</s>, the Dharma, and the <s>Saṅgha</s> — this triad is a priceless jewel. O seeker of liberation,

children.text: eṣo 'haṃ tatparaḥ syāmparamayanamito nāsti me satyametat

children.translated_text: May I be his disciple! I bow to this, worshipped by the thirty gods, ten million times! //
I shall be entirely devoted to that — there is nothing higher for me; this is the truth.

children.text: nāhaṃ lābhārcanārthī na ca bhayacakito nāpi satkīrtikāmo
na tvaṃ dharmāṃśuvaṃśaprabhava iti mune nāpi vidyāśayā te /
children.translated_text: not because you are born in the lineage of Dharma-rays, O Sage, nor with desire for your knowledge —
I am not one who seeks gain or honor, nor frightened by fear, nor desirous of good fame;

children.text: pāramparyānnaca tvāṃ śaraṇamupagataḥ kintu te sārvajanyaṃ
samyagjñānaṃ samīkṣya tvayi bhavajaladhiṃ santarītuṃ pravṛttaḥ //
children.translated_text: right knowledge meant for all, I am moved to cross the ocean of existence through you. //
nor have I gone to you as refuge through tradition; but having examined your omniscient
— dispassion, compassion for all beings, wisdom, and the rest — I am unable to go elsewhere.
Fallen into the ocean of sandal-paste fragrant with your various qualities

children.text: bhūpā vā yadi daṇḍayanti vibudhā nindanti vā bāndhavā
muñcanti kṣaṇamapyahaṃ jina pitarjīvāmi na tvāṃ vinā //
children.translated_text: O <s>Jina</s>, O Father, I will not live without you even for a moment! //
Whether kings punish me, or the wise censure, or kinsmen abandon,

children.text: svarge vā vasatirmamāstu niraye tiryakṣu kiṃ vāsure

children.translated_text: in the city of <s>pretas</s>, or in the human world, or anywhere else by karma —
Whether my dwelling be in heaven or in hell, among animals or <s>asuras</s>,
which flow as nectar to the ears, sinless — I have no other prayer for happiness. //
O Omniscient One, from here and there, may my mind cling to your qualities,
I am yours alone — a disciple trained by your own words;
I am yours alone — a slave purchased by the price of your qualities;

children.text: guro buddhasvāmin mama janaka māṃ pāhi bhavataḥ //
children.translated_text: O Teacher, O <s>Buddha</s>-Lord, O my Father, protect me from existence! //
I am yours alone — a son made happy by remembrance, gone to that destination.

children.text: pitā mātā bhrātā tvamasi bhaginī tvaṃ ca vipadi

children.translated_text: a steadfast friend, kinsman, lord, the highest guru who initiates into the deathless.
You are father, mother, brother — you are sister in misfortune;

children.text: tvamaiśvaryyaṃ bhogo tvamasi dhanadhānyaṃ ca mahimā
yaśo vidyā prāṇastvamasi mama sarvajña sakalam //
children.translated_text: fame, knowledge, life — you are everything to me, O Omniscient One! //
You are sovereignty, enjoyment; you are wealth, grain, and greatness;
O Lord of Sages free from passion, ocean of compassion, <s>Sugata</s>, breaker of the great cage of existence,

children.text: adhigatāmṛta buddha mano 'mbujaṃ mama tavānagha gandhakuṭīyatām //
children.translated_text: O <s>Buddha</s> who has attained the deathless, O Sinless One — may my mind-lotus become your fragrant chamber! //
In this selfless, impermanent, impure, suffering-upon-suffering, endless cycle of <s>saṃsāra</s>, as I wander —

children.text: tvamekosi māṃ trātumīśo dayābdhe prabho 'taḥ prasīda prasīda prasīda //
children.translated_text: you alone are able to save me, O ocean of compassion, O Lord — therefore be gracious, be gracious, be gracious! //

children.text: prasīdeśa deveśa lokeśa jiṣṇo jagadvandya madvandya sadvandya buddha /
children.translated_text: Be gracious, O Lord, O God of gods, O Lord of the world, O Conqueror, O one worshipped by the world, worthy of my worship, worthy of the saints' worship, O <s>Buddha</s>!

children.text: aghore bhavāre smarāre tamore tavaivāsmi bhakto vapurvāṅmanobhiḥ //
children.translated_text: O fearless one, O enemy of existence, O enemy of <s>Māra</s>, O enemy of darkness — I am your devotee in body, speech, and mind! //

children.text: sa tava kulasutaḥ sa eva bhaktaḥ sa bhavati śāsanadhūrvahaḥ sa śiṣyaḥ /
children.translated_text: He is your true son of the family, he is the true devotee, he is the bearer of the yoke of your teaching, he is the disciple,

children.text: sa ca śaraṇagataḥ sa eva dāsaḥ kathamapi yo na vilaṅghayet tavājñām //
children.translated_text: he is the refugee, he is the servant — whoever would never transgress your command! //

children.text: jagadupakṛtireva buddha! pūjā tadapakṛtistava lokanātha! pīḍā /
children.translated_text: Benefiting the world is worship of you, O <s>Buddha</s>! Harming it is your pain, O Lord of the world!

children.text: jina jagadapakṛt kathaṃ na lajje gaditumahaṃ tava pādapadmabhaktaḥ //
children.translated_text: O <s>Jina</s>, how am I, a devotee of your lotus-feet, not ashamed to say that I harm the world? //
Wealth, people, power, life, body, kingdom — all were given by you a hundredfold for the world's benefit;

children.text: tamahitamapakartturasya lokaṃ kva mama kṛpā muditā kva vā ca maitrī //
children.translated_text: where is my compassion, where my joy, where my friendliness toward this world that harms its benefactor? //
Like an unchaste woman going to a paramour, the activity of my mind goes toward the five sense-pleasures, abandoning you;

children.text: api ca viṣayiṇo na mokṣasiddhiḥ kimu karavāṇi munīndra dehi dāsyam //
children.translated_text: and moreover, the attainment of liberation is not for the sensual — what shall I do, O Lord of Sages? Grant me servitude! //
O most beloved, O Supreme Person, O foremost <s>Buddha</s>, O remover of weariness, O Accomplished One, O one of fame renowned in the world,
be my refuge, O bestower of unsurpassed grace — I am the servant of your servant at every step! //
O Ten-Powered One, I am weak in this age of <s>Kali</s>, drowning in the high waves of the long ocean of sin;

children.text: tava kathamanuyāmi dharmanāvaṃ jina mama dehi kṛpākarāvalambam //
children.translated_text: how shall I follow your Dharma-boat? O <s>Jina</s>, give me the support of your hand of compassion! //
This prostration of mine to you is repeated many times — seeing much the suffering of existence, I am frightened with fear;

children.text: dhara gurutaratṛṣṇayā patantaṃ jina mama dehi kṛpākarāvalambam //
children.translated_text: support me who am falling, weighed down by the heaviest craving — O <s>Jina</s>, give me the support of your hand of compassion! //

children.text: jagati tava kṛpā hi nirviśeṣā prapavatayā jina māṃ ca doṣaduṣṭam /
children.translated_text: In the world, your compassion is indeed impartial; O <s>Jina</s>, let it also fall upon me, corrupt with faults;

children.text: alamahamiaha no sukhī bhavendurna samakaraścaratīva sādhvasādhve(dhvoḥ) //
children.translated_text: enough of 'I am unworthy' — the moon does not shine only for the virtuous, does it? //
O Friend of the wretched, look upon this person — blinded by accumulated great delusion,
devoid of compassion, bereft of the fragrance of self and kinsmen, departed from virtue and knowledge, risen in sin, lacking discernment! //

children.text: akaravamuruduṣkṛtaṃ purā yad mama vapuṣā manasā ca cetasā ca /
children.translated_text: Whatever great evil I committed formerly, with body, mind, and thought —

children.text: anukalamakhilaṃ pralīyatāṃ tat tava caraṇasmaraṇena sarvavedin //
children.translated_text: may all of that, moment by moment, be dissolved through remembering your feet, O All-Knower! //

children.text: sugata tava puraḥ puraḥ pṛthivyāṃ madhuramate patito 'smi daṇḍanatyā /
children.translated_text: O <s>Sugata</s>, O Sweet-Minded One, I have fallen before you upon the earth in the prostration of a staff;

children.text: akuśalamakhilaṃ tavānubhāvāt prapatatu notpatatāt punaḥ sahaiva //
children.translated_text: may all unwholesomeness fall away through your power, and may it not arise again! //

children.text: tava caraṇasarojameva vande tava padapaṅkajameva pūjayāmi /
children.translated_text: Your lotus-feet alone I worship; your lotus-feet alone I honor;

children.text: tava padayugameva bhāvaye 'haṃ tava padameva sadaiva daivataṃ me //
children.translated_text: your pair of feet alone I contemplate — your feet alone are always my divinity. //

children.text: kamapi na kathayāmi nārcayāmi kamapi na naumi na cintayāmi nehe /
children.translated_text: I do not speak of anyone else, nor worship anyone else, nor praise, nor think of, nor love anyone else;

children.text: kamapi na śaraṇaṃ vrajāmi hitvā tava caraṇaṃ pitarasmi kiṅkaraste //
children.translated_text: I do not go to any other refuge, abandoning your feet — O Father, I am your servant! //

children.text: sadasi sadasi vāci siddhaṃ pathi pathi sadmani sadmanīha buddham /
children.translated_text: In assembly after assembly, in speech after speech, on path after path, in dwelling after dwelling —

children.text: bhuvi bhuvi mama vāri vāri cetaḥ kalayatu nityamimaṃ hi lokanātham //
children.translated_text: in land after land, in water after water — may my mind always contemplate this Lord of the World, the <s>Buddha</s>! //
Unceasingly I behold the <s>Buddha</s>, as if with the eye of a mind free from passion;

children.text: svapimi niśi nidhāya yaddhṛdi tvāṃ na mama samaṃ virahastvayā ta eva //
children.translated_text: at night I sleep placing you in my heart — there is no separation from you for me! //

children.text: mama tadiha dinaṃ hi durdinaṃ syād aśitaghanasthagitaṃ na durdinaṃ me /
children.translated_text: That day would be a dark day for me — not one obscured by dark dense clouds is dark for me,
but one devoid of the remembrance of the <s>Buddha</s>-jewel name, equal to nectar — may that day never be! //

children.text: amṛtada ṣaḍabhijña dharmarāja tribhuvanavandya munīndra gotameti /
children.translated_text: O giver of nectar, O six-fold knower, O Dharma-King, O one worshipped by the three worlds, O Lord of Sages, O <s>Gotama</s> —
those men who celebrate your name day after day — I bow even to those blessed ones who are hostile! //

children.text: daśabala jina siddha vajrabuddhe sugata tathāgata buddha śākyasiṃha /
children.translated_text: 'Ten-Powered, <s>Jina</s>, Accomplished, <s>Vajra-Buddha</s>, <s>Sugata</s>, <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Buddha</s>, Lion of the <s>Śākyas</s>' —

children.text: iti nigadati yaḥ kvacit kadācit tamabhinamāmyapi dāsavaṃśajātam //
children.translated_text: whoever says this anywhere, at any time — I bow even to one born in a family of servants! //
O Conqueror of <s>Madana</s> (Kāma), O Conqueror over the conquered, O Teacher, O Lord of Splendor, O Guide, O Knower of All, O Best of the Excellent,

children.text: kavivara vadatāṃvareśa śuddhodanasuta śākyamune mune prasīda //
children.translated_text: O Best of Poets, O Lord of the Best Speakers, O Son of <s>Śuddhodana</s>, O Sage of the <s>Śākyas</s>, O Sage — be gracious! //

children.text: amṛtamapi nipīya nirjarendra punarapi te 'pi śunīstanaṃ dhayanti /
children.translated_text: Even the <s>Indra</s> of immortals, having drunk nectar, again suckles the breast of a bitch (is reborn);

children.text: sakṛdapi tava vāksudhārasajño na viśati jātu sa mātureva garbham //
children.translated_text: but one who has once tasted the nectar-flow of your speech never enters the womb of a mother again. //
O Blessed One, I here am unable to endure the afflictions of birth, old age, death, and disease;

children.text: kuru mama karuṇaṃ diśo na jāne guru tadavekṣya ca tiryagādiduḥkham //
children.translated_text: show me compassion — I do not know the directions; O Teacher, look upon the suffering of animal realms and the rest! //
Considering further old age — the helplessness of hands, feet, eyes, and the rest —

children.text: agatikamativepate mano me jina kimahaṃ karavai prabho prasīda //
children.translated_text: my mind trembles greatly, without refuge — O <s>Jina</s>, what shall I do? O Lord, be gracious! //
Even toward a happiness-producing thing that has merely entered the path of hearing but never been seen before, I exert craving;

children.text: aviratamata eva śāntibīje tvayi valate ramate mamātra cetaḥ //
children.translated_text: all the more then does my mind here turn and delight in you, the seed of peace, unceasingly! //

children.text: savipadi ramate na me mano 'taḥ suranaraśarmaṇi pūrvapūrvabhukte /
children.translated_text: My mind no longer delights in the happiness of gods and men, enjoyed again and again before;

children.text: anudinamanubhūya śarkarāyāmapi viratiṃ kurute hi dṛṣṭadoṣaḥ //
children.translated_text: having experienced it day by day, even toward sugar one develops weariness — for one who has seen the faults! //
A fool disregards even a priceless wish-fulfilling gem held in the palm with a mere gesture;

children.text: kathamahamapahāya buddharatnaṃ jagati dhanī guṇavāṃśca paṇḍitaśca //
children.translated_text: how could I, abandoning the <s>Buddha</s>-jewel, be wealthy, virtuous, or wise in the world? //

children.text: sa bhavati matimān sa nākulīnaḥ sa ca guṇavān sa ca kīrtimān sa śūraḥ /
children.translated_text: He is the intelligent one, he is the noble-born, he is the virtuous, he is the famous, he is the hero,

children.text: sa jagati mahitaḥ sukhī sa eva tvayi jina yasya suniścalāsti bhaktiḥ //
children.translated_text: he is honored in the world, he alone is happy — in whom, O <s>Jina</s>, there is firm devotion to you! //

children.text: api sakalamadhītamatra tena śrutamapi sarvamanuṣṭhitaṃ ca tena /
children.translated_text: All has been studied by him here, all has been heard and practiced by him,

children.text: api jitamajitena tena viśvaṃ tvayi jina yasya suniścalāsti bhaktiḥ //
children.translated_text: the entire unconquered world has been conquered by him — in whom, O <s>Jina</s>, there is firm devotion to you! //

children.text: tyajati nijaparamparādareṇetarasamayasya jano na dṛṣṭa dṛṣṭim /
children.translated_text: A person does not abandon the view of another system out of respect for his own tradition;

children.text: asuharamapi gauraveṇa māturna khalu śiśurviṣamodakaṃ tu muñcet //
children.translated_text: nor indeed would a child, out of respect for its mother, release a poisoned sweet! //

children.text: kavivaramahamasmi paṇḍitaste jina na jahāmi kathannu kurgṛhītam /
children.translated_text: I am the best of poets, I am your learned one, O <s>Jina</s> — how could I abandon what is badly grasped?

children.text: nudati hi tamasantatiṃ pravṛttāṃ mihiramarīcisahāyinī sudṛṣṭiḥ //
children.translated_text: A good view, aided by the sun's rays, indeed drives away an advancing mass of darkness! //

children.text: sugatapadaparāṅmukhasya puṃsaḥ kimu tapasā yaśasā ca kiṃ kimanyaiḥ /
children.translated_text: For a man turned away from the <s>Sugata</s>'s feet — what use is austerity? What use is fame? What use are other things?

children.text: sugatapadaparāṅnukhasya puṃsaḥ kimu tapasā yaśasā ca kiṃ kimanyaiḥ //
children.translated_text: For a man turned toward the <s>Sugata</s>'s feet — what use is austerity? What use is fame? What use are other things? //

children.text: sugatapadi na bhaktirasti yeṣāmajananireva mahītale 'stu teṣām /
children.translated_text: For those in whom there is no devotion to the <s>Sugata</s>'s feet — let their existence on earth be as non-birth!

children.text: kathitamiha kṛtāgasāṃ narāṇāṃ nirayagatirniyataṃ na cānyato yat //
children.translated_text: It is said of sinful men that their destination is certainly hell, and not otherwise. //
One who knows all scriptures, elevated, of noble birth, excellent form, youth, and the rest —

children.text: jina bhavadanupāsakaṃ nṛpāsaṃ tyajatu mano mala nīcavattu jātyā //
children.translated_text: O <s>Jina</s>, may my mind abandon such a king who does not worship you, as if he were of low birth by nature! //
One who has abandoned pride, conceit, jealousy, and the rest, compassionate, moral, possessed of <s>samādhi</s>, discerning,

children.text: tava padadṛḍhabhaktirantyajo 'pi pratibhavamastu narottamaḥ sakhā me //
children.translated_text: with firm devotion to your feet — even if an outcaste, may he be my friend, the best of men, in every birth! //
Even ten days of life is praiseworthy for a devotee who has performed worship of the <s>Jina</s>'s feet;
but not ten million thousand crores of ages for one who has not worshipped the lotus-feet of the Lord of Sages! //

children.text: sa bhavati surasundarīsakho 'nyaiḥ kṛtamabhinandati vārcanaṃ ca bhaktyā /
children.translated_text: He becomes a companion of divine beauties, and he rejoices even in worship done by others through devotion —
if, O Guru of gods and men, through helplessness one is unable to perform your worship! //
One who brings to the path of the eyes an image of your exceedingly varied and beautiful form —
that generous person's long-accumulated evil deeds are destroyed, O Lord of Poets! //

children.text: maṇikanakaśilādinirmitāṃ yaḥ praṇamati te pratimāṃ tayośca tulyam /
children.translated_text: One who bows to an image of you made of gems, gold, stone, or the like — the fruit is equal for them.

children.text: phalamiha manasaśca samprasādādanuparataṃ jina yo 'grato namet tvām //
children.translated_text: And from the serenity of mind, O <s>Jina</s>, the result is unending for one who merely bows before you! //

children.text: sakṛdapi tava pādapadmapūjā vanakusumairapi yaḥ karoti dhīmān /
children.translated_text: Even once, the wise one who makes an offering of forest flowers to your lotus-feet —
he attains that pure sovereignty, brilliant with the garlands of crowns of bowing assemblies of gods! //
If the heap of merit born from a single moment's taking refuge, with unified mind, in your form, is high,
O Refuge of multitudes, O virtuous <s>Samantabhadra</s>, then it exceeds even the entire sky! //

children.text: tava guṇakathane tu yaḥ prasannastamanuviśanti mune guṇāstvadīyāḥ /
children.translated_text: He who is devoted to the narration of your qualities — your qualities enter him, O Sage,
as frost from the rays of the moon enters a moonstone when the moon rises serene! //

children.text: sakṛdapi samadāyi deva kiñcid bhavaratimutsṛjatā janena tubhyam /
children.translated_text: Even the slightest offering given to you, O God, by a person abandoning delight in existence —

children.text: sugata tadakhilān lunāti dhārā vadasiriva drumamāśravādidoṣān //
children.translated_text: O <s>Sugata</s>, it cuts down all faults of clinging and the rest, as a torrent cuts a tree, as you have declared! //

children.text: kṛtamiha sukṛtaṃ mṛṣādṛśā yajjanayati tat kila tasya durvipākam /
children.translated_text: Whatever good deed is done here with false vision — that indeed produces bitter ripening for him,
just as a neem seed, when planted, leads the earth-water-juice to its own bitter nature! //

children.text: tava padanaline nipatya bhūyo nipatati naiva caturṣvapāyakeṣu /
children.translated_text: One who has fallen at your lotus-feet does not fall again into the four evil destinations;

children.text: nahi kuśalakaro naraḥ kadāpi kvacidapi durgatimeti nātha kaścit //
children.translated_text: for never does a doer of good go to an evil destiny, O Lord — no one at all! //

children.text: iti bhavadupadeśato viditvā tava padapaṅkajapūjane rato 'smi /
children.translated_text: Thus, having understood through your teaching, I am devoted to the worship of your lotus-feet;

children.text: dṛḍhayatu bhagavān yuge yuge me kumatimudasya bhave bhave 'ryabhaktim //
children.translated_text: O Blessed One, may you strengthen in me, age after age, noble devotion, destroying wrong views, in every birth! //

children.text: sthiramapi bhagavan kṣaṇaṃ tavoktau karacaraṇāni dṛgādi vairivargaḥ /
children.translated_text: Even when firmly established for a moment in your teaching, O Blessed One, the enemy host of hands, feet, eyes, and the rest

children.text: vyathayati hṛdayaṃ balādvicālya tvamidamanāthamanīśa pāhi pāhi //
children.translated_text: disturbs the heart, forcibly shaking it — O helpless one, O Lord, protect, protect me! //

children.text: yadi nayanamayaṃ vaśe vidhātuṃ yatati tadā dravati śravo yadā tat /
children.translated_text: If one strives to bring the eye under control, then the ear runs away; when that is restrained,
then the tongue, nose, and body — alas, alas! — are mutually difficult to grasp, and thus it goes. //
The course of the extremely fickle mind would be, in this world, like the unobstructed wind in the sky;

children.text: kabhamapi bhajate krameṇa dhairyaṃ ciaramidamabhyasanena saṃviraktyā //
children.translated_text: yet somehow, gradually, it attains steadiness through long practice and through <s>saṃvairagya</s> (dispassion). //

children.text: viśadamapi manaḥ svabhāvato me cirakṛtakilviṣakālimāhṛtaṃ syāt /
children.translated_text: My mind, though naturally clear, may have been seized by the darkness of long-committed sins;
how then can it be washed clean by the droplets of wholesome water earned by one of such a mind as mine? //
With streams of the nectar of your most pure words, me whose stream of consciousness has been thoroughly stained,
O Supreme Lord, me who am greatly afflicted — purify me at once! I bow like a staff before you. //

children.text: sati sakalaguro mune prasanne kimiha durāpamamutra kiṃ durāpam /
children.translated_text: When the all-venerable <s>Muni</s> (Sage) is pleased, what is unattainable here, what is unattainable hereafter?
For your servants of pure mind do not even mentally regard the status of <s>Indra</s> (lord of gods). //
The senses cause great fear when grasping the poison of sense objects, through the vision of their faults;
indeed, even a child who well understands the future burning danger would not grasp the tip of a lamp flame. //

children.text: na bhavati jina yāvadeṣa jīrṇo viṣayapiśācaniṣevaṇena tāvat /
children.translated_text: O <s>Jina</s> (Conqueror), as long as this body is not worn out by the haunting of the demons of sense objects,

children.text: jhaṭiti sukṛtakarmaṇi prayojya svava śaraṇāgatavatsalāgataṃ mām //
children.translated_text: quickly employ me in meritorious action — me who has come seeking refuge in you, O lover of those who seek shelter! //
Even if I know that sons, wife, one's own body, home and the like are equal to the water of a mirage,

children.text: sthagayati mamatā ca māmahantā tadapi hi mohavijṛmbhitaṃ garīyaḥ //
children.translated_text: still possessiveness, the great destroyer, obscures me — for the manifestation of delusion is indeed mighty. //

children.text: ajani ca nijakāraṇena sarvaṃ nirasati jīryati naśyati svahetoḥ /
children.translated_text: Everything arose from its own cause, ceases, decays, and perishes due to its own cause;

children.text: ahamapi hi tathaiva dhātupuñjaḥ kathamahamasya kathaṃ mune mamedam //
children.translated_text: I too am just such a heap of elements — how can I say 'I'? How can I say 'mine,' O <s>Muni</s>? //

children.text: ātmabuddhiriha yasya jāyate sā ca tasya janayedahaṅkṛtim /
children.translated_text: The notion of self that arises in a person, that in turn generates ego-sense;

children.text: sā tanoti sutarāṃ bhavaspṛhāṃ saiva mohajananī muhurmuhuḥ //
children.translated_text: that ego-sense exceedingly spreads the craving for existence — it is the mother of delusion again and again. //

children.text: tena karma kurute śubhāśubhaṃ taddhi duḥkhajanakaṃ bhavatraye /
children.translated_text: Through that, one performs good and bad <s>karma</s>, and that indeed generates suffering in the three realms of existence;

children.text: duḥkhamūlamata eva sātmadhīḥ tāṃ lunīhi jina me vaco 'sinā //
children.translated_text: therefore the notion of self is the root of suffering — cut it away in me with the sword of your words, O <s>Jina</s>! //
Now, the all-knowing one, the ocean of compassion, the cause of the cause of the three worlds, the noble one,
the omniscient, infinite, abiding in peace — I praise the lord, the swan of the minds of sages. //

children.text: snāne karmaṇi bhojane vitaraṇe ghrāṇe tathākarṇane

children.translated_text: in meditation, touching, seeing, and the rest, and likewise in conversation and other activities —
In bathing, in ritual action, in eating, in giving, in smelling, and likewise in hearing,

children.text: prātaḥ sāyamatho divā ca niśi ca tvatpādapadme vibho
cittaṃ me ramatāṃ munīndra satataṃ yūnāṃ yuvatyāmiva //
children.translated_text: may my mind delight, O Lord of Sages, constantly, as a young man delights in a young woman. //
in the morning, in the evening, and also by day and by night, at your lotus feet, O All-pervading Lord,
my mother, my object of worship, my dear friend, my true refuge, my father!
O my master, my wish-fulfilling tree, my deity, my guru,

children.text: manmukte madudārabhāgya madaso madbuddha māṃ pālaya //
children.translated_text: my liberation, my great fortune, my hope — O my <s>Buddha</s>, protect me! //
My learning, remover of all my sorrows, my object of meditation, my treasure,
<s>Viṣṇu</s> fell prey to craving, the poet became no poet, the Lord became no lord —
<s>Brahmā</s> became crooked-faced, the teacher became no teacher, the guide of days became no guide,

children.text: ko 'haṃ mūḍho varākastridaśanarapate kīrttane te guṇānām //
children.translated_text: who am I, a foolish, wretched one, O Lord of gods and men, to hymn your virtues? //
<s>Śeṣa</s> became one of remaining powers — in praising you, O <s>Sugata</s>, the speech of even <s>Indra</s> is shattered;
the body of that great being blazes with the marks of a <s>Mahāpuruṣa</s> (Great Being);
With the thirty-two shining major marks and the eighty minor marks,

children.text: kalāmapi na ṣoḍaśīṃ bhajati tasya puṇyātmanaś
caturmukhamukho gaṇo diviṣadāṃ nṛṇāṃ kā kathā //
children.translated_text: is attained by the host led by <s>Brahmā</s> among the gods — what then to speak of humans? //
not even a sixteenth part of the merit of that blessed one
your beautiful and resplendent halo always shines forth;
Like a fresh rainbow upon a golden mountain, on all sides

children.text: dṛśo bhavati gocaraṃ tadiha yasya tasya tvarān

children.translated_text: it dispels far away the supreme mass of darkness, both inner and outer. //
for whomever it becomes visible to the eyes, for that person swiftly
your voice enchants the entire world, your compassion is most serene;
Your form is a delight to the eyes, your speech is a flood of bliss to the ears,

children.text: pāṇḍityaṃ prathitaṃ jagatsu bhagavan sarvajñanāmnaiva te
sāmrājyasya ca yauvane nirasanaṃ vairāgyasīmā sphuṭam //
children.translated_text: and your renunciation of sovereignty in youth is the very limit of <s>vairāgya</s> (dispassion). //
your learning, O Blessed One, is renowned in the worlds by the very name 'Omniscient,'
by which that world of gods and demons was conquered — wonderful!
Your valor against your adversaries, through crushing their pride, was acknowledged by the gods;
what shall we say of the strength and glory of the Blessed One — it is unbearable for the world! //
Your heroic power was manifested supremely through the realization of <s>Nirvāṇa</s>;
out of love for living beings — therefore none is more compassionate than you;
Where the Veda prescribes the slaughter of goats and horses, even that you condemn,

children.text: evaṃ te guṇasampado na viṣayā buddherasūyātmanāṃ
te mūḍhāḥ pralapanti hanta sugato madvedanindītyayam //
children.translated_text: those deluded ones prattle — alas, O <s>Sugata</s>! — saying 'He condemns our Vedas!' //
thus your wealth of virtues is not within the range of the intellect of the envious;
your auspicious fame, friend of the white lotuses of the milk ocean —
The <s>Mandākinī</s> (celestial Ganges), flowing gently from the breasts of bathing celestial nymphs,
O physician of the disease of attachment, O Blessed One, this too is my prayer! //
that which does not now embrace one of ill fortune — may I have no attachment even to that;

children.text: ye tvāṃ gacchanti buddhaṃ śaraṇamiti na te durgatiṃ yānti santas

children.translated_text: and having abandoned human bodies, they obtain divine ones of surpassing bliss;
Those good ones who go to you, the <s>Buddha</s>, as refuge — they do not go to a bad destiny,

children.text: duḥkhaṃ durvyādhayo 'pi kvacidiha kuśalān nopasarpanti caivam //
children.translated_text: suffering, and terrible diseases — these do not anywhere approach the virtuous ones. //
bad dreams, ill omens, harmful snakes, evil planets, wicked beings,

children.text: chatraṃ brahmā vyadhātte maṇimayamamalaṃ cāmaraṃ cakrapāṇi

children.translated_text: <s>Hara</s> (Śiva), the weighty serpent lord (<s>Śeṣa</s>), praised with prose and verse, and great <s>Indra</s> blew the conch;
<s>Brahmā</s> held the jeweled parasol, and <s>Cakrapāṇi</s> (Viṣṇu) the immaculate flywhisk,
when you, O Lord of Sages, descended to earth after having taught the <s>Dharma</s> in heaven. //
others stood with lamps, water-pots, banners, flowers and garlands in their hands, bowing in devotion —

children.text: mātevāsīt parastrī bhavati paradhane na spṛhā yasya puṃso
mithyāvādī na yaḥ syānna pibati madirāṃ prāṇino yo na hanyāt /
children.translated_text: who would not speak falsehood, who does not drink liquor, who would not kill a living being,
He for whom another's wife was like a mother, who had no desire for another's wealth,

children.text: dharmātmā te sa eva prabhavati bhagavan pādapūjāṃ vidhātum //
children.translated_text: he alone, O Blessed One, that righteous soul, is worthy to worship your feet. //
who fears the breach of moral boundaries, whose heart is compassionate, who has abandoned all pride —
from false speech, and from liquor, who eats at the proper time, who is turned away from untimely eating,
He who is restrained from all killing of living beings, from taking another's wealth, from union with women,

children.text: apyāsīddhīmān sa eva tridaśanaraguro tvatsuto nātra śaṅkā //
children.translated_text: that wise one was indeed your son, O Lord of gods and men — there is no doubt in this. //
and also from singing, garlands, perfumes, ornaments, dancing, and from high seats and beds —
those faults, cut at the root, their existences destroyed — by their fruits they attain peace;
The paths beginning with stream-entry, endowed with their limbs, destroy the faults of passion and the rest;

children.text: dharmāṇāṃ hetureṣāṃ tava jina vacanaṃ tasya hetustvameva //
children.translated_text: <s>dharmas</s> (qualities) — the cause of these is your word, O <s>Jina</s>, and the cause of that is you yourself. //
the destruction of afflictions on the paths is the cause of the deathless, unaging, and new
uprooting all the evil <s>karma</s> that arose from the sins of passion, hatred, and the rest,
Having split with the immaculate <s>vajra</s> (thunderbolt) of knowledge the mountain of the twenty types of <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s> (view of self-identity),
from you comes the Eightfold Noble <s>Saṅgha</s>; we no longer think of them as separate, O Lord of Sages. //
the four who have attained the paths and the four corresponding fruits —
this entire vast circle of world-systems is infinite;
The sky is infinite, all beings are infinite,

children.text: tava ca guṇamanantaṃ vedasī buddha caivam //
children.translated_text: and your virtues too are infinite — thus you know, O <s>Buddha</s>. //
you speak, O <s>Jina</s>, having known through your infinite course of knowledge,
may there be, may there be devotion in birth after birth!
In you, O Blessed One, whose name 'Bhavat' (Lord) destroys existence, whose power is unerring,
may the <s>Saṅgha</s> be the unsurpassed field of merit! //
May the <s>Dharma</s> in every way be my teacher,
whatever abundant and most pure merit has been earned here —
Having praised you, the <s>Buddha</s>, honored by the three worlds,
with their manifold sins dispelled through meditative cultivation, proceed to it! //
by that, may all beings in the world, having attained <s>Sambuddha-bodhi</s> (Perfect Awakening),
ruler of <s>Śrī Laṅkā</s>, <s>Parākramabāhu</s>, was governing the earth by righteous policy,
When the king of kings, lord of the illustrious solar lotus-clan,
composed this <s>Bhaktiśataka</s> (Century of Devotion), bestowing <s>dharma</s>, <s>artha</s>, and <s>mokṣa</s>. //
the noble Gauḍa, the poet <s>Bhārati</s>, the earthly sage, the wise <s>Śrī Rāmacandra</s>,

children.text: śrīśākyamunerbhagavataḥ sarvajñasya paramopāsakena gauḍadeśīyaśrībauddhāgamacakravarttinā bhūsureṇācāryeṇa mahāpaṇḍitena
children.translated_text: By the supreme devotee of the Blessed <s>Śrī Śākyamuni</s>, the Omniscient One, the Gauḍa-born <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, the teacher, the great <s>Paṇḍita</s>, emperor of the glorious Buddhist scriptures,
the <s>Bhaktiśataka</s> is completed. /
The king <s>Parākrāntibhuja</s> (Parākramabāhu), the crest-jewel of earth-lords, the friend of the assembly of scholars,
he made <s>Rāmacandra</s>, the poet <s>Bhārati</s>, the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, the emperor of the Buddhist scriptures. //

children.text: buddho me jayatāṃ jinaḥ sa bhagavān taddeśanā nirmalā

children.translated_text: may it endure for the benefit of beings, may the <s>Saṅgha</s>, its support, flourish!
May the <s>Buddha</s> be victorious for me! May that Blessed <s>Jina</s>'s teaching remain pure,

children.text: varṣantu stanayitnavaśca samaye maitrīṃ labhantāṃ prajāḥ //
children.translated_text: may the clouds rain in season, and may the people obtain loving-kindness! //
May kings led by the lord of <s>Laṅkā</s> always protect the earth for long,
of the foremost teacher, the lord of sages, the eloquent <s>Śrī Rāhula Svāmin</s>,
Of the master of the holy site, the ascetic <s>Tripiṭakācārya</s> (Master of the Three Baskets), of royal lineage,
with compassion composed a commentary on the <s>Munīndra-bhaktiśataka</s> (Century of Devotion to the Lord of Sages). //
a disciple, the younger <s>Sumaṅgala Muni</s>, the wise one, in his own language,

children.text: namo buddhāya gurave namo dharmāya śāsine /
children.translated_text: Homage to the <s>Buddha</s>, the guru! Homage to the <s>Dharma</s>, the ruler!

children.text: namaḥ saṅghāya mahate tribhyo 'pi satataṃ namaḥ //
children.translated_text: Homage to the <s>Saṅgha</s>, the great! To all three, constant homage! //
Perfection! //

children.text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 19: Buddhabhaṭṭārakastotram
children.translated_text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 19: <s>Buddhabhaṭṭārakastotra</s> (Hymn to the Lord Buddha)
Oṃ, homage to the <s>Buddha</s>!
The Fully Awakened One, lotus-eyed, omniscient, whose nature is compassion,
<s>Samantabhadra</s>, the Teacher, the Lion of the <s>Śākyas</s> — I bow to him. //
Glorious in majesty, endowed with <s>Śrī</s> (splendor), the best, the cool-rayed one, the auspicious one,
the glorious, the bestower of fortune, the peaceful, the embodiment of peace — I bow to him. //
The proponent of non-self, the moon, the faultless, the supportless,
the knower of scripture, the pure-souled, the subtle — I bow to him. //
The restrainer, the eternally wise, the undifferentiated, the <s>Tathāgata</s> (Thus-Gone),
the determined, the treasure-crowned, the one beyond conceptual elaboration — I bow to him. //
The lord of the universe, the knower of liberation, the one of universal form, the guide,
the universal <s>Brahman</s>, fully accomplished, free from passion — I bow to him. //
Endowed with knowledge and conduct, the lord of all, of spotless radiance,
the knower of distinctions, the resolute, free from delusion — I bow to him. //
The tamer of the untamed, the peaceful, the pure, the son of <s>Śuddhodana</s>, the sage,
the <s>Sugata</s> (Well-Gone), of good destiny, the gentle, of resplendent fame — I bow to him. //
The lord of <s>yoga</s>, the one of ten powers, the knower of the world, worshipped by the world,
the teacher of the world, the embodiment of the world, the protector of the world — I bow to him. //
Of golden form, the ocean of <s>karma</s>, the spotless, the bearer of arts,
of beautiful form, the vessel of compassion, golden-hued — I bow to him. //
Of great wisdom, of great heroism, of great discernment, of great strength,
of great majesty, of great steadfastness, of mighty arms — I bow to him. //
The primordial, the sacred, that <s>Brahman</s>, the unconquered, the wondrous,
the noble, the benefactor of others, the protector, <s>Amitābha</s> (Infinite Light) — I bow to him. //
The god of gods, the great god, the divine, the worshipped, the imperishable,
the authoritative one, the lord of gods, of divine form — I bow to him. //
The supreme truth, the supreme light, the supreme, the supreme lord,
the creator and destroyer, the best, the Blessed One — I bow to him. //
The conqueror of the four <s>Māras</s>, the knower of truth, the beneficent, the auspicious,

in the <s>caitya</s>-place resembling a mountain-city, the descent of the God of gods —

children.text: śrāvastyāṃ lumbikāyāṃ kuśinagaravare kāpilākhye ca sthāne /

At <s>Vaiśālī</s>, at the Dharma-wheel, at the famous foremost <s>Jina</s>'s <s>Gṛdhrakūṭa</s> mountain,

children.text: ye cānye dhātucaityā daśabalabalitā tān namasyāmi buddhān //
children.translated_text: and whatever other relic-<s>caityas</s> empowered by the Ten-Powered One — I pay homage to those <s>Buddhas</s>. //
at <s>Kauśālī</s>, at <s>Sthūlakūṭa</s>, at the lovely city of <s>Mathurā</s>, at the garden of <s>Nandagopa</s> —

children.text: kailāśe hemakūṭe himavati nilaye mandare merūśṛṅge

children.translated_text: in <s>Pātāla</s>, in <s>Vaijayanta</s>, in the abode of the Lord of Wealth, in the world of <s>Siddhas</s> and <s>Gandharvas</s>,
On <s>Kailāsa</s>, on <s>Hemakūṭa</s>, in the <s>Himalayan</s> abode, on <s>Mandara</s>, on the peak of <s>Meru</s>,

children.text: ye cānye dhātucaityā daśabalavalitā tān namasyāmi buddhān //

in the egg of <s>Brahmā</s>, in the land of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, in the city of <s>Paśupati</s>, surpassing the moon and sun —

In <s>Kāśmīra</s>, in the land of <s>Cīna</s> (China), in the great city of <s>Khasata</s>, in <s>Balkh</s>, or in <s>Siṃhala</s> (Sri Lanka),

children.text: ye cānye dhātucaityā daśabalavalitā tān namasyāmi buddhān //

those in the underworld, those on earth, those on mountain peaks, and those established all around,

children.text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 23: Cakrasaṃvarastutiḥ (herukaviśuddhistotraṃ vā)
children.translated_text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 23: Praise of <s>Cakrasaṃvara</s> (or Hymn of Purification of <s>Heruka</s>)
Oṃ, homage to glorious <s>Cakrasaṃvara</s>!
I bow to glorious <s>Heruka</s>, the great hero, the <s>Saṃvara</s> of <s>Cakrasaṃvara</s>,
the conqueror of <s>Māra</s>, the leader of the <s>Ḍākinī</s> hosts. //
I honor <s>Vajravārāhī</s>, who embodies great passion,

children.text: ḍākinīṃ ca tathā lāmāṃ khaṇḍarohāṃ ca rūpiṇīm //
children.translated_text: the <s>Ḍākinī</s>, and <s>Lāmā</s>, and <s>Khaṇḍarohā</s> of beautiful form. //
The four vessels of nectar, filled with <s>bodhicitta</s>,
the fierce <s>Vajraḍākinī</s> on the peak of <s>Pullīramalaya</s>. //
And at <s>Jālandhara</s>'s peak, <s>Caṇḍākṣī</s>, free from sin,
at the place called <s>Oḍiyāna</s>, the goddess <s>Prabhāvatī</s> at the ears. //
At <s>Arbuda</s>, at the back of the spine, I bow to <s>Mahānāsā</s>;

children.text: godāvarīṃ pure vāme karṇe vīramatīṃ śubhām //
children.translated_text: at <s>Godāvarī</s>, in the city, at the left ear, the auspicious <s>Vīramatī</s>. //
<s>Rāmeśvarī</s> between the eyebrows, <s>Kharvarī</s> of excellent complexion,
the one established at <s>Devīkoṭṭa</s>, of the radiance of <s>Maitreya</s>, the glory of <s>Mallaṅkeśvarī</s>. //
In <s>Mālava</s>, at the shoulder region, I bow to <s>Drumacchāyā</s>;
in <s>Kāmarūpa</s>, at the two armpits, the auspicious goddess <s>Airāvatī</s>. //
In <s>Oḍra</s>, at the two breasts, the glorious great <s>Bhairavā</s>, faithful;
at the place called <s>Triśakuni</s>, at the navel, the delightful <s>Vāyuvegā</s>. //
In <s>Kośala</s>, at the tip of the nose, I bow to <s>Surābhakṣī</s>;
in <s>Kaliṅga</s>, at the lovely mouth, the eternal goddess <s>Śyāmādevī</s>. //
In <s>Lampāka</s>, at the throat region, the beautiful <s>Subhadrā</s>;
at the heart of the <s>Kāñcī</s> corpse-ground, the delightful <s>Hayakarṇā</s>. //
In the <s>Himālaya</s> city, at the phallus, I pay homage to <s>Khagānanā</s> (Bird-Faced);
in the Corpse-City, at the <s>liṅga</s>, in the northern quarter, <s>Śasyanīśvarī</s>. //
The household goddess at the anus, the captivating <s>Khaṇḍarohā</s>;
in <s>Saurāṣṭra</s>, at the pair of thighs, the happiness-bestowing <s>Śauṇḍinī</s>. //
In the Golden Isle (<s>Suvarṇadvīpa</s>), at the calf, the established <s>Cakravarmiṇī</s>;
in the city, at the place of the toes, the excellent <s>yoginī Suvīrā</s>. //

children.text: sindhau ca pādayoḥ pṛṣṭhe sthitāṃ devīṃ mahābalām /
children.translated_text: In <s>Sindhu</s>, at the backs of the feet, the established goddess <s>Mahābalā</s>;
in <s>Maru</s> (desert), at the pair of big toes, the established <s>Cakravartinī</s>. //
In <s>Kulatā</s>, at the pair of knees, I bow to the goddess of great vigor,
<s>Khaṇḍakapāla</s>, <s>Vīra</s>, and the rest, whose forms are instructed by their own <s>prajñā</s>. //
With my devotion, to the great heroine who pervades the <s>cakras</s> of body, speech, and mind,
<s>Kākatuṇḍī</s> (Crow-Faced), <s>Ulūkāsyā</s> (Owl-Faced), <s>Śvānāsyā</s> (Dog-Faced), <s>Śūkarānanā</s> (Boar-Faced), //
<s>Yamadāḍhī</s>, <s>Yamadūtī</s>, <s>Yamadaṃṣṭrī</s>, <s>Yamāntikā</s> —
I pay homage to these goddesses established in the directions and intermediate directions. //
Having praised <s>Heruka</s>, the lord of heroes and heroines, the supreme lord,
and this wheel of deities — whatever merit I have earned thereby,
by that merit may the world become <s>Vajraḍāka</s>, the teacher of the world! //
The praise of glorious <s>Cakrasaṃvara</s> is complete. //

durganetraṃ hūṃ hūṃ hūṃkārarūpaṃ prahasitavadanaṃ khaṅgapāśān dharantam /

Oṃ, homage to glorious <s>Caṇḍikā</s>! ŪṂ ŪṂ ŪṂ — fiercely wrathful, startled and startled, swaying,

DAṂ DAṂ DAṂ — staff in hand, with the beating ḍim-ḍim of the ḍamaru drum, whirling about,

children.text: ghraṃ ghraṃ ghraṃ ghorarūpaṃ ghughuritaghuritaṃ ghargharīnādaghoṣaṃ

BHRŪṂ BHRŪṂ BHRŪṂ — lord of <s>bhūtas</s>, benefiting all people, with bodies of <s>piśācas</s>,

children.text: vraṃ vraṃ vraṃ vyomaghoraṃ bhramati bhuvanataḥ saptapātālatālaṃ

children.translated_text: TAṂ TAṂ TAṂ — of intense form, removing my fear — to <s>Siddhi-Caṇḍī</s>, homage! //
DHŪṂ DHŪṂ DHŪṂ — of smoke-color, wandering through the world, with the noose of Death and trident,

children.text: raṃ raṃ raṃ rāyarudraṃ rurudhitarudhitaṃ dīrghajihvākarālaṃ
