RAṂ RAṂ RAṂ — royal <s>Rudra</s>, weeping and weeping, with long tongue, fierce,

children.text: hrīṃ hrīṃ hrīṃkāranāde bhavabhayaharaṇaṃ siddhicaṇḍī namaste //
children.translated_text: HRĪṂ HRĪṂ HRĪṂ — with the sound of HRĪṂ-KĀRA, removing the fear of existence — to <s>Siddhi-Caṇḍī</s>, homage! //
in battle, delighting, victorious — the maker of creation and destruction,
HŪṂ-KĀRĪ, of terrible sound, with supreme fiery crest, stealing, tawny-eyed,
HŪṂ-KĀRĪ, of the form of Time, human-flesh-mouthed, with a dense and terrible tongue,

born in the mire, born well-born, churning and churning, the desired one, thorn-throated,

children.text: kaṃ kaṃ kaṃ kālarūpaṃ ghughuritaghuritaṃ ghuṃ ghumā bindurūpī /
children.translated_text: KAṂ KAṂ KAṂ — of the form of Time, rumbling and rumbling, GHUṂ GHUMĀ — of dot-form,
ṢṬRĪṂ ṢṬRĪṂ ṢṬRĪṂ — with the sound of ṢṬRĪṂ-KĀRA, bowed to by the three worlds, terrible, more terrible, most terrible,

children.text: dhūṃ dhūṃ dhūṃ dhūmravarṇā bhramati bhuvanataḥ kālapāśatriśūlaṃ
taṃ taṃ taṃ tīvrarūpaṃ mama bhayaharaṇaṃ siddhicaṇḍī namaste //
children.translated_text: TAṂ TAṂ TAṂ — of intense form, removing my fear — to <s>Siddhi-Caṇḍī</s>, homage! //
DHŪṂ DHŪṂ DHŪṂ — of smoke-color, wandering through the world, with the noose of Death and trident,

children.text: jhrīṃ jhrīṃ jhrīṃkāravṛnde pracaritamahasā vāmahaste kapḥlaṃ

children.translated_text: KHAṂ KHAṂ KHAṂ — sword in hand, with the beating ḍim-ḍim of the ḍamaru drum, beautifully adorned with a garland of skulls,
JHRĪṂ JHRĪṂ JHRĪṂ — in the multitude of KĀRA, pervading with radiance, with a skull in the left hand,

RUṂ RUṂ RUṂ — adorned with ornaments of <s>Rudra</s>-garland, with long tongue, fierce —

of desire-form, great goddess, fierce <s>Caṇḍī</s> — homage to you! //
The glorious Staff-Verse Hymn to <s>Caṇḍikā</s> is complete. //

children.text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 25: Catuḥṣaṣṭisaṃvarastotram
children.translated_text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 25: Hymn to the Sixty-Four <s>Saṃvaras</s>
Glorious <s>Heruka</s>, the great hero, pure, lord of the <s>vajra</s> —
I bow with my whole being, adorned by hosts of <s>Ḍākinīs</s>. //
To <s>Saṃvara</s>, homage to you! To the one of dual form, homage, homage!
To the god established in the <s>cakra</s>, O <s>Cakrasaṃvara</s>, homage to you! //
To the ram-faced one, homage! To the one of the nature of <s>Śiva</s>-<s>Śakti</s>,
to the one of the nature of great wrath, O Ram-<s>Saṃvara</s>, homage to you! //
To the horse-faced god, delighting in the act of love,
bestower of enjoyment and liberation, O Horse-<s>Saṃvara</s>, homage to you! //
To the tiger-faced one, homage! To the one united with <s>Śakti</s>, homage!
Always delighting in wine and flesh, O Tiger-<s>Saṃvara</s>, homage to you! //
To the tortoise-faced one, homage! To the one who delights in love,
homage to the god of gods, O Tortoise-<s>Saṃvara</s>, homage to you! //
I bow to the fish-faced one, benefiting humankind,

children.text: namo namaste deveśa matsyasaṃvara te namaḥ //
children.translated_text: homage, homage to the lord of gods, O Fish-<s>Saṃvara</s>, homage to you! //
To the <s>makara</s>-shaped-faced one, bearer of great power,
bestower of heart's desires, O <s>Makara</s>-<s>Saṃvara</s>, homage to you! //
To <s>Saṃvara</s> camel-faced, embracing <s>Śakti</s>,
devoted to sexual union, O Camel-<s>Saṃvara</s>, homage to you! //
I bow to the elephant-faced one, who places the <s>liṅga</s> in the <s>yoni</s>,

children.text: namo bhagavate tubhyaṃ gajasaṃvara te namaḥ //
children.translated_text: homage to the Blessed One, O Elephant-<s>Saṃvara</s>, homage to you! //
To the frog-faced lord, lord of the three worlds, homage!
Homage to the god of gods, and to Frog-<s>Saṃvara</s>! //
I bow to the snake-faced one, always delighting in love,
homage to the lord of gods, O Serpent-<s>Saṃvara</s>, homage to you! //
To the parrot-faced god, beautiful in the form of duality,

children.text: namo namaste bhīmāṅga śukasaṃvara te namaḥ //
children.translated_text: homage, homage to the terrible-bodied one, O Parrot-<s>Saṃvara</s>, homage to you! //
To <s>Saṃvara</s>, homage! To the one united with <s>Śakti</s>, homage!

children.text: siṃhānanāya vai nityaṃ siṃhasaṃvara te namaḥ //
children.translated_text: To the lion-faced one always, O Lion-<s>Saṃvara</s>, homage to you! //
To the monkey-faced god, delighting in kissing <s>Śakti</s>,
homage, homage to you, O Monkey-<s>Saṃvara</s>, homage to you! //
To the dog-faced one, homage! To the one who kisses <s>Śakti</s>,

children.text: namaste bhagavan deva śvānasaṃvara te namaḥ //
children.translated_text: homage to the Blessed god, O Dog-<s>Saṃvara</s>, homage to you! //
To the excellent boar-faced one, who sports with the <s>yoni</s>,
I bow to the one united with <s>Śakti</s>, O <s>Ghṛṣṭi</s>-<s>Saṃvara</s>, homage to you! //
To the jackal-faced god, embracing <s>Śakti</s>,
the remover of all sins, O <s>Śivā</s>-<s>Saṃvara</s>, homage to you! //
I bow to the vulture-faced one, homage to the destroyer of suffering,
to the god of dual-form <s>siddhi</s>, O Vulture-<s>Saṃvara</s>, homage to you! //
To the crow-faced one, pure <s>yakṣa</s>, bearer of the form of passion,

children.text: namo bhagavate tubhyaṃ kākasaṃvara te namaḥ //
children.translated_text: homage to the Blessed One, O Crow-<s>Saṃvara</s>, homage to you! //
To the owl-faced one, bestower of great bliss,
the god who performs <s>yoni</s>-union — O Owl-<s>Saṃvara</s>, homage to you! //
To the <s>Garuḍa</s>-faced god, the savior from the ocean of existence —
Homage to you, homage to you, homage to <s>Garuḍa Saṃvara</s>!
Homage to you, O cow-faced one, O remover of the sin of cow-slaughter,
O bestower of the growth of lineage — homage to you, <s>Dhenu Saṃvara</s> (cow-protector)!
O donkey-shaped-faced one, O destroyer of the decline of coming and going,
O lord of hosts, O god — homage to you, <s>Khara Saṃvara</s> (donkey-protector)!
O buffalo-faced god, O causer of the great dissolution,
O god endowed with power — homage, <s>Mahiṣa Saṃvara</s> (buffalo-protector)!
Homage to you, O cat-faced one, O one who sports in urinal pools!
O excellent one, O supreme lord — homage, <s>Mārjāra Saṃvara</s> (cat-protector)!
I bow to the <s>śālva</s>-faced one, resplendent as a single one of two bodies.
I bow, O Lord of the Gods of Gods — homage, <s>Śarabha Saṃvara</s>!
To the accomplished one, of accomplished form, to virtue, to the abider in virtue —
homage to the crane-faced one — homage to you, <s>Krauñca Saṃvara</s> (crane-protector)!
To the meteor-faced one, to the pure, to the supreme — homage, homage!
To the fierce, to the one of terrible form — homage to you, <s>Ulka Saṃvara</s> (meteor-protector)!
Homage to the swan-faced one, O one of swan-sound-nature!
O one whose form is 'Haṃsa-So'ham' — homage to you, <s>Haṃsa Saṃvara</s> (swan-protector)!
To the deer-faced god, I bow, O Supreme Lord!
O bestower of miraculous powers and accomplishments — homage to you, <s>Mṛga Saṃvara</s> (deer-protector)!
Homage to you who are endowed with power, O <s>cakravāka</s>-faced one!
Homage, homage to the <s>Saṃvara</s> called <s>Cakravāka</s> (ruddy goose)!
To the goat-faced hero, homage, O destroyer of ignorance!
For the attainment of the fruit of liberation — homage to you, <s>Aja Saṃvara</s> (goat-protector)!
To the rooster-faced god, to the increaser of family —
homage to the lord of wonders — to you, <s>Kukkuṭa Saṃvara</s> (rooster-protector)!
To the black-antelope-faced one, homage, O born of <s>karma</s>!
To the destroyer of death, O god — homage to you, <s>Eṇa Saṃvara</s> (antelope-protector)!
To the mouse-faced one, to the complete one, to the giver of knowledge — homage, homage!
To the destroyer of all <s>daityas</s> (demons) — homage to you, <s>Mūṣa Saṃvara</s> (mouse-protector)!
Homage to the otter-faced one, O bestower of boons such as honor!
O bestower of accomplishment and wisdom — homage, <s>Sālūka Saṃvara</s>!
Homage to the pigeon-faced one, O one whose form is wisdom and means!
Homage to you, O great hero — and to <s>Kapota Saṃvara</s> (pigeon-protector)!
I bow to the crocodile-faced one, O bestower of enjoyment and liberation!
Homage, O lord of all beings — homage to you, <s>Grāha Saṃvara</s> (crocodile-protector)!
Homage to the <s>cihla</s>-faced one, homage to the one delighting in union!

children.text: namaste bhagavan deva cihlasaṃvara te namaḥ //
children.translated_text: Homage, O blessed god — homage to you, <s>Cihla Saṃvara</s>!
To the sparrow-faced god, homage to you, O guru of the world!
Homage, O lord of virtues — homage to you, <s>Caṭaka Saṃvara</s> (sparrow-protector)!
Homage to you, O crane-faced one, homage, O ocean of virtues!
Homage to you, O Blessed One — and to <s>Sārasa Saṃvara</s> (crane-protector)!
To the wagtail-faced god, homage to you, O great god!
O bestower of the station of <s>Nirvāṇa</s> — and to <s>Khañjarīṭa Saṃvara</s> (wagtail-protector)!
Homage to the <s>kṣemakari</s>-faced one, O bestower of enjoyment and liberation!
Homage, O blessed god — to you, <s>Kṣemakari Saṃvara</s>!
Homage to you, O rabbit-faced one, homage, O Lord of the World!
O bestower of <s>karma</s> always — homage, <s>Śaśaka Saṃvara</s> (rabbit-protector)!
Homage to the bear-faced one, O one devoted to amorous sport!
O bestower of success in undertakings — homage, <s>Bhallūka Saṃvara</s> (bear-protector)!
Homage to you, O cuckoo-faced one, O accomplisher of <s>mantra</s>-success!
To the lord of the three worlds, to the all — homage to you, <s>Pika Saṃvara</s> (cuckoo-protector)!
I bow to the heron-faced one, O lord of hosts endowed with power!
I bow, O Lord of the Gods of Gods — homage to you, <s>Vaka Saṃvara</s> (heron-protector)!
To the rhinoceros-faced god, always I bow with my head!
Homage to the supreme lord — homage to you, <s>Khaṅgi Saṃvara</s> (rhinoceros-protector)!
Homage to you, O crab-faced one, homage, O cause of <s>saṃsāra</s>!
O destroyer of the mass of sins — homage, <s>Karkaṭa Saṃvara</s> (crab-protector)!
Homage to the porcupine-faced one, O averter of all faults!
O destroyer of the noose of <s>saṃsāra</s> — homage, <s>Śallaki Saṃvara</s> (porcupine-protector)!
Homage to you, O scorpion-faced one, O bestower of strength and auspiciousness!
Homage, homage to you, O god — homage, <s>Vṛścika Saṃvara</s> (scorpion-protector)!
To the bee-faced god, homage, O one delighting in the joy of bees!
O destroyer of the bee-world — homage to you, <s>Ali Saṃvara</s> (bee-protector)!
Homage to the <s>jāhaka</s>-faced one, O causer of the bewilderment of people!
O bestower of victory and auspiciousness — homage, <s>Jāhaka Saṃvara</s>!
To the yak-faced one, always, O bestower of the fruit of skillfulness,
O bestower of the four goals of life — homage, <s>Camari Saṃvara</s> (yak-protector)!
Homage to you, O <s>sīmni</s>-faced one, O bestower of the fruit of accomplishment!

children.text: namo bhagavate nityaṃ sīmnisaṃvara te namaḥ //
children.translated_text: Homage always, O Blessed One — homage to you, <s>Sīmni Saṃvara</s>!
I bow to the iguana-faced one, homage to the one of terrible valor!
Homage to the divine-eyed one — homage to you, <s>Godhā Saṃvara</s> (iguana-protector)!
Homage to you, O <s>cakora</s> (partridge)-faced one, O destroyer of the fault of fickleness!
Homage to you, O Blessed One — and to <s>Cakora Saṃvara</s> (partridge-protector)!
To the lizard-faced one, constantly, O one who creates and destroys,
homage, O supreme bliss — and to <s>Godhikā Saṃvara</s> (lizard-protector)!
To the honey-bee-faced one, homage, O bestower of honor!
To the omniscient, to the supreme lord — homage, <s>Mākṣika Saṃvara</s> (honey-bee-protector)!

children.text: pataṅgavaktra te nityaṃ parameśa namaḥ sadā /
children.translated_text: To the moth-faced one, always, O supreme lord, homage always!
To the divine, to the lord of days — homage, <s>Pataṅga Saṃvara</s> (moth-protector)!
To the human-faced god, homage to the destroyer of hells!
O one who assumes manifold forms — homage to you, <s>Nara Saṃvara</s> (human-protector)!
O form of creation, O abode of the world, who creates all beings —

children.text: namo namaste satataṃ sṛṣṭisaṃvara te namaḥ //
children.translated_text: homage, homage to you constantly — homage to you, <s>Sṛṣṭi Saṃvara</s> (creation-protector)!
To the god whose form is maintenance, to virtue, to the abider in virtue,
homage, O destroyer of essence — homage to you, <s>Sthiti Saṃvara</s> (maintenance-protector)!
To the maker of the dissolution of all worlds, O supreme lord —
therefore I worship — homage, <s>Pralaya Saṃvara</s> (dissolution-protector)!
O luminous-faced one, O supreme abode, homage, O Lord of the World!
Supreme beyond the supreme, subtle — homage to you, <s>Jyotiḥ Saṃvara</s> (light-protector)!
This <s>Saṃvara</s> Stotra, rare in the three worlds,
is a supreme hymn, sixty-four in measure.
Of the sixty-four in measure, the first of the first has been recited;
moreover, from this treatise, only the first has been set forth by me.

children.text: kanyārthī labhate kanyāṃ dhanārthī labhate dhanam /
children.translated_text: One desiring a maiden obtains a maiden; one desiring wealth obtains wealth;
one desiring knowledge obtains knowledge; one desiring liberation attains liberation.
Subjugation, expulsion, killing, enchantment, immobilization,
attraction, enmity, metallic transmutation, and <s>rasāyana</s> (rejuvenation),
magical pill, flying-shoe accomplishment, sword-accomplishment likewise,
<s>khecarī</s> (sky-traveling) accomplishment, medical arts, <s>mantra</s>-accomplishment, and eloquence,
entering another's body, and attraction of objects —
one obtains through this King of Stotras — truly, truly, as declared by me.
In famine, calamity, one who recites it obtains auspiciousness.
In excessive rain, in drought, and when great plague arises,
in loss of kingdom, loss of knowledge, loss of a woman, and loss of wealth,

children.text: kalahe ca vivāde ca paṭhate stotramuttamam //
children.translated_text: in quarrel and dispute — one should recite this excellent stotra.
The fruit is equal to giving to thousands of mendicants;
why say more — the fruit equals the gift of the entire universe!

From the Śrī <s>Saṃvara Āgama</s> Mahātantra, in the conversation of <s>Amitābha</s> and <s>Vairocana</s>, the Hymn to the Sixty-Four <s>Saṃvaras</s> beginning with Śrī <s>Cakrasaṃvara</s> is complete.

children.text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 26: Daśabhūmīśvaro nāma mahāyānasūtraratnarājastotram
children.translated_text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 26: <s>Daśabhūmīśvara</s>, the Jewel-King Stotra of the Mahāyāna Sūtra.
resembling the path of birds, equal to the sky,
Of those devoted to calm and self-control, of peaceful and disciplined minds,
hear the supreme distinctions of the <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, the excellent ones!
with impurities and stains shaken off, established in path-knowledge —
having worshipped a hundred thousand well-awakened ones and received their teaching,
Having accumulated a hundred thousand wholesome deeds over eons,
for the welfare of the entire world, the thought of awakening (<s>bodhicitta</s>) arises.
having worshipped innumerable excellent <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> —
whose conduct draws upon sacred examples, who have arisen in merit and knowledge,
Of those who have practiced severe austerities, who have reached the perfection of patience,
the thought of awakening arises, equal to the Ten Powers.
of vast course and intellect, whose aspiration is in merit and knowledge —
always exerting for the welfare of the entire world,
Of those of joyful, excellent minds, delighting in the dharma of giving,
the thought of awakening arises, working for the welfare of the three worlds.
devoted to the virtues of the <s>Jinas</s>, with vows to protect beings —
delighting in vows and observances, with peaceful and gentle senses,
Of those who have ceased unwholesome deeds, established on the pure path,
the thought of awakening arises, to be accomplished for the welfare of the three worlds.
who have taken refuge in the <s>Jinas</s>, whose aspiration is the conduct of awakening —
who have realized the taste of virtues, who have abandoned the festival of pride,
Of those who follow the wholesome, who share in the essence of patience,
the thought of awakening arises, for the arrangement of universal welfare.
whose auspicious minds are firmly set, whose aspiration is gentle giving —
for the welfare of all people, the lion of the mind arises.
When auspicious work advances, steadfast vigor is their companion;
instantly in the mind of those, the thought of awakening arises.
With unceasing pursuit of virtues, having conquered the hosts of afflictions —
with intoxication and pride vanished, having abandoned the afflicted path,
With well-composed minds, with the darkness of delusion destroyed,
instantly in the mind of those, the thought of awakening arises.
those who delight in equal happiness, who have abandoned attachment to <s>saṃsāra</s> —
having slain the <s>Māra</s> <s>Namuci</s>, having vomited the pride of afflictions,
With minds pure as stainless sky, knowing knowledge and discernment,
at once in the mind of those, the thought of awakening arises.
established in the refuge of the <s>Jina</s>'s station, having obtained the body of true meaning —
possessing miraculous power in the method of overcoming elephant-strength,
Steadfast in the knowledge of skillful means for the welfare of the three worlds,
at once in the mind of those, the thought of awakening arises.
those who aspire to the qualities of the <s>Sugata</s> and delight in merit —
with resolute minds, practice even what is difficult to do —
Those who desire the welfare of the three worlds, for the completion of the accumulations of awakening,
At once in the mind of those, the thought of awakening arises.
may the <s>Bodhisattvas</s> arise in unceasing good deeds!
having conquered the flood of elephant-strength, having abandoned attachment to pride,
Those who desire the qualities of the Ten Powers, devoted to the conduct of awakening,
instantly in the mind of those, the thought of awakening arises.
following the auspicious path, having obtained Dharma, <s>artha</s>, and <s>kāma</s> —
May those with aspirations for the <s>Jina</s>'s station obtain true prosperity!
Thus, may those of enumerated portions of virtue practice the conduct of awakening!
Purified in the Triple Refuge, may they become <s>Bodhisattvas</s>!
Purified in the three worlds, may they obtain <s>bodhicitta</s>!
Having fulfilled the ten <s>pāramitās</s>, one becomes the Lord of the Ten Stages.
This will be told further — listen to it thus in summary.
When, having generated <s>bodhicitta</s>, one performs the act of giving,
then one attains the <s>Pramuditā</s> (Joyful) stage and becomes lord of <s>Jambudvīpa</s>.
Stationed there, one protects beings by providing according to their wishes;
establishing oneself in giving, one also engages others in it.
Having established all in awakening, having reached the far shore of giving,
through the power of these deeds, one should undertake the <s>saṃvara</s> (vow).
Having properly maintained morality, one becomes accomplished in the vow;
then, one attains the <s>Vimalā</s> (Stainless) stage and becomes lord of the four continents.
Stationed there, one protects beings and prevents the unwholesome;
establishing oneself in morality, one also engages others in it.
Having established all in awakening, one becomes fully accomplished.
Through the ripening of these dharmas, one should undertake the vow of patience.

children.text: samyak kṣāntivrataṃ dhṛtvā kṣāntibhṛt kuśalī bhavet /
children.translated_text: Having properly held the vow of patience, the patient one becomes accomplished;
then, one attains the <s>Prābhākarī</s> (Luminous) stage and becomes lord of the Thirty-Three gods.
Stationed there, one protects beings by averting the path of afflictions;
establishing oneself in the vow of patience, one also engages others in it.
Having established beings in awakening, one reaches the far shore of peace.
Through the ripening of this merit, one should take up the power of vigor.
Having properly maintained vigor, the vigorous one becomes accomplished;
then, one attains the <s>Arciṣmatī</s> (Blazing) stage and becomes lord of the <s>Sudhāma</s> (Yāma heaven).
Dwelling there, protecting all beings, he should ward off wrong views.
Having established them in right view and awakened them with effort,
himself abiding in the vow of meditation, he should also engage others.
Having established all in awakening, he becomes one who has reached the far shore of meditation.
By the ripening of this merit, he should undertake the perfection of meditation.
Having conquered all <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions), he becomes well-established in <s>samādhi</s>.
Having properly established meditation, he becomes skilled in <s>samādhi</s>.

children.text: tataḥ sudurjayāṃ prāptaḥ sa tuṣitādhipo bhavet //
children.translated_text: Then, having attained <s>Sudurjayā</s> (the 'Hard to Conquer' stage), he becomes lord of <s>Tuṣita</s> heaven.
Dwelling there, he should protect beings by warding off the paths of <s>tīrthikas</s> (non-Buddhist teachers).
Having established them in the dharma of beings and awakened them with effort,
himself abiding in the vow of meditation, he should also engage others.
Having established all in awakening, he becomes one who has reached the far shore of meditation.
By the ripening of this merit, he should resort to the vow of wisdom.
Having conquered all <s>Māras</s>, he becomes endowed with the riches of wisdom and superknowledge.
Having properly established wisdom, he becomes skilled in his own superknowledges.
Then, having attained <s>Abhimukhī</s> (the 'Facing' stage), he becomes lord of <s>Sunirmita</s> heaven.
Dwelling there, he should protect beings by warding off conceit.
Having well-established emptiness and awakened them with effort,
himself abiding in the vow of wisdom, he should also engage others.
Having established all in awakening, he becomes one who has reached the far shore of wisdom.
By the ripening of this merit, he should practice the vow of skillful means.
Having conquered all the wicked, the wise one becomes skilled in the true Dharma.
By the method of skillful means, he should engage beings in awakening.
Then, having attained <s>Dūraṅgamā</s> (the 'Far-Going' stage), he becomes lord of <s>Vaśavartin</s> heaven.
Dwelling there, he should protect beings through teachings of realization.
Having established them in the certainties of <s>bodhisattvas</s>, he should awaken them.
Himself abiding in skillful means, he should also engage others.
Having established all in awakening, he becomes one who has reached the far shore of skillful means.
By the power of this merit, he should resort to excellent aspirations.
Having conquered wrong views, he is made one of right view by the wise.
With a well-established mind, he is established in perfect awakening.
Then, having attained <s>Acalā</s> (the 'Immovable' stage), he becomes lord of a thousand-fold <s>Buddha</s>-realm.
Dwelling there, he should protect beings; he should slowly drink the triple liberation.
Having established them in full knowledge of the world-realm, he should awaken them.
Himself abiding in excellent aspiration, he should also engage others.

children.text: sarvān bodhau pratiṣṭhāpya prāṇiṣu pārago bhavet //
children.translated_text: Having established all in awakening, he becomes one who has reached the far shore regarding beings.
Following this merit, he should resort to the vow of power.
Having conquered all the wicked, he becomes resolute regarding complete awakening.
With right effort and energy, he should conquer all <s>tīrthikas</s>.

children.text: tataḥ sādhumatīṃ prāpto mahābrahmā bhavet kṛtī //
children.translated_text: Then, having attained <s>Sādhumatī</s> (the 'Good Intelligence' stage), he becomes the accomplished Great <s>Brahmā</s>.
Dwelling there, protecting beings through instructions in the <s>Buddha</s>-vehicle,
establishing them in full knowledge of the diversity of beings, he should awaken them in perfect enlightenment.
Himself established in power, he should also engage others.
Having established all in awakening, he becomes one who has reached the far shore of power.
By the ripening of this merit, he should resort to the vow of knowledge.
Having conquered the four <s>Māras</s>, he becomes a mine of <s>bodhisattva</s> qualities.
Having properly established right knowledge, he becomes skilled in the true Dharma.

children.text: dharmameghāṃ tataḥ prāpto maheśvaro bhavet kṛtī //
children.translated_text: Then, having attained <s>Dharmameghā</s> (the 'Cloud of Dharma' stage), the accomplished one becomes <s>Maheśvara</s>.
Dwelling there, protecting all through awakening of all aspects,
having established them in the supreme knowledge of all aspects, he should awaken them.
Himself established in knowledge, he should also engage others.
Having established all in awakening, he becomes one who has reached the far shore of knowledge.
By the power of this merit, he becomes a <s>Jina</s>, lord of the ten stages,
the foundation of all qualities of all aspects, omniscient, attainer of the Dharma.
Thus knowing, those on earth, for the attainment of the perfect <s>Buddha</s>'s state,
should practice with concentration in the form of the ten <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections).

children.text: tathā bodhiṃ śivāṃ prāpya caturmārān vinirjayet /
children.translated_text: Thus, having attained auspicious awakening, one should conquer the four <s>Māras</s>.
Having established all in awakening, one will then attain <s>Nirvāṇa</s>.
Having known this, practice according to its scope in the teaching of awakening.
Attaining awakening without obstacles, obtain the state of the <s>Sugata</s>!

children.text: etāstā khalvāha jinaputro daśabodhisattvabhūmayaḥ samāsato nirdiṣṭāḥ sarvākāravaropetāḥ sarvajñānānugatā draṣṭavyāḥ / tasyāṃ velāyāmayaṃ trisāhasralokadhātuṣaḍvikāraṃ prākampata vividhāni ca puṇyāni viyatto nyapatan / divyamānuṣakāṇi ca bhūtāni saṃpravāditānyabhūvan, anumodanāṃśagena ca yāvadakaniṣṭhabhuvanaṃ vijñaptamabhūt //
children.translated_text: These indeed, said the Son of the <s>Jina</s>, are the ten <s>Bodhisattva</s> stages, briefly explained, endowed with all aspects of excellence, to be seen as following all knowledge. At that time, this three-thousand world-system shook in six ways, and various merits fell from the sky. Divine and human musical instruments were sounded, and through the portion of rejoicing, notification reached as far as the <s>Akaniṣṭha</s> heaven. //
From the <s>Śrī Bodhisattvacaryāprasthāna</s>, the stotra called 'Lord of the Ten Stages,' a jewel-king of <s>Mahāyāna</s> sūtras, is complete. //

children.text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 27: Dharmadhātunāmastavaḥ
children.translated_text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 27: Hymn of the Names of <s>Dharmadhātu</s>
The syllable <s>vaṃ</s>, <s>Vajrasattva</s>, always established on the <s>vajra</s>-seat,
pervading the water-<s>maṇḍala</s> — homage to you, <s>Vairocana</s>! //
The syllable <s>a</s>, whose nature is the primordial, pervading space likewise,
with brilliance like the sun and blue — homage to the glory of <s>Akṣobhya</s>! //
The syllable <s>ra</s>, whose nature is prosperity, manifold with various jewels,

children.text: raṃ vyāpitaṃ ca pṛthvīṃ ratnasaṃbhava namo 'stu te //
children.translated_text: <s>raṃ</s> pervading the earth — homage to you, <s>Ratnasaṃbhava</s>! //
The syllable <s>a</s>, of unstable nature, with radiance like a lotus-<s>nāga</s>,
established in the <s>samādhi</s> of fire's brilliance — homage to you, <s>Amitābha</s>! //
The syllable <s>a</s>, its nature being that, with radiance like the wind,
the syllable <s>a</s>, the universal <s>vajra</s> — homage to you, <s>Amoghasiddhi</s>! //
The syllable <s>dha</s>, whose nature is Dharma, having the form of the Dharma and <s>Saṅgha</s>,

children.text: dhātvaṣṭakaṃ kīrtitaṃ ca dharmadhātu namo 'stu te //
children.translated_text: proclaimed as the eightfold elements — homage to you, <s>Dharmadhātu</s>! //
The syllable <s>sa</s>, all prosperity, seeking all auspiciousness,
you are all <s>siddhis</s> (accomplishments) — homage to you, <s>Siddhivajra</s>! //
The Śrī <s>Dharmadhātunāmastava</s> is complete. //

children.text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 28: Dharmadhātuvāgīśvaramaṇḍalastotram
children.translated_text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 28: Hymn to the <s>Dharmadhātu-Vāgīśvara</s> Maṇḍala
To <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, the great hero, destroyer of all <s>Māras</s>,
lord of all <s>siddhis</s>, the protector, lord of speech — I bow! //
To <s>Mañjughoṣa</s>, the great hero, destroyer of all <s>Māras</s>,
bestower of all forms, the <s>Dharmadhātu</s> — I bow! //
To <s>Mahoṣṇīṣa</s>, the white parasol, mass of brilliance, arisen in victory,
and to the radiating, risen, fiercely brilliant one — I bow! //
To <s>Akṣobhya</s>, to great <s>Bodhi</s>, to <s>Vajrasattva</s> — I bow!
To <s>Vajrarāja</s>, <s>Vajrarāga</s>, <s>Vajrasādhu</s> — I bow! //
To Śrī <s>Ratnasambhava</s>, the protector, to <s>Vajraratna</s> — I bow!
To <s>Vajrasūrya</s>, <s>Vajraketu</s>, <s>Vajrahāsa</s> — I bow always! //
To <s>Amitābha</s>, the great king, to <s>Vajradharma</s> — I bow!
To <s>Vajratīkṣṇa</s>, the great banner, to <s>Vajrabhāṣa</s> — I bow, I bow! //
To <s>Amoghasiddhi</s>, lord of <s>siddhi</s>, to <s>Vajrakarma</s> — I bow!
To <s>Vajrarakṣa</s>, <s>Vajrayakṣa</s>, <s>Vajrasandhi</s> — I bow always! //
To the great goddess called <s>Locanā</s>, to the one called <s>Pāṇḍarā</s> — I bow!

children.text: māmakīṃ caiva devīṃ tāṃ tārādevīṃ name name //
children.translated_text: To the goddess <s>Māmakī</s> and to the goddess <s>Tārā</s> — I bow, I bow! //
To <s>Vajrāṅkuśa</s>, the great hero, to <s>Vajrapāśa</s> of great splendor,
to <s>Vajrasphoṭa</s>, the great lord, to <s>Vajrāveśa</s> — I bow, I bow! //
To the stage of <s>Adhimuktī</s> (Aspiration), to <s>Pramuditā</s> (the Joyful) — I bow!
To the great stage called <s>Vimalā</s> (Stainless), to <s>Prabhākarī</s> (the Radiant) — I bow, I bow! //
To <s>Arciṣmatī</s> (the Blazing), to <s>Sudurjayā</s> (Hard to Conquer), to <s>Abhimukhī</s> (the Facing) — I bow!
To <s>Dūraṅgamā</s> (the Far-Going), to the one called <s>Acalā</s> (Immovable), to the lady <s>Sādhumatī</s> (Good Intelligence) — I bow! //
To <s>Dharmameghā</s> (Cloud of Dharma), to the great cloud, to the one called <s>Samatā</s> (Equality), to Radiance — I bow!
To the goddess <s>Ratnapāramitā</s>, to <s>Dānapāramitā</s> (Perfection of Giving) — I bow! //
To the goddess <s>Śīlapāramitā</s> (Perfection of Morality), to <s>Kṣāntipāramitā</s> (Perfection of Patience) — I bow!
To the goddess <s>Vīryapāramitā</s> (Perfection of Vigor), to <s>Dhyānapāramitā</s> (Perfection of Meditation) — I take refuge! //
To the goddess <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> (Perfection of Wisdom), to the one called <s>Upāya</s> (Skillful Means) — I bow!
To <s>Praṇidhāna-bala</s> (Power of Aspiration), to <s>Jñānapāramitā</s> (Perfection of Knowledge) — always! //
To the goddess <s>Karmapāramitā</s> (Perfection of Action) — I bow constantly likewise.
To the purification of life and mind, to the one of karmic rebirth — I bow! //
To the one called <s>Ṛddhi</s> (Supernatural Power), to <s>Adhimukti</s> (Aspiration), to <s>Praṇidhāna</s> (Vow) — I bow!
To the goddess of mastery called <s>Jñāna</s> (Knowledge), to the mastery called <s>Dharma</s> — I bow! //
To <s>Tathatā</s> (Suchness), the great goddess, to <s>Buddhabodhi</s> (Buddha-Awakening) — I bow!
To <s>Vasumatī</s>, to <s>Mahālakṣmī</s>, to <s>Ratnajvālā</s> — I bow, I bow! //
To the goddess <s>Uṣṇīṣavijayā</s>, to <s>Mārīcī</s>, to <s>Parṇaśābarī</s>,

The treasure obtained by the destitute, the sacred ford called <s>Ākara</s> (Mine), worshipped by the devoted,

at the sacred ford called <s>Cintāmaṇi</s> (Wish-fulfilling Gem), where through consecrations desires were attained,

the elevated <s>Śaṅkha</s> (Conch), and the beautiful <s>Jātoccaya</s> mountain <s>caitya</s>, that <s>Caityabhaṭṭāraka</s>,
The subsidiary sacred fords beginning with the source and tail of the <s>Vāgmatī</s>, and the hair-<s>caityas</s> (<s>keśacaitya</s>),

the elevated <s>Phulloca</s>, the goddess <s>Draṣṭadevī</s>, and then those established in meditation of the <s>Bhagavatī</s>,
the five god-cities built by <s>Śāntaśrī</s>, where natural dwellings exist,
The <s>caitya</s> called <s>Mañjuśobhā</s>, situated on <s>Mañjuśrī</s>'s mountain, fashioned by attendants,

the supreme <s>caitya</s> at the tail-tip, where the incomparable hope of <s>Śāketa</s> city was proclaimed,
and the <s>Nāga</s> in the world of <s>Ānanda</s>, in the dynasty of the three worlds called <s>Harihariharivāha</s>,
The one called <s>Ādhāra</s> (Support), dwelling in the heart, with <s>Gaṇa</s> and the serpent-lord, <s>Vighnarāja</s> and <s>Antaka</s>,

children.text: kalyāṇaṃ vaḥ kriyāsuḥ kvacidapi saratāṃ tiṣṭhatāṃ naumyahaṃ tāḥ //

<s>Lokeśa</s> (Lord of the World), may he be gracious! Then the sole lord of the world who fulfills aspirations,
the hero <s>Yogāmbara</s>, <s>Yama</s>, the death-dealer, and the other ten wrathful kings,
<s>Hevajra</s>, <s>Saṃvara</s>, with their retinue and hosts, <s>Caṇḍavīra</s>, lord of the three worlds,

children.text: kalyāṇaṃ vaḥ kriyāsuḥ kvacidapi saratāṃ tiṣṭhatāṃ naumyahaṃ tāḥ //
children.translated_text: may they bring you auspiciousness! Wherever they flow or abide, I bow to them! //
all the secret and outer ones, headed by the measured ones, expounded in the <s>Nāmasaṃgīti</s>,

children.text: chitvā śoṣe hrade 'smin puravarakamalo lokavāsāḥ parasya /
children.translated_text: having cut through the drought in this lake, the supreme lotus city, the dwelling of the world beyond —

children.text: kalyāṇaṃ vaḥ kriyāsuḥ kvacidapi saratāṃ tiṣṭhatāṃ naumyahaṃ tāḥ //
children.translated_text: may they bring you auspiciousness! Wherever they flow or abide, I bow to them! //
established in restored waters, worshipping all the supreme <s>Jinas</s>, <s>Mañjunātha</s> (Lord Mañju),

children.text: saukhāvatyāśca vaṅgaṃ tadanu janahite potale prāgamad yaḥ

children.translated_text: the peaceful one, removing the fault of planetary seizure, entered the excellent city of <s>Lalitapura</s>, summoned by the gods —

that glorious <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>, with <s>Jaṭādhara</s> (the matted-hair bearer), <s>Hayagrīva</s>, attendants, and <s>Gaṇeśa</s>,
The <s>Kalyāṇapañcaviṃśati</s> hymn, extracted from the <s>Śrī Svayambhūpurāṇa</s>, is complete. //

children.text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 35: Kalyāṇatriṃśatikāstotram
children.translated_text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 35: <s>Kalyāṇatriṃśatikāstotram</s>
Having entered into the syllable <s>evaṃ</s>, through body, speech, mind, and intellect,

children.text: karomi satataṃ tasyā nutiṃ pūjāṃ pradakṣiṇām //
children.translated_text: I constantly perform praise, worship, and circumambulation of her. //
She who is the goddess of all beings, the cause of creation and destruction —
homage to her, homage to her, homage to her, salutations! //
She who is the goddess established in the protection of all creatures —
homage to her, homage to her, homage to her, salutations! //
She who is the goddess abiding in the form of the deity of all divine goddesses —
homage to her, homage to her, homage to her, salutations! //
She who is the goddess, terrifying in the form of burning fire against the wicked <s>Daityas</s> —
homage to her, homage to her, homage to her, salutations! //
She who is the goddess, the thousand-headed serpent-queen of all <s>Nāgas</s> —
homage to her, homage to her, homage to her, salutations! //
She who is the goddess established in peaceful form in the seven <s>Pātālas</s> (netherworlds) —
homage to her, homage to her, homage to her, salutations! //
She who is the goddess, the mother of the <s>Vedas</s> for men and women, <s>Cidambikā</s> (Mother of Consciousness) —
homage to her, homage to her, homage to her, salutations! //
She who is the goddess worshipped by <s>Kṣatriya</s>, <s>Vaiśya</s>, <s>Śūdra</s>, and all castes —
homage to her, homage to her, homage to her, salutations! //
She who is the goddess, of great supernatural power, for the protection of the world of the departed (<s>Pretaloka</s>) —
homage to her, homage to her, homage to her, salutations! //
She who is the goddess among all animals, the savior, the destroyer of suffering —
homage to her, homage to her, homage to her, salutations! //

children.text: yā devī nārakīyāṇāṃ duḥkhabhājāṃ ca mātṛkā /
children.translated_text: She who is the goddess, the mother of those in the hells who partake of suffering —
homage to her, homage to her, homage to her, salutations! //
She who is the goddess, the destroyer of the sixteen hells —
homage to her, homage to her, homage to her, salutations! //
She who is the goddess, made fierce against those possessed by hatred, passion, and delusion —
homage to her, homage to her, homage to her, salutations! //
She who is the goddess established in the form of wrath against lust and anger —
homage to her, homage to her, homage to her, salutations! //
She who is the goddess, slow to act for the overcoming of greed and gain —
homage to her, homage to her, homage to her, salutations! //

children.text: yā devī māyāyā mātā mātṝṇāṃ vajrayogiṇī /
children.translated_text: She who is the goddess, the mother of <s>Māyā</s> (Illusion), the <s>Vajrayoginī</s> of all mothers —
homage to her, homage to her, homage to her, salutations! //
She who is the goddess, the destroyer of kings, thieves, fire, lions, and enemies —
homage to her, homage to her, homage to her, salutations! //
She who is the goddess, the savior from floods, serpents, snakes, famine, and fear —
homage to her, homage to her, homage to her, salutations! //

children.text: yā devī pañcabhūtānāṃ candre sūrye pratiṣṭhitā /
children.translated_text: She who is the goddess of the five elements, established in the moon and sun —
homage to her, homage to her, homage to her, salutations! //
She who is the goddess, the material wave, moving through the <s>āli</s> and <s>kāli</s> (vowels and consonants) —
homage to her, homage to her, homage to her, salutations! //
She who is the goddess, the mistress of all <s>pīṭhas</s> (sacred seats), <s>Upacaṇḍikā</s> in the form of the sacred field —
homage to her, homage to her, homage to her, salutations! //
She who is the goddess known as <s>Pīla</s>, united with <s>Upapīla</s> —
homage to her, homage to her, homage to her, salutations! //
She who is the goddess adorned with the zodiac signs and ascendants in the twelve <s>cakras</s> —
homage to her, homage to her, homage to her, salutations! //
She who is the goddess in the six-limbed realm, with the moonlight of an awakened face —
homage to her, homage to her, homage to her, salutations! //
She who is the goddess moving through the fierce <s>cakras</s>, the supreme sovereign —
homage to her, homage to her, homage to her, salutations! //
She who is the goddess moving in body, speech, and mind in the form of <s>mantra</s> —
homage to her, homage to her, homage to her, salutations! //
She who is the goddess, the pure-souled <s>Śrī</s>, bestower of power, <s>siddhi</s>, and strength —
homage to her, homage to her, homage to her, salutations! //
She who is the goddess, always bringing auspiciousness to all creatures —
homage to her, homage to her, homage to her, salutations! //

children.text: ya idaṃ paṭhate dhīmān devyā bhaktisamanvitaḥ /
children.translated_text: The wise one who recites this, endowed with devotion to the goddess —

children.text: buddhatvaṃ labhate śīghraṃ kalyāṇaṃ maṅgalaṃ śivam //
children.translated_text: swiftly attains <s>Buddhahood</s>, auspiciousness, blessings, and bliss. //
The <s>Kalyāṇatriṃśatikāstotra</s> of <s>Śrī Vajradevī</s>, who dwells in the three <s>kāyas</s> (bodies), is complete. //

children.text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 36: Kamalākarasarvatathāgatastotram
children.translated_text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 36: <s>Kamalākarasarvatathāgatastotram</s>
Then indeed, in the lotus-grove, he praised the <s>Buddhas</s>, the Blessed Ones of the past, future, and present, with this hymn to all <s>Tathāgatas</s>:

children.text: ye jinapūrvakāye bhavanti ye ca dhriyanti daśadiśi loke /
children.translated_text: Those <s>Jinas</s> who existed in former bodies, and those who abide in the ten directions of the world —

children.text: tān hi jināṃśca karomi praṇāmaṃ taṃ jinasaṃghamahaṃ prabhijaṣye //
children.translated_text: to those <s>Jinas</s> I make obeisance; that assembly of <s>Jinas</s>, I shall worship! //
The peaceful, tranquil, and pure Lord of Sages, whose body is radiant with the splendor of gold and fine gold,
whose voice is the sweet sound of all gods and <s>asuras</s>, whose roar is the sound and voice of <s>Brahmā</s>. //
Whose hair is like trees swarmed by six-legged bees, dark, beautifully curled, and brilliant as lightning,
whose teeth are white as conch shells and snow, whose navel shines with golden radiance. //
Whose eyes are blue, vast, pure, and beautiful, like a field of blossoming blue <s>utpalas</s> (lotuses),
whose tongue is beautiful like a golden lotus, with the splendor and comfort of a lotus in bloom. //
Resembling a conch shell and lotus stalk, the beautiful form of bliss, with right-turning spiral patterns,
like the fine crescent moon diminishing in the night sky, with a navel beautiful as a lotus of sacred <s>mantras</s>,
with a nose beautiful as millions of golden peaks, with leaves of feet soft and elevated,
with the foremost tip of the lower lip and the tip of the nose most excellent — that one, gentle-handed, conqueror of all, forever. //
With each single hair-tip on the face, with fine body-hair turning clockwise,
born with brilliant blue earrings, with a beautiful neck adorned by a blue diadem. //
With limbs of equal radiance as gold, worshipped in all ten directions of the world,
having pacified the endless suffering of the world, and having satisfied the world with all happiness. //
In the hells, in the animal realms, in the <s>preta</s> (hungry ghost), <s>asura</s> (demon), and human destinies,
bestowing happiness upon all beings including <s>piśācas</s> (flesh-eating spirits), bringing peace in all lower realms. //
Of beautiful complexion, shining like gold, with body radiant as heated gold,
with a gentle face pure as the moon, with a blooming, resplendent, and spotless countenance. //
With limbs tender as the tips of young sprouts, with the roar and stride of a lion's challenge,
with hanging hands and long arms, with a tongue [gentle] like a <s>śāla</s> tree swayed by the wind. //
Releasing radiant beams blazing in the sky, scorching with brilliance like the sun,
the lord of sages with pure and excellent limbs, illuminating infinite fields. //
The net of moon, night-luminary, and sun — in infinite thousands of fields,
all of these too have surely come into being for the illumination of the <s>Buddha's</s> radiance. //
The <s>Buddha</s>, the day-maker, the lamp of the world, the thousand rays of the <s>Buddha</s>-sun —
in infinite thousands of fields, behold the <s>Tathāgata</s>-sun of the world! //
Having performed hundreds and thousands of meritorious deeds, with body adorned with all excellent qualities,
resembling a mighty <s>Airāvaṇa</s> elephant, with arms purified and adorned, victorious in strength. //
Like the surface of the earth, equal to rice-stalks, <s>Buddhas</s> who have come like fine particles of dust,

children.text: sūkṣmarajopama ye ca bhavanti sūkṣmarajopama ye tiṣṭhanti //
children.translated_text: those who are like fine dust-particles, and those who abide like fine dust-particles — //

children.text: tāṃśca jinān prakaromi praṇāmaṃ kāyena vācā manasā prasannā /
children.translated_text: to all those <s>Jinas</s> (Victors) I make obeisance, with body, speech, and mind, with serene faith,
with offerings of flowers, offerings of fragrance, with a hundred praises, pure, I remember them. //
Even with a hundred tongues, to speak of the <s>Buddha's</s> virtues, even in hundreds of thousands of <s>kalpas</s> (eons),

children.text: ye ca sunirvṛtasādhujinānāṃ sā ca lalāṭa vicitra anekaiḥ //
children.translated_text: and of those well-liberated noble <s>Jinas</s> — their foreheads are marvelous with many [marks]. //

children.text: ekajinasya guṇān nahi śakyo jihvasahasreṇa bhāṣitu kiṃcit /
children.translated_text: The virtues of even a single <s>Jina</s> cannot be spoken even with a thousand tongues,

children.text: kāmamaśakti hi sarvajinānāṃ ekaguṇasya hi vistaravaktum //
children.translated_text: indeed it is impossible to expound in detail even one virtue of all the <s>Jinas</s>. //
The entire assembly of gods and human families, all the waters of existence filled to the brim,

children.text: ye jalagrahaṇatu śakyapramāṇaṃ naiva tu ekaguṇā sugatāntam //
children.translated_text: even if measurable by grasping all water, not even one virtue [reaches] the end of the <s>Sugatas</s> (Well-Gone Ones). //
All the <s>Jinas</s> have been well-praised and extolled, with body, speech, and this serene mind,

children.text: prameya saṃcita puṇyaphalāgraṃ tena ca sattva prabhotu jinatvam //
children.translated_text: by this immeasurable accumulated merit and its fruit — may beings thereby attain <s>Jinahood</s> (Buddhahood)! //

children.text: eva tu viśvaṃ narapatibuddhaṃ eva karomi nṛpaḥpraṇidhānam /
children.translated_text: Thus to the universal <s>Buddha</s>, lord of men, thus I, a king, make this aspiration:

children.text: yatra ca kutra ci mabhyabhaveta jāti anāgata kalpamanantā //
children.translated_text: wherever and whenever birth may occur for me, in infinite future <s>kalpas</s> — //

children.text: īdṛśabherī paśyami svapne īdṛśanādaṃ tatra śṛṇomi /
children.translated_text: may I see such a drum in my dreams, may I hear such a sound therein,

children.text: īdṛśa jinastuti kamalākareṇa jāti jarāsmara tatra labheyam //
children.translated_text: may I [compose] such praise of the <s>Jinas</s> with a lotus-cluster, and may I attain birth free from aging and death therein! //

children.text: buddhaguṇāni anantamatulyaṃ ye 'pi ca durlabha kalpasahasram /
children.translated_text: The <s>Buddha's</s> virtues are infinite and incomparable, they are rare even in thousands of <s>kalpas</s>,

children.text: anuśruta ye ca svapnagate 'pi teṣu ca deśayi divasagato 'pi //
children.translated_text: those who have heard them even in dreams — to them may [the Dharma] be taught even when the day has passed! //

children.text: duḥkhasamudra vimocayi sattvā pūrayi ṣaḍabhiḥ pāramitābhiḥ /
children.translated_text: May [I] liberate beings from the ocean of suffering, may [I] fulfill the six <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections),
may I obtain supreme <s>bodhi</s> (awakening) through merit, may [I] become a <s>kṣatriya</s> through that radiant aspiration! //
By the fruit and ripening of the gift of a drum, and for the sake of praising all the <s>Jinas</s>,

children.text: saṃmukhapaśyami śākyamunīndraṃ vyākaraṇaṃ hyahu tatra labheyam //
children.translated_text: may I behold <s>Śākyamuni</s>, the lord of sages, face to face, and may I receive a prophecy (<s>vyākaraṇa</s>) there! //

children.text: yau ima dārakadvau mama putrau kanakendra kanakaprabhāśvarau /
children.translated_text: These two boys are my sons, <s>Kanakendra</s> and <s>Kanakaprabha</s>, radiant ones,

children.text: tau ubhi dāraka tatra labheyaṃ bodhimanuttaravyākaraṇaṃ ca //
children.translated_text: may both those boys obtain therein the prophecy of supreme <s>bodhi</s> (awakening)! //

children.text: ye pi ca sattva anekamanantā śaraṇavihīnā vyasanagatāśca /
children.translated_text: And those beings, many and infinite, devoid of refuge, fallen into calamity,
to all of them in the future may I become devoted to protection, a giver of refuge. //
A destroyer of the arising of suffering, and a source of all happiness,

children.text: kalpa anāgata bodhi careyaṃ yattahu pūrvaṃ koṭi gatāśca //
children.translated_text: may I practice <s>bodhi</s> (awakening) in future <s>kalpas</s>, as [I have] in the past through countless millions. //
By the teaching of the <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsottama</s> (Golden Light Sūtra), may the ocean of sin be dried up for me,

children.text: karmasamudra vikīryatu mahyaṃ kleśasamudra vichidyatu mahyam //
children.translated_text: may the ocean of <s>karma</s> be scattered for me, may the ocean of <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) be cut asunder for me! //

children.text: puṇyasamudraṃ pūryatu mahyaṃ jñānasamudra viśodhyatu mahyam /
children.translated_text: May the ocean of merit be filled for me, may the ocean of knowledge be purified for me,

children.text: vimalajñāna prabhāsavareṇa kāma prabhā ca bhaviṣyatu mahyam //
children.translated_text: by the excellence of pure knowledge's radiance, may a radiance of desire [for Dharma] arise for me! //

children.text: puṇyaprabhāsa vilocanatā ca sarvatriloki viśiṣṭa bhaveyam /
children.translated_text: May I have the vision of merit's radiance, may I become preeminent in all three worlds,

children.text: puṇyavareṇa samanvita nityaṃ duḥkhasamudra uttārayitā ca //
children.translated_text: always endowed with excellent merit, and one who ferries [beings] across the ocean of suffering! //

children.text: sarvasukhasya ca sāgarakalpaṃ kalpamanāgata bodhi careyam /
children.translated_text: Like an ocean of all happiness, may I practice <s>bodhi</s> in future <s>kalpas</s>,
with diligence as in the past through countless millions — preeminent in such a field in the three worlds! //
The Praise of All <s>Tathāgatas</s> by <s>Kamalākara</s>, spoken in the <s>Śrī Suvarṇaprabha</s> (Golden Light Sūtra), is complete. //

children.text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 37: Lokanāthastotram
children.translated_text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 37: <s>Lokanāthastotram</s>

children.text: kalpādike bhavasi ko hi mamāgabhāva sarvasvasāra karuṇāmaya viśvamūrte /
children.translated_text: At the beginning of the <s>kalpa</s>, who was the primal being for me? O essence of all, O compassion-filled one, O universal form!

children.text: kāryādike praṇamatīti samantakaṃ tvāṃ śrīlokanātha tava pādayugaṃ name 'ham //
children.translated_text: At the beginning of action, [all] bow to you completely — O <s>Śrī Lokanātha</s>, I bow to your pair of feet! //

children.text: ākṛṣṇakena rajasā vinivartamānaścāyāsi saumya sakalaḥ prativāsare ca /
children.translated_text: Turning away from dark <s>rajas</s> (passion), you come forth, O gentle one, complete, day after day,

children.text: hemasvarūparathakena samujjvalena śrīlokanātha tava pādayugaṃ name 'ham //
children.translated_text: brilliant with a chariot of golden form — O <s>Śrī Lokanātha</s>, I bow to your pair of feet! //

children.text: brahmā tvameva hi sa viprakulaprasiddho viṣṇuśca vaiṣṇavamate varadharmaketuḥ /
children.translated_text: You indeed are <s>Brahmā</s>, renowned among the brahmin families; you are <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the banner of supreme Dharma in the <s>Vaiṣṇava</s> doctrine;

children.text: sarvajñako 'si vimate prabhavo 'vyayaśca śrīlokanātha tava pādayugaṃ name 'ham //
children.translated_text: you are the omniscient one, the imperishable source in the doctrine of non-duality — O <s>Śrī Lokanātha</s>, I bow to your pair of feet! //

children.text: bauddhānvaye bhavasi vajrakasūryarūpo yogeśvaro hi śubhayogakamārgakeṣu /
children.translated_text: In the Buddhist lineage, you are of <s>vajra</s>-sun form, the lord of <s>yoga</s> on the auspicious paths of <s>yoga</s>,

children.text: gaṅgādharo bhavabhayasya vināśakāri śrīlokanātha tava pādayugaṃ name 'ham //
children.translated_text: the bearer of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, the destroyer of the fear of existence — O <s>Śrī Lokanātha</s>, I bow to your pair of feet! //
With a heart of compassion, innately radiant, with the mass of defilements completely severed, an ocean of virtues,

children.text: cintāmaṇistvamasi lokaguruḥ kṛpeśa śrīlokanātha tava pādayugaṃ name 'ham //
children.translated_text: you are the wish-fulfilling gem, the teacher of the world, O lord of mercy — O <s>Śrī Lokanātha</s>, I bow to your pair of feet! //
O one of <s>bandhūka</s>-flower complexion, of many forms, with wide eyes, redeemer of all beings, with beautiful teeth,

children.text: tvaṃ padmapāṇi vimalottama mitrarūpaḥ śrīlokanātha tava pādayugaṃ name 'ham //
children.translated_text: you, O <s>Padmapāṇi</s> (Lotus-Handed), of supreme purity, of friend-like form — O <s>Śrī Lokanātha</s>, I bow to your pair of feet! //
Yet with garrulous devotion, you are praised by me here;
Who is able to speak of your manifold deeds?
a hymn of praise is like a garland of flowers, it is worship through devotion alone. //
whatever impure words [I have used], forgive all of that —
The hymn to the glorious noble lord <s>Āryāvalokiteśvara</s> is complete. //

children.text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 38: Lokātītastavaḥ
children.translated_text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 38: <s>Lokātītastavaḥ</s>
Homage to you who transcend the world, who know the wisdom of solitude,
you who, for the welfare of the world alone, have long been wearied by compassion. //
Since there is no being apart from mere aggregates (<s>skandhas</s>), therefore,
you, O great sage, underwent weariness for the sake of beings. //
Those aggregates too were revealed by you, O wise one, to the wise,
as resembling illusions, mirages, <s>gandharva</s>-cities (castles in the air), and dreams. //

children.text: hetutaḥ saṃbhavo yeṣāṃ tadabhāvānna santi ye /
children.translated_text: Those which arise from causes, and which do not exist in the absence of those [causes] —
how is it not clear that they are like reflections? //
The elements are not graspable by the eye, so how can visible form, which is composed of them, [be real]?
By speaking thus, you have refuted the grasping of form. //
Without something to be felt, feeling (<s>vedanā</s>) does not exist — therefore it is without self;
and that object of feeling too does not exist by its own nature — this is your view. //
If perception (<s>saṃjñā</s>) and its object were non-different, the mouth would be burned by fire;
if different, there would be no apprehension — so you, the speaker of truth, declared. //
The agent is not independent, and action too — this you stated conventionally;
but their establishment through mutual dependence is your accepted view. //

children.text: na kartā 'sti na bhoktā 'sti puṇyāpuṇyaṃ pratītyajam /
children.translated_text: There is no doer, no experiencer; merit and demerit arise dependently —

children.text: yatpratītya na tajjātaṃ proktaṃ vācaspate tvayā //
children.translated_text: what arises dependently is not [truly] born — so you, O lord of speech, declared. //

children.text: ajñāpyamānaṃ na jñeyaṃ vijñānaṃ tadvinā na ca /
children.translated_text: Without being cognized, there is no object of knowledge; without that, there is no consciousness (<s>vijñāna</s>) —

children.text: tasmāt svabhāvato na sto jñānajñeye tvamūcivān //
children.translated_text: therefore, knowledge and the knowable do not exist by their own nature — so you taught. //
If the mark (<s>lakṣaṇa</s>) were other than the marked (<s>lakṣya</s>), then the marked would be without a mark;
and in their non-difference, [both are] absent — this you clearly stated. //
Free from the marked and the mark, beyond the reach of words and expression,
this world is peaceful — so it was seen by you with the eye of wisdom. //

children.text: na sannutpadyate bhāvo nāpyasan sadasanna ca /
children.translated_text: An existent entity does not arise, nor does a non-existent one, nor one both existent and non-existent;

children.text: na svato nāpi parato na dvābhyāṃ jāyate katham //
children.translated_text: not from itself, not from another, not from both — how then is anything born? //
For an existent entity endowed with stability, destruction is not tenable;
for a non-existent one, equal to the horn of a horse — how can there be equality [with destruction]? //
Destruction is not considered to be something other than the entity, nor is it considered non-different;
if different, [the entity] would be eternal; and if non-different, it would [also] not exist. //
In oneness, the destruction of an entity is not tenable;
in separateness, the destruction of an entity is [also] not tenable. //
From a destroyed cause, the arising of an effect is not logical;
nor from an undestroyed one — arising is considered by you as equal to a dream. //
Whether from a ceased or an unceased seed, the sprout arises —
all arising is declared by you to be like the production of an illusion. //
Therefore, this world is known by you to have arisen from conceptual construction (<s>parikalpana</s>),
understood as unreal, unborn, and not subject to destruction. //
For the permanent, there is no <s>saṃsāra</s> (cycle of rebirth); nor is there <s>saṃsāra</s> for the impermanent;
<s>saṃsāra</s> is like a dream — so you, O best among knowers of reality, declared. //
Self-made, other-made, made by both, or causeless —
suffering is thus conceived by logicians; but you declared it to be dependently arisen. //

children.text: yaḥ pratītyasamutpādaḥ śūnyatā saiva te matā /
children.translated_text: That which is dependent origination (<s>pratītyasamutpāda</s>) — that itself is emptiness (<s>śūnyatā</s>), according to you;
there is no independent entity — this is your incomparable lion's roar. //
The nectar-teaching of <s>śūnyatā</s> was given for the abandonment of all conceptual constructions;
but one who grasps even at that [emptiness] — such a one was censured by you. //
Effortless, free, empty, arising from conditions like illusions —
all <s>dharmas</s> (phenomena) have been revealed by you, O Lord, as without inherent nature (<s>niḥsvabhāva</s>). //
Nothing whatsoever was produced by you, nor was anything whatsoever ceased;

children.text: yathā pūrvaṃ tathā paścāt tathatāṃ buddhavānasi //
children.translated_text: <s>Tathatā</s> (Suchness), as it was before so it is after — thus you, O <s>Buddha</s>, understood. //
Without resorting to this meditation cultivated by the noble ones,
the knowledge of the signless does not somehow arise here. //
Without attaining the signless, there is no liberation — so you declared;
therefore, in the <s>Mahāyāna</s> (Great Vehicle), that was shown by you in its entirety. //

children.text: yadavāptaṃ mayā puṇyaṃ stutvā tvāṃ stutibhājanam /
children.translated_text: Whatever merit has been obtained by me through praising you, who are worthy of praise,
may the entire world thereby become free from the bondage of signs! //
The glorious <s>Lokātītastava</s> (Hymn to the World-Transcendent One) is complete. //

children.text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 39: Lokeśvaraśatakam vajradattācāryaviracitam
children.translated_text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 39: <s>Lokeśvaraśatakam</s> composed by <s>Vajradatta Ācārya</s>
<s>Oṃ</s>! Homage to <s>Lokanātha</s> (Lord of the World)!
upon the lotus-seated head bowed with devotion, resembling a garland of smiling <s>mālatī</s> flowers,
Radiant as a blazing ruby on the crown, upon the bowing supreme head of <s>Indra</s>, lord of the sky,
may the radiances of the pure toenails of <s>Lokeśa's</s> (Lord of the World's) feet, beautiful as the moon, bring peace to the world! //
upon the crest of <s>Śambhu</s> (Śiva), dispelling the slightly tawny hue of the closing crescent moon —
nor gently by the ruby-splendors of <s>Hari's</s> (Viṣṇu's) crown,
Not shaken off from the lord <s>Dhūrjaṭi</s> (Śiva) by the sharp, tawny, unattached rays of his matted locks,
may the irresistible radiances of <s>Lokeśvara's</s> (Lord of the World's) toenails bring you the pacification of darkness! //
nor dissolved by the darkness, nor hidden among the hair-rows on the foreheads of the host of gods —
removing the fear and dread of dire affliction from those separated from their loved ones —
the cause of the attainment of the full, expansive enjoyment of the blossoming lotus of abundant, excellent treasure,
may the unprecedented moonlight of the cool-rayed toenails of <s>Lokeśa's</s> feet purify you! //
the fear born of terrible planetary seizures is not pacified even by the hurling of attacks —
their playful glances dispel the dense, binding darkness of delusion throughout the three worlds —
The lofty flames of the great fire that burns the fuel of the entire mass of <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) —
may the radiances of the toenails, born from the feet of the lotus-bearer, destroy <s>saṃsāra</s>! //
unfailing upon the columns of fire, they are streams of wide-spreading nectar-water in the realm of hell —
the mind-captivating necklace-splendors that pacify the arising of dread and fear of deep affliction,
Of those incomprehensible wish-fulfilling gems (<s>cintāmaṇi</s>), skilled in granting desires that cut freely at will,
may the shadow of the rays of the toenails, born from <s>Lokeśvara's</s> feet, protect you! //
the mirror-surfaces bearing clearly manifested multitudes of various virtues —
may that assemblage of the brilliantly shining toenail-radiances of his feet long exalt you!
Of the lord, the blazing, supremely brilliant radiances, shining with immeasurable luster, resplendent at the crest —
adorned with the rainbow-like display of the scattered brilliant radiances of various luminaries! //
May it be supremely elevated, with the beautiful jewel-heaps on the bowing heads of gods skilled in its worship,
unsurpassed in granting the attainment of desired objects through the elevation of glorious enjoyments —
Generating delight on all sides for the devoted ones, whose radiance is unwavering,

children.text: toṣaṃ māṇikyadīpā iva dadatu nakhāḥ padmapāṇeḥ padorvaḥ //
children.translated_text: may the toenails of <s>Padmapāṇi's</s> (Lotus-Handed One's) feet, like lamps of ruby, grant you satisfaction! //
mocking the moon with their peerlessly pure surface, destroying the faults of darkness —

children.text: udbhedo bhedako 'sau bhavatu bhavabhiyāṃ nirbharāṇāṃ bharaṃ vaḥ /
children.translated_text: may that effulgence, the breaker, become the support of those filled with fear of existence (<s>bhava</s>)!
Of the radiances of the toenails born from the lotus-feet of the king who bears the lotus,
abundant, like a cluster of sprouts of wish-fulfilling trees, having received the seed of knowledge. //
Born from the ground of his body, rendered beneficial by the water of unceasing compassion,
splendid as the rays of unfailing arrows placed at the mouths of crimson quivers,
The toenail-radiances born from <s>Lokeśa's</s> lotus-feet, which strike terror into the armies of <s>Māra</s>'s enemies,
may they cause you to ascend to the supreme station of great, hard-to-attain wealth! //
ropes ever ready for the rescue of beings fallen into the terrible pit of <s>saṃsāra</s>,
keen-witted, weighty stars for people, perceiving faults from afar —
Radiant, heroic in severing the suffering of the world overpowered by the toil of <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) and <s>karma</s>,
may those inconceivable, worry-dispelling toenails of <s>Kamalakara</s> (Lotus-Handed), born from his feet, be victorious! //
bestowing dense bliss, bearing the beauty of the full moon, free from blemish —

children.text: nyastā ratnāvalī vā kimu niratiśayotkaṇṭhayā bodhilakṣmyā /
children.translated_text: Or was a garland of gems placed there by <s>Bodhilakṣmī</s> (the Fortune of Awakening) with unsurpassed longing?
Was this arrangement made by <s>Śambhu</s> (Śiva) with fragments of the brilliant crescent moon?
May the row of toenails, born from <s>Lokanātha's</s> feet, which generates such wonder, delight you! //
Or is it perhaps a garland of incomparable divine flowers suspended by the gods? —
And where is the prostration with head touching the surface of the earth?
Where is this one, born of the lotus, whose foot-dust sleeps forever on the lofty ruby bed of the bowing heads of immortals? —

children.text: itthaṃ saṃjātahāsā iva rucinicayairdanturā ye durantā

children.translated_text: may those toenails, born from <s>Lokeśvara's</s> feet, be yours for the destruction of darkness! //
Those that seem to have burst into laughter with their masses of radiance, tusked and boundless —
ramparts against the assault of <s>Māra</s>, the cruel one who shoots dreadful, far-reaching arrows,
Heroic in removing torment, causing showers of the coolest nectar-spray,

children.text: ghoraṃ vaḥ saṃharantāṃ caraṇanakharucaḥ śrīkarāḥ padmapāṇeḥ //
children.translated_text: may the auspicious toenail-radiances of <s>Padmapāṇi's</s> feet destroy them for you! //
the terrible varieties of vast, fierce suffering in the prison-house of <s>saṃsāra</s> —
like a curtain blocking the inescapable, all-pervading arrows released by <s>Māra</s> —
The radiances of the toenails born from <s>Lokeśa's</s> feet, creating confusion
triumph as great victory-banners conquering the three worlds, invincible in the three realms of existence! //
resembling a great constellation of banners clearly signaling the destruction of the host of afflictions (<s>saṃkleśa</s>),
like the great wind of the path of liberation that has burned away the mass of affliction-ashes,
Like the assemblage of radiances shining forth from the moon of the mind of perfect awakening (<s>samyaksaṃbodhi</s>),
may the cluster of toenail-radiances born from the feet of <s>Padmapāṇi</s>, thus contemplated, protect you! //
like a slab of cloud-white crystal placed in view, unbreakable by the cruel <s>Māras</s> —
of the lord whose unworn side has no defect of injury, spotless and imperishable —
Gazed upon with abashment, skilled in dispelling the unequaled darkness in an instant, of the night-makers (moons),
may the toenails of <s>Lokeśvara's</s> feet, a protection, protect you without a moment's delay! //
whose vow of protecting the world is unbroken, skilled in destroying the undiminished enemy host,
seeking to conquer the glory of the three worlds — may the incomparable rising be yours!
Of the mass of toenail-radiances, whose stronghold is the foot of the supreme lotus-bearer, the means of attaining true wealth,
may it protect — the cause of the accomplishment of the great vehicle (<s>Mahāyāna</s>) against the enemy of all calamities and dangers! //
Of that which has attained supreme growth, supported by a friend whose rise is manifest,
the desire for <s>Śauri's</s> (Viṣṇu's) beauty somehow fades through the accomplished <s>Kaustubha</s> gem,
Without shame, <s>Paśupati</s> (Śiva) wears on his crest the half-moon ornament that <s>Kāma</s> destroyed,
may that cluster of toenails of <s>Padmapāṇi</s>, whose luster is thus contemplated by the world, be victorious! //
and upon seeing this, even the great crown-jewel of <s>Maghavat</s> (Indra) is rendered futile — so people of discernment think:
rising with frost-like radiance, pure, the cause of darkening the faces of enemies,
Rising high, spread far above, a star for those in the hells below,
may the mass of toenail-rays, depending on the lotus-feet, of the Buddha-crowned one protect you! //
of inconceivable power, manifesting extremely clear vision to the entire world —
shining forth, the ground bewildered by the ashes of <s>Hara's</s> (Śiva's) matted locks bowing with the weight of devotion,
Seen, with the camphor-dust released by the beautiful brides of the delighted lord of gods, skilled in worship,
may the spreading mass of toenail-rays, born from the feet of <s>Padmahasta</s> (Lotus-Handed), protect you from calamity! //
fine as the pollen from the tips of stamens falling from the lotus-hands of <s>Lakṣmī</s> scattered in worship,
a hero extinguishing the crimson glory, robbing the diminished green luster of <s>Hari's</s> (Viṣṇu's) horses,
On <s>Meru</s>, having absorbed the yellow luster, the extensive vermilion-dust of the celestial elephant —
beheld by the trembling divine brides at the swelling of the milk-ocean, protect you! //
with closing blue radiance — may the spreading toenail-luster from <s>Padmabhṛt's</s> (Lotus-Bearer's) lotus-feet,

children.text: bhaktyārambheṇa rambhe parikirasi mudhā kiṃ nu karpūradhūlīḥ /
children.translated_text: 'O <s>Rambhā</s>, do you vainly scatter camphor-dust in the beginning of devotion?'
'Is beauty to be achieved in this one with moon-white yak-tail fans?'

children.text: kiṃ te puṣpaiḥ prakīrṇaiḥ śaciśucibhiriti svāminā svarbhuvāṃ vaḥ

children.translated_text: described the cluster of toenail-radiances born from <s>Abjapāṇi's</s> (Lotus-Handed's) feet — may it protect you! //
'What use are flowers strewn by you, pure as <s>Śacī</s>?' — thus at the worship, the lord of gods
the playful grace of beauty smeared, the whitened ray of <s>Pūṣan's</s> horse with its green hue removed —
Upon <s>Kailāsa</s>-bright <s>Vindhya</s>, in the blackness of the body of <s>Bali's</s> conqueror swallowed up,
may the moon, on the pretext of a basin heaped by the gods skilled in worship, protect you! //
'What is this to me!' — as if crumbled, the vast rays of the toenails of <s>Lokeśa's</s> feet —
constructed as a great bridge for crossing to the far shore of the ocean of <s>saṃsāra</s>,
The feet, born from the feet of the Buddha-crowned one, of the toenails bearing vast extension,

children.text: svacchandācchacchaṭābhā jhaṭiti vighaṭanaṃ kurvatāṃ vo bhavasya //
children.translated_text: with radiances transparent and cloud-white, freely flowing, may they swiftly bring about the destruction of your existence (<s>bhava</s>)! //
water of the great accumulation of merit that extinguishes the rising, unstoppable fire of suffering —
a mocking laughter at the radiances, a defeat also of the whiteness of the Himalaya-hued one,
A surpassing of the beauty of the dark-hued moon, excelling the abundant <s>Kailāsa</s> mountain —
may the expanse of toenail-radiances of <s>Lokeśvara's</s> feet protect you! //
a flooding even of the milk-ocean's fullness, a shattering even of the shadow of the celestial elephant's tusks
where the self-born one (<s>Brahmā</s>), devoted to service, stood uneasy upon the closing lotus,
Where the <s>Pārijāta</s> of his worship causes the swarm of bees to coil, while the lotus of <s>Śrī</s> closes,
may that foot of <s>Padmapāṇi</s>, with the moonlight of its toenail-moons playing, protect you! //
by which the beauty of day became undimmed, and the night became free from the fault of wearying the divine brides —
bearing bright beauty, like a cluster of lotus stalks, with splendor born from the glow of the toenails,
Beautiful, worshipped with glances by the hosts of bewildered, lovely immortal maidens,
may the foot of <s>Padmapāṇi</s>, anointed with abundant sandal-paste from the city of the gods, protect you! //
engaged in manifold wanderings, overpowered by the spread of abundant desire, like a lover —
when the swarm of bees shines forth as if upon a terrible mass of <s>Kālakūṭa</s> poison of <s>Kālīya</s> —
When the <s>Pārijāta</s> is scattered by the hands of the gods, glittering with the radiance of abundant bliss,
of <s>Padmapāṇi's</s> lotus-feet, the cause of unfailing joy, bestow auspiciousness upon you! //
may the <s>Śrī</s> (Fortune) arising from the midst of the milk-ocean of the radiance of the pure, spotless toenails
whose beauty is veiled by bees deceived by the resemblance to lotus-luster,
Towering like a flame of fire cutting through the sorrow of the interruption of desires,
may the foot, whose hand-luster is sprinkled with lotus-beauty, grant you the fulfillment of wishes without hardship! //
not trivial, with freely swelling clusters of pure toenail-rays, unfading —
bearing a multitude of auspicious marks brought about by countless, incomparable merits of virtues,
With a radiance of the <s>cakra</s> (wheel) that has arisen and shines, with pure toenails of unequaled, risen splendor,
may the foot, the sovereign of the world whose lords bow to it, long protect you! //
of the Buddha-crowned one, whose sovereignty extends over all the islands and continents, immeasurably great —
What use is song itself, when rows of bees wander in confusion on the blooming lotus?
'What virtue is there in these buds of golden lotuses scattered from the celestial Ganges?

children.text: yatpūjāyāṃ sureśaḥ sa jayati caraṇo vārijavyagrapāṇeḥ //
children.translated_text: the lord of gods at the worship — may that victorious foot of the one with lotus in hand prevail! //
Can beauty be enhanced by a string of rubies on this toenail of unmatched radiance?' — thus spoke

children.text: yo nāthasyaiva nāsīdapi khalu sugateḥ kāraṇaṃ janmabhājāṃ
yasmin padmābhilāṣī na madhupanivahaḥ pakṣapātī jano 'pi /
children.translated_text: In whom the swarm of bees desiring the lotus does not take sides, nor does the partisan one —
He who was not even the Lord's, yet was indeed the cause of the birth of those born, O <s>Sugata</s> (Well-Gone One)!
may that foot of the one whose crown is illumined by the moonlight of the <s>Sugata</s> protect the world! //
by whom the earth, not too heavy, and the three worlds, bowed by that most weighty bow, were sustained —
in whom the stalk is not diminished, and greenness is in no way lacking, the basis of supreme beauty —
He who, by giving drink to the bees, created an assembly of attendants held in delight,
the abode of <s>Śrī</s> (Fortune), whose stamens laugh with the rays of the toenails, bestow auspiciousness upon you! //
may that foot-lotus of the lord of the world, whose dust rests forever on the heads of immortals,
for the invocation of <s>siddhi</s> (attainment), alas! The delight of the great expanding glory —
The weapon of fierce hostility against the body, aimed at embodied beings, the desire
may the effulgence born from the feet of <s>Padmahasta</s> (Lotus-Handed), removing [all that], be a stream of many benefits! //
the burning fire of suffering arrayed by hostility against the host of <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions), the oblation offered —

children.text: vācālā nirvicārā racayatu caraṇotsarpiṇī saṃpadaṃ vaḥ /
children.translated_text: voluble, free from doubt — may the radiance rising from his feet create prosperity for you!
Born from the foot of the Buddha-ornamented-crowned one, a garland of bees carrying the illusion of a perfect lotus,
placed like a chain of thick black iron, by abundant compassion. //
Solely devoted to the protection of beings, for the purpose of establishing a firmer, more enduring abiding,
the ground for shattering the host of weapons hurled by the enraged enemy,
Beautiful with the succession of inner petals of the lotus, soft, yet with the essence of <s>vajra</s> (diamond), expansive,

indivisible, of unfathomable extent, like a thunderbolt of great enterprise, both moving and unmoving;

of the calamity of the <s>tīrthikas</s> (heterodox teachers) — may that instructive teaching of the Lord destroy existence for you! //

the treasury of splendor, the ornament of ornaments that has beautified the entire world —
struck down by the most restless waves of thirst in that ocean of beauty —
The pride of [other] forms is withered in the world, [while his form] attains fruitfulness through the eyes of the meritorious;
if even this one face surpasses [them all] — victorious be that face of <s>Padmapāṇi</s> (Lotus-Handed)! //
I think that even by countless [beings] like the moon and others, of incomparable loveliness,
have repeatedly become burning and clearly afflicting for embodied beings;
In whom, for those harboring hatred, the unceasing clouds flooding with streams of beauty-water
may that summit of the <s>Buddha's</s> abode, [his] face of most wondrous deeds, be exceedingly bliss-giving for you! //
washed clean, with attachments destroyed, the series of stains of abundant impure soot-smears —
with a distinct, embracing, brilliant canopy of the pinkish radiance of <s>Amitābha's</s> splendor,
Of the one with a beloved lotus in his unafflicted hand, seated within the clearly visible, formidable chamber's pavement,
may [that] be armor for you against the harsh affliction of the hostile friend of the deceitful mass of matted locks! //
with a dense mass of bonds of splendid, imposing grandeur, an unseen dense assemblage above —
surpassingly beautiful with peerless purity,
Having gained growth through the sprinkling of the abundant waters of <s>Amitābha's</s> radiance, spread unceasingly for the cause of supreme delight,
may the cluster of creeper-like matted locks of the lotus-bearer be for your prosperity! //
worshipped with heaps of divine, wonderfully fragrant blossoms, [granting] the attainment of wished-for goals —

children.text: niḥsāmānyāṃ vibhūṣāṃ janayati vapuṣā yāsu nātho 'mitābhaḥ /
children.translated_text: producing an incomparable ornament with his body;
Being bound to which, one attains certain liberation; in which the lord <s>Amitābha</s> has his unequalled dwelling,
may those exceedingly formidable matted locks of <s>Lokeśa</s> take away from you the inevitably obtained death! //
which cut off all fragrance, [yet are] smeared with the incomparable fragrance of <s>āmoda</s> (delight), pervading all directions —
nor is [its] beauty a flood of nectar that revives the world tormented by the fire of suffering;
The mass of matted locks is not a heap of snares for binding the minds of all people,

children.text: pratyāśā poṣasiddhiṃ diśatu jinaśaśiśleṣikeśaḥ śriyo vaḥ //
children.translated_text: may the one whose locks embrace the <s>Jina</s>-moon grant you the fulfillment of expectations, prosperity and fortune! //
nor is the lotus [merely] a means of stealing away the <s>kleśa</s>-faults, the whip of the subduing horse of death for the wicked —
like the fire of cosmic destruction, delighting in the rapid devouring of the frightened, unprotected three worlds,
With the unbounded spread of tawny radiance creating bewilderment of burning in all directions,
may that gaze of <s>Lokeśvarī</s> (the Goddess of the World), momentarily overwhelmed by incomparable compassion, protect you! //
biting the lip, with an angry gaze blazing, with a neck [taut] like an untamed horse's, bound with fortune —
being pulverized, even the infinite oceans are drying up;
The world is clearly headed to destruction; today, swiftly, all the great mountains are
the lotus-holder, with incomparable arm-strength, trembled — may he be victorious! //
thus, seeing the goddess emerging from the terrible forehead [furrowed] with the weight of frowning brows born of the wrath of the Destroyer —

children.text: stutyaiḥ stutyā gurūṇāmapi jagati gururvanditā vandanīyair

children.translated_text: in body endowed with the genuine power to protect all worlds, gained through countless <s>kalpas</s> (eons),
Praised by those worthy of praise, the teacher even of teachers in the world, worshipped by the worshipful,
may <s>Tārā</s>, who carries away the heavy, brilliant cause [of suffering] from the prison of <s>saṃsāra</s>, [protect] you! //
she who cuts the world's suffering, who emerged from the lotus-born one herself through incomparable compassion —
unfathomed even by the most profound and clearly flowing, swan-like, mighty [words],
Sung by the host of gods, of virtues worthy of weighty reckoning, [yet] to be grasped [only] by the foremost words of <s>Bṛhaspati</s> (Lord of Speech),
