may the flood of virtues of the lotus-born one, fully comprehensible [only] through the words of the <s>Sugata</s>, protect you! //
uttered by deep-sounding voices — the sung praises receive but a small portion of [his] declared greatness;
May I be a poet in birth after birth, devoted to the feet of <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>,
of supreme intellect, refuge by nature, charged with the weighty task of benefiting others. //
The <s>Śrī Lokeśvaraśatakam</s> (Century of Verses on the Lord of the World), composed by the poet <s>Śrī Vajradatta</s>, the great <s>kṣapaṭalika</s>, is complete. //

children.text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 40: Lokeśvarastotram
children.translated_text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 40: <s>Lokeśvarastotram</s>

I worship <s>Śrī Lokanātha</s>, the wise one, bestower of auspiciousness — of many forms, virtuous, the refuge of the world, who inevitably [conquers] with the qualities of <s>Lokeśa</s>, <s>Keśava</s>, <s>Hara</s>, and the Self,
who crosses the ocean of <s>saṃsāra</s>, with lotus-wide eyes. //
I worship <s>Śrī Lokanātha</s>, the wise one, bestower of auspiciousness — the giver of protection to all frightened people, with a beautiful face, with ears adorned by golden earrings,
resplendent with ornaments of necklaces and jewels. //

children.text: bhaktyā natasya manujasya vipadvirāmaṃ svargāpavargaphaladaṃ varadaṃ dayālum /
children.translated_text: I worship <s>Śrī Lokanātha</s>, the wise one, bestower of auspiciousness — who brings the cessation of calamities for the person who bows with devotion, who bestows the fruits of heaven and liberation, the boon-granter, the compassionate one,
the god of gods, the immortal, endowed with the <s>Jina</s>-assembly. //

I worship <s>Śrī Lokanātha</s>, the wise one, bestower of auspiciousness — with a <s>tilaka</s> (mark) of refined gold, the ornament of the gods, a mine of jewels, with a hand beautiful with a golden spear,
radiant, who shows the direction of wearing ornaments. //
I worship <s>Śrī Lokanātha</s>, the wise one, bestower of auspiciousness — the remover of foul destinies, the dispeller of misdeeds, the destroyer of famine, the mine of compassion,

children.text: vidyāpradaṃ guṇanidhiṃ śubhaśuddhadehaṃ śrīlokanāthavibudhaṃ śubhadaṃ bhajāmi //
children.translated_text: the bestower of knowledge, the treasure of virtues, of auspicious and pure body. //
I worship <s>Śrī Lokanātha</s>, the wise one, bestower of auspiciousness — thus the best, the lord of all beings, the lord of the three worlds, worshipped even by the immortals,

children.text: evaṃ kvacid rathavare sukhasaṃpraviṣṭaṃ śrīlokanāthavibudhaṃ śubhadaṃ bhajāmi //
children.translated_text: thus comfortably seated upon the finest chariot. //
I worship <s>Śrī Lokanātha</s>, the wise one, bestower of auspiciousness — bowed to in reverence for universal benefit by <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, humans, sages, <s>nāgas</s>,

children.text: sarvopakāranamitaṃ puṭitā grahastaiḥ śrīlokanāthavibudhaṃ śubhadaṃ bhajāmi //
children.translated_text: <s>vidyādharas</s>, hosts of gods, <s>dānavas</s> (demons), and <s>piśācas</s> (flesh-eating spirits), with palms joined by householders. //
I worship <s>Śrī Lokanātha</s>, the wise one, bestower of auspiciousness — anointed with sandalwood paste and musk,
with limbs beautifully adorned by the application of camphor, saffron, fine <s>haricandana</s> (yellow sandalwood). //

I worship <s>Śrī Lokanātha</s>, the wise one, bestower of auspiciousness — whose auspicious name destroys diseases for devotees, who removes grief and suffering, who is to be contemplated for happiness,
whose words are like nectar, whose body is soft and beautiful. //

I worship <s>Śrī Lokanātha</s>, the wise one, bestower of auspiciousness — with hands reaching to the knees, with the gait of a lordly elephant, with a peak like a pool of beauty, with teeth [clear] as crystal,
of exceedingly beautiful body, with limbs bearing auspicious marks. //

children.text: ye lokanāthasya sadā surabhyaṃ stotraṃ paṭhiṣyanti janā sabhāvāḥ /
children.translated_text: Those people of noble character who always recite this fragrant hymn to <s>Lokanātha</s>,
<s>Śrī Lokanātha</s> himself swiftly grants their desired aims, grasping [them] with his own hands. //
The <s>Śrī Lokeśvarastotram</s> (Hymn to the Lord of the World) is complete. //

children.text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 41: Madhyamakaśāstrastutiḥ ācārya-candrakīrtikṛtā
children.translated_text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 41: <s>Madhyamakaśāstrastutiḥ</s>, composed by Ācārya <s>Candrakīrti</s>
skillful in following the conduct of the people, based upon the two truths —
The teaching that was proclaimed by the <s>Buddhas</s> here in nine forms beginning with <s>sūtras</s>,

children.text: tasmin rāganirākṛtau nahi kathā dveṣakṣaye jāyate
dveṣasyāpi nirākṛtau nahi kathā rāgakṣaye jāyate //
children.translated_text: even in the refutation of hatred, the discourse on the destruction of passion does not arise. //
in that [teaching], there is no talk of the removal of passion, nor does the cessation of hatred arise

children.text: mānāderapi yat kṣayāya vacanaṃ nānyaṃ malaṃ hanti tat
tasmādvayāpitaraṃ na tatra ca punastāstā mahārthāḥ kathāḥ /
children.translated_text: therefore, the discourses of great import do not extend further beyond that.
That which is spoken for the destruction of pride and the like does not destroy other defilements;

children.text: mā mohasya parikṣayāya tu kathā kleśānaśeṣānasau

children.translated_text: that destroys all <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) without remainder, for all afflictions are rooted in delusion, so the <s>Jinas</s> (Victors) have declared. //
But the discourse for the complete destruction of delusion —

children.text: mohasyāsya parikṣayāya ca yato dṛṣṭāḥ pratītyādaya
stattvaṃ tat pratipacca saiva sugataiḥ saṃkīrtitā madhyamā /
children.translated_text: that very truth, having been realized, was proclaimed by the <s>Sugatas</s> (Well-Gone Ones) as the <s>Madhyamā</s> (Middle Way).
Because for the complete destruction of this delusion, dependent origination and the like were taught —

children.text: kāyo dharmamayo muneḥ sa ca yataḥ sā śūnyatetyucyate
buddhānāṃ hṛdayaṃ sa cāpi mahatī vidyeti saṃkīrtyate //
children.translated_text: it is proclaimed as the heart of the <s>Buddhas</s>, and also as the great <s>Vidyā</s> (Knowledge). //
Since the body of the Sage is made of <s>Dharma</s>, that [Middle Way] is called <s>Śūnyatā</s> (Emptiness);
is described at greater length, in its primary form, in the treatise called <s>Madhyamaka</s>.
Since this [teaching] is proclaimed by the <s>Buddhas</s> as the source of all virtues, that discourse
it was set forth with care by <s>Nāgārjuna</s>, that wise son of the <s>Buddhas</s>. //
With a mind melted by compassion, having understood the teaching as it truly is,

children.text: gambhīraṃ jinaśāsanaṃ na hi jano yo vetti tatsaṃvide
maunīndrād vacasaḥ pṛthaṅnigadituṃ vāñchanti tattvaṃ ca ye /
children.translated_text: those who wish to explain the truth separately from the words of the Lord of Sages,
The profound teaching of the <s>Jina</s> (Victor) — the person who does not understand it — to communicate that understanding,

children.text: anye ye 'pi kubuddhayaḥ pravacanaṃ vyācakṣate cānyathā
teṣāṃ cāpi nirākṛtau kṛtamidaṃ śāstraṃ hatāntardvayam //
children.translated_text: for the refutation of those [views] also, this treatise was composed, destroying both [errors] within. //
and others of false understanding who explain the teaching wrongly —
with words followed even by <s>Deva</s> (Āryadeva), taught for a long time.
Clearly, <s>Nāgārjuna</s>, accompanied by <s>Rāhulabhadra</s>, upholding that doctrine,
they too upheld the teaching of the best of sages for a long time. //
His disciples, with minds established through the discernment of those treatises, having conquered all the heretics,

children.text: āyātāya śiro 'rthiṃne karuṇayā protkṛtya dattvā śiraḥ
saṃyāte tu sukhāvatīṃ jinasute nāgārjune tatkṛtāḥ /
children.translated_text: when the son of the <s>Jina</s>, <s>Nāgārjuna</s>, departed to <s>Sukhāvatī</s> (the Pure Land),
Having compassionately cut off and given his head to the one who came seeking it,

children.text: granthāḥ śiṣyagaṇāśca te 'pi bahunā kālena nāśaṃ gatāḥ
tattvārke 'stamite 'dhunā na hi mataṃ spaṣṭaṃ tadasti kvacit //
children.translated_text: now that the sun of truth has set, that doctrine is clearly no longer found anywhere. //
the treatises he composed and the communities of disciples also perished over a long time;
far gone from the true path, deranged,
In a world now mostly intoxicated, having drunk the wine of logic, skilled only in fabricated meanings,

children.text: dhanyo 'sau kṣaṇamapyapāsya vimatiṃ yaḥ śūnyatāṃ gāhate //
children.translated_text: blessed is that person who, even for a moment, setting aside doubt, plunges into <s>Śūnyatā</s> (Emptiness)! //
in a Buddhist doctrine confused, devoid of the realization of truth proclaimed by the Omniscient One —

children.text: ścittvotplutya ca yāti vastuparikhāṃ caiko mṛgo 'sau mahān /
children.translated_text: the one great deer who, cutting through and leaping, crosses the moat of [real] entities —
Bound by the snares of treatises constructed out of fear of commitment to [real] entities,

children.text: taṃ pratyadya na cintayā mama guṇaścaikastu yo nādhunā
taṃ pratyeva tadanyaśāstramathanī vṛttiḥ kṛteyaṃ mayā //
children.translated_text: with regard to that, this commentary, a crusher of other treatises, was composed by me. //
with regard to that one, I have no concern now; but the one quality that does not exist now —
and having diligently practiced the verses spoken in the treatises for a very long time,
Having studied the <s>Sūtrasamuccaya</s>, the <s>Parikathā</s>, the <s>Ratnāvalī</s>, the <s>Saṃstutis</s> (Hymns of Praise),

children.text: yā cāsāvatha vigrahasya racitā vyāvartinī tāmapi //
children.translated_text: and that which was composed as a refutation of disputes (<s>Vigrahavyāvartanī</s>) — those too. //
the <s>Yuktyākhyā</s> (Yuktiṣaṣṭikā — Sixty Stanzas on Reasoning), the <s>Śūnyatāsaptati</s> (Seventy Stanzas on Emptiness) with its supplement,

children.text: dṛṣṭvā tacchatakādikaṃ bahuvidhaṃ sūtraṃ gabhīraṃ tathā
vṛttiṃ cāpyatha buddhapālitakṛtāṃ sūkṣmāṃ ca yadbhāvinā /
children.translated_text: and also the commentary composed by <s>Buddhapālita</s>, and the subtle one by <s>Bhāviveka</s>,
Having studied those <s>Śataka</s> (Catuhśataka) and others, as well as the various profound <s>sūtras</s>,
having condensed all that, this is presented for the satisfaction of those of elevated minds. //
and that which was obtained by me through investigation from the tradition handed down —
the meanings present here, clear and unconfused, for those of keen intelligence,
This orb of reflection, crusher of [false] reasoning, directly illuminating with rays of speech
having risen for the worlds, destroys false views together with dense darkness. //
and producing this most lucid commentary — the illustrious <s>Candra</s> (Candrakīrti) now,
relying on reasoning and scripture for establishing certainty among the faithful and wise —
Having composed this commentary with clear words, a proper method, with care,

children.text: yatpuṇyaṃ mama śūnyateva vipulaṃ tenaiva loko 'khila

children.translated_text: abandoning the host of [wrong] views, proceed to the path that cuts through all conceptual proliferation! //
whatever merit is mine, vast as <s>Śūnyatā</s> (Emptiness) itself, by that alone may the entire world,

children.text: sambuddhān sakalaṃ jinātmajagaṇaṃ dharmaṃ ca tairbhāṣitam /
children.translated_text: to the entire assembly of sons of the <s>Jina</s>, and to the <s>Dharma</s> spoken by them,
Having bowed to <s>Gautama</s>, the Teacher, and to those <s>Sambuddhas</s> (Fully Awakened Ones) established in his <s>Dharmatā</s> (true nature),

children.text: yo 'muṃ madhyamakaṃ cakāra kṛpayā nāgārjunastaṃ name //
children.translated_text: to <s>Nāgārjuna</s>, who composed this <s>Madhyamaka</s> out of compassion, I bow! //
he who became the eye of beings for perceiving the infinite word of the <s>Buddha</s> —
The glorious <s>Madhyamaka-śāstra-stuti</s> (Praise of the Madhyamaka Treatise) composed by <s>Candrakīrti</s> is complete. //

children.text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 42: Mahābodhibhaṭṭārakastotram
children.translated_text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 42: <s>Mahābodhibhaṭṭārakastotram</s>
<s>Oṃ</s>! Homage to <s>Śākyasiṃha</s>!

children.text: siddhaṃ prasiddhaṃ vijitāmaraṃ ca śāntaṃ virāgaṃ suviśuddhaśīlam /
children.translated_text: Accomplished, well-accomplished, conqueror of the immortals, peaceful, free from passion, of supremely pure conduct,

children.text: viśveśvaraṃ sarvaguṇākaraṃ vai śrīśākyasiṃhaṃ praṇamāmi nityam //
children.translated_text: lord of the universe, source of all virtues — to <s>Śrī Śākyasiṃha</s> I bow always! //
With a head like an umbrella-canopy, with excellent dark-blue hair, with a forehead beautifully adorned with the <s>ūrṇā</s> (auspicious mark),

children.text: nīlotpalābhaṃ nayanaṃ viśālaṃ śrīśākyasiṃhaṃ praṇamāmi nityam //
children.translated_text: with wide eyes resembling blue lotuses — to <s>Śrī Śākyasiṃha</s> I bow always! //
With a prominent nose, full and weighty cheeks, lips like <s>bimba</s> fruit, and the chest of a lion-king,
with a golden complexion like heated gold — to <s>Śrī Śākyasiṃha</s> I bow always! //
With a treasury-like chest, with beautiful ears adorned, with three lines on the neck, wearing a fine garment,
with arms reaching to the knees, with a nose like an elephant's trunk — to <s>Śrī Śākyasiṃha</s> I bow always! //
Honored by men with various flowers, endowed with auspicious pairs of <s>śrīvatsa</s> marks,
with a body adorned with eighty minor marks — to <s>Śrī Śākyasiṃha</s> I bow always! //
The foremost Teacher, the hero among heroes of men, the son of <s>Māyā</s>, the compassionate one, the lord of <s>Jinas</s>,

children.text: śauddhodaniṃ lokavidaṃ munīndraṃ śrīśākyasiṃhaṃ praṇamāmi nityam //
children.translated_text: the descendant of <s>Śuddhodana</s>, the knower of the world, the lord of sages — to <s>Śrī Śākyasiṃha</s> I bow always! //
With wheel-marked palms, radiant as fresh leaf-shoots, walking with the grace of an intoxicated elephant,
with feet honored by gods and <s>asuras</s> — to <s>Śrī Śākyasiṃha</s> I bow always! //

children.text: traiduḥkhaduḥkhād bhayavedilokān trāṇaṃ ca nītuṃ varabodhimātraiḥ /
children.translated_text: To save beings experiencing the suffering of the three sufferings, through the supreme means of awakening alone,

children.text: jihvā ca mattehi sucakṣu sarvaṃ śrīśākyasiṃhaṃ praṇamāmi nityam //
children.translated_text: with tongue and excellent eyes seeing all — to <s>Śrī Śākyasiṃha</s> I bow always! //
The <s>Mahābodhibhaṭṭārakastotra</s> is complete. //

children.text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 43: Mahābodhivandanāṣṭakam
children.translated_text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 43: <s>Mahābodhivandanāṣṭakam</s>
<s>Oṃ</s>! Homage to the <s>Buddha</s>!
Of golden complexion, with a voice like the <s>kalaviṅka</s> bird, with <s>Brahma</s>'s voice, compassionate, most worthy of devotion,
the supreme among men, with a body purified by moral conduct — to the glorious great <s>Bodhi</s> (Awakening), I bow! //
With a divine body born from the lineage of <s>Śākya</s> chiefs, the cutter of craving, the crusher of <s>Māra</s>, the lord of <s>Jinas</s>,
the abode of knowledge, the destroyer of <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions), the lord of the day — to the glorious great <s>Bodhi</s>, I bow! //
Universally auspicious (<s>Samantabhadra</s>), with limbs bearing the excellent marks, accomplishing the welfare of beings, worthy of homage through merit,
the bestower of blessings, with a mind solely devoted to the welfare of beings — to the glorious great <s>Bodhi</s>, I bow! //
He who, out of compassion, released the water of <s>Dharma</s> for those beings burning in the fire of passion,
that rain-cloud of perfect awakening, bringing happiness — to the glorious great <s>Bodhi</s>, I bow! //
The <s>Tathāgata</s>, who became a bridge for crossing the ocean of existence, the knower of reality, a lion among men,
the lord of the three worlds, the jewel of supreme awakening — to the glorious great <s>Bodhi</s>, I bow! //
Established in excellent vows for the accomplishment of all purposes, the son of <s>Māyā</s>, the crusher of <s>Māra</s>, the conqueror of enemies,
the foremost Teacher, the excellent <s>Bodhisattva</s> — to the glorious great <s>Bodhi</s>, I bow! //
The lord of the lords of the world, the lord of the lord <s>Hari</s> (Viṣṇu), the lord of the lords of beings, the lord of the lords of gods,
the lord of the lord of death, the lord of the lords of men — to the glorious great <s>Bodhi</s>, I bow! //

children.text: sa buddharūpaḥ sa hi dharmarūpaḥ sa eva saṃgho 'pi vineyakānām /
children.translated_text: He is the form of the <s>Buddha</s>, he is the form of the <s>Dharma</s>, he himself is also the <s>Saṅgha</s> for those to be disciplined;
he became the refuge of those who seek refuge — to the glorious great <s>Bodhi</s>, I bow! //
The glorious <s>Mahābodhivandanāṣṭaka</s> (Eight Verses of Homage to the Great Awakening) is complete. //

children.text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 44: Mahācakravartināmāṣṭottaraśatastotram
children.translated_text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 44: <s>Mahācakravartināmāṣṭottaraśatastotram</s>
O <s>Vajrasattva</s>, great <s>vajra</s>, lord of <s>vajra</s>, excellent practitioner,
O <s>Vajrābhiṣeka</s> (Vajra-Consecration), <s>Vajrābha</s> (Vajra-Radiant), <s>Vajraketu</s> (Vajra-Banner) — homage to you! //
O <s>Hāsavajra</s> (Laughing Vajra), great <s>Dharma</s>, <s>Vajrakośa</s> (Vajra-Treasury), most excellent,
supreme king of all <s>maṇḍalas</s>, free from conceptual proliferation — homage to you! //
O <s>Vajrakarma</s> (Vajra-Action), great protector, <s>Caṇḍayakṣa</s> (Fierce Yakṣa), great seizer,
O <s>Vajramuṣṭi</s> (Vajra-Fist), great <s>mudrā</s>, all <s>mudrās</s> — homage to you! //
O <s>Bodhicitta</s>, great awakening, <s>Buddha</s>, all <s>Tathāgatas</s>,
O <s>Vajrayāna</s>, great knowledge, <s>Mahāyāna</s> — homage to you! //
O all-purpose one, one whose purpose is all realities, great being of all purposes, all-knowing one,

children.text: sarvajña sarvakṛt sarva sarvadarśi namo 'stu te //
children.translated_text: omniscient, all-accomplishing, all, all-seeing — homage to you! //
O <s>Vajra</s>-natured one, foremost excellent <s>vajra</s>, <s>vajra</s>-powered, bearer of the supreme <s>vajra</s>,
great <s>samaya</s> (vow), one whose purpose is reality, great truth — homage to you! //
O <s>Vajrāṅkuśa</s> (Vajra-Hook), great desire, delightful one, of supremely great radiance,
O <s>Vajraprabha</s> (Vajra-Light), radiant, <s>Buddhaprabha</s> (Buddha-Light) — homage to you! //
O supreme <s>Vajra</s>-king, foremost <s>vajra</s>, foremost among the foremost <s>vidyās</s> (knowledges), supreme among men,
O <s>Vajrottama</s> (Supreme Vajra), foremost of the great foremost, supreme <s>vidyā</s> — homage to you! //
O <s>Vajradhātu</s> (Vajra-Realm), great secret, <s>Vajraguhya</s> (Vajra-Mystery), bearer of the supreme secret,
O <s>Vajrasūkṣma</s> (Subtle Vajra), great meditation, <s>Vajrakārya</s> (Vajra-Action) — homage to you! //
O foremost <s>Buddha</s>, foremost <s>Buddha-vajra</s>, <s>Buddha</s>-awakening, greatly wise,
O <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge, great <s>Buddha</s>, <s>Buddha</s> of <s>Buddhas</s> — homage to you! //
O great worship of <s>Buddha</s>-worship, worship of beings, supreme worshipper,
O great skillful means, great accomplishment, <s>Vajrasiddhi</s> (Vajra-Attainment) — homage to you! //
O <s>Tathāgata</s>, great body, <s>Tathāgata</s>-<s>Sarasvatī</s> (Eloquence of the Tathāgata),
O great mind of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Vajracitta</s> (Vajra-Mind) — homage to you! //
O sovereign of the <s>Buddhas</s>, executor of the <s>Jina's</s> command, friend of the <s>Buddha</s>, foremost of <s>Jinas</s>,
O great <s>Vairocana</s>, all-pervading, peaceful and wrathful — homage to you! //
O great reality of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, summit of reality, great method,
O knowledge of all <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections), supreme truth — homage to you! //
O <s>Samantabhadra</s>, supreme in conduct, O <s>Māra</s>, scorcher of <s>Māra</s>,
supreme in all, knowledge of equality, omnipresent — homage to you! //
O <s>Buddha-Huṃkāra</s>, <s>Huṃkāra</s>, <s>Vajra-Huṃkāra</s>, tamer,
O one with <s>viśvavajra</s> limbs, fierce <s>vajra</s>, <s>Vajrapāṇi</s> — homage to you! //
Worthy of worship, worthy of honor, worthy of respect, to be revered by <s>Tathāgatas</s> —
because your mind is as firm as a <s>vajra</s>, you are called <s>Vajrasattva</s>. //

children.text: tvadadhīnā hi saṃbodhiḥ pitā tvaṃ sarvadarśinām /
children.translated_text: Awakening depends upon you; you are the father of all the all-seeing ones;
all <s>Tathāgatas</s> have arisen and shall arise, having relied upon you. //
Whoever praises [you] with this king of hymns with great devotion,
whoever sings and praises — that one too shall become equal to <s>Vajradhara</s>. //
We entreat you, O Lord, who bring all <s>Buddhas</s> under your power —
for the sake of accomplishing the welfare of all beings, manifest your own family! //
The <s>Mahācakravartin</s> One-Hundred-and-Eight Name Entreaty-Hymn is complete. //

children.text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 45: Mahākālastotram
children.translated_text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 45: <s>Mahākālastotram</s>
I bow to great <s>Mahākāla</s>, the bestower of all prosperity,
dwarfish, pot-bellied, dark-blue, adorned with eight <s>Nāgas</s> (serpents)! //
Two-armed, one-faced, heroic, with a crown made of skulls,
clad in a tiger-skin at the waist, wearing a garland of fifty heads! //
Discerning existence and non-existence, causing the awakening of the world,
the embodiment of all states of being, O Lord, lord of the world — homage to you! //
Of dark complexion, of great splendor, protector of <s>siddhas</s> (accomplished ones) and practitioners,
O Lord bearing a chopper and skull-cup, O <s>Mahākāla</s> — homage to you! //
Wearing a garment of tiger-skin, embodying great wrath,
radiant as twelve suns, O <s>Mahākāla</s> — homage to you! //
With a terrifying mouth of great fangs, with lolling tongue, frightful,
with eyes blazing red, O <s>Mahākāla</s> — homage to you! //
Waving a garland of human heads, adorned with the king of <s>Nāgas</s>,
with a prominent beard, worthy of worship, O <s>Mahākāla</s> — homage to you! //
With furrowed brows, three-eyed, with tawny upright hair,
Resembling the mass of fire at the end of an age — O <s>Mahākāla</s>, homage to you! //
Terrifying to all <s>Daityas</s> (demons), devourer of bones and flesh,
protector of the devoted — O <s>Mahākāla</s>, homage to you! //
Destroyer of those who obstruct the <s>mantra</s> of <s>siddhi</s>-accomplishment,
giver of reassurance to the couple — O <s>Mahākāla</s>, homage to you! //
A boat, the sole vehicle for crossing to the other shore of the ocean of <s>saṃsāra</s> (cyclic existence),
you are your own radiance in the boat-vehicle — O <s>Mahākāla</s>, homage to you! //

children.text: mahākālastavaṃ caitad yaḥ paṭhed bhaktimān naraḥ /
children.translated_text: Whoever, a devoted person, recites this hymn to <s>Mahākāla</s>,
is freed from fear when terrified, and anxiety about enemies ceases. //
Having bowed to <s>Mahākāla</s>, one born in the proper lineage
obtains a good birth and becomes devoted to all accomplishments. //
The glorious <s>Mahākālastotra</s> (Hymn to Mahākāla) is complete. //

children.text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 46: Mahāpratisarāstotram
children.translated_text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 46: Mahāpratisarāstotram
<s>Oṃ</s>! Homage to the glorious <s>Mahāpratisarā</s>!

children.text: yasyāḥ smaraṇamātreṇa sarve pāpāḥ kṣayaṃ gatāḥ /
children.translated_text: By the mere remembrance of whom all sins are destroyed —

children.text: yayā yukto vajrakāyo namastasyai namo namaḥ //
children.translated_text: united with whom one becomes <s>vajra</s>-bodied — homage to her, homage, homage! //

children.text: yāṃ smaran rākṣasaḥ krūro māṭharaṃ kukṣisaṃsthitam /
children.translated_text: Remembering whom, a cruel <s>Rākṣasa</s> (demon) threw the child dwelling in the womb

children.text: prākṣipad goviṣaṃ nadyāṃ namastasyai namo namaḥ //
children.translated_text: into a river of cow-poison — homage to her, homage, homage! //
She who protected a merchant's son from a cruel serpent intent on killing,
and one dying from the burning of poison — homage to her, homage, homage! //
The great king <s>Brahmadatta</s>, whose head was protected by her —
having conquered his enemy, became resplendent — homage to her, homage, homage! //
A monk of bad conduct, afflicted with disease, who had [the dhāraṇī] bound at his throat by her —

children.text: prāṇānmuktvā yayau svargaṃ namastasyai namo namaḥ //
children.translated_text: freed from death, went to heaven — homage to her, homage, homage! //
When the ship was tossed about in the ocean, the protector of the merchants' lives —
remembering whom, the caravan-leader was saved — homage to her, homage, homage! //
When she was bound upon a wife, [the king] obtained a son —
the king with outstretched arms — homage to her, homage, homage! //

children.text: daridro yāṃ prati smṛtvā dīnārān pradadau jine /
children.translated_text: A poor man, remembering her, gave gold coins to the <s>Jina</s> (Victor) —
the king became a bestower of desired things — homage to her, homage, homage! //
Having bound her in his crest-jewel, <s>Śakra</s> (Indra), the lord, fought with the <s>Asuras</s> —

children.text: labdhavān vijayaṃ vajrī namastasyai namo namaḥ //
children.translated_text: the <s>vajra</s>-wielder obtained victory — homage to her, homage, homage! //
By the power of whose <s>mantra</s>, having fulfilled the six <s>Pāramitās</s> (Perfections),
the <s>Māras</s> were conquered by the victorious <s>Buddhas</s> — homage to her, homage, homage! //
Even one destitute of courage, condemned to death, cast into every peril —
remembering whom, was completely freed — homage to her, homage, homage! //
With her bound at his throat, he was freed from the peril of sins,
and became a leader in the city — homage to her, homage, homage! //
She who is the unconquered <s>vidyā</s> (spell), upheld by all <s>Buddhas</s>,
sealed, spoken, constantly recited, and proclaimed, //
written, rejoiced in, always worshipped for the benefit of beings,

children.text: smṛtā kāyagatā kṛtvā namastasyai namo namaḥ //
children.translated_text: remembered, made present in the body — homage to her, homage, homage! //
By the mere remembrance of whom, nothing is unattainable in the three worlds —
or by recitation and study — homage to her, homage, homage! //
She, the <s>vidyā</s> (spell), rare among <s>Buddhas</s>, prophesied, praised even in sleep,
the great <s>dhāraṇī</s> famed as the destroyer of all sins, //
of great strength, great valor, great splendor, great radiance,
the <s>vidyā</s> of great virtue, the destroyer of all burdens, //
the smasher of the bonds of sin, the liberator from the fetters of <s>Māra</s>,
the mother of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, the destroyer of all evil ones, //
the protectress, the nourisher, the sustainer, the annihilator of hostile <s>mantras</s>,
the auspicious one who destroys the effects of <s>kārkhoda</s>-poisons, //
for those devoted to great meditation, those who grasp, those who write [her] always,
those who constantly recite and study, those who hold and listen, //

children.text: parebhyo deśitā caiva nityaṃ manasi bhāvitā /
children.translated_text: and those who teach her to others, constantly contemplating her in mind,
having made her into a book-form, worshipping and paying homage — //
the auspicious one who removes all sins, the fulfiller of the accumulations for awakening —
homage to her, homage to her, homage to her, homage, homage! //
By the power of whose <s>mantra</s>, all fears and calamities,
evil gods, humans, <s>Daityas</s>, <s>Gandharvas</s>, and <s>Rākṣasas</s>, //
<s>Grahas</s> (seizing spirits), <s>Skandas</s> (child-afflicting spirits), epileptic demons, <s>Piśācas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>,
<s>Ḍākinīs</s>, hosts of <s>Śākinīs</s>, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Kārkhoda</s>-diseases, //
fevers, various diseases, those caused by hostile magic,
poisons, fire, weapons, hostile <s>mantras</s>, lightning, untimely winds, //
excessive rain, drought, all fears from enemies,

children.text: tathānye pāpasargā vā vinaśyanti na saṃśayaḥ //
children.translated_text: and other evil emanations — are destroyed without doubt. //
All undertakings succeed — homage to her, homage, homage! /

children.text: yaścaitāṃ dhārayedvidyāṃ kaṇṭhe bāhau ca mastake //
children.translated_text: Whoever bears this <s>vidyā</s> at the throat, on the arm, or on the head, //

children.text: nityaṃ rakṣanti devāstaṃ daityā nāgāśca mānuṣāḥ /
children.translated_text: the gods constantly protect that person — <s>Daityas</s>, <s>Nāgas</s>, and humans,
<s>Gandharvas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Bhūtas</s> (ghosts), <s>Pretas</s> (hungry ghosts), and <s>Piśācas</s>, //
<s>Ḍākinīs</s>, <s>Rākṣasas</s>, female messengers, <s>Kūṣmāṇḍas</s>, <s>Kaṭhapūtanās</s> —

children.text: trisandhyaṃ yaḥ paṭhennityaṃ buddhā rakṣanti taṃ sadā //
children.translated_text: whoever recites [her] constantly at the three junctures of the day, the <s>Buddhas</s> always protect that one. //
<s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> (Solitary Awakened Ones) and <s>Śrāvakas</s> (Hearers), <s>Bodhisattvas</s> of great power,
<s>yogins</s>, those with accomplished <s>mantras</s>, the great sages of great valor, //
<s>Vajrapāṇi</s> and the lord of <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Śakra</s> (Indra) together with the thirty [gods],
the four great kings, <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Maheśvara</s>, //
<s>Nandi</s>, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, <s>Mahākāla</s>, <s>Kārtikeya</s>, <s>Gaṇeśvara</s> (Lord of Gaṇas),
the <s>Bhairavas</s>, the <s>Mātṛkās</s> (Mother-goddesses), the <s>Durgās</s>, and other <s>Māra</s>-bodied ones, //
the <s>Vidyā</s>-goddesses of great valor, of great strength and prowess,
<s>Māmakī</s>, <s>Bhṛkuṭī</s>, <s>Tārā</s>, <s>Aṅkuśī</s>, <s>Vajraśṛṅkhalā</s>, //
<s>Mahāśvetā</s>, <s>Mahākālī</s>, <s>Vajradūtī</s>, <s>Supāśikā</s>,
<s>Vajramālā</s>, <s>Mahāvidyā</s>, <s>Suvīryā</s>, <s>Amṛtakuṇḍalī</s>, //
<s>Vajrā</s>, <s>Aparājitā</s> (the Unconquered), <s>Caṇḍī</s>, <s>Kālakarṇī</s>, <s>Mahābalā</s>,
and <s>Dhanyā</s>, the greatly fortunate, and <s>Padmakuṇḍalī</s>, //
<s>Maṇicūḍā</s>, <s>Puṣpadantī</s>, <s>Svarṇakeśī</s>, and <s>Piṅgalā</s>,
<s>Ekajaṭā</s>, the great goddess, <s>Dhanyā</s>, <s>Vidyunmālinī</s>, //
<s>Kapālinī</s> and <s>Laṅkeśī</s>, <s>Brahmakṣitikanāyikā</s> (Mistress of Brahmā's earth),
<s>Hārītī</s>, <s>Pāñcikā</s>, <s>Śaṅkhinī</s>, <s>Kūṭadantinī</s>, //
<s>Śrī</s>, <s>Sarasvatī</s>, <s>Lakṣmī</s>, <s>Siddheśvarī</s>, the constant attendant —

children.text: tamevā 'nye 'pi rakṣanti yasya vidyā kare sthitā //
children.translated_text: these and others too protect the one in whose hand this <s>vidyā</s> resides. //

children.text: sa bhavet sarvasattvānāṃ mokṣārthaṃ ca samudyataḥ /
children.translated_text: Such a one becomes devoted to the liberation of all beings;
homage to her, homage to her, homage to her, homage, homage! //
The glorious <s>Mahāpratisarāstotra</s> (Hymn to the Great Amulet-goddess) is complete. //

children.text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 47: Mahogratārāṣṭakastotram
children.translated_text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 47: Mahogratārāṣṭakastotram
standing in the <s>pratyālīḍha</s> posture upon the heart of a corpse, with a smiling lotus-face,
O Mother <s>Nīlasarasvatī</s> (Blue Sarasvatī), bestower of good fortune and prosperity upon those who bow,
and a sword — you alone are my refuge; I take shelter in you, O Goddess! //
endowed with three eyes like full blue lotuses, holding a cleaver, a skull-cup, a lotus,
who instantly grants the accomplishment of all purposes through the composition of natural prose and verse,
O Mistress of Speech, wish-fulfilling creeper of devotees, mistress of all accomplishments,
sprinkle one such as me with compassion, raining the nectar of good fortune! //
endowed with three eyes like blue lotuses, O ocean of compassion —
whose beautiful waist is wrapped in tiger-skin, marked with shaking bells,
O short one, whose body is filled with pride and dignity, shining with ornaments of serpents and the like,
adorned with garlands of rows of knotted human skulls — O Terrifying One, destroy [our] fear! //
whose hair-knots are [formed of] two freshly-severed dripping heads,
you who are the <s>Huṃphaṭkāra</s> itself — you alone are the refuge for one such as me, O <s>mantra</s>-natured one!
O you whose nature is <s>Māyā</s> (illusion), the passion-born transformation of form, <s>Bindu</s> (dot) and half-moon,

children.text: vedanāṃ nahi gocarā kathamapi prāptāṃ nu tāmāśraye //
children.translated_text: beyond the reach of the <s>Vedas</s> — I take refuge in that [form] which is somehow attained. //
Your form, O Mother, is threefold: gross, extremely subtle, and supreme,
with that glorious Supreme Goddess, three-eyed, of the gentle nature of <s>Brahmā</s> and others;
By service to your lotus feet, the meritorious attain union

children.text: mātastvatpadasevane hi vimukhān ko mandadhīḥ sevate //
children.translated_text: O Mother, what dull-witted one would serve those who are averse to the service of your feet? //
those who are keen-bodied, the foremost gods led by <s>Indra</s>, [yet who are] drowning in the ocean of <s>saṃsāra</s> —
they are victorious in the battle of gods and <s>Asuras</s>, fearlessly seated on [Śiva's] lap;
Those whose crore of crowns bear the seal-mark of the dust of the pair of your lotus feet,

children.text: devo 'haṃ bhuvane na me sama iti sparddhāṃ vahantaḥ pare
tattulyā niyataṃ tathā ciramamī nāśaṃ vrajanti svayam //
children.translated_text: those of equal [arrogance] indeed inevitably go to destruction of their own accord. //
others, carrying the pride 'I am a god, none in the world is my equal' —

children.text: tvannāmasmaraṇāt palāyanaparā draṣṭuṃ ca śaktā na te

children.translated_text: the hosts of <s>Bhūtas</s> (ghosts), <s>Pretas</s> (hungry ghosts), <s>Piśācas</s> (goblins), <s>Rākṣasa</s> groups, <s>Yakṣas</s>, and <s>Nāga</s>-lords,
By the remembrance of your name, [they are] intent on fleeing and unable even to see you —

children.text: ḍākinyaḥ kupitāntakāśca manujā mātaḥ kṣaṇaṃ bhūtale //
children.translated_text: <s>Ḍākinīs</s>, enraged messengers of death, and humans — O Mother, [flee] in an instant from the earth! //
<s>Daityas</s>, the foremost <s>Dānavas</s>, sky-goers, creatures such as tigers,
immobilization also on the battlefield, the immobilization of elephant-formations, and enchantment —
<s>Lakṣmī</s> (wealth), hosts of <s>siddhas</s> (accomplishments) including sandals and such, <s>siddhis</s>, as well as the immobilization of waters,

children.text: mātastvatpadasevayā khalu nṛṇāṃ siddhyanti te te guṇāḥ
kāntiḥ kāntatarā bhavecca mahatī mūḍho 'pi vācaspatiḥ //
children.translated_text: radiance becomes most beautiful, and even a fool becomes a lord of speech! //
O Mother, by the service of your feet, indeed these various powers are accomplished for people;
That person with devotion who recites this delightful eight-verse [hymn] to <s>Tārā</s>,
in the morning, at midday, and in the evening, disciplined and pure, //
obtains divine poetic power, becomes a knower of the meaning of all <s>śāstras</s> (scriptures);
having attained imperishable <s>Lakṣmī</s> (prosperity), enjoying desired pleasures, //

children.text: kīrti kāntiṃ ca nairujyaṃ sarveṣāṃ priyatāṃ vrajet /
children.translated_text: he attains fame, beauty, freedom from disease, and the affection of all;
and having attained renown in the worlds, finally obtains <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation). //
The glorious <s>Mahogratārāṣṭakastotra</s> (Eight-verse Hymn to the Greatly Fierce Tārā) is complete. //

children.text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 48: Mahogratārāstutiḥ
children.translated_text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 48: Mahogratārāstutiḥ
<s>Oṃ</s>! Homage to the glorious <s>Ugratārā</s> (Fierce Tārā)!
wearing a garland of human heads, with a voice deep as thunder,
With prominently fierce fangs, with terrifying, dreadful laughter,
holding a skull-cup in her palm — may <s>Ugratārā</s> (Fierce Tārā) protect you! //
the sustainer of the people of the three worlds, with a sword placed in hand,
O terrifying one, O one of great voice, O destroyer of all enemies —

children.text: bhaktebhyo varade devi trāhi māṃ śaraṇāgatam //
children.translated_text: O Goddess, granter of boons to devotees, protect me who has come to your refuge! //
O Goddess worshipped by gods and <s>Asuras</s>, attended by <s>Siddhas</s> and <s>Gandharvas</s>,
O Goddess who removes dullness and sin, protect me who has come to your refuge! //
O you who abide in the center of all <s>maṇḍalas</s>, beneficent to all beings, sinless one,

children.text: siddhānāṃ pūjite devi trāhi māṃ śaraṇāgatam //
children.translated_text: O Goddess worshipped by <s>Siddhas</s>, protect me who has come to your refuge! //
O Goddess standing in a terrifying form, praised as the remover of all life-breaths,

children.text: ugratāre namo nityaṃ trāhi māṃ śaraṇāgatam //
children.translated_text: O <s>Ugratārā</s>, constant homage — protect me who has come to your refuge! //
Adorned with matted locks piled high, with a lolling tongue extended upward,
O Goddess who swiftly grants intelligence, protect me who has come to your refuge! //
In the form of <s>Soma</s> (Moon), in the form of <s>Koṭṭa</s>, in the form of the moon — homage to you!
In the form of <s>Śakti</s> (Power) — homage to you! Protect me who has come to your refuge! //
I am dull, I am devoid of strength, I am incapable of attaining you;
I am slow, of slow intellect — protect me who has come to your refuge! //

children.text: snāne dāne tathā jāpye balidāne tathā kratau /
children.translated_text: In bathing, in giving, in recitation, in offering <s>bali</s> (oblations), in sacrificial rites,

children.text: prasthāne ca na śakto 'haṃ trāhi māṃ śaraṇāgatam //
children.translated_text: and in setting forth — I am incapable; protect me who has come to your refuge! //
Devoid of strength, without a protector, beset with all sins,

children.text: tvāṃ vinā na gatiryasya trāhi māṃ śaraṇāgatam //
children.translated_text: one who has no refuge other than you — protect me who has come to your refuge! //
<s>Gaurī</s>, <s>Lakṣmī</s>, <s>Mahāmāyā</s> (Great Illusion), <s>Umā</s>, the Goddess, <s>Sarasvatī</s> —
you are all of them, O Mother — protect me who has come to your refuge! //
With perfume, flowers, and other offerings, and with acts of worship,

children.text: devīṃ sampūjya yatnena labhate vāñchitaṃ phalam //
children.translated_text: having worshipped the Goddess with effort, one obtains the desired fruit. //

children.text: aṣṭamyāṃ ca caturdaśyāṃ navamyāṃ yaḥ paṭhennaraḥ /
children.translated_text: Whoever recites [this] on the eighth, fourteenth, and ninth [lunar days],
obtains supreme <s>siddhi</s> (accomplishment) — there should be no doubt about this. //

children.text: mokṣārthī labhate mokṣaṃ dhanārthī labhate dhanam /
children.translated_text: One seeking <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation) obtains liberation; one seeking wealth obtains wealth;
one seeking knowledge obtains knowledge of logic, grammar, and the like. //

children.text: idaṃ stotraṃ paṭhitvā tu saṃgrāme praviśennaraḥ /
children.translated_text: Having recited this hymn, a person may enter battle —

children.text: tasya śatruḥ kṣayaṃ yāti sadā prajñā prajāyate //
children.translated_text: his enemy goes to destruction, and wisdom is always born [in him]. //
In affliction, in negotiation, in calamity, and in fear —

children.text: ya idaṃ paṭhate stotraṃ śubhaṃ tasya na saṃśayaḥ //
children.translated_text: whoever recites this hymn — auspiciousness is his, without doubt. //
The glorious <s>Mahogratārāstuti</s> (Praise of the Greatly Fierce Tārā) is complete. //

children.text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 49: Maṅgalaṣoḍaśastutiḥ
children.translated_text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 49: <s>Maṅgalaṣoḍaśastutiḥ</s>
<s>Oṃ</s>! Homage to <s>Samantabhadra</s>!
He who, while dwelling in the forest of merit, kept numerous kings such as <s>Divodāsa</s> obedient to the teaching —

children.text: divodāsādayo bhūpāḥ sa no rakṣatu mārajit //
children.translated_text: may that conqueror of <s>Māra</s> protect us! //
For the protection of people bound by planetary afflictions, in the forest of merit,

children.text: grahānadamayad yo vai sa no rakṣatu tadbhayāt //
children.translated_text: he who indeed subdued the planets — may he protect us from that fear! //
The great sages beginning with <s>Kāśyapa</s>, and the <s>brāhmaṇas</s> beginning with <s>Ānanda</s> —

children.text: prāvrājayat sumuktyarthaṃ sa no rakṣatu muktidaḥ //
children.translated_text: he caused them to go forth for the sake of supreme liberation — may that giver of liberation protect us! //
He who protected the destitute <s>brāhmaṇa</s> by giving golden grain —

children.text: durbhikṣabhayato nityaṃ sa no rakṣatu śākyarāṭ //
children.translated_text: may that king of the <s>Śākyas</s> always protect us from the fear of famine! //
He who, having become the son of <s>Maitra</s>, overcame the one who betrayed his mother,

children.text: cakraṃ dūrīkṛtaṃ yena sa no rakṣatu mātṛvān //
children.translated_text: he by whom the wheel [of harm] was removed — may that protector of mothers protect us! //
<s>Supriyo</s>, with showers of gems obtained from the pilgrimage to <s>Badaradvīpa</s> (Jujube Island),

children.text: kāśīyān prākarodāḍhyān sa no rakṣatu kāñcanaiḥ //
children.translated_text: made the people of <s>Kāśī</s> wealthy — may he protect us with his gold! //

children.text: bhūtvā yaḥ sudhano nāma nidhānaṃ samadarśayat /
children.translated_text: He who, having become one named <s>Sudhana</s>, revealed a treasure —

children.text: dāridrayaduḥkhato nityaṃ sa no rakṣatu sarvavit //
children.translated_text: may that all-knowing one always protect us from the suffering of poverty! //
He who entered <s>Rājagṛha</s> to cure leprosy and other diseases —
may that king of <s>Dharma</s> always protect us from the fear of such diseases! //
He who, having become King <s>Kuśa</s>, revealed the supreme greatness of the eighth [lunar day]

children.text: prakāśayannije dehe sa no rakṣatu dharmavit //
children.translated_text: upon his own body — may that knower of <s>Dharma</s> protect us! //
He who established <s>Saudāsa</s> in <s>Kāśī</s> through truthful speech, and freed kings
from bondage — may that all-knowing one protect us! //

children.text: gopān rarakṣa yo devyāḥ prabhāvaṃ saṃprakāśayan /
children.translated_text: He who protected the cowherds by manifesting the power of the Goddess,
from the fear of fire, burning, and enemies — may that destroyer of fear protect us! //

children.text: yo 'ndhībhūtāṃ mātaraṃ svāṃ cūḍāratnaṃ jale vyadhāt /
children.translated_text: He who, when his own mother became blind, placed the crest-jewel in the water,

children.text: divyanetrān janān kṛtvā sa no rakṣatu netradaḥ //
children.translated_text: restoring divine sight to people — may that giver of eyes protect us! //
He who transformed his deformed son, seated in shadow, into one supremely beautiful,
endowed with all auspicious marks — may that giver of all things protect us! //
He who consecrated the one named <s>Sakalānanda</s> (Universal Joy) to the kingdom,
establishing the continuation of the lineage — may that creator of stability protect us! //
He who endured his brother who had given poison, and protected the monks who had consumed poison,

children.text: rarakṣa dhāraṇīvijñaḥ sa no rakṣatu nirviṣaḥ //
children.translated_text: being a knower of <s>dhāraṇī</s> — may that one free from poison protect us! //
He who set out from <s>Kapila</s> (Kapilavastu) to lead the Nepalese

children.text: kapilān prasthito yo 'sau sa no rakṣatu santatam //
children.translated_text: to the vision of <s>Śrī Svayambhū</s> — may he always protect us! //
The <s>Maṅgalaṣoḍaśastuti</s> (Sixteen Verses of Auspiciousness) of <s>Śākyasiṃha</s>, extracted from the <s>Bhadrakalpāvadāna</s>, is complete. //

children.text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 50: Maṅgalāṣṭakam
children.translated_text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 50: <s>Maṅgalāṣṭakam</s>
<s>Maitreya</s>, <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>, <s>Sukhakara</s>-lotus, <s>Rāhula</s>, <s>Bhadrapāla</s>,
<s>Mañjuśrī</s>, <s>Lokanātha</s>, <s>Jinavara</s>-crowned, <s>Jambhala</s>, <s>Vajrasattva</s>,

children.text: stuṣṭāḥ sarvārthasiddhiṃ dadatu samarasā maṅgalaṃ bodhisattvāḥ //
children.translated_text: may these <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, pleased and of equal savor, grant the accomplishment of all aims and auspiciousness! //
the <s>Buddha</s>, <s>Vairocana</s> and others, bowed to by the three worlds, with all faults completely exhausted —

children.text: hṛṣṭo hūṃkāravajraḥ paśupatidamako vajraghaṇṭā ca hṛṣṭ

children.translated_text: the yellow <s>Hālāhalāsya</s>, the crusher of enemy hosts, the great-souled <s>Ṭakkirāja</s>,
The joyful <s>Hūṃkāravajra</s>, the tamer of <s>Paśupati</s> (Śiva), and the joyful <s>Vajraghaṇṭā</s>,

children.text: stuṣṭāḥ sarvārthasiddhiṃ dadatu samarasā maṅgalaṃ bodhisattvāḥ //
children.translated_text: may these <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, pleased and of equal savor, grant the accomplishment of all aims and auspiciousness! //
<s>Akṣobhya</s>, <s>Ratnaketu</s>, the daily immovable <s>Gaṇḍahasti</s>, <s>Yamāri</s> —
<s>Bodhi</s>, <s>Ānandasiddha</s> (Bliss-Accomplished), conqueror of the stain of strife, <s>Heruka</s>, <s>Nīladaṇḍa</s> (Blue Staff),
The <s>Saṅgha</s>, kinsman of the three worlds, the abode of hosts of virtues, <s>Bodhicitta</s> (Awakening Mind), <s>Sucitta</s> (Good Mind),

children.text: tuṣṭāḥ sarvārthasiddhiṃ dadatu samarasā maṅgalaṃ bodhisattvāḥ //
children.translated_text: may these <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, pleased and of equal savor, grant the accomplishment of all aims and auspiciousness! //
the <s>Buddha</s>, king of spotted deer (<s>Sāraṅga</s>), conqueror of the <s>Jina's</s> virtues, compassionate to all beings —
<s>Mārīcī</s>, slayer of <s>Māra</s>, remover of all fears, yellow-colored, three-faced,
<s>Prajñā</s> (Wisdom), <s>Candrāvatārā</s> (Moon-Descent), and her younger sister <s>Bhṛkuṭī</s>, bearing the burden of the accumulation of knowledge,

children.text: māyūrī māmakī ca kṣapitaripugaṇā pāṇḍarā rocanādyā
stuṣṭāḥ sarvārthasiddhiṃ dadatu samarasā maṅgalaṃ bodhisattvāḥ //
children.translated_text: may these <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, pleased and of equal savor, grant the accomplishment of all aims and auspiciousness! //
<s>Māyūrī</s> and <s>Māmakī</s>, destroyers of enemy hosts, <s>Pāṇḍarā</s>, <s>Rocanā</s> and others —
<s>Vārāhī</s>, <s>Vajrahastā</s>, bearer of sword and axe, and <s>Dharmadhātvīśvarī</s>,
<s>Gāndhārī</s> and <s>Jāṅgulī</s>, seizing the hoods of serpents, fierce with sword, noose, and goad,

children.text: keyūrī jñānasārā dhvajanihitakarā ṣaṭkarā śābarī ca
tuṣṭāḥ sarvārthasiddhiṃ dadatu samarasā maṅgalaṃ bodhisattvāḥ //
children.translated_text: may these <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, pleased and of equal savor, grant the accomplishment of all aims and auspiciousness! //
<s>Keyūrī</s>, essence of knowledge, with hand placed on a banner, six-armed <s>Śābarī</s> —

children.text: vaiṇyā mālyā sugītā prathitajinavare śābarī dhūpavajrā

children.translated_text: <s>Vaitālī</s>, <s>Gandhavajrā</s> (Perfume-Vajra), the laughing-faced one, <s>Svargatī</s> (Heaven-Goer), noble <s>Tārā</s>,
<s>Vaiṇyā</s> (Lute-Bearer), <s>Mālyā</s> (Garland-Bearer), <s>Sugītā</s> (Sweet-Singer), the renowned supreme <s>Jina's</s> <s>Śābarī</s>, <s>Dhūpavajrā</s> (Incense-Vajra),

children.text: tuṣṭāḥ sarvārthasiddhiṃ dadatu samarasā maṅgalaṃ bodhisattvāḥ //
children.translated_text: may these <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, pleased and of equal savor, grant the accomplishment of all aims and auspiciousness! //
<s>Lakṣmī</s> of the <s>Buddha</s>, <s>Bodhi</s>, remover of all fears, <s>Śāradā</s> (Sarasvatī), <s>Dīpavajrā</s> (Lamp-Vajra) —
at <s>Śrāvastī</s>, at <s>Lumbinī</s>, with hand touching the earth, at <s>Koṅkaṇa</s>, at the <s>Bodhi</s> tree,
At <s>Vaiśālī</s>, at the <s>Dharmacakra</s> (Wheel of Dharma), on the mountain of renowned power, at <s>Gṛdhrakūṭa</s> (Vulture Peak),

children.text: tuṣṭāḥ sarvārthasiddhiṃ dadatu samarasā maṅgalaṃ bodhisattvāḥ //
children.translated_text: may these <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, pleased and of equal savor, grant the accomplishment of all aims and auspiciousness! //
the <s>Śrīvatsa</s> mark, the <s>aśvattha</s> (fig) leaf, bowed to by the chief gods, the <s>śrīphala</s> (bilva fruit), conch and wheel —

children.text: chatraṃ dūrvā ca padmaṃ dhvajamapi nihitaṃ lo(ro)canā matsyakūrma

children.translated_text: boar, full water-pot, the word of the supreme sage, the sound of the <s>vajra</s>-bell,
Parasol, <s>dūrvā</s> grass, lotus, and banner placed, <s>Locanā</s>, fish, tortoise,

children.text: stuṣṭāḥ sarvārthasiddhiṃ dadatu samarasā maṅgalaṃ bodhisattvāḥ //
children.translated_text: may these <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, pleased and of equal savor, grant the accomplishment of all aims and auspiciousness! //
the miracles of the <s>Buddhas</s>, bowed to by the chief gods, the graces of laughter and dance —
The <s>Maṅgalāṣṭakam</s> (Eight Verses of Auspiciousness) is complete. //

children.text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 51: Mañjuśrīstotram
children.translated_text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 51: <s>Mañjuśrīstotram</s>
We worship <s>Śrī Mañjunātha</s>, seated on a lotus throne, with a jeweled crown, lord of knowledge, sovereign of the world-sphere,
of serene form, splendidly shining, worthy of being lord of meditation, the noble one venerated by gods, humans, and <s>Asuras</s>. //
Of youthful form, with brilliant, playful hands [holding] blue lotuses, with cheeks adorned by armlets, necklace, and jeweled earrings,
wearing sixteen [ornaments], of delicate form — we worship <s>Mañjughoṣa</s> (Sweet-Voiced), honored by the chief gods. //
Revolving within the pores of the tips of his body-hair, the creator of the entire phenomenal world, of the son of the <s>Sugata</s> —

children.text: traividyamantra tava nātha guṇārṇaveṇa sūkṣmāya buddhatanayāya namo 'stu tasmai //
children.translated_text: O Lord, the three-knowledge <s>mantra</s>, by the ocean of your virtues — homage to that subtle son of the <s>Buddha</s>! //
Established in the happiness of the path of the profound doctrine, the ocean of knowledge that fulfills the aims of all beings,
the immeasurable treasure of wisdom, ocean of virtues — I constantly bow to <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, son of the <s>Jina</s>. //
One who knows all truths, who removes the suffering of beings, beneficent to the three worlds, remover of all sorrow,
a hero who crushes <s>Kāma</s> (desire), of beautiful and graceful form — may <s>Mañjughoṣa</s>, the delight of the people of the three worlds, protect me! //
Of radiance beautiful as the young moon, adorned with excellent ornaments,
with eyes like the pure petals of the lotus of wisdom — I always worship <s>Mañjuśrī</s>. //
He who holds in his left hand a bowl resembling clasped hands, spinning,
in whose name there is complete <s>Lakṣmī</s> (prosperity) — I bow to <s>Mañjughoṣa</s>. //
To the one with sword and book in hand, who abides in the orb of the moon,
the sun that dispels the darkness of ignorance — homage to <s>Mañjughoṣa</s>! //
The banner of the light of supreme knowledge, and the aspiration of [great] resolve,
<s>Mañjughoṣa</s> of pacified senses — I bow with devotion. //
The glorious <s>Mañjuśrīstavastotra</s> (Praise-Hymn to Mañjuśrī) is complete. //

children.text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 52: Mañjuvajrastotram
children.translated_text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 52: <s>Mañjuvajrastotram</s>
Composed by <s>Mañjugarbha</s>. Homage to <s>Śrī Mañjuvajra</s>!
of excellent radiance, pure and peaceful, wearing five locks, a youth,
Bright as the moon, with sword and book in hand,
skilled in burning away false views — I bow to <s>Mañjughoṣa</s>! //
of vast and supreme liberation, with eyes wide as lotus petals,
a vehicle for gods, <s>Dānavas</s>, and humans, the foremost <s>Bodhisattva</s>,
Riding a lion-vehicle, giving gifts to devotees,
with a lotus-arrow in hand — I bow to <s>Mañjughoṣa</s>! //
the treasury of all virtues, the canopy of all knowledge,
delighting in remembrance and worship, far from the faults of passion and the rest,
Bearing the entire treasury, washing away the fault of ignorance,
drying up the dullness [of beings] — I bow to <s>Mañjughoṣa</s>! //
nourishing the gods, a maiden bestowing <s>siddhi</s> (accomplishment),
radiant as the moon, with eyes like blue lotuses,
Surrounded by <s>Gaṇapati</s>, <s>Śara</s> (Skanda), <s>Janma</s>, <s>Śrī</s>, <s>Mahākāla</s>, and Lions,
with a beautiful garland on his chest — I bow to <s>Mañjughoṣa</s>! //
bearing sword, arrow, prayer-beads, and a book,
<s>Vāyu</s> (Wind), <s>Pramatha</s>, and the guardians surround him, his face smiling,
For the pacification of <s>Indra</s> (lord of gods), this friend: <s>Agni</s>, <s>Rakṣa</s> (guardian),
with devotion offered at his feet — I bow to <s>Mañjughoṣa</s>! //
with <s>Garuḍa</s> (king of birds) as his vehicle-body, venerated by <s>Brahmā</s>, by <s>Ramā</s> (Lakṣmī) and <s>Umā</s> —
whose <s>mantra</s>, sprinkled on every limb with streams of all waters,
He whose sword-edge, hard and sharp, was the path for cutting and carrying away,
I bow to <s>Mañjughoṣa</s> of exceedingly great glory! //
shone even on the earth of a river, in a place of much familiarity —
the essence of all the <s>Nigamas</s> (sacred texts), brilliantly shone forth —
The secret goddess, pleased by your ever-fresh praise,
from whom the greatly fierce has flowed away — I bow to <s>Mañjughoṣa</s>! //
the far shore of the ocean of existence, the summit of the wish-granting tree of generosity,
established upon a lotus of a thousand and ten petals, the lordly light —
The world of people perceives the <s>Dharmadhātu</s> (Realm of Dharma), the great lord,
perceives the lord of serpents — I bow to <s>Mañjughoṣa</s>! //
and also your praised divine greatness, O lord,
he becomes a king of poets, seated on the lion-throne of debate,
Whoever recites this beloved poem composed in <s>Mālinī</s> meter,
endowed with all knowledge, an ornament, capable and auspicious. //
with the stream of speech-nectar blazing brightly in all assemblies,
The <s>Mañjuvajrastotra</s>, composed by <s>Mañjugarbha</s>, extracted from the <s>Svayambhūpurāṇa</s>, is complete. //

children.text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 53: Māravijayastotram
children.translated_text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 53: <s>Māravijayastotram</s>
The one who conquered the strife of <s>Māra</s>, the sole teacher of the world, bowed to by gods, <s>Yakṣas</s>, great serpents, and <s>Daityas</s> —
this cloud of virtues who well taught the path of the Four Noble Truths — I always bow to him. //
Seeing the wretched people crying out in misery, caught in the midst of the fearsome, great ocean of existence (<s>bhava</s>),

children.text: parimocayituṃ ya iha praṇidhiṃ pracakāra vibhuṃ tamahaṃ praṇataḥ //
children.translated_text: he who made the vow (<s>praṇidhāna</s>) here to liberate them — I bow to that all-pervading one. //
Like the king of mountains, with intellect [bright] as the autumn moon, of beautiful face, beautiful arms, bearing an excellent form,

children.text: sugataṃ gatamapratimaṃ sugataṃ praṇato 'smi sadā jagadarthakaram //
children.translated_text: the <s>Sugata</s> (Well-Gone One), gone to the incomparable well-gone state — I always bow to the one who acts for the welfare of the world. //
His body saturated with golden radiance, deep-voiced like the excellent thunder-drum-cloud,
of slow, majestic gait like the elephant or the swan — I bow my head to the sole treasury of virtues. //
With steady eyes like the young sun, with fierce, thunderous, terrifying roars,

children.text: namucipraharairasiśaktidharaiścalito 'si vibho na hi tvaṃ vikṛtaiḥ //
children.translated_text: by the strikes of <s>Namuci</s> (Māra), bearing swords and spears — O Lord, you were not at all shaken by those distortions! //
With ear-lobes white as <s>lavalī</s> fruit, their body-creepers bending under the weight of breasts,

children.text: nahi tvāmaśakan khalu nāgasutāḥ śvasitaiḥ skhalitairapi kampayitum //
children.translated_text: even the daughters of the <s>Nāga</s> were truly unable to make you tremble with their sighs and faltering steps. //
Trees adorned with clusters of blossoms, and mountains studded with thousands of many jewels —

children.text: na tathābhiratiṃ janayanti satāṃ janayanti yathā tava vīraguṇāḥ //
children.translated_text: do not generate such delight in the good as your heroic virtues generate. //

children.text: sphuṭacitrapadaṃ bahuyuktiyutaṃ gamakaṃ vacanaṃ tava karṇasukham /
children.translated_text: Your speech, with clearly beautiful words, full of many reasons, persuasive, pleasant to the ear,
producing the fruit of the auspicious path — upon examining it, people do not recite any other word than yours. //

children.text: iti vaḥ śaraṇaṃ samavekṣya janā na patantyapi kalpaśatairniraye /
children.translated_text: Thus, seeing you as their refuge, people do not fall into hell even for hundreds of <s>kalpas</s> (aeons),

children.text: vinihatya ca doṣaripūn bahulān pariyanti śubhaṃ varamokṣapuram //
children.translated_text: and having destroyed the abundant enemy-faults, they proceed to the excellent city of liberation (<s>mokṣa</s>). //

children.text: tava saumyatayā 'pyabhibhūtatamo na virājati śītakaro gagane /
children.translated_text: Even the cool-rayed moon in the sky does not shine, overwhelmed by your gentleness and its darkness,

children.text: tava kāñcanakuṅkumasaprabhayā prabhayā 'bhihato na vibhāti raviḥ //
children.translated_text: and the sun does not shine, struck down by the radiance of your golden saffron-like luster. //

children.text: tava nātha śubhe vadanāmburūhe nayanabhramarā nipatanti nṛṇām /
children.translated_text: O Lord, upon the auspicious lotus of your face, the bee-eyes of people alight,

children.text: pratibuddhadale kamale vimale bhramarā iva puṣpaśatākulitāḥ //
children.translated_text: like bees confused among hundreds of flowers upon a pure, awakened-petalled lotus. //

children.text: iti toṭakamantravarairatulaiḥ parikīrtya mayā tava varṇalavān /
children.translated_text: Thus, having proclaimed with incomparable excellent <s>Toṭaka</s> verses the splendor of your qualities,

children.text: yadupārjitamadya śubhaṃ vipulaṃ śivamastu tato bhuvi devanṛṇām //
children.translated_text: whatever abundant merit has been earned by me today — may it bring welfare to gods and humans on earth! //
The glorious <s>Māravijayastotra</s> (Hymn to the Conquest of Māra) is complete. //

children.text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 54: Nairātmāṣṭakastotram
children.translated_text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 54: <s>Nairātmāṣṭakastotram</s>
Without support, without form, embodying non-conceptualization,

children.text: nairātmā varadā devī nityameva namo 'stu te //
children.translated_text: O <s>Nairātmā</s> (Selfless One), boon-granting goddess — eternal homage to you! //
One-faced, three-eyed, with tawny upward-streaming hair,
bearing a chopper and skull-cup in her hands — I bow to the Mother of the Universe! //
Adorned with the nine dances, embodying a thousand faces,
O <s>Yogeśvarī</s> (Mistress of Yoga), attainable through yoga — I bow to the one embodying wisdom! //
Mounted upon a corpse, of great splendor, the cutter of all evil beings,
the goddess who removes all sins — I bow to the sovereign of the world! //

children.text: gaurīṃ caurīṃ ca vetālīṃ ghasmarīṃ pukkasīṃ tathā /
children.translated_text: To <s>Gaurī</s>, <s>Caurī</s>, <s>Vetālī</s>, <s>Ghasmarī</s>, <s>Pukkasī</s>, likewise
<s>Śabarī</s>, <s>Cāṇḍālī</s>, <s>Ḍombī</s> — I bow to the eight <s>yoginīs</s>! //
The destroyer of <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Śiva</s>, <s>Indra</s>, and the four <s>Māras</s>,
the goddess who enchants the three worlds — I bow to the beauty among the gods! //
With limbs adorned with a rosary of beads, born from the seed-syllable <s>A</s>,
the goddess eternally devoted to meditation — I bow to the Mother of the Universe! //
The goddess dear to all beings, the awakener of all <s>mantras</s>,
O Mother pervading all <s>mantras</s> — to you, <s>Nairātmā</s>, I bow! //
The <s>Nairātmāṣṭakastotra</s> (Eight-verse Hymn to the Selfless Goddess) is complete. //

children.text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 55: Narakoddhārastotram
children.translated_text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 55: <s>Narakoddhārastotram</s>
Sunk in the mire of poverty, in the great ocean called <s>saṃsāra</s>,

children.text: pratijñātaṃ samutpāde trāhi māṃ hi tathāgata //
children.translated_text: as vowed at the arising [of your resolve] — save me, O <s>Tathāgata</s>! //
Dwelling in the house of darkness, experiencing harm and suffering,

children.text: bandhuvargaiḥ parityaktaṃ trāhi māṃ hi tathāgata //
children.translated_text: abandoned by all kinsmen and relatives — save me, O <s>Tathāgata</s>! //
Mother, father, sister and others, son, wife, friends, and people —
all are seen to be like a magic show — save me, O <s>Tathāgata</s>! //
The good and bad <s>karma</s> (deeds) I performed for the sake of enemies and people —

children.text: ekākī taṃ hi bhokṣyāmi trāhi māṃ hi tathāgata //
children.translated_text: I alone shall experience [their fruit] — save me, O <s>Tathāgata</s>! //
In a ruined well, most terrible, in an unfathomable ocean,

children.text: andhībhūto 'smyahaṃ nātha trāhi māṃ hi tathāgata //
children.translated_text: I have become blind, O Lord — save me, O <s>Tathāgata</s>! //
Mounted on a decrepit boat, attempting to cross the great ocean,

children.text: durlaṅghyaṃ ca mayā dṛṣṭaṃ trāhi māṃ hi tathāgata //
children.translated_text: I see it is impossible to cross — save me, O <s>Tathāgata</s>! //

children.text: dharmādharma na vijñātaṃ gamyāgamyaṃ na veditam /
children.translated_text: <s>Dharma</s> (right) and <s>adharma</s> (wrong) I have not discerned; what is accessible and inaccessible I have not understood;

children.text: acetano 'smyahaṃ nātha trāhi māṃ hi tathāgata //
children.translated_text: I am without awareness, O Lord — save me, O <s>Tathāgata</s>! //
Matricide and the other five <s>ānantarya</s> (heinous) sins have been committed by me;

children.text: pacyāmi narake ghore trāhi māṃ hi tathāgata //
children.translated_text: I am being cooked in a terrible hell — save me, O <s>Tathāgata</s>! //
I have committed the breaking of <s>stūpas</s>, destroyed the affairs of the <s>Saṅgha</s>,

children.text: kṛtā mayā sattvahiṃsā trāhi māṃ hi tathāgata //
children.translated_text: I have committed violence against beings — save me, O <s>Tathāgata</s>! //
In this world, deprived of happiness; in the next world, no feeling [of joy] —

children.text: veṣṭitaṃ karmasūtreṇa trāhi māṃ hi tathāgata //
children.translated_text: bound by the thread of <s>karma</s> — save me, O <s>Tathāgata</s>! //
Like a <s>kāśa</s> (reed) flower in the sky, tossed about by the wind,

children.text: īdṛśaṃ jīvitaṃ loke trāhi māṃ hi tathāgata //
children.translated_text: such is life in this world — save me, O <s>Tathāgata</s>! //
The forest is covered with thorns, crowded with many trees;

children.text: panthānaṃ nātra paśyāmi trāhi māṃ hi tathāgata //
children.translated_text: I see no path here — save me, O <s>Tathāgata</s>! //
Innocent animals were killed by me in anger, without cause;

children.text: rājahatyāṃ tadā manye trāhi māṃ hi tathāgata //
children.translated_text: that I consider equal to regicide — save me, O <s>Tathāgata</s>! //
As I am being cooked in hell, who will be my savior?

children.text: gacchāmi śaraṇaṃ kasya trāhi māṃ hi tathāgata //
children.translated_text: Whose refuge shall I seek? — save me, O <s>Tathāgata</s>! //
You are the king of physicians among physicians, the healer of all diseases,
O lord of the world, savior of existence, in the three worlds of the moving and unmoving! //
The <s>Narakoddhārastotra</s> (Hymn of Rescue from Hell) is complete. //

children.text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 56: Niraupamyastavaḥ
children.translated_text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 56: <s>Niraupamyastavaḥ</s>
O Incomparable One, homage to you, proclaimer of the meaning of non-inherent nature (<s>niḥsvabhāva</s>),
you who are devoted to the welfare of the world, whose views have gone astray. //

children.text: na ca nāma tvayā kiñcid dṛṣṭaṃ bauddhena cakṣuṣā /
children.translated_text: Indeed, nothing whatsoever was seen by you with the eye of a <s>Buddha</s>;
yet unsurpassed, O Lord, is your vision that sees the true nature of reality. //

children.text: na boddhā na ca boddhavyamastīha paramārthataḥ /
children.translated_text: There is no knower nor anything to be known here, in the ultimate sense;
how marvelous — you have awakened to the <s>dharmatā</s> (true nature of things) that is supremely difficult to comprehend! //

children.text: na tvayotpāditaḥ kaścid dharmo nāpi nirodhitaḥ /
children.translated_text: No <s>dharma</s> (phenomenon) was produced by you, nor was any ceased;
through the vision of equality alone, the unsurpassed state was attained. //
You did not seek <s>nirvāṇa</s> by distancing yourself from <s>saṃsāra</s>;
your peace was attained, O Lord, without opposing <s>saṃsāra</s>. //
You realized the single taste of defilement and purification,
and through the non-differentiation of the <s>dharmadhātu</s> (realm of reality), you are purified in every way. //
Not a single syllable was uttered by you, O All-pervading One,
yet the entire multitude of those to be trained was satisfied by the rain of <s>Dharma</s>. //

children.text: na te 'sti saktiḥ skandheṣu na dhātvāyataneṣu ca /
children.translated_text: You have no attachment to the <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates), nor to the <s>dhātus</s> (elements) and <s>āyatanas</s> (sense-bases);
with a mind like space, you abide in all <s>dharmas</s>. //

children.text: sattvasaṃjñā ca te nātha sarvathā na pravartate /
children.translated_text: The concept of 'being' (<s>sattvasaṃjñā</s>) does not arise for you in any way, O Lord,
yet toward beings afflicted by suffering, you are exceedingly compassionate. //
In happiness and suffering, self and non-self, permanent and impermanent, and the like, O Lord —
in such various conceptualizations, your understanding does not cling. //
There is neither going nor coming of phenomena — such is your understanding;
you were proclaimed as one not situated anywhere, O knower of the ultimate meaning of <s>Dharma</s>. //
You have followed everywhere, yet you have not gone anywhere;
through your birth-body and <s>Dharma</s>-body, you are inconceivable, O great Sage. //
Devoid of oneness and otherness, like an echo, the world —
gone to the destruction of transmigration — you, O blameless one, have awakened to this. //
Free from eternalism and nihilism, devoid of the characterized and the characteristic,
you have understood <s>saṃsāra</s> to be like a dream and an illusion, O Lord. //
The rivers of <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions), from their root in latent tendencies to their end, have been conquered;
and from the very nature of the <s>kleśas</s> themselves, the deathless (<s>amṛta</s>) was obtained by you. //
By you, the mark-less was boldly perceived — form as formless;
yet with a body radiant with the [major] marks, you are seen in the realm of form. //

children.text: na ca rūpeṇa dṛṣṭena dṛṣṭa ityabhidhīyase /
children.translated_text: You are not called 'seen' by the form that is seen;

children.text: dharmadṛṣṭyā sudṛṣṭo 'si dharmatā na ca dṛśyate //
children.translated_text: you are truly seen through the vision of <s>Dharma</s>, yet <s>dharmatā</s> (the true nature) is not visible. //

children.text: śauṣīryo nāsti te kāyo māṃsāsthirudhiro na ca /
children.translated_text: There is no hollowness in your body, nor flesh, nor bone, nor blood;
like a rainbow, you have displayed a body without [material substance]. //

children.text: nāmayo nāśuciḥ kāye kṣuttṛṣṇāsambhavo na ca /
children.translated_text: There is no disease in your body, no impurity, no occurrence of hunger or thirst;
by you, worldly actions were displayed for the sake of conforming to the world. //
The fault of <s>karmāvaraṇa</s> (karmic obscuration) does not exist for you in any way, O sinless one;
by you, the fruits of <s>karma</s> were displayed out of compassion for the world. //
Since the <s>dharmadhātu</s> (realm of reality) is undivided, there is no division of vehicles, O Lord;
the three vehicles were proclaimed by you for the sake of beings' entry [into the path]. //

children.text: nityo dhruvaḥ śivaḥ kāyastava dharmamayo jina /
children.translated_text: Your body made of <s>Dharma</s> is eternal, stable, and auspicious, O <s>Jina</s> (Victor);
yet for the sake of those to be trained, cessation (<s>nirvṛti</s>) was displayed by you. //
In countless world-systems, you are again beheld by your devotees,
who eagerly [await your] descent, birth, perfect awakening, turning of the wheel, and final cessation. //

children.text: na te 'sti manyanā nātha na vikalpo na ceñjanā /
children.translated_text: You have no conceit, O Lord, no conceptualization, no effort;
effortlessly, your <s>Buddha</s>-activity proceeds in the world. //
Thus, having scattered flowers of virtues upon the <s>Sugata</s>, inconceivable and immeasurable, the merit I have gained —
may beings here become, through that, vessels of the supremely profound <s>Dharma</s> of the Lord of Sages! //
The <s>Niraupamyastava</s> (Hymn to the Incomparable One) is complete. //

children.text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 57: Pañcākṣarastotram
children.translated_text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 57: <s>Pañcākṣarastotram</s>

children.text: namo buddhāya na jāto na mṛtaścaiva na rūpo nāpi rūpavān /
children.translated_text: Homage to the <s>Buddha</s>! Neither born nor dead, neither with form nor possessing form,

children.text: na saṃsāre na nirvāṇe na kārastena sūcyate //
children.translated_text: neither in <s>saṃsāra</s> nor in <s>nirvāṇa</s> — the syllable <s>NA</s> signifies this. //
He who always destroys delusion, the bestower of the bliss of liberation,
the deluder of all <s>Māras</s> — the syllable <s>MO</s> signifies this. //
The meditation proclaimed by the <s>Buddhas</s>, the gathering-place of the <s>Buddhas</s>,
the <s>Buddha</s> free from afflictions, the Fully Awakened One — the syllable <s>BU</s> signifies this. //
He who is upheld by <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, who always follows the path of <s>dharmadhātu</s>,
the supreme <s>Dharma</s> of all <s>dharmas</s> — the syllable <s>DHA</s> signifies this. //

children.text: yathā nāsti tathā nāsti yathā nāsti tathāsti yaḥ /
children.translated_text: He who is as he is not, who is not as he is, who exists as he does not exist,
whose actions accord with his words — the syllable <s>YA</s> signifies this. //
This five-syllabled [mantra] is meritorious, sacred, and the destroyer of sin;

children.text: ye paṭhanti divārātrau te yānti paramāṃ gatim //
children.translated_text: those who recite it day and night attain the supreme state. //
The glorious <s>Pañcākṣarastotra</s> (Five-Syllable Hymn) is complete. //

children.text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 58: Pañcarakṣādevīstotrāṇi
children.translated_text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 58: <s>Pañcarakṣādevīstotrāṇi</s>
1. <s>Mahāpratisarāstotram</s>
<s>Oṃ</s>! Homage to the glorious <s>Mahāpratisarā</s>!
The <s>Tathāgatas</s> and others attained the supreme state of <s>Tathatā</s> (Suchness) through the reality
of bearing this <s>dhāraṇī</s> — to <s>Pratisarā</s> I bow! //
<s>Indra</s> conquered the <s>Daityas</s> in battle, bearing the banner of [this] <s>dhāraṇī</s>, the many [foes];
to her who grants victory in battle, the fearsome <s>Pratisarā</s>, I bow! //
By whose power King <s>Brahmadatta</s> obtained a kingdom free of thorns —
to the goddess who grants universal sovereignty, <s>Pratisarā</s>, I bow! //
Even one who had committed many offenses, through devotion to her, obtained the authority of kingship;
to her who destroys the fear of weapons and the like, <s>Pratisarā</s>, I bow! //
Merchants who emerged from the ocean obtained jewels by remembering her;
to her who pacifies all afflictions, <s>Pratisarā</s>, I bow! //
The Hymn to <s>Śrī Mahāpratisarā</s>, the Protective Goddess, is complete.
2. <s>Mahāmantrānusāriṇīstotram</s>
<s>Oṃ</s>! Homage to the glorious <s>Mahāmantrānusāriṇī</s>!
Through the <s>Buddha's</s> blessing, granting fearlessness to <s>Buddhas</s>, destroyer of fear,
for those drowning in the ocean of existence — homage to <s>Mantrānusāriṇī</s>! //
By the mere utterance of whose <s>mantra</s>, the six terrible types [of afflictions]
go to destruction — to the boon-granting <s>Mantrānusāriṇī</s>, homage! //
Those who follow <s>Mantrānusāriṇī</s> — no other <s>mantra</s>-born <s>grahas</s> (seizing spirits)
can torment them or their loved ones — homage to <s>Mantrānusāriṇī</s>! //
The <s>Buddha</s> spoke those verses after the recitation of her <s>mantra</s>,
by which there is well-being everywhere — homage to <s>Mantrānusāriṇī</s>! //
In this <s>Kali</s> age, devoid of the <s>Buddha</s>, she acts for the welfare of the worlds;
the pacifier of sins and calamities — homage to <s>Mantrānusāriṇī</s>! //
The Hymn to <s>Śrī Mahāmantrānusāriṇī</s> is complete.
3. <s>Mahāmāyūrīstotram</s>
<s>Oṃ</s>! Homage to the glorious <s>Mahāmāyūrī</s>!

children.text: duṣṭaṃ kṛṣṇabhujaṅgaṃ ca naraḥ svāntikaṃ pālayet /
children.translated_text: A person could tame a vicious black serpent nearby
by the power of her <s>mantra</s> — to <s>Māyūrī</s> (Peahen Goddess) I bow! //
<s>Brahmā</s> and the other world-protectors obtained
their respective dominions through her <s>dhāraṇī</s> — to <s>Māyūrī</s> I bow! //
A fool with his rosary could not harm the golden-colored peacock
even with an infallible noose — to <s>Māyūrī</s> I bow! //
By reciting her <s>mantra</s>, beings came to life and withered trees revived;
to the goddess who revives the dead, <s>Māyūrī</s>, I bow! //
By association with her <s>mantra</s>, even the wind becomes a pacifier of great calamities;

children.text: buddhānāṃ bodhidāṃ nityaṃ māyūrīṃ praṇamāmi tām //
children.translated_text: to her who always grants awakening to the <s>Buddhas</s>, <s>Māyūrī</s>, I bow! //
The Hymn to <s>Śrī Mahāmāyūrī</s>, the Protective Goddess, is complete.
4. <s>Mahāśītavatīrakṣādevīstotram</s>
<s>Oṃ</s>! Homage to <s>Mahāśītavatī</s>!
By reciting her <s>dhāraṇī</s>, <s>Rāhula</s> obtained auspiciousness,
though tormented by all the <s>grahas</s> (planetary spirits) — to <s>Śītavatī</s> I bow! //
She who brings coolness in the heat of sin, [who protects] from the affliction of cold and other calamities,
the pacifier of the suffering of cold and heat — to <s>Śītavatī</s> I bow! //
By wearing the threads knotted with <s>mantras</s>, travelers for a hundred <s>yojanas</s> (leagues)
are protected — to <s>Śītavatī</s> I bow! //
She who was formerly recited by the Sage dwelling in the cremation ground,
for the pacification of planetary afflictions — to <s>Śītavatī</s> I bow! //
For those afflicted by <s>grahas</s> (seizing spirits), [and] those who bear the knotted verses,
the pacifier of the fear of <s>grahas</s> — to <s>Śītavatī</s> I bow! //
The Hymn to <s>Śrī Mahāśītavatī</s>, the Protective Goddess, is complete.
5. <s>Mahāsāhasrapramardinīstotram</s>
<s>Oṃ</s>! Homage to the glorious <s>Mahāsāhasrapramardinī</s>!
In the great thousandfold world, for those who act for the welfare of thousands,
I bow to <s>Sāhasramardīnī</s> (Crusher of a Thousand), the mother of a thousand beings! //
Since there is always a great festival in <s>Vaiśālī</s> when it is afflicted,
I bow to <s>Sāhasramardīnī</s>, the pacifier of great calamities! //
The subduer of <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>rākṣasas</s>, and <s>bhūtas</s> (spirits) of wicked minds,
I bow to <s>Sāhasramardīnī</s>, the destroyer of misfortunes and afflictions! //
By the recitation of whose <s>dhāraṇī</s> the lion of the <s>Śākyas</s> was protected —
I bow to that <s>Sāhasramardīnī</s>, smeared with poison against poison! //
A medicine mixed with honey, the remedy for all diseases,
the reviver of the dead in the world — I bow to <s>Sāhasramardīnī</s>! //
The hymn to the glorious <s>Mahāsāhasramardīnī</s>, the protective goddess, is complete. //

children.text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 59: Pañcatathāgatastotram
children.translated_text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 59: <s>Pañcatathāgatastotram</s>

children.text: śrībuddha buddhādhipa buddharūpa buddhānvitān bodhayase vibuddhaḥ /
children.translated_text: O glorious <s>Buddha</s>, supreme among <s>Buddhas</s>, of <s>Buddha</s>-form — awakened, you awaken those endowed with <s>Buddha</s>[-nature],

children.text: buddhyā samastān khalu buddhaputra santoṣya yogena tu buddhameghām //
children.translated_text: with wisdom, O son of the <s>Buddha</s>, having satisfied all, through <s>yoga</s> you [send forth] the <s>Buddha</s>-cloud! //

children.text: śrīvajra vajrāmala jātavajra vajreṇa dīptena pradīpya lokam /
children.translated_text: O glorious <s>Vajra</s>, stainless <s>Vajra</s>, born as <s>Vajra</s> — having illuminated the world with the blazing <s>vajra</s>,

children.text: dadan yogena tu vajrasaṃvarṣaṃ vajrātmabhāvaṃ kuruṣe suvajra //
children.translated_text: bestowing through <s>yoga</s> the <s>vajra</s>-rain, O excellent <s>Vajra</s>, you create the <s>vajra</s>-nature! //

children.text: śrīratna ratnākara ratnamegha ratnena ratnaṃ ramase suratna /
children.translated_text: O glorious <s>Ratna</s> (Jewel), mine of jewels, jewel-cloud — O excellent jewel, with your jewel you delight in the jewel,
splitting asunder the dense [cloud of] poverty of beings with your great, brilliant jewel-banner! //
O glorious <s>Padma</s> (Lotus), supreme lotus, lotus-being — having awakened all lotuses with lotus-nets,

children.text: vibodhya padmodbhava padmatoyaiḥ padme kule sthāpayase supadma //
children.translated_text: O lotus-born one, with lotus-waters you establish [beings] in the lotus family, O excellent lotus! //

children.text: śrīviśva viśvāviśa viśvajñānaṃ viśvena viśvaviṣayena lipta /
