children.translated_text: O glorious <s>Viśva</s> (Universal One), pervading all, universal knowledge — anointed with the universal, all-pervading object,

children.text: viśvena sattvān vinayeṣu viśvaṃ vidyāṃ suvidyḥṃ sukhapḥcitḥmiti //
children.translated_text: with the universal [method] you discipline beings in all trainings, with excellent knowledge, accumulated happiness. //
The glorious <s>Pañcatathāgatastotram</s> (Hymn to the Five Tathāgatas) is complete. //

children.text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 60: Pañcatathāgatastutigāthā
children.translated_text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 60: <s>Pañcatathāgatastutigāthā</s>
<s>Oṃ</s>! Homage to the glorious Destroyer of the Five Elements!
Homage to you, O foremost king of boon-granters! Homage to you, O <s>Bhūtakoṭi</s> (Limit of Reality)!
Homage to you, O womb of emptiness (<s>śūnyatā</s>)! Homage to you, O <s>Buddhabodhi</s> (Buddha-Awakening)! //
Homage to you, O <s>Buddharāga</s> (Buddha-Passion)! Homage to you, O <s>Buddhakāma</s> (Buddha-Desire)!
Homage to you, O <s>Buddhaprīti</s> (Buddha-Joy)! Homage, homage to <s>Buddhamoda</s> (Buddha-Delight)! //
Homage to you, O <s>Buddhasmita</s> (Buddha-Smile)! Homage, homage to <s>Buddhahāsa</s> (Buddha-Laughter)!
Homage to you, O <s>Buddhavāca</s> (Buddha-Speech)! Homage, homage to <s>Buddhabhāva</s> (Buddha-Being)! //
Homage to you, O one born from non-existence (<s>Abhavodbhava</s>)! Homage to you, O <s>Buddhasaṃbhava</s> (Buddha-Born)!
Homage to you, O one born from space (<s>Gaganodbhava</s>)! Homage to you, O <s>Jñānasaṃbhava</s> (Knowledge-Born)! //

children.text:
māyājāla namastubhyaṃ namaste buddhanāyaka /
      namaste sarvasarvebhyo jñānakāya namo 'stu te /
children.translated_text: Homage to you, O Net of Illusion (<s>Māyājāla</s>)! Homage to you, O leader of the <s>Buddhas</s>! Homage to you, O all of all! Homage to you, O <s>Jñānakāya</s> (Knowledge-Body)!
The glorious <s>Pañcatathāgatastutigāthā</s> (Verses of Praise to the Five Tathāgatas) is complete. //

children.text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 61: Paramārthastavaḥ
children.translated_text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 61: <s>Paramārthastavaḥ</s>
How shall I praise that Lord, unborn, without foundation,
who transcends worldly conventions, whose domain lies beyond the path of speech? //
Yet, whatever you are like, [you who are] operative in the meaning of <s>Tathatā</s> (Suchness) —
relying upon worldly convention, I shall praise you, the Guru, with devotion. //
Since your nature is unborn, your arising is not found;
there is no going, no coming — O Lord, homage to you who are non-existence! //

children.text: na bhāvo nāpyabhāvo 'si nocchedo nāpi śāśvataḥ /
children.translated_text: You are neither existent nor non-existent, neither annihilated nor eternal,
neither permanent nor impermanent — homage to you who are non-dual (<s>advaya</s>)! //
You are not of one color — green, madder-red — no color of yours is apprehended,

children.text: na pītaḥ śuklaḥ kṛṣṇo vā avarṇāya namo 'stu te //
children.translated_text: neither yellow, white, nor black — homage to you who are colorless! //

children.text: na mahān nāpi hrasvo 'si na dīrghaḥ parimaṇḍalaḥ /
children.translated_text: You are neither large nor small, neither long nor round;
having attained the state of the immeasurable — homage to you who are beyond measure! //

children.text: na dūre nāpi vāsanne nākāśe nāpi vā kṣitau /
children.translated_text: Neither far nor near, neither in space nor on earth,

children.text: na saṃsāre na nirvāṇe asthitāya namo 'stu te //
children.translated_text: neither in <s>saṃsāra</s> nor in <s>nirvāṇa</s> — homage to you who abide nowhere! //
Not abiding in any <s>dharma</s> (phenomenon), having attained the state of the <s>Dharmadhātu</s> (realm of reality),

children.text: parāṃ gambhīratāṃ prāpto gambhīrāya namo 'stu te //
children.translated_text: having reached the supreme depth — homage to you who are profound! //

children.text: evaṃ stute stuto bhūyādathavā kiṃ vata stutaḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus praised, may [you] be praised — or what indeed is praise?

children.text: śūnyeṣu sarvadharmeṣu kaḥ stutaḥ kena vā stutaḥ //
children.translated_text: When all <s>dharmas</s> are empty, who is praised and by whom? //
Who can praise you, who are free from arising and perishing,

children.text: yasya nānto na madhyaṃ vā grāhyagrāho na vidyate //
children.translated_text: for whom there is no end, no middle, and no grasping of grasper [and grasped]? //

children.text: na gataṃ nāgataṃ stutvā sugataṃ gativarjitam /
children.translated_text: Having praised the <s>Sugata</s> (Well-Gone One) who has neither gone nor come, who is devoid of destination,

children.text: tena puṇyena loko 'yaṃ vrajatāṃ saugatīṃ gatim //
children.translated_text: by that merit, may this world proceed to the path of the <s>Sugata</s>! //
The glorious <s>Paramārthastavaḥ</s> (Hymn to Ultimate Reality) is complete. //

children.text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 62: Pīṭhastavaḥ
children.translated_text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 62: <s>Pīṭhastavaḥ</s>

children.text: brahmāṇī tattvarūpā vividhaghanaravā ghoracaṇḍī ca raudrī
kaumārī kīrtikāmā pibati madhumadaṃ vaiṣṇavī gāyamānā /
children.translated_text: <s>Kaumārī</s>, desiring fame, drinks honey-wine; <s>Vaiṣṇavī</s>, singing,
<s>Brahmāṇī</s>, of the form of truth, with various dense voices, and fierce <s>Caṇḍī</s>, the terrifying one,

children.text: cāmuṇḍā cāpi lakṣmīrharagaṇasahitā mātaro vaḥ punantu //
children.translated_text: and <s>Cāmuṇḍā</s>, as well as <s>Lakṣmī</s>, accompanied by the hosts of <s>Hara</s> (Śiva) — may the Mothers purify you! //
<s>Vārāhī</s>, beating sharp drums; <s>Aindrī</s> (Indrāṇī), dancing,
<s>Gaṇapati</s>, <s>Heramba</s>, <s>Vighnarāja</s> (King of Obstacles), <s>Vināyaka</s>,
the son of gods, of great valor, of great strength and prowess, //
with a great belly, with a great body, one-tusked, elephant-faced,
of white complexion, of great radiance, three-eyed, the leader of the <s>gaṇas</s> (hosts), //
with a rosary and the boon-granting [gesture] placed in the right hand,
with an axe and a skull-bowl held in the left hand, //
a god delighting in various flowers, anointed with various fragrances,
with a serpent as sacred thread, the destroyer of all obstacles — //
worshipped by gods, <s>asuras</s>, and humans, by <s>siddhas</s>, <s>gandharvas</s>, and <s>kinnaras</s>,
I bow to the destroyer of obstacles, who rides a mouse! //
<s>Brahmāṇī</s>, <s>Brahmasāvitrī</s>, the knower of <s>Brahman</s>-truth,
four-armed, four-faced, devoted to the four gods, //
pervading the four directions for a long time, the benefactress of the four ages,
seated on a swan-yoked vehicle, of gentle form, the grandmother (<s>Pitāmahī</s>), //
holding a book and a flower-garland, bearing the boon-granting and fear-dispelling [gestures],
a goddess delighting in yellow flowers, yellow-limbed, resembling yellow, //
attended with yellow offerings, anointed with yellow fragrances,
dwelling in the <s>Udumbara</s> tree, residing in the sacred field of <s>Prayāga</s> — //
eternally established in the eastern <s>pīṭha</s> (seat), homage to you, O <s>Brahmaśakti</s> (Power of Brahmā)!
<s>Māheśvarī</s>, the great goddess, the purifier of delusion and <s>māyā</s> (illusion), //
mounted upon a great bull, making the great sound of <s>Hūṃ</s>,
with a body [bright] like gold and pearls, with a skull and crescent moon as crest-ornament, //
three-eyed, bearing a trident, with a rosary and water-vessel,
with all limbs adorned with various ornaments, granting boons with the right [hand], //
the sovereign of sovereigns over creation, preservation, and destruction in every way,
a goddess delighting in white flowers, anointed with white fragrances, //
wearing white garments, adorned with <s>mudrā</s>-ornaments,
dwelling in the <s>Tāla</s> tree in the great sacred field of <s>Vārāṇasī</s> — //

children.text: uttare saṃsthitā pīṭhe māheśvarī namo 'stu te /
children.translated_text: established in the northern <s>pīṭha</s>, homage to you, O <s>Māheśvarī</s>!
<s>Kaumārī</s>, greatly fierce in youthful form, with red eyes, //
a goddess bearing red complexion, with a body ruddy as vermillion,
four-armed, bearing a spear, a rosary-thread, and a <s>siddha</s>-vessel, auspicious, //
<s>Kaumārī</s>, the supreme <s>śakti</s> (power), riding upon a peacock-vehicle,
wearing red garments, subsisting on red flesh, //
dwelling in the <s>vaṭa</s> (banyan) tree in the great sacred field of <s>Kolāpura</s>,

children.text: agnipīṭhasthitā nityaṃ kaumārī te namo namaḥ //
children.translated_text: eternally established in the <s>pīṭha</s> of fire — homage, homage to you, O <s>Kaumārī</s>! //
<s>Vaiṣṇavī</s>, the <s>māyā</s> (illusion) of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the destroyer of the fiercely arrogant <s>Daityas</s>,
with limbs of green-dark complexion, seated upon <s>Garuḍa</s>, //
bearing conch, discus, and mace in hand, adorned with four arms,
with red flames, of great sport, adorned with various ornaments, //
with green flower-fragrance, wearing green garments,
dwelling in the <s>Kadamba</s> tree in the great sacred field of <s>Aṭṭahāsa</s>, //

children.text: svarge martye ca pātāle sthitirūpeṇa saṃsthitā /
children.translated_text: abiding in the form of stability in heaven, on earth, and in the netherworld,
standing in the southwestern <s>pīṭha</s> — homage to you, O <s>Nārāyaṇī</s>! //
<s>Vārāhī</s>, of fiercely red limbs, red-haired, great-bellied,
deep-voiced with fangs, red-eyed, three-eyed, //
wearing a garland-necklace of skulls, adorned with multicolored flowers,
mounted upon a great boar, with splendor equal to blazing fire, //
adorned with a goad, a flaying knife, a staff, and bone-ornaments,
three-eyed, with a blazing body, the destroyer of the pride of the wicked, //
situated in the sacred field of <s>Jayantī</s>, sheltered by a <s>Nimba</s> (neem) tree,

children.text: yāmyapīṭhe sthitā nityaṃ kolarūpī namo 'stu te //
children.translated_text: eternally established in the southern <s>pīṭha</s> — homage to you, O <s>Kolarūpī</s> (Boar-Form)! //
<s>Śakreśvarī</s> (Indra's sovereign), thousand-eyed, with a body ruddy as saffron,
the sovereign of the gods, goddess of gods, adorned with all ornaments, //
four-armed, wide-eyed, bearing a parasol and a bell,
the great <s>vajra</s>-bearing goddess, standing upon <s>Airāvata</s> elephant, //
a goddess delighting in various flowers, adorned with various jewels,
with limbs smeared with various fragrances, resplendent in various garments, //
established in the <s>Karañja</s> tree in the great sacred field of <s>Cīra</s> (or <s>Cīna</s>),
eternally established in the <s>pīṭha</s> of the serpent — homage to you, O <s>Śakreśvarī</s>! //
<s>Cāmuṇḍā</s>, <s>Caṇḍikā</s>, <s>Caṇḍī</s>, the fiercely beautiful among the gods,
with fierce laughter, fierce-eyed, destroyer of the fiercely fierce, //
with terrible fangs, red-bodied, tawny-haired, great-bellied,
emaciated, terrifying, dreadful, fearsome with a lolling tongue, //
mounted upon a great corpse-seat, resplendent with eight arms,
bearing a sword and shield in hands, holding a <s>ḍamaru</s> (drum) and a <s>khaṭvāṅga</s> (skull-staff), //
with a flaying knife and skull-cup in hand, adorned with boon-granting and fear-dispelling [gestures],
with all limbs adorned with bone-ornaments, fond of the blood of enemies, //
radiant as a thousand suns, in every pit [of suffering],
enveloped in a garland of flames, with splendor equal to ten million suns, //
<s>Bhūtas</s> (ghosts), <s>Vetālas</s> (vampires), and <s>Ḍākinīs</s> are her retinue, along with <s>Rākṣasas</s>;
dwelling in the <s>Aśvattha</s> (sacred fig) tree in the great sacred field of <s>Ekamākṣa</s>,
established in the <s>pīṭha</s> of the wind-region — homage to <s>Cāmuṇḍā</s>! //
<s>Mahālakṣmī</s>, the great goddess, rich in enjoyments, beautiful in virtues,
wearing <s>vaidūrya</s> (lapis lazuli) sandals, seated on a lion-throne, of great wisdom, //
four-armed, wide-eyed, bearing a sword and a shield,
the goddess bearing a vessel and a <s>bindu</s> (drop), with half-garland and earrings, //
with all limbs studded with jewels, adorned with a crest-jewel,
with variegated flower-jewels, and fragrant garment-ointments, //
the goddess pervading the three worlds, present everywhere, in the moving and unmoving,
bowed to by <s>Siddhas</s> and <s>Gandharvas</s>, worshipped by <s>Vidyādharas</s> and gods, //
the excellent and powerful one, established in the <s>Plakṣa</s> (fig) tree in the great sacred field of <s>Devīkoṭa</s>,
established in the <s>pīṭha</s> of <s>Īśāna</s> (northeast) — homage to <s>Mahālakṣmī</s>! //
O Mother of all <s>Buddhas</s>, the one who produces satisfaction in all,
you yourself are of all forms, you yourself are of universal form. //
Terrifying, dreadful, fierce, of terrible and profound form,
with a body pure as the stainless one, a great festival of all desires, //
covered with many arms, bearing various garments, auspicious,
with tawny hair on half the head, with radiance like a forest fire, //
three-eyed, of great splendor, with radiance equal to fire and sun,

children.text: triśūlaṃ muṇḍaṃ khaṭvāṅgaṃ ḍamaruṃ tarjanīṃ dhvajam //
children.translated_text: bearing a trident, a skull, a <s>khaṭvāṅga</s> (skull-staff), a <s>ḍamaru</s> (drum), a threatening finger, and a banner, //
wisdom (<s>Prajñā</s>) and a book, and also bearing a sword and a shield, auspicious,
the god bearing a noose and a goad, the great bearer of a <s>vajra</s>-needle, //
a skull-cup, a flaying knife, and a discus, wrapped in an elephant-hide,
with a face terrible with fangs, with waist wrapped in a tiger-skin, //
with all limbs adorned with ornaments, beautiful with human bone-flowers,
the goddess bearing a garland of heads, [dwelling in] the auspicious hollow of skulls, //
with a crest-jewel of great radiance, with a skull adorned by the moon,
always [seated] on a great corpse-seat, always led forth as the beloved, //
radiant as a thousand suns, endowed with a parasol and <s>bindu</s> (drop),
eternally established in the four <s>pīṭhas</s>, dwelling in the eight sacred fields, //
the goddess established in eight forms, dear to the eight <s>yoginīs</s>,
eternally established in the auspicious <s>pīṭha</s>, surrounded by <s>Bhadrakālī</s>, //
you are the cause of auspiciousness — homage to you, O <s>Vīrabhadra</s>!
<s>Asitāṅga</s>, <s>Ruru</s>, <s>Caṇḍa</s>, and <s>Krodha Bhairava</s>, //
and <s>Unmatta Bhairava</s>, <s>Kapālī</s>, the terrifying one,
and <s>Saṃhāra Bhairava</s> — homage to the eight <s>Bhairavas</s>! //
Established in their own places, in their own offices, in their own forms, with their own heroes,
with their own pure trees spread out — along with the divine eye, and the earth-dwellers. //
To the protectors of fields in the ten directions, and the fourteen sacred fields,
to the fifty field-protectors — O <s>Kṣetrapāla</s> (Field-Protector), homage to you! //
O Lord, Lord of lords, great Lord, primordial Lord, O great-minded one,
O glorious Lord, <s>Siddhanātha</s>, <s>Mīnanātha</s> — homage to you! //
O Lord of sacred fields, Lord of sacred seats, Lord of islands, O great soul,
O Lord of ghosts, Lord of spirits, <s>Baḍhanātha</s> — homage to you! //
To the three Lords, the nine Lords, and the supreme sixteen Lords,
to the twenty-seven, fifty, and eighty-four — homage to you! //
Of all the accomplished Lords, you are the eternal eye and doctrine;

children.text: potasadma tathā vīrastataḥ sarva namo 'stu te //
children.translated_text: the vessel-dwelling one and also the hero — to all, homage to you! //

children.text: ekavāraṃ dvivāraṃ ca trivāraṃ yaḥ paṭhennaraḥ /
children.translated_text: He who recites [this] once, twice, or thrice,
or revolves it a hundred times, obtains the supreme fruit. //
It destroys grief, worry, and the like; it destroys the circle of obstacles;
it destroys disease and quarrels; it destroys suffering and hardship. //
It destroys fear and poverty; it destroys fear arising from enemies;
it destroys [harm from] fire, thieves, and the like; it destroys that arising from royal wrath. //
It destroys terrible conflict and hostile sorcery (<s>abhicāra</s>) performed by others;
it destroys hatred, passion, and the like; it destroys all sins. //
It increases life, health, sovereignty, wealth, and grain;
it increases fame and good fortune for [the attainment of] <s>dharma</s>, <s>artha</s> (wealth), <s>kāma</s> (desire), and <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation). //

children.text: ṛddhiṃ siddhiṃ śriyaṃ lakṣmīṃ vidyāṃ jñānaṃ sutādi ca /
children.translated_text: Supernatural powers, accomplishments, prosperity, <s>Lakṣmī</s> (fortune), knowledge, wisdom, sons and the rest,

children.text: buddhiṃ prajāṃ sumitrāṇi vardhayecca dine dine //
children.translated_text: intelligence, progeny, good friends — it increases [all these] day by day. //

children.text: nākāle maraṇaṃ caiva utpātaṃ nāśayet sadā /
children.translated_text: There is no untimely death, and it always destroys calamities;
all diseases are pacified, and long life is obtained. //
The glorious <s>Śrīpīṭhastava</s> hymn is complete. //

children.text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 63: Potalakāṣṭakam
children.translated_text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 63: <s>Potalakāṣṭakam</s> (Eight Verses on Potalaka)
Victory! To the guru of <s>Siddhas</s>, gods, <s>Asuras</s>, and the world, whose pair of feet rests on a lotus seat,
who holds a lotus adorned with the ten <s>pāramitās</s> and more — I always bow to the supreme compassionate one. //
Who has obtained boons from many <s>koṭis</s> (millions) of kings of men — victory to the well-established Lord, the <s>Muni</s>!
Who has crossed beyond the ocean of existence, the supreme authority, the one who accomplishes the welfare of beings who seek refuge. //
Who bears beautiful, excellent form on a lotus seat, who wears <s>Amitābha Tathāgata</s> on his crown,
whose excellent limbs are adorned with radiant lotuses, whose brilliance shines like the newly risen sun. //
Whose face is beautiful with soft, coppery fingernails, whose gentle face is equal in radiance to the moon's disc,
whose body is worthy of worship as a mine of the six super-knowledges and virtues, adorned with excellent anklets and necklaces. //
Whose pair of cheeks is adorned with jeweled earrings, whose deep voice is like the rumbling of thunder,
who dwells radiantly in mountain caves, who has a hundred lifespans of the bull-vehicle, the swan, and the deer. //
Praised by hosts of sages and chiefs of gods, whose nature bears the form of the <s>Jinas</s>, devoted to awakening,
the supreme among bipeds, the lord, the ruler of gods, who effects the liberation and release of many beings. //
Whose left hand is beautifully adorned with a banner and parasol, who delights in <s>Malaya</s> mountain sandalwood incense,
who wears garlands of lotuses, blue lotuses, and <s>pāṭalī</s> flowers — I bow to the one who brings the growth of <s>pāṭalī</s>. //
Who removes leprosy, freeing from fever and disease, who effects great, cloudless, auspicious awakening,
who grants the path that destroys the nine bad destinies — the lord of the universe, of compassion and <s>tathatā</s> (suchness), non-dual. //
The <s>Potalakāṣṭaka</s> (Eight Verses on Potalaka) of the noble <s>Avalokiteśvara</s> is complete. //

children.text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 64: Prajñāpāramitāstotram lakṣā bhagavatīkṛtam
children.translated_text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 65: <s>Prajñāpāramitāstotra</s> (Hymn to the Perfection of Wisdom) composed by <s>Lakṣā Bhagavatī</s>
Oṃ! Homage to the glorious <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> (Perfection of Wisdom)!
O <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, the immeasurable, free from conceptual construction — homage to you!
You whose every limb is blameless are perceived by the blameless ones. //
Unstained like the sky, beyond conceptual elaboration, beyond letters —

children.text: yastvāṃ paśyati bhāvena sa paśyati tathāgatam //
children.translated_text: he who sees you with [right] understanding sees the <s>Tathāgata</s> (Thus-Gone One). //

children.text: tava cārye guṇāḍhyāyā buddhasya ca jagadguroḥ /
children.translated_text: Between you, O Noble One rich in virtues, and the <s>Buddha</s>, guru of the world,
the good ones see no difference — as between the moon and the moonlight. //
Taking refuge in you, who are the essence of compassion, with the <s>Buddha-dharma</s> as foremost,
they easily attain incomparable greatness, O you who are loving to devotees! //
Even one who, with a pure intention, beholds you properly even once —
by that person too, accomplishment is certainly attained, O you of unfailing vision! //
Of all the heroes whose minds are devoted to the welfare of others,
you are the pervading, loving mother of this world. //
The <s>Buddhas</s>, the compassionate gurus of the world, are your sons;
therefore, O auspicious one, you are the grandmother of all beings. //
You, unblamed, [adorned] with all the pure <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections),
are strung on all sides, like the crescent moon with its stars. //
Having reached the beings to be trained, by the <s>Tathāgatas</s> in each place,
you alone, though one, are seen in many forms under many names. //
Just as dewdrops inevitably [vanish] upon reaching the rays of the blazing sun,

children.text: tvāṃ prāpya pralayaṃ yānti doṣāvādāśca vādinām //
children.translated_text: so upon reaching you, the faults and objections of disputants dissolve. //
You yourself are the cause of terror to the childish, being fearsome in appearance,
and also the cause of reassurance to the wise, being gentle in appearance. //
Even your lord (<s>Buddha</s>) has no attachment to you;
O Mother! How then could passion and hatred exist elsewhere [in relation to you]? //
You come from nowhere, and you go nowhere;
in any place whatsoever, you are not apprehended by the wise. //

children.text: ye tvāmeva na paśyanti prapadyante ca bhāvataḥ /
children.translated_text: Those who do not see you [directly] yet take refuge [in you] with devotion,
and having taken refuge are liberated — this is a great marvel! //
Seeing you, one is bound; not seeing, one is not bound;
seeing you, one is liberated; not seeing, one is not liberated. //
Ah, you are wondrous! You are profound, O illustrious one!

children.text: sudurbodhāsi māyeva dṛśyase na ca dṛśyase //
children.translated_text: You are most difficult to comprehend — like an illusion, you are seen yet not seen. //
Resorted to by <s>Buddhas</s>, <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, and <s>Śrāvakas</s> —
you are the sole path to liberation; there is no other — this is certain. //
For the sake of conventional designation and the meaning of terms for embodied beings,
out of compassion, by the protectors of the world, you are spoken of — and yet you are not spoken of. //
Who here is able to praise you, who are without any cause, without any stain?
You who transcend the range of all, you who rest nowhere. //
Even so, by conventional means, with words of such meaning, we,
having praised you who are beyond praise, are well satisfied in having praised. //
Having praised the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, whatever merit has been accumulated by me —
by that, may the entire world quickly become devoted to the far shore of wisdom! //
The <s>Prajñāpāramitāstotra</s> composed by the glorious <s>Lakṣā Bhagavatī</s> is complete. //

children.text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 65: Prajñāpāramitāstutiḥ
children.translated_text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 65: <s>Prajñāpāramitāstuti</s> (Praise of the Perfection of Wisdom)
Oṃ! Homage to the glorious <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>!
O you who are free from conceptual construction, without support, faultless, unstained,

children.text: nityānitye nirvikāre prajñe devi namo 'stu te //
children.translated_text: eternal yet non-eternal, unchanging — O Goddess <s>Prajñā</s> (Wisdom), homage to you! //
O Queen, mother of the <s>Buddhas</s>, grandmother of the <s>Bodhisattvas</s>,

children.text: prapitāmahi sattvānāṃ prajñe devi namo 'stu te //
children.translated_text: great-grandmother of all beings — O Goddess <s>Prajñā</s>, homage to you! //
Of those people who constantly call out 'Mother, Mother, Mother of the world!' —

children.text: manorathaprade śuddhe prajñe devi namo 'stu te //
children.translated_text: O pure granter of wishes — O Goddess <s>Prajñā</s>, homage to you! //

children.text: lakṣmīstvamasi kalyāṇi śrīrdhīḥ śraddhā dhṛtiḥ smṛtiḥ /
children.translated_text: You are <s>Lakṣmī</s>, you are auspicious, you are <s>Śrī</s> (glory), intelligence, faith, steadfastness, memory;

children.text: sarvasvarūpe sarveśi prajñe devi namo 'stu te //
children.translated_text: O you of all forms, O ruler of all — O Goddess <s>Prajñā</s>, homage to you! //
In the supramundane and the mundane, O <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, the immeasurable,

children.text: daśa pāramitākāre prajñe devi namo 'stu te //
children.translated_text: embodiment of the ten <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections) — O Goddess <s>Prajñā</s>, homage to you! //
The glorious <s>Prajñāpāramitāstuti</s> (Praise of the Perfection of Wisdom) is complete. //

children.text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 66: Pratisarāstotram
children.translated_text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 66: <s>Pratisarāstotra</s> (Hymn to Pratisarā)
Oṃ! Homage to the glorious <s>Pratisarā</s>! O <s>Pratisarā</s>!

children.text: amaraughaiḥ pūjitāṃ tvāṃ nato 'smi pratipadajanarakṣākāriṇīṃ sarvakālam /
children.translated_text: Worshipped by hosts of immortals, I bow to you, who at every step protect beings at all times,
who protect in the suffering of falling from cliffs, fires, and oceans, who destroy enemies, poison, and fear, who bestow sovereignty and enjoyments! //
Surrounded by her own retinue, granting liberation to the devoted, destroying the company of evils, the sole path to the attainment of liberation,
the creator of the assemblies of men and gods, the causer of the destruction of <s>Anaṅga</s> (Kāma, the god of love), whose praises are the roar of sages, the sole companion of all protection. //
Who has removed all obstacles, the sole honored one of all worlds, made fortunate by the ten powers, the best among the five goddesses,

children.text: viṣamapadaśaraṇye sarvadā tvāṃ namasye vasita iva araṇye dāvadagdhe virasye //
children.translated_text: the refuge in dangerous places — I always bow to you, as one dwelling in a forest burned by wildfire, weary. //
A wish-fulfilling cow in fulfilling the desires of all people, the foremost vine of the wish-fulfilling tree for obtaining desired fruits,
whose pair of lotus-feet is worshipped by <s>Asuras</s>, gods, humans, and others, adorned on her chest with graceful garlands of various jewels. //
Brilliant as a hundred moons, white as conch and <s>kunda</s> flowers, who pacifies the fear of planets, whose nature is <s>Vajrasattva</s> —

children.text: śravaṇalalitalole kuṇḍale saṃvahantīṃ mukuṭamaṇiśikhābhiḥ kāśitāṃ tāṃ namāmi //
children.translated_text: who wears earrings gracefully swaying at her ears, who shines with the rays of crown-jewels — to her I bow. //

children.text: sapadi vigatarakṣāṃ rakṣa me mātaraṃ ca /
children.translated_text: Protect at once me who is without protection, and my mother too!
O Mother, you who rescue from all suffering — be gracious!
who has fallen into a lake — you are my refuge, you are the refuge of our boat! //
Me, weeping with compassion, made well by your mercy,
from the fear of fire, water, poison, thieves, and tigers,
Whoever recites this hymn to <s>Pratisarā</s> always,
at every step she unbreaks the broken, granting the attainment of courage to those who desire it. //
and from [fear of] those bearing disease and death, she destroys —
freed from hosts of enemies, enjoying nothing but happiness,
Surrounded by her own people, increased in <s>dharma</s>, <s>kāma</s>, and <s>artha</s>,
having destroyed all sins, in the end they attain <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation). //
she bestows abundant enjoyments, granting desires always;
thus he offered praise to the mother of the three worlds;
With tears flowing from his eyes, hands folded, lamenting,

children.text: bhavatu mama tu saṃpat sarvabhāvā kṛśāno

children.translated_text: May my body be well protected by virtue' — thus, with a pure mind: //
'May prosperity of every kind come to me, of all forms, O Fire!

children.text: vipacatu mayi sarvaṃ mādṛśaṃ karma bhogyaṃ

children.translated_text: of those with gods and humans as their assembly, those hostile to brothers and mothers;
'May all experienceable <s>karma</s> of beings such as me ripen in me,

children.text: kuruta kuruta dhairyaṃ yena mokṣaṃ sulabhyaṃ

children.translated_text: may there never be sin in the dwelling of the womb!' //
make, make courage! By which liberation is easily attained;
with an ever-virtuous, pure mind — I shall accomplish awakening;
'Those who dwell in the hell of the belly, they with their descent,
thus, with a joyful, pure mind, his consciousness anointed by [wholesome] <s>karma</s>. //
having effected protection for the world, by which the attainment of <s>kaivalya</s> (absolute liberation)' —
thus speaking constantly, he censured his own <s>karma</s>;
'O <s>Pratisarā</s>, bring down the divine descent with the Mother — do not delay!' —

children.text: muhuriha hi śaraṇyāṃ tāṃ smaran sarvarakṣām //
children.translated_text: repeatedly here remembered her, the refuge, the all-protector. //
that child, standing [still], anointed with the poison of fear,
Ah! How fortunate is the sole Mother of the world! With destiny advanced, feared by hosts of enemies —
by whose power, from even the most grievous sin, fire attains the coolness of water. //

children.text: prabhāvatāho punareva tasyāḥ vahniṃ jalaṃ cāpi giriṃ sthalaṃ vai /
children.translated_text: Ah, the power again of that one! Fire, water, mountain, and dry land indeed —

children.text: yasyāḥ smṛtenaiva savismatīyān vaiśvānaraḥ prāpa dvidhākṛtiṃ tām //
children.translated_text: by whose mere remembrance, with amazement, the universal fire (<s>Vaiśvānara</s>) attained a twofold form! //
The cowherd's body, cold from falling into a lake, cold as if for the purpose of destruction, exceedingly hot,
given by fate to his kinsmen on all sides — [she rescued the one] given over to extreme sin from far away. //
The <s>Pratisarāstotra</s>, extracted from the glorious <s>Bhadrakalpāvadāna</s>, composed by the child in <s>Yaśodharā's</s> womb, is complete. //

children.text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 67: Rakṣākāla(kara)stavaḥ
children.translated_text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 67: <s>Rakṣākāla(kara)stava</s> (Hymn of Protection-Making)
Oṃ! Homage to <s>Lokanātha</s> (Lord of the World)!
The sins committed by me through accumulations of body, speech, and mind —

children.text: tatsarvaṃ hara me nātha rakṣa māṃ lokanāyaka //
children.translated_text: all that, remove for me, O Lord — protect me, O Guide of the World! //
In <s>Nepāla</s>, for twelve years there was drought, a great calamity;
having established <s>Narendradeva</s> [as king] — protect me, O Guide of the World! //
In the realm of mortals and in the netherworld, many worldly beings suffer;
O you who increase their happiness — protect me, O Guide of the World! //
Wherever you have gone, there, out of compassion for all beings,
you lift them up from sins — protect me, O Guide of the World! //

children.text: saṃsāre vyāpito 'haṃ tu kathaṃ pāraṃ prayāsyate /
children.translated_text: I am entangled in <s>saṃsāra</s> (cyclic existence) — how shall I cross to the other shore?

children.text: tvameva śaraṇaṃ tatra rakṣa māṃ lokanāyaka //
children.translated_text: You alone are my refuge there — protect me, O <s>Lokanāyaka</s> (Leader of the World)! //
You are the embodiment of all gods, and the embodiment of all <s>Buddhas</s>;
you are the embodiment of all <s>siddhis</s> (accomplishments) — protect me, O <s>Lokanāyaka</s>! //

children.text: sadā kṛpāmayastvaṃ hi sadā rakṣāmayo 'si ca /
children.translated_text: You are always full of compassion, you are always full of protection,

children.text: sadā prajñāmayastvaṃ hi rakṣa māṃ lokanāyaka //
children.translated_text: you are always full of wisdom — protect me, O <s>Lokanāyaka</s>! //

children.text: yena yena kṛtaṃ karma tena tenaiva dhāritam /
children.translated_text: Whatever action has been done, by that very means it has been sustained;
whatever wish you grant — protect me, O <s>Lokanāyaka</s>! //
As long as all beings have not reached <s>Sukhāvatī</s> (the Blissful Realm),
so long in this pit of <s>saṃsāra</s> — protect me, O <s>Lokanāyaka</s>! //
For the wise you are the form of wisdom; for the suffering you are the remover of suffering;
for those with desires you are the form of desire — protect me, O <s>Lokanāyaka</s>! //
You are worthy of worship, O Lord of the World, bearing the very nature of <s>Praṇava</s> (<s>Oṃ</s>);

children.text: vandanīyaḥ sadā tvaṃ hi rakṣa māṃ lokanāyaka //
children.translated_text: you are always worthy of veneration — protect me, O <s>Lokanāyaka</s>! //

children.text: bharti vā bhartiko vāpi mitraṃ vā śatruko 'pi vā /
children.translated_text: Whether master or servant, whether friend or foe —

children.text: sarvatra ca dayāyukto rakṣa māṃ lokanāyaka //
children.translated_text: you are endowed with compassion toward all — protect me, O <s>Lokanāyaka</s>! //
O <s>Lokanātha</s> (Lord of the World), O Sovereign of the Universe, with a mind made of pure devotion,

children.text: tvāṃ namāmi punarbhūyo rakṣa māṃ lokanāyaka //
children.translated_text: I bow to you again and again — protect me, O <s>Lokanāyaka</s>! //
I am the recipient of countless sufferings, beset by terrible hardships and distress;

children.text: dayasva cāvalokeśa mocayasva ca māṃ kṣaṇāt //
children.translated_text: have compassion, O <s>Avalokeśa</s> (Avalokiteśvara), and free me at once! //
Always keeping your gaze for the arrival of [those in need], make my [merits] inexhaustible;

children.text: astu te karuṇā mahyaṃ bhaktiṃ caivācalāṃ kuru //
children.translated_text: may your compassion be upon me, and make my devotion unshakable! //
The protective hymn of praise to the glorious noble lord <s>Āryāvalokiteśvara</s> is complete. //

children.text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 68: Ratnamālāstotram
children.translated_text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 68: Ratnamālāstotram
Composed by <s>Ācārya Vanaratnapāda</s>. To <s>Lokeśvara</s> (Lord of the World):
whose mind is moist with compassion born of pure emptiness, whose speech conveys meaning through teachings renowned for knowledge of the path,
whose pure body is complete with omniscience and other [qualities], who is graceful through the authority of wisdom — I bow with my head! //
Because, though one, you appear in many reflections according to the variety of those to be trained, like the moon in water-vessels —
you are perceived as intent solely on the welfare of others; therefore, O <s>Buddha</s>-nature, your form is supremely astonishing! //
In your moon-full face, graceful, from the forehead-region arose the divine son <s>Maheśvara</s> (Śiva);
for the purpose of awakening the followers of <s>Śiva</s>, you, O Lord among the gods, are the supreme <s>Īśvara</s>! //

children.text: vaineyakomalabhavapratibodhanāya kiṃ dhāma saṃbhṛta mahāśubhalakṣaṇaṃ te /
children.translated_text: For the awakening of the gentle beings to be trained — what a radiance yours, endowed with the great auspicious marks!

children.text: niryāta eva hi pitāmahadevapūjāṃ lokeśvareśvaraparaṃ śirasā namāmi //
children.translated_text: Having come forth indeed for the worship of the grandfather-god (<s>Brahmā</s>) — I bow with my head to the supreme lord <s>Lokeśvara</s>! //
For the awakening of the Vaiṣṇava followers to be trained, he emerged from the heart of the Lotus-handed one (<s>Padmapāṇi</s>) —

children.text: nārāyaṇo 'pi bhuvaneśvara eva tasmāt puṃsāṃ tvameva paramottama eva nānyaḥ //
children.translated_text: he is <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> himself, the Lord of the World; therefore, you alone are the supreme among beings, none other! //
For showing [himself] to those devoted with reverence to the sun and moon, from his two beautifully dark eyes like blue elephants,

children.text: yanniḥsṛtau śaśiravī bhuvi locanābhyāṃ dhvastāntarālatamasaṃ tamahaṃ namāmi //
children.translated_text: from which the moon and sun came forth upon the earth from his eyes, dispelling the darkness in between — him I worship! //
For the awakening of those devoted to learning and discipline, here the blessed <s>Sarasvatī</s>
was seen before you, born from the son of the <s>Jina</s> (Victor) — the giver of the fruit of the desire for wisdom — him I worship! //
For accomplishing the path of syllables produced by the wind among those to be trained, the <s>Sugata</s> (Well-gone One), O <s>Lokanātha</s>, came forth —

children.text: devaḥ samīraṇavaro bhuvi janmabhājāmīryāpathārthaphaladaṃ tamahaṃ namāmi //
children.translated_text: that excellent wind-god upon earth for those who have taken birth, the giver of the fruit of the four modes of conduct — him I worship! //
For the awakening of those desiring the auspicious path of <s>Varuṇa</s> among those to be trained, from the belly of the sons of the <s>Sugata</s>,
the excellent god <s>Varuṇa</s> came forth suddenly — the giver of the fruit of sovereign power — him I worship! //
For the accomplishment of those desiring fruits approved by those to be trained, from the excellent lotus-feet bearing supreme marks,

children.text: yanniḥsṛtā bhagavatī dharaṇī prasiddhā trailokyanāthamasamaṃ satataṃ namāmi //
children.translated_text: the blessed <s>Dharaṇī</s> (Earth Goddess) came forth, renowned — I constantly bow to the peerless Lord of the Three Worlds! //

children.text: saṃsāramuktamapi susthitameva tatra kāruṇyataśca bhavacāriṇi sattvavarge /
children.translated_text: Even though liberated from <s>saṃsāra</s>, remaining well-established there, and through compassion among beings wandering in existence —

children.text: bhūyāt sthitirmama sadāsthirasā bhavantamevaṃ mahāśayavaraṃ paramaṃ namāmi //
children.translated_text: may my abiding always be steadfast toward you; thus I bow supremely to the excellent great-souled one! //
With a single sole of your foot, in the world-realm within the <s>Cakra</s>-<s>Saṃvara</s> [enclosure],
in a world burned at the end of a <s>kalpa</s> (cosmic age), the blazing fierce fire would be extinguished by the force of the wind of your breath. //

children.text: svāṃ tarjanīṃ mukhadhṛto 'hitatarjanena saṃcālitāśca bahumerugaṇā nakhasya /
children.translated_text: Holding his forefinger in his mouth, threatening the wicked, the many <s>Meru</s>-mountains are shaken by [the point of] his nail;

children.text: koṣoddhṛtaṃ jaladhitoyamaśeṣataḥ syāt sāmarthyamīdṛśamaho bhavataḥ kuto 'nyat //
children.translated_text: the water of the ocean would be entirely drawn out as from a sheath — such is his power! Ah, from whom else could it come? //

children.text: kvedaṃ ca śaiśavaparaṃ nanu cārurupaṃ saṃdarśanīyavarakomalabālacandram /
children.translated_text: Where is this supremely charming childlike form, beautiful as a tender young moon fit to behold,

children.text: durvāramāramathanaṃ ca mayaikasahyaṃ vikrāntaduḥsahaparaṃ kva ca ceṣṭitaṃ te //
children.translated_text: and where is your irresistible feat of crushing <s>Māra</s>, endured by me alone, supremely difficult to bear? //
Behold! That row of dark collyrium-black curls, charmingly twisted and wild, at the tips of your own hair —

children.text: kleśendhane jvalitavisphuritatvavahnerdhūmāvalīva vimalā nanu lakṣyate te //
children.translated_text: is it not perceived as a pure trail of smoke from your fire blazing and sparking in the fuel of the <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions)? //
A fraction of your radiance, pure, spreading in all ten directions — the full beauty of the desired moon, waning thin in the dark fortnight —

children.text: paryanta iṣṭaśaśino bhavaneṣu yatte manye virāji nikhilaṃ tava kāntileśāt //
children.translated_text: whatever shines in the worlds, I consider all of it to be a mere fraction of your radiance. //

children.text: bandhurhi ko mārgikasaṃmataṃ mataṃ naro narī sā sa ca satpathaṃ patham /
children.translated_text: Who is the kinsman? The doctrine accepted by those on the path. What is a [true] man or woman? One [who follows] the good path.
The best vow is that undertaken for the benefit of others — I bow to the <s>Jina</s> (Victor), the Lord-King of the Earth (<s>Bhūmīśvara</s>)! //
Established firmly in the station of impermanent <s>Nirvāṇa</s>, the beneficial composition presided over by luminosity,

children.text: śamīkṛtāśeṣajanaṃ śivaṃ śivaṃ namāmi bhūmīśvararājinaṃ jinam //
children.translated_text: having pacified all beings, auspicious, ever auspicious — I bow to the <s>Jina</s>, the Lord-King of the Earth! //

children.text: gabhastimālāmitasaṃkulaṃ kulaṃ tatra svapāṇau dhṛtapaṅkajaṃ kajam /
children.translated_text: His lineage resplendent with garlands of rays, holding a lotus in his own hand,
adorned and delighting with the following of jewels — I bow to the <s>Jina</s>, the Lord-King of the Earth! //
His own <s>Dharmadhātu</s> (realm of reality), supreme in compassion, well-filled with the accumulation of merit and other [qualities],

children.text: vikalpahīnaṃ dhvanideśakaṃ śakaṃ namāmi bhūmīśvarājinaṃ jinam //
children.translated_text: free from conceptual elaboration, the teacher of truth with power — I bow to the <s>Jina</s>, the Lord-King of the Earth! //
Hundreds [of teachings] stilled by the non-duality of <s>Tathatā</s> (Suchness) and its [manifestation], the <s>Dharma</s>-discourse fulfilling the real and the unreal,
supreme in the truth adorned by what is to be spoken — I bow to the excellent Lord-King of the Earth! //
In the form of an excellent lotus, pervading the world, most beautiful with lotus-eyes,
supreme in the purity of essence even swiftly — I bow to the excellent Lord-King of the Earth! //
Delighting in the welfare of others through excellent created enjoyments, holding the <s>Dharma</s> of emptiness, unstained, delightful,
supreme in accomplishments adorned by the Lord of the Earth — I bow to the excellent Lord-King of the Earth! //
With a moon-face of excellent innate truth, whose well-spoken words are the station of liberation for beings,
supreme in the marks that adorn his feet — I bow to the excellent Lord-King of the Earth! //
O <s>Lokeśvara</s>! This jewel-garland for you was composed by the glorious <s>Vanaratnapāda</s>;

children.text: avāpi yattena śubhapraviṣṭaṃ tenaiva loko 'stu samantabhadraḥ //
children.translated_text: may the merit entered thereby make the world entirely <s>Samantabhadra</s> (all-good)! //
The <s>Ratnamālāstotra</s> (Jewel-garland Hymn) to the glorious noble lord <s>Āryāvalokiteśvara</s> is complete. //

children.text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 69: Rūpastavaḥ
children.translated_text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 69: Rūpastavaḥ

children.text: sarvabhūtamaṇikampita tubhyaṃ kṣāntimeva caritaṃ tava rūpam /
children.translated_text: All beings tremble [in reverence] — to you who have practiced forbearance as your very form,
the most excellent divine form among all forms — I bow to the excellent form of the Ten-powered One (<s>Daśabala</s>)! //
Hair beautiful as the crest of the king of bees (<s>bhṛṅgarāja</s>), divinely beautiful hair like the crest of a cuckoo,
glossy, dark, soft, and curling hair — I bow to the excellent hair of the <s>Daśabala</s>! //
Body-hair [white as] conch, jasmine, and night-lily, free from the suffering of birth, free from [coarse] body-hair,
free from disease and sorrow, free from [coarse] body-hair — I bow to the excellent body-hair of the <s>Daśabala</s>! //
Face adorned with the radiance of the full moon, face auspicious with a high nose shining like a jewel,
face immortal like a <s>Buddha</s>-lotus — I bow to the excellent face of the <s>Daśabala</s>! //
Crown variegated with thousands of rays, crown worshipped with hundreds of showers of flowers,
crown worshipped with hundreds of showers of jewels — I bow to the excellent crown of the <s>Daśabala</s>! //
Head from which eye-banners hang, head upon which golden parasols are placed,
head beautifully adorned with eye-canopies — I bow to the excellent head of the <s>Daśabala</s>! //
A crown of divine cloth, a jewel crown, a crown of moonlight radiance and jewels,
come upon the head, an unbroken crown — I bow to the excellent crown of the <s>Daśabala</s>! //
Eyes [beautiful] as lotuses with charming petals, wide, eyes vast and wide with divine knowledge,
eyes well-fashioned with <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation) and <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation) — I bow to the excellent eyes of the <s>Daśabala</s>! //
Pure ears, auspicious, beautifully pure ears, ears adorned with excellent pure wisdom,
ears of excellent pure knowledge, beautifully pure — I bow to the excellent ears of the <s>Daśabala</s>! //
Teeth [white as] bright jasmine, moon, and lotus, teeth sharp, well-marked, and spotless,
twenty-five beautiful teeth of the universe — I bow to the excellent teeth of the <s>Daśabala</s>! //
A tongue of lofty speech among gods and <s>Asuras</s>, a tongue that has destroyed sin through the knowledge of <s>Dharma</s>,
a tongue [sweet as] fragrance and incense among gods and <s>Asuras</s> — I bow to the excellent tongue of the <s>Daśabala</s>! //
A voice sounding like clouds and great drums, a voice well-known for the true path of <s>Dharma</s>,
a voice resounding with divine and supreme eloquence — I bow to the excellent voice of the <s>Daśabala</s>! //
A neck, a beautiful neck among [all] ten necks, your beautiful neck of patience and vigor,
a beautiful neck [shining] like gold and jewels — I bow to the excellent neck of the <s>Daśabala</s>! //
A body [powerful as] a lion, [white as] snow and jasmine, a body that is an ocean of the qualities of the <s>dhyāna</s>-body,
a body spotless with the eighty excellent marks — I bow to the excellent body of the <s>Daśabala</s>! //
Garment adorned with auspicious white and red, garment colored in blue, yellow, and green,
garment beautifully adorned with dazzling white necklaces — I bow to the excellent garment of the <s>Daśabala</s>! //
Arms fashioned like golden serpent-trunks, arms adorned with the offering of flowers,
arms captivating with steadfast vigor — I bow to the excellent arms of the <s>Daśabala</s>! //
Hands adorned with fly-whisks and discus, hands pure, soft as lotuses,
hands that are the refuge of <s>Bhūtas</s> (ghosts) and <s>Pretas</s> (hungry ghosts) — I bow to the excellent hands of the <s>Daśabala</s>! //
A mind free from the body of passion and hatred, a mind cultivated equally for tens of millions of <s>kalpas</s> (cosmic ages),
a mind cultivated equally with morality and wisdom — I bow to the excellent mind of the <s>Daśabala</s>! //
A navel adorned auspiciously like a lotus-navel, a navel adorned auspiciously like a lotus-womb,
a navel beautifully adorned with the light of <s>Brahmā</s> — I bow to the excellent navel of the <s>Daśabala</s>! //
Feet adorned with the excellent mark of a wheel, feet resplendent with the goad and <s>śakti</s> (spear),
feet worshipped by hosts of <s>Nāgas</s> and <s>Yakṣas</s> — I bow to the excellent feet of the <s>Daśabala</s>! //
Feet radiant with the splendor of the sun, feet worshipped by hosts of gods and <s>Dānavas</s>,
feet worshipped by all the hosts of gods — I bow to the excellent feet of the <s>Daśabala</s>! //
Head worshipped by all the hosts of gods, head resplendent as tens of millions of suns,
head ablaze with divine radiant flames — I bow to the excellent head of the <s>Daśabala</s>! //
Head worshipped with hundreds of flowers and incenses, head worshipped with hundreds of lamps and fragrances,
head worshipped with hundreds of garlands and garments — I bow to the excellent head of the <s>Daśabala</s>! //
Worshipped with the <s>uṣṇīṣa</s> (crown-protuberance) of the threefold-world <s>Dharma</s>-art, with jewel parasols, crowns, and the like —

children.text: ye paṭhanti sugatastavamenaṃ te labhanti śubhamokṣapathādhigamam //
children.translated_text: those who recite this hymn to the <s>Sugata</s> (Well-gone One) obtain the attainment of the auspicious path of liberation. //
The <s>Rūpastava</s> (Hymn to the Form) of the glorious noble lord <s>Āryāvalokiteśvara</s> is complete. //

children.text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 70: Ṣaḍabhijñastotram
children.translated_text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 70: Ṣaḍabhijñastotram
Complete in the marks of form, one who serves the low, high, and equal alike,
always displaying generosity — homage to you, O one who has gone beyond <s>dāna</s> (giving)! //
Complete in the marks of sound, resplendent, an ocean of virtues,
always proclaiming moral conduct — homage to you, O one who has gone beyond <s>śīla</s> (morality)! //
Complete in the marks of fragrance, of divine breath, a leader —
bestow patience, O <s>Jina</s> — homage to you, O one who has gone beyond <s>kṣānti</s> (patience)! //
Complete in the marks of taste, with an excellent tongue, a teacher of <s>Dharma</s>,
proclaim the <s>Dharma</s> of the <s>Sugata</s> — homage to you, O one who has gone beyond <s>vīrya</s> (vigor)! //
Complete in the marks of touch, unobstructed, free from [self-]effort,
bestow meditation, O <s>Jina</s> — homage to you, O one who has gone beyond <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation)! //
Complete in the marks of dharma, one who thinks equally toward all beings,
one who has greatly attained skillful means and wisdom — homage to you, O one who has gone beyond <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom)! //
Whoever recites this <s>Ṣaḍabhijñastava</s> (Hymn to the Six Superknowledges) with devotion at the three junctures [of the day],

children.text: saṃsārabandhanaṃ hitvā sa yāti paramāṃ gatim //
children.translated_text: abandoning the bonds of <s>saṃsāra</s>, shall attain the supreme state. //
The <s>Ṣaḍabhijñastotra</s> of the glorious great lord <s>Buddha</s> is complete. //

children.text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 71: Ṣaḍgatistotram
children.translated_text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 71: <s>Ṣaḍgatistotram</s>
To the one seated on a lotus, with lotus-feet, beautiful as the reddish <s>bandhūka</s> flower,
lotus in hand, wearing matted locks — homage to that one full of compassion! //
Auspicious one born in the <s>Kā</s>-son country, in the form of the lord of <s>Jinas</s>, a <s>Tathāgata</s>,
one who has crossed the ocean of the suffering of <s>saṃsāra</s> — homage to that one full of compassion! //
To <s>Samantabhadra</s>, worshipped by gods, adorned with a golden necklace,
bearing a crest-jewel on the crown — homage to that one full of compassion! //
To the one of dense beauty, seated upon a bull, the <s>Tathāgata</s> who destroys the afflictions of devotees,
adorned with precious jewels — homage to that one full of compassion! //
To the one with a beautiful neck, captivating the mind, whose prosperity is worshipped in the three worlds,
whose lotus-heart is filled with compassion — homage to that one full of compassion! //

children.text: stotraṃ pracakre bhuvi śaṃkhakarma puṇyārthato yacchatarājadhīmān /
children.translated_text: This hymn was composed on earth by the wise <s>Śaṃkhakarma</s>, bearer of the parasol-king, for the sake of merit;

children.text: ye ye paṭhiṣyanti narāḥ prayatnāt te te gatāḥ śrīsuraharmyaramyam //
children.translated_text: whoever among people shall recite it with effort, they shall go to the beautiful celestial mansions of glory. //
The <s>Ṣaḍgatistotra</s> (Hymn of the Six Destinies) of the noble <s>Āryāvalokiteśvara</s> is complete. //

children.text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 72: Saptabuddhastotram
children.translated_text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 72: <s>Saptabuddhastotram</s>
whose lifespan was eighty thousand years — teacher of gods and humans, among those who have passed —
He who was born in <s>Bandhumatī</s>, in a noble royal family, by the name <s>Vipaśyin</s>,

children.text: taṃ vande jñānavāri praṇamitasakalaṃ kleśavahniṃ jinendram //
children.translated_text: I bow to that lord of <s>Jinas</s>, the water of wisdom, before whom all <s>kleśa</s>-fires are extinguished! //
who attained <s>Jina</s>-hood, possessing the ten powers, at the root of the <s>Potalā</s> tree —

children.text: vaṃśe pṛthvīśvarāṇāṃ mahati puravare yaḥ prajāto 'rūṇākṣo

children.translated_text: whose lifespan, that treasury of all virtues, was seventy thousand years —
He who was born with red eyes in the great foremost city, in the lineage of earthly lords,

children.text: saṃprāptā yena bodhiḥ parahitapaṭunā puṇḍarīkasya mūle

children.translated_text: I bow to <s>Śikhin</s>, the foremost sage, the mass of wisdom, who has reached the other shore of <s>saṃsāra</s>! //
who attained awakening, skilled in the welfare of others, at the root of the <s>puṇḍarīka</s> (white lotus) tree —
whose lifespan of great intellect was sixty thousand years —
He who was born in <s>Anupamā</s>, in the widely-famed lineage of kings,
I bow to that <s>Dharma</s>-king, benefactor of the world, named <s>Viśvabhū</s>! //
having conquered all <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) without remainder, who attained the deathless at the root of the <s>śāla</s> tree —

children.text: kṣemāvatyāṃ prajāto manujapatisame yo vaśī vipravaṃśe

children.translated_text: whose lifespan, treasury of excellent virtues, was forty-eight thousand years —
He who was born in <s>Kṣemāvatī</s>, self-controlled, in a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> lineage equal to [that of] a king of men,
I bow to <s>Kakucchanda</s>, the incomparable <s>Sugata</s>, lion-bodied, lord of sages! //
who attained the <s>Jina</s>-lordship that destroys the three realms [of existence], as lord of the sword of knowledge —
whose lifespan of most excellent form was thirty thousand years —
He who was born in the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> lineage honored by kings, in <s>Śobhāvatī</s>,
I bow to that Teacher, the sage <s>Kanakamuni</s>, whose darkness of delusion is destroyed! //
who attained Buddhahood, weighty as a jewel mountain, at the <s>udumbara</s> (fig) tree —
whose lifespan of most exalted honor was twenty thousand years —
He who was born in the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> lineage honored by the farmer-king, in <s>Vārāṇasī</s>,

children.text: taṃ vande vandanīyaṃ munivaramanaghaṃ kāśyapaṃ lokanātham //
children.translated_text: I bow to that praiseworthy one, the excellent sage, the sinless <s>Kāśyapa</s>, lord of the world! //
who nourished the ocean of the three realms of existence at the root of the <s>nyagrodha</s> (banyan) tree through the divine path —
whose lifespan was one hundred autumns, the sole friend of all the worlds —
He who was born in the glorious great city of <s>Kapilavastu</s>, in the lineage of <s>Śākya</s> kings,
I bow to <s>Śākyasiṃha</s>, bowed to by gods and humans, the <s>Buddha</s>, kinsman of the Sun! //
having gone forth, who attained the unsurpassed awakening at the root of the <s>aśvattha</s> (bodhi) tree, [vanquishing] even <s>Namuci</s> (Māra) —
who shall attain Buddhahood, that treasury of supreme virtues, at the root of the <s>Nāga</s> tree —
Having taken birth in the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> lineage honored by great kings, in <s>Ketumatī</s>,
I bow to Lord <s>Maitreya</s>, the future lord of the world, dwelling in the great city of <s>Tuṣita</s>! //
whose supreme lifespan as the future Blessed One shall be eighty-eight thousand years —

children.text: maitreyaṃ ca stuvan vai tuṣitapuragataṃ bhāvinaṃ lokanātham /
children.translated_text: and having praised <s>Maitreya</s> dwelling in <s>Tuṣita</s> city, the future lord of the world —
Having praised the seven <s>Buddhas</s>, all of whom have fully passed, radiant as the sun of seven sevens,

children.text: chitvā saṃkleśapāśān munaya iva caran nirvṛtiṃ sa prayātu //
children.translated_text: cutting the bonds of defilement, may he walk like the sages and proceed to final cessation! //
whatever merit has arisen, giving the fruit of auspicious rebirth to all embodied beings,
The glorious <s>Saptabuddhastotra</s> (Hymn to the Seven Buddhas) is complete. //

children.text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 73: Saptajinastavaḥ
children.translated_text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 73: <s>Saptajinastavaḥ</s>
The teacher of the world, worshipped by gods and humans, skilled in compassion, the instructor of the welfare and liberation of others —

children.text: vipaśyinaṃ tribhavamahaughasāragaṃ namāmi taṃ sugatagatiṃ tathāgatam //
children.translated_text: <s>Vipaśyin</s>, who crossed the great flood of the three realms of existence — I bow to that <s>Tathāgata</s>, gone to the state of the <s>Sugata</s>. //
Seeing the world drowning in this boundless ocean of existence,

children.text: prakāśito yena hitāya dharmo namo 'stu tasmai śikhine jināya //
children.translated_text: by whom the <s>Dharma</s> was proclaimed for [their] benefit — homage to that <s>Jina</s>, <s>Śikhin</s>! //
I bow to the <s>Buddha Viśvabhū</s>, whose splendor surpasses the moon and sun,
unfathomable as the flood of the ocean, in knowledge and discipline. //
By whose glories resembling moon-rays this earth is adorned and shines,
wondrous like the <s>udumbara</s> (fig) flower — I bow to <s>Kakucchanda</s>, the great lord of sages! //
By one of generous, stainless mind, free from passion, always acting for the welfare of others,

children.text: hataṃ tamo vigatamalena yena taṃ surārcitaṃ kanakamuniṃ namāmyaham //
children.translated_text: by whom darkness was destroyed with stainless [wisdom] — to that <s>Kanakamuni</s>, worshipped by gods, I bow! //
Resplendent with rays like heated <s>cāmīkara</s> (refined gold), with blazing splendor surpassing a thousand suns,
the best in the world, to be honored by all people — I bow to the one named <s>Kāśyapa</s>! //
Having awakened the world with nets of speech-rays, like nets of sun-rays [awakening] a lotus grove,

children.text: yo nirvṛtaḥ śākyamunipradīpastasmaiḥ namaḥ paramakāruṇikāya śāstre //
children.translated_text: he who attained cessation — the lamp <s>Śākyamuni</s> — homage to that supremely compassionate Teacher! //
The one named <s>Maitreya</s>, dwelling in <s>Tuṣita</s>, whose awakening is separated by only one birth,

children.text: utpatsyate yaḥ sugataḥ pṛthivyāṃ sarvātmanā 'haṃ praṇato 'smi tasmai //
children.translated_text: who shall arise as a <s>Sugata</s> on earth — with my entire being, I prostrate to him! //
Having praised the seven <s>Jinas</s> who have passed, and the eighth, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> yet to come,
whatever immeasurable merit has been obtained — may beings be free from affliction through that! //
The glorious <s>Saptajinastavaḥ</s> (Hymn to the Seven Victors) is complete. //

children.text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 74: Saptākṣarastotram
children.translated_text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 74: <s>Saptākṣarastotram</s>
<s>Oṃ</s>! Homage to <s>Lokanātha</s>, to <s>Matsyendra</s>, to <s>Viṣṇu</s>!
I bow to the lord of <s>Jinas</s>, the ordainer of the eternal and the transient,
to the one who sports without garments (i.e., free from coverings), to the one free from conceptualization — homage to you! //
The giver of liberation, who has accomplished liberation, the bestower of the bliss of liberation,
to the one who grants liberation, dwelling in the center of the <s>Meru</s>-<s>maṇḍala</s> — homage to you! //
To the one [who frees from] the trembling noose of desire, to <s>Lokeśa</s> (Lord of the World), the great-souled one,
to the protector of the world, to the divine one, to <s>Lokanātha</s> — homage to you! //
Dwelling in the center of the golden mountain, attended by <s>Kinnaras</s>,
for the sake of fame, through meditation — we worship you, the giver of beauty. //
To the Lord adorned with blazing <s>mantra</s>-radiance, bearing <s>Nāga</s> ornaments,
to the blameless <s>Buddha</s>, the giver of awakening — homage to you! //
O steadfast one who protects [one's] station, O protector of those fallen from their station,
to <s>Locanā</s>, <s>Māmakī</s>, <s>Tārā</s>, and <s>Pāṇḍarā</s> — repeated homage! //
To the one who removes the fear of <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Rākṣasas</s>, <s>Vetālas</s>, and serpents,
to the one wearing the crown of <s>Amitābha</s>, the giver of <s>siddhi</s> (accomplishment) — homage to you! //
O one with thousands of hair-pores as monks, homage to you as protector of monks!
This meritorious eight-verse hymn has been proclaimed to you, O lord of <s>samādhi</s>. //
The <s>Saptākṣarastotra</s> (Seven-Syllable Hymn) of the glorious noble <s>Āryāvalokiteśvara</s> is complete. //

children.text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 75: Saptavidhānuttarastotram
children.translated_text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 75: <s>Saptavidhānuttarastotram</s>
Homage to the glorious <s>Lokanātha</s>!
destroyer of sins committed, with eyes free from delusion and illusion,
With <s>Amitābha</s> (Infinite Light) upon his head, with eyes wide as lotus petals,
with bowed head, I salute that <s>Lokanātha</s> (Lord of the World)! //
holding a golden lotus in hand, the sole skilled protector of the world —
wearing a jeweled crown, the bridge across the ocean of <s>saṃsāra</s>,
The cause of awakening and knowledge, with the radiance of dawn-red and <s>Varuṇa</s>,
with bowed head, I salute that <s>Lokanātha</s>! //
the destroyer of <s>Manmatha</s> (Kāma), the foremost banner of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> —
the hope of gods, humans, and demons, radiant as the full moon,
Dwelling on a lotus, far from the noose of desire,
with bowed head, I salute that <s>Lokanātha</s>! //
the delight of the virtuous, shining like ten million suns —
the divider of the ocean of existence, the sole path to the bliss of liberation,
With a serpent placed upon the chest, having released all passion,
with bowed head, I salute that <s>Lokanātha</s>! //
with limbs [radiant as] heated gold, devoted solely to the awakening of awakening —
with a beautifully graceful serpent-king, spreading a lovely shade,
The royal tree among the sons of the <s>Jina</s>, resplendent with garlands of pearls,
with bowed head, I salute that <s>Lokanātha</s>! //
a delighted king of offerings, protector of the king of immortals —
in the excellent form of a horse, a king with <s>Siṃhala</s> (Śrī Laṅkā) teeth,
Bearing the form of a bee, a well in which the noose of hunger is destroyed,
with bowed head, I salute that <s>Lokanātha</s>! //
fragrant as <s>aguru</s> (agarwood) incense, bearing all forms —
this daily recitation, a lament in the circle of gods,
Removing the triple suffering and the threefold sins that I have accumulated,
with bowed head, I salute that <s>Lokanātha</s>! //
a bundle of the fear of hell, a bow that shatters ignorance —
whose impurities have dissolved, who delight in worship with devotion —
For the virtuous people who are intent on being freed from suffering,
with bowed head, I salute that <s>Lokanātha</s>! //
they obtain the collection of excellent merits through their own devotion —
for those afraid of birth and death, led [astray] by the snares of <s>Māra</s>,
The accomplishment created by the Ten Powers, the awakening of <s>Buddha</s>-<s>bodhi</s>,
with bowed head, I salute that <s>Lokanātha</s>! //
for those of impure mind, whose wealth is ignorance —
I take refuge here, [the teaching that] has caused the destruction of <s>Anaṅga</s> (bodiless Kāma),
The excellent jewel of the <s>Sugata</s>, the <s>Dharmakāya</s>, and the <s>Saṅgha</s>,
with bowed head, I salute that <s>Lokanātha</s>! //
attained with a delighted mind, the sole effort for obtaining awakening —
composed with the nectar of joy, rich in expansive homage,
This [hymn], a lotus of devotion to the lotus-feet of the glorious <s>Lokanātha</s>,
is indeed a path-maker for the journey to <s>Sukhāvatī</s> (the Pure Land). //
endowed with the seven modes of worship, charming and heartfelt,
whatever merit has been obtained, may [all] go by that merit to <s>Sukhāvatī</s>!
Having praised this lord of the world, the lord of sages, the granter of all accomplishments —
[this hymn] that removes the afflictions of the world, having conquered the supreme invincible one — pure and liberated! //
Arisen from the sole joy and delight of the nectar of the lotus-feet of the glorious <s>Lokeśvara</s>,
The <s>Saptavidhānuttarastotra</s> (Hymn of Seven Unsurpassed Modes) of the glorious noble <s>Āryāvalokiteśvara</s> is complete. //

children.text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 76: Ṣaṭpāramitāstotram
children.translated_text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 76: <s>Ṣaṭpāramitāstotram</s>
The <s>Buddha</s> arose through the power of <s>dāna</s> (giving); the sovereign of the power of giving is a lion among men;

children.text: dānabalekṣaka śrūyati śabdaḥ kāruṇikena pure praviśantam //
children.translated_text: the sound is heard of the observer of the power of giving — the compassionate one entering the city. //
The <s>Buddha</s> arose through the power of <s>śīla</s> (moral conduct); the sovereign of the power of conduct is a lion among men;

children.text: śīlabalekṣaka śrūyati śabdaḥ kāruṇikena pure praviśantam //
children.translated_text: the sound is heard of the observer of the power of conduct — the compassionate one entering the city. //
The <s>Buddha</s> arose through the power of <s>kṣānti</s> (patience); the sovereign of the power of patience is a lion among men;

children.text: kṣāntibalekṣaka śrūyati śabdaḥ kāruṇikena pure praviśantam //
children.translated_text: the sound is heard by the one who observes through the power of patience, entering the city with compassion. //
The <s>Buddha</s> who arose through the power of vigor, the lord of the power of vigor in the <s>Narasiṃha</s> (Man-lion);

children.text: vīryabalekṣaka śruyati śabdaḥ kāruṇikena pure praviśantam //
children.translated_text: the sound is heard by the one who observes through the power of vigor, entering the city with compassion. //
The <s>Buddha</s> who arose through the power of meditation (<s>dhyāna</s>), the lord of the power of meditation in the <s>Narasiṃha</s>;

children.text: dhyānabalekṣaka śruyati śabdaḥ kāruṇikena pure praviśantam //
children.translated_text: the sound is heard by the one who observes through the power of meditation, entering the city with compassion. //
The <s>Buddha</s> who arose through the power of wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>), the lord of the power of wisdom in the <s>Narasiṃha</s>;

children.text: prajñabalekṣaka śrūyati śabdaḥ kāruṇikena pure praviśantam //
children.translated_text: the sound is heard by the one who observes through the power of wisdom, entering the city with compassion. //
The glorious <s>Ṣaṭpāramitāstotra</s> (Hymn to the Six Perfections) is complete. //

children.text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 77: Ṣaṭtriṃśatsaṃvarastutiḥ
children.translated_text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 77: Ṣaṭtriṃśatsaṃvarastutiḥ
The glorious <s>Saṃvara</s>, the great hero, and also <s>Vārāhī</s> the <s>yoginī</s> —
I bow with my entire being to the lord of the <s>yoginī</s>-net! //

children.text: ḍākinīṃ ca tathā lāmāṃ khaṇḍarohāṃ ca rūpiṇīm /
children.translated_text: <s>Ḍākinī</s>, <s>Lāmā</s>, <s>Khaṇḍarohā</s> of beautiful form,
and the four vessels of nectar filled with <s>bodhicitta</s> (awakening-mind). //
Born in <s>Pullīramalaya</s>, <s>Khaṇḍakapāla</s>-<s>Saṃvara</s>,
the hero embracing <s>Pracaṇḍā</s> — I bow to the one stationed at the crown of the head! //
Born from <s>Jālandhara</s>, <s>Mahākaṃkāla</s>-<s>Saṃvara</s>,
the hero embracing <s>Caṇḍālī</s> — I bow to the one stationed at the topknot! //
Born from <s>Oḍiyāna</s>, <s>Saṃvara</s> named <s>Kaṃkāla</s>,
united with <s>Prabhāvatī</s> — I bow to the one stationed at the right ear! //
Standing in the middle of the <s>Arbuda</s> sacred site, <s>Saṃvara</s> with terrible fangs,
united with <s>Mahānāsā</s> — I bow to the one stationed at the back! //
Born from the <s>Godāvarī</s>, <s>Surāvīriṇa</s>-<s>Saṃvara</s>,
the hero in union, named <s>Matyā</s> — I bow to the one stationed at the left ear! //
Born from <s>Rāmeśvara</s>, the hero, <s>Amitābha</s>-<s>Saṃvara</s>,
the lord in union with <s>Kharvarī</s> — I bow to the one stationed between the eyebrows! //
Born from <s>Devīkoṭa</s>, the lord, <s>Vajraprabha</s>-<s>Saṃvara</s>,
united with <s>Laṅkeśvarī</s> — I bow to the one stationed at the corner of the eye! //
Born from the place called <s>Mārāva</s>, <s>Vajradeha</s>-<s>Saṃvara</s>,
united with <s>Drumacchāyā</s> — I bow to the one stationed at the shoulder-region! //
Born from <s>Kāmarūpa</s>, the hero, <s>Aṅgulikā</s>-<s>Saṃvara</s>,
united with <s>Airāvatī</s> — I bow to the one stationed at the armpit! //
Born from the station of <s>Okāra</s>, <s>Vajrajaṭila</s>-<s>Saṃvara</s>,
the hero embracing <s>Bhairavī</s> — I bow to the one born at the pair of limbs! //
Born from <s>Triśakunī</s>, the lord, <s>Mahāvīra</s>-<s>Saṃvara</s>,
united with <s>Vāyuvegā</s> — I bow to the one stationed at the navel! //
Born in <s>Kauśalā</s>, <s>Vajrahūṃkāra</s>-<s>Saṃvara</s>,
united with <s>Surābhakṣī</s> — I bow to the one before the nose! //
Born at the <s>Kaliṅga</s> sacred site, <s>Saṃvara</s> named <s>Suprabha</s>,
united with goddess <s>Śyāmā</s> — I bow to the one stationed at the mouth! //
Born from the station of <s>Lampāka</s>, <s>Vajraprabha</s>-<s>Saṃvara</s>,
the hero embracing <s>Subhadrā</s> — I bow to the one born at the throat! //
Born at the sacred site called <s>Kāñcī</s>, <s>Mahābhairava</s>-<s>Saṃvara</s>,
united with <s>Hayakarṇā</s> — I bow to the one stationed at the middle of the heart! //
Born from the <s>Himālaya</s>, the hero, <s>Virūpākṣa</s>-<s>Saṃvara</s>,
united with <s>Khagānanā</s> — I bow to the one stationed at the secret place! //
Born in the city of the dead (<s>Pretapurī</s>), <s>Mahābala</s>-<s>Saṃvara</s>,
united with <s>Cakravegā</s> — I bow to the one stationed at the <s>liṅga</s> (generative organ)! //
Born from the cave-region, <s>Ratnavajra</s>-<s>Saṃvara</s>,
united with <s>Khaṇḍarohā</s> — I bow to the one stationed at the anus! //
Born in the <s>Saurāṣṭra</s> region, <s>Hayagrīva</s>-<s>Saṃvara</s>,
the hero embracing <s>Śauṇḍinī</s> — I bow to the one stationed at the middle of the thigh! //
Born from <s>Suvarṇadvīpa</s> (the Golden Island), <s>Ākāśagarbha</s>-<s>Saṃvara</s>,
united with <s>Cakravarmiṇī</s> — I bow to the one stationed at the middle of the calf! //
Standing in the middle of the <s>Nagara</s> sacred site, <s>Saṃvara</s> named <s>Śrīheruka</s>,
the hero embracing <s>Suvīrā</s> — I bow to the one stationed at the toes! //
Born from the <s>Sindhu</s> region, <s>Padmanṛtya</s>-<s>Saṃvara</s>,
united with <s>Mahābalā</s> — I bow to the one stationed at the top of the foot! //
Born at the <s>Marutī</s> sacred site, <s>Vairocana</s>-<s>Saṃvara</s>,
united with <s>Cakravartinī</s> — I bow to the one stationed at the middle of the thumb! //
Born from <s>Kulatā</s>, <s>Vajrasattva</s>-<s>Saṃvara</s>,
united with <s>Mahāvīryā</s> — I bow to the one stationed at both knees! //
Standing at the eastern gate, the hero, <s>Vajracaṇḍa</s>-<s>Saṃvara</s>,
the hero embracing <s>Kākāsyā</s> (Crow-faced one) — I bow to the lord of the gods! //
Standing in the middle of the northern gate, <s>Vajrānala</s>-<s>Saṃvara</s>,
united with <s>Ulūkāsyā</s> (Owl-faced one) — I bow to the lord of the <s>Yakṣas</s>! //
Standing in the middle of the western gate, <s>Vajroṣṇīṣa</s>-<s>Saṃvara</s>,
the hero in union with <s>Śvānāsyā</s> (Dog-faced one) — I bow to the lord of the <s>Nāgas</s>! //
Standing in the middle of the southern gate, <s>Vajrakuṇḍali</s>-<s>Saṃvara</s>,
united with <s>Śūkarāsyā</s> (Boar-faced one) — I bow to the lord of <s>Yama</s> (Death)! //
Standing in the southeastern direction, <s>Vajrayakṣa</s>-<s>Saṃvara</s>,
united with <s>Yamadāḍhī</s> — I bow to the lord of fire (<s>Agni</s>)! //
Standing in the southwestern direction, <s>Vajrakīla</s>-<s>Saṃvara</s>,
united with <s>Yamadūtī</s> — I bow to the lord of the <s>Rākṣasas</s>! //
Standing in the northwestern direction, the one called <s>Vajramahābala</s>,
united with <s>Yamadaṃṣṭrī</s> — I bow to the lord of wind (<s>Vāyu</s>)! //
Standing in the northeastern direction, <s>Vajrabhīṣaṇa</s>-<s>Saṃvara</s>,
united with <s>Yamamathanī</s> — I bow to the lord of <s>Bhūtas</s> (spirits)! //
I bow to these gods, well-established in the directions and intermediate directions,
to the heroes, to all the heroines, and to <s>Heruka</s>, the supreme lord, //
the god whose nature is innate bliss (<s>sahajānanda</s>), pure, engaged in the cosmic dance (<s>tāṇḍava</s>),
abiding in the midst of the <s>Ḍākinī</s>-net, accessible to one's own inner realization. //
Having praised this circle of deities, whatever merit has been acquired by me,
by that merit may the world become devoted to <s>Vajraḍāka</s>! //
The glorious praise of the thirty-six <s>Saṃvara</s> assembly-circle <s>maṇḍala</s> is complete. //

children.text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 78: Sattvārādhanagāthā ārya nāgārjunakṛtā
children.translated_text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 78: Sattvārādhanagāthā, composed by the noble <s>Nāgārjuna</s>

children.text: sattvārthameva mayi tiṣṭhati sattvaśraddhā nānyatra sā, hyahamaho 'dhigṛhītasattvaḥ /
children.translated_text: Faith in beings resides in me solely for the sake of beings, not elsewhere — ah, I have truly grasped the essence of beings!

children.text: caryā 'dhamā karuṇayā rahitā bhaved yā saṃbhāvyate karuṇayaiva prahāṇamasyāḥ //
children.translated_text: That conduct would be base which is devoid of compassion; by compassion alone is its abandonment accomplished. //

children.text: sattveṣu yasya nitarāṃ karuṇāpravṛttirārādhakaḥ sa mama śāsanamarmavettā /
children.translated_text: He in whom compassion flows intensely toward beings — he is my worshipper, the knower of the essence of my teaching;

children.text: śīlaṃ śrutiśca karuṇā ca sudhośca yasya nityaṃ sa eva sugatārcanakṛnnigadyate //
children.translated_text: he who constantly has morality, learning, compassion, and nectar — he alone is called the true worshipper of the <s>Sugata</s> (Well-gone One). //

children.text: kalyāṇakāramadhikṛtya gato 'smi siddhiṃ sattvārthameva tanumeṣa samudvahāmi /
children.translated_text: Having undertaken virtuous deeds, I have attained accomplishment; for the sake of beings alone I bear this body;

children.text: naivaṃ kriyeta yadi sattvahitaṃ mayā ced vyarthaṃ karomi tanupoṣaṇamannapānaiḥ //
children.translated_text: if I were not to do what benefits beings, then I would be nourishing this body with food and drink in vain. //

children.text: sattvān hinasti manasāpi hi yaḥ sa kasmānmāmeva saṃśrayati yo mayi nirvyapekṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: Why does one who harms beings even in thought take refuge in me — one who is indifferent to me?

children.text: pūjā tu sā bhavati sattvahitekṣaṇāpi pūjyasya yā manasi tuṣṭimupādadāti //
children.translated_text: But that worship which is directed even at a glance toward the welfare of beings — that worship produces satisfaction in the mind of the one worthy of worship. //

children.text: hiṃsātmikā paraviheṭhanasambhavā vā pūjā na pūjyamanugacchati saṃskṛtāpi /
children.translated_text: Worship that involves harm or arises from tormenting others — even if prepared elaborately — does not accompany the one worthy of worship;

children.text: dārāḥ sutāśca vibhavaśca mahattva(cca) rājyaṃ māṃsaṃ ca śoṇitavase nayate śarīram //
children.translated_text: wife, sons, wealth, great dominion, and the kingdom — the body leads flesh and blood into subjugation. //

children.text: yeṣāṃ priyatvamadhikṛtya mayojjhitaṃ yat yastān viheṭhayati tena viheṭhito 'ham /
children.translated_text: For the sake of whose dearness I have renounced what I did — whoever harms them, by that I am harmed;

children.text: sattvopakāraparamā hi mamāgrapūjā sattvāpakāraparayā ca parābhavaḥ syāt //
children.translated_text: the supreme worship of me is that which is devoted to benefiting beings, and harm to beings would be [my] defeat. //
the <s>Pāramitās</s> (Perfections) were attained — all this by remaining for the purpose of the assembly of beings;
Through beings, I performed meritorious deeds, the <s>Tathāgatas</s> (Thus-gone Ones) were worshipped,

children.text: sattvārthena samudyatena manasā mārasya bhagnaṃ balaṃ
sattvaireva tathā tathā viracitaṃ yenāsmi buddhaḥ kṛtaḥ //
children.translated_text: thus, in various ways, through beings I was made a <s>Buddha</s>! //
by a mind exerted for the welfare of beings, the army of <s>Māra</s> was broken —

children.text: kasmin vastuni siddhyatāmiha kṛpā maitrī ca kvālambatāṃ

children.translated_text: Where is the domain of equanimity, sympathetic joy, and the like? In what are the liberations and other [attainments]?
In what object should compassion succeed here? Where should loving-kindness find its support?

children.text: na syurjanmani janma(ni) priyavidhau mitraṃ yadi prāṇinaḥ //
children.translated_text: If living beings were not dear, there would be no friend in birth after birth in the practice of affection. //
For whose sake was patience cultivated for a long time with a mind full of compassion?

children.text: sattvā eva ca pātratāmupagataṃ deyaṃ mayā grāhitāḥ /
children.translated_text: beings themselves became the vessels, and what was to be given was accepted by them;
Beings themselves, taking the forms of elephants and others, were given by me countless times;

children.text: sattvāneva na pālayāmi yadi cet kasyārthamarthaḥ kṛtaḥ //
children.translated_text: if I do not protect beings, then for whose sake was the purpose accomplished? //
through beings themselves, by going through various states, our compassion was increased —
who, through the deception of the cycle of births, reach the world of <s>Yama</s> (Death) and are absorbed —
If in <s>saṃsāra</s>, full of calamities and afflictions, there were no living beings

children.text: kasyārthena samīhitaṃ yadi na me sattvā bhaveyuḥ priyāḥ //
children.translated_text: for whose purpose would it have been undertaken, if beings were not dear to me? //
then this <s>Saugata</s> (Buddhist) crossing of <s>saṃsāra</s>, this supremely wonderful greatness,

children.text: yāvaccedaṃ jvalati jagataḥ śāsanaṃ śāsanaṃ me

children.translated_text: so long should you remain, devoted to the welfare of others, treating others as yourselves;
As long as this teaching of mine blazes forth in the world,

children.text: khedaḥ kāryo na ca tanumimaṃ muktasāraṃ bhavadbhiḥ //
children.translated_text: do not weary yourselves, nor cast off this body, the essence of liberation! //
hearing again and again what I have composed for the sake of beings, untiringly —
The <s>Sattvārādhanagāthā</s> (Verses on Pleasing Beings), spoken by the Perfectly Awakened One, is complete. //

children.text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 79: Śākyasiṃhastotram brahmaṇā kṛtam
