children.translated_text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 79: Śākyasiṃhastotram, composed by <s>Brahmā</s>
Homage to the Lord of the <s>Śākyas</s>! /
Homage to you, O Lord of the World, O <s>Śākya</s>-King, O sun to the lotus of the true <s>Dharma</s>!
To you who have struck down the host of enemies — the <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions), whose net of delusion is destroyed by the lamps of perfect awakening! //
That which cannot be attained by the hosts of <s>Brahma-ṛṣis</s>, <s>Rāja-ṛṣis</s>, and <s>Sura-ṛṣis</s> with their many jewels —

children.text: prāptaṃ tvayā jñānamanantadharmaṃ yenākariṣyaḥ sakalasya haityam //
children.translated_text: that knowledge of infinite <s>Dharma</s> was attained by you, by which you accomplished the welfare of all! //

children.text: pravartitaṃ yena sudharmacakraṃ yasmin mahī sodadhiśailarājā /
children.translated_text: He by whom the excellent <s>Dharmacakra</s> (Wheel of the Law) was set in motion, at which the earth with its oceans and king of mountains

children.text: ānanditeva calitā hyajasraṃ namo 'stu tubhyaṃ tribhavādhipāya //
children.translated_text: trembled as if delighted, ceaselessly — homage to you, O Lord of the Three Realms of Existence! //

children.text: yasmiṃśca vātāstriguṇena yuktā vavurnabhasto nipatanti vastrāḥ(rṣāḥ) /
children.translated_text: In whose [presence] the winds, endowed with the three qualities, blew, and rains fell from the sky,

children.text: vicitrapuṣpāṇi sugandhi vāri namo 'stu tubhyaṃ jagadekanātha //
children.translated_text: with various flowers and fragrant water — homage to you, O sole Lord of the World! //
<s>Namuchi</s> (<s>Māra</s>), unconquered by any other, surrounded by his foremost armies numbering hundreds of millions —

children.text: jitaṃ tvayaikena nirāyudhena namo 'stu tubhyaṃ balavartanāya //
children.translated_text: was conquered by you alone, without weapons — homage to you, O Wielder of Strength! //
He who, in order to protect the three worlds, blazed forth from the created illusion,
the destroyer of birth, old age, and death by nature — homage to you, O sole Lord of the World! //
He who, to spread in the worlds of the three realms that <s>Bodhicaryā</s> (Awakening-practice), the bridge to liberation,

children.text: tuṣitāyuto janma cakāra martye namo 'stu tubhyaṃ varabodhirāja //
children.translated_text: took birth in the mortal world endowed with <s>Tuṣita</s> [heaven] — homage to you, O excellent King of Awakening! //

children.text: samyak pratijñāṃ pratikṛtya yena saṃpreṣyate mokṣapure janaughaḥ /
children.translated_text: He by whom the proper vow was made, and the multitude of people is sent to the city of <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation),

children.text: tadarthamāyāsi ca martyaloke namo 'stu tubhyaṃ sumahatpratijña //
children.translated_text: and for that purpose he came to the mortal world — homage to you, O one of the supremely great vow! //

children.text: yaścāṣṭakaṃ brahmakṛtaṃ supuṇyaṃ paṭhiṣyati śākyavarāgrataḥ sthaḥ /
children.translated_text: Whoever shall recite this auspicious eight-verse [hymn] composed by <s>Brahmā</s>, standing before the supreme <s>Śākya</s>,

children.text: duḥkhaṃ mahāpāpabhayaṃ ca hitvā śrīśrīghane yāsyati pattane mudā //
children.translated_text: having abandoned suffering, great sin, and fear — shall go with joy to the city of the glorious and fortunate! //
The glorious <s>Śākyasiṃhastotra</s> (Hymn to the Lion of the Śākyas), composed by <s>Brahmā</s>, is complete. //

children.text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 80: Śākyasiṃhastotram
children.translated_text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 80: Śākyasiṃhastotram
In the meter <s>Amṛtoddhṛta</s>:
I bow to him who sits at the foot of a tree, accompanied by hosts of monks,
whose feet possess marks proclaimed one after another — those born of the <s>Upajāti</s> [meter]! //
The charming crest-ornament of the lineage of the Lord of the <s>Śākyas</s>, shining more than partially, more radiant than gold —
I bow to the <s>Buddha</s>, accomplished in <s>Upajāti</s>, the excellent prince named <s>Sarvārthasiddha</s> (All-purposes-accomplished)! //
I bow always to the one of faultless conduct, unstained, of pure bodily form,
whose single thought is the deliverance of all beings without remainder, moon-faced, with bright lotus-feet! //
The son of <s>Śuddhodana</s>, nurtured by <s>Gautamī</s>, the son of <s>Māyā</s>, the conqueror of <s>Māra</s>, the great one,
whose form is honored by <s>Maheśvara</s> (Śiva) and others, of immeasurable greatness, of immeasurable <s>Dharma</s> — //
Him who has crossed the ocean of existence, of infinite merit, whose feet are worshipped by the gods beginning with <s>Bhava</s> (Śiva),
who is to be contemplated by infinite noble beings of beautiful form — I bow to him whose limbs are adorned with brilliant ornaments. //

children.text: babhāṇa vaṃśasthaviro nṛpādhipo janān pratītyāhvayatātmajaṃ mama /
children.translated_text: The elder of the dynasty, the king, spoke, addressing people, and called his own son:

children.text: kṛtāribhaṅgaṃ jinarājamīśvaraṃ gataṃ ṣaḍabdaṃ ca viyogabhāvayoḥ //
children.translated_text: 'The king of <s>Jinas</s>, the lord who has crushed his enemies, who has gone for six years into the states of separation.' //

children.text: bhajasva vaṃśasthaviraṃ munīśvaraṃ mahāvane vṛkṣatale śucisthale /
children.translated_text: 'Worship the elder of the dynasty, the lord of sages, at the foot of a tree in the great forest, in a pure place,
the benefactor of the world, born of the birth that ends old age, born from the right side of the mother of the world.' //
Praising <s>Śrī Śākyasiṃha</s>, the moon risen from the ocean of the <s>Śākya</s> dynasty, with four faces,

children.text: prāśiṣṭa brahmā caturānanaṃ svakaṃ caturguṇaṃ puṇyamavāptamityaho //
children.translated_text: <s>Brahmā</s> consumed his own four-facedness — 'Oh, fourfold merit has been obtained!' //
<s>Janārdana</s> (Viṣṇu), the fire of the <s>Daitya</s>-chief dynasty, making <s>añjali</s> with his two [hands] on the lotus-seat,
touched the four arms with both shoulders — 'Twofold merit has been obtained by me.' //
The <s>Śrī Śākyasiṃha</s> hymn, extracted from the <s>Chandāmṛta</s>, is complete. //

children.text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 81: Śākyasiṃhastotram durgatipariśodhanoddhṛtam
children.translated_text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 81: <s>Śākyasiṃhastotram</s>, extracted from the <s>Durgatipariśodhana</s>
<s>Oṃ</s>! Homage to <s>Śākyasiṃha</s>!
Homage to you, <s>Śākyasiṃha</s>, turner of the wheel of <s>Dharma</s>,
who purifies the entire world of the three realms of all evil destinies! //
Homage to you, <s>Vajroṣṇīṣa</s> (Vajra Crown-Protuberance), of the nature of the <s>Dharmadhātu</s> (Realm of Dharma),
teacher of the essence of the Self for the benefit of all beings! //
Homage to you, <s>Ratnoṣṇīṣa</s> (Jewel Crown-Protuberance), by those who contemplate reality in all directions,
bestower of consecration (<s>abhiṣeka</s>) upon all that abides in the three realms! //
Homage to you, <s>Padmoṣṇīṣa</s> (Lotus Crown-Protuberance), revealer of the inherent nature,
who comforts beings and sets in motion the nectar of <s>Dharma</s>! //
Homage to you, <s>Viśvoṣṇīṣa</s> (Universal Crown-Protuberance), established in the natural state,
the universal creator, indeed, for the pacification of beings' suffering! //
Homage to you, <s>Tejoṣṇīṣa</s> (Radiance Crown-Protuberance), teacher of the three realms,
who will make beings visible through all skillful means! //
Homage to you, <s>Dhvajoṣṇīṣa</s> (Banner Crown-Protuberance), bearer of the <s>Cintāmaṇi</s> (wish-fulfilling gem) banner,
fulfiller of all wishes of all beings through generosity! //
Homage to you, <s>Tṛṣṇoṣṇīṣa</s> (Thirst Crown-Protuberance), cutter of <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) and secondary afflictions,
who shattered the power of the four <s>Māras</s> for beings' attainment of awakening! //
Homage to you, <s>Chatroṣṇīṣa</s> (Parasol Crown-Protuberance), whose parasol is most beautiful,
who leads the entire world of the three realms to the attainment of <s>Dharma</s>-kingship! //

children.text: lāsyā mālā tathā gītā nṛtyā devīcatuṣṭayam /
children.translated_text: <s>Lāsyā</s> (Dance), <s>Mālā</s> (Garland), likewise <s>Gītā</s> (Song), <s>Nṛtyā</s> (Dance) — to this quartet of goddesses,

children.text: puṣpā dhūpā ca dīpā ca gandhādevī namo 'stu te //
children.translated_text: <s>Puṣpā</s> (Flower), <s>Dhūpā</s> (Incense), and <s>Dīpā</s> (Lamp), and goddess <s>Gandhā</s> (Perfume) — homage to you! //
Those who stand in the midst of the gates, bearing hooks, nooses, and hammers,
known through the disposition of faith — to the gate-guardians, homage to you! //

children.text: vedikādau sthitā ye ca catasro dvārapālikāḥ /
children.translated_text: Those four female gate-guardians standing at the railing and elsewhere,

children.text: muditādau daśa sthitvā bodhisattva namostu te //
children.translated_text: and the ten <s>Bodhisattvas</s> standing in joy and the rest — homage to you! //
<s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Indra</s>, <s>Rudra</s> (Śiva), Moon, Sun, the world-guardians (<s>Lokapālas</s>) of the four directions,
<s>Agni</s> (Fire), <s>Rākṣasa</s> (demon), <s>Vāyu</s> (Wind), and lord of <s>Bhūtas</s> (spirits) — homage to you! //
With this king of hymns, standing before the <s>maṇḍala</s>,
the <s>mantra</s>-holder bearing the <s>vajra</s>-bell should recite this hymn. //
The <s>Śrī Śākyasiṃha</s> hymn, extracted from the <s>Durgatipariśodhana</s>, is complete. //

children.text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 82: Śākyasiṃhastotram navagrahakṛtam
children.translated_text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 82: <s>Śākyasiṃhastotram</s>, composed by the Nine Planets
I bow to the <s>Jina</s> (Victor), the <s>Sugata</s> (Well-Gone One), whose body has the luster of refined gold,
whose palms are adorned with the excellent wheel, the remover of the sins of gods, <s>Asuras</s>, and humans. //
I bow to the graceful guru, lord of sages, who always conquered <s>Māra's</s> troubling forces,
the awakener of the ten <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections), the awakener of the Four Noble [Truths], the easy-to-accomplish one. //
I bow to the beneficent divine-human, the supreme god worshipped by humans, <s>Nāgas</s>, and immortals,
the remover of harm from the six realms beginning with the gods, the remover of the fear of birth, old age, and death. //
I bow to the bearer of awakening that creates happiness; from a mind of compassion, he gave away his own happiness,
making the unbearable suffering of others his own, born in the faultless, untroubled <s>Śākya</s> clan. //

children.text: praṇamāmi ca lokahitāya gṛhaṃ vijahau pitaraṃ ramaṇīsahitam /
children.translated_text: I bow to him who, for the welfare of the world, left his home, his father, and his wife,
and surrounded by the horse <s>Kaṇṭhaka</s>, <s>Chandaka</s>, and the gods, joyfully went to the beautiful, solitary forest. //

children.text: praṇamāmi tapovanasubhramitaṃ pracakāra ca yastu maharṣigaṇān /
children.translated_text: I bow to him who wandered beautifully in the forest of austerities, and who guided the hosts of great sages
to the four noble <s>Brahmavihāras</s> (divine abodes), devoted to the sole austerity-vow of remembering the <s>Sugata</s>. //
I bow to the <s>vajra</s>-holder seated on a grass seat at the supreme base of the great tree,
who destroyed the weapons and forces of a hundred <s>koṭi</s> (ten million) <s>Māras</s>, surrounded by sons of <s>Tathāgatas</s> numbering in the hundreds. //

children.text: praṇamāmi ca mallikapañcaśatā vaṇijaḥ pratipālanameva kṛtāḥ /
children.translated_text: I bow — the five hundred <s>Mallikā</s> merchants indeed performed the act of protection,
and the merchants offered the five excellent foods, and the preparation of auspicious milk-rice for eating. //
I bow to the excellently turned supreme <s>Dharma</s>, at the deer-park (<s>Mṛgadāva</s>) grove, with four seats,
surrounded by <s>Vidhi</s> (Brahmā), <s>Śakra</s> (Indra), gods, <s>Asuras</s>, and worldly beings, with a beautiful body blazing brilliantly in all directions. //

children.text: gurunirmitakaṃ sugatastavakaṃ paṭhanaṃ kurute kila yo manujaḥ /
children.translated_text: The person who recites this hymn to the <s>Sugata</s>, composed by the teacher,

children.text: graharogabhayaṃ nahi tasya sadā sa tu yāsyati mokṣapure supure //
children.translated_text: for him there is never fear of planetary affliction and disease; and he shall go to the excellent city of liberation (<s>mokṣa</s>). //
The <s>Śrī Śākyasiṃha</s> hymn, composed by the nine planets beginning with <s>Āditya</s> (Sun), is complete. //

children.text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 83: Śākyasiṃhastotram śaṅkarakṛtam
children.translated_text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 83: <s>Śākyasiṃhastotram</s>, composed by <s>Śaṅkara</s>
radiant as a thousand suns, pure as ten million moons,
I bow to the <s>Jina</s> (Victor), the follower of <s>Sugata</s>, resplendent with a brilliant canopy,
adorned with lotus-feet, hands, and the thousand-spoked wheel. //
from whose every body-hair pore flows supremely subtle radiance,
the ender of old age, misfortune, and fear, the one who ferries across the ocean of existence,
I worship the leader of the world, the destroyer of sorrow and disease,
the contemplation of the world in the three realms, the sole purifier of the triple world. //
seated on an awakened lotus, awakened in the grove of <s>Bodhi</s>,
in the pure ocean of the <s>Śākyas</s>, like the moon in the ocean of milk,
Homage! He who protected and made a human birth in the world,
you will destroy, blazing, the darkness of delusion of the triple net! //
you who are now made of the nectar of discourse, who will delight,
who conquered the army of <s>Māra</s>, who took refuge in the grass-seat,
To you who stood at the seat of <s>Bodhi</s>, for the benefit of the multitude of worlds,
surrounded by the <s>Bodhi</s>-vows — homage to you, O <s>Dharma</s>-King! //
well-born as a <s>Śākya</s> king, endowed with the ultimate truths,
arisen from the glory of supreme awakening, radiant as the auspicious mountain, of auspicious portion,
I worship the auspicious and noble one, the breaker of the nature of existence,
shining like the auspicious sun, well-cultivated, bringing auspiciousness. //
who bore the burden of awakening to break the weight of the flood of existence,
beautifully shining like a fully blossomed tree of a thousand <s>kalpas</s>,
At the base-pavilion of the lord of <s>Jinas</s>, with a brilliant, spread canopy,
I always bow to the supreme <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Śākya</s> follower of <s>Sugata</s>. //
seated on a golden jewel-railing grass-seat, the all-pervading lord —

children.text: paṭhanti ye jināgrato vinirmitaṃ hareṇa tat

children.translated_text: with the five excellent fly-whisks, thrice daily as an auspicious [practice] —
Those who recite this hymn composed by <s>Hara</s> (Śiva) before the <s>Jina</s>,
and they go to <s>Sukhāvatī</s>, to the excellent blissful <s>Sukhāvatī</s>, with happiness. //
endowed with fame and <s>Dharma</s>, the seven prosperities shine,
The <s>Śrī Śākyasiṃha</s> hymn composed by <s>Śaṅkara</s> is complete. //

children.text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 84: Śākyasiṃhastotram surapatikṛtam
children.translated_text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 84: <s>Śākyasiṃhastotram</s>, composed by <s>Surapati</s> (Indra)
the omniscient one, the knowledge-body, free from the three impurities, the follower of <s>Sugata</s>, the king of awakening,
I bow to <s>Śrī Śākyasiṃha</s>, the benefactor of all, the king of <s>Dharma</s>, the great lord,
the fully awakened one, the lord of the world, the remover of all fears, abiding in the mortal world. //
the foundation of <s>Dharma</s>, the lord of sages, possessing the ten powers, of dense glory, of universal form,

children.text: rityākhyāṃ bodhihetustadanu ca tuṣitā cāgatā bodhirāja /
children.translated_text: the cause of awakening — then from <s>Tuṣita</s> heaven you came, O king of awakening,
You who are the lord supreme of <s>Dharma</s>, attended by all sons of the <s>Jinas</s>, known as <s>Śvetaketu</s> (White Banner),
you entered the pure, stainless, jewel-arrayed womb of <s>Māyā</s>. //
having installed <s>Maitreya</s> with delighted mind on your own seat, consecrating him,

children.text: garbhe sthitvā 'pi yastvaṃ sakalahitakarīṃ dharmavyākhyāṃ karoṣi

children.translated_text: and at the [due] time, you were born from the right side of your mother, manifesting with all your own hands.
Though abiding in the womb, you delivered the <s>Dharma</s>-discourse beneficial to all,

children.text: lokācāraṃ ca kṛtvā vihitadaśavidhiṃ vai vivāhādi tattat
tyaktvā sarvāṃśca rājyaṃ sakalajanahite nirgataṃ tvāṃ name 'ham //
children.translated_text: renouncing all, including the kingdom, you departed for the welfare of all people — I bow to you! //
Having performed the worldly customs, the ten prescribed rites, including marriage and the rest,
rises blazingly, destroying the darkness of delusion in the caverns of the three worlds,
From whose <s>ūrṇā</s> (forehead mark), constantly every day, rightward-spiraling radiance

children.text: proddhṛtvā svargaloke suratarukalite sthāpitā yena vande //
children.translated_text: by whom they were lifted up and established in the heavenly world adorned with wish-fulfilling trees — I worship him! //
with rays flowing from forty excellent teeth, illuminating the hell-beings —
the radiant goddess Earth, surrounded by her hosts, having split open that earth,
Whose hands bear the wheel-mark, granting desired fruits, one who has gone to the perfection of generosity,

children.text: sākṣībhūtā nilīnā praṇamitaśirasā tvāṃ name 'haṃ jinendram //
children.translated_text: she became a witness, and bowing her head, disappeared — I bow to you, O lord of <s>Jinas</s>! //
standing before [him], having worshipped, having rebuked <s>Namuci</s> (Māra) who had come, the hostile one —
are unable to see — what then of those like me dwelling in the human city?
Before whose uplifted neck, even <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Śiva</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s> (Madhuhṛt), and the skilled beings established in the world

children.text: ūrdhvaṃ lokottarākhye nijabhuvanavare bhāsitaṃ tvāṃ name 'ham //
children.translated_text: above, in the supreme world of his own called 'transcendent' — I bow to you who shine! //
Having transcended the cosmic egg (<s>Brahmāṇḍa</s>), the sun and moon, the sky, and the world of stars,
in which the cosmic egg yawns, encircled by the host of worlds, like a pericarp —
Whose face is like a lotus, rich with divine-toothed stamens and petal-ears,

children.text: kṛtvā kecitprayātāḥ śaraṇamabhimataṃ śrīghanaṃ tvāṃ name 'ham //
children.translated_text: some departed, taking their desired refuge — I bow to you, O one of dense glory! //
seeing which, <s>Namuci</s> (Māra) fainted, his followers were terrified — O omniscient Lord,

children.text: taiḥ sarvairmīlayitvā yadi tava mahimā varṇyate kalpakālam /
children.translated_text: if all of them together were to describe your greatness for an entire <s>kalpa</s>-age,
The scholars skilled in numerical knowledge who dwell in the abode of the three worlds —

children.text: pāraṃ gantuṃ samarthā nahi nikhilaguṇakṣīrasindhoḥ kathañcid
ekākī kiṃ samarthāstadapi mama mano bodhanārthaṃ name tvām //
children.translated_text: how then could I alone be capable? Nevertheless, I bow to you for the awakening of my mind. //
they would not at all be capable of reaching the far shore of the milk-ocean of your complete virtues;
the world-guardians beginning with <s>Śakra</s> (Indra), with their attendants on every step, will effect protection.
Those who recite this hymn composed by <s>Surapati</s> (Indra), in the meter called <s>Sragdharā</s>,

children.text: saukhyaṃ bhuktveha loke tadanu surapateḥ kalpavṛkṣābhikīrṇe

children.translated_text: having abided, they go at last to the land of the sons of the <s>Sugata</s>, the sole destination of all worldly beings. //
Having enjoyed happiness in this world, then in [the realm] of <s>Surapati</s> (Indra) adorned with wish-fulfilling trees,
The <s>Śrī Śākyasiṃha</s> hymn composed by <s>Surapati</s> (Indra) is complete. //

children.text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 85: Śākyasiṃhastotram viṣṇukṛtam
children.translated_text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 85: <s>Śākyasiṃhastotram</s>, composed by <s>Viṣṇu</s>
<s>Oṃ</s>! Homage to the Omniscient One!

children.text: name śrīghana tvāṃ sadābhāvabhakto bhavāmbhodhisetuṃ lasanmokṣahetum /
children.translated_text: I bow to you, O <s>Śrīghana</s> (Dense Glory), always with devotion of the heart, the bridge across the ocean of existence, the radiant cause of liberation,

children.text: tridhātuṃ vidhātuṃ surakṣāṃ virakṣāṃ sudakṣaṃ sukakṣāṃ sujātaṃ sudāntam //
children.translated_text: who has arranged the three realms, for excellent protection, free from [danger], skillful, of excellent side, well-born, well-tamed. //
I bow to the state of the <s>Sugata</s>, who has gone to the perfection of great knowledge, [endowed with] generosity, morality, patience, meditation, and vigor,
who rescues the world through the four <s>Brahmavihāras</s> (divine abodes), of beautiful appearance, teaching the <s>Dharma</s> of the Four Noble Truths. //

children.text: name bodhirājaṃ sugamye virājaṃsuramye vane devarājādigamyam /
children.translated_text: I bow to the king of <s>Bodhi</s> (Awakening), reigning in the accessible, delightful forest, reached by <s>Indra</s> and other gods,
seated on the fourth seat, bestowing the purpose of welfare, who has established many in well-being, stationed for the protection of the world. //

children.text: caturmāralokaṃ mahadvīryavantaṃ jayantaṃ hasantaṃ trijālaṃ ca kālam /
children.translated_text: Conquering, laughing at the world of the four <s>Māras</s>, of great heroic power, and the time of the triple net,

children.text: kṣamānaddhadehaṃ name muktagehaṃ trilokyaikanāthaṃ tathā śākyanātham //
children.translated_text: with a body bound by patience — I bow to the abode of liberation, the sole lord of the three worlds, and also the lord of the <s>Śākyas</s>. //

children.text: name mārasainyaṃ jitaṃ yena sarvaṃ nirastreṇa sāhāyyamuktena nūnam /
children.translated_text: I bow — by whom the entire army of <s>Māra</s> was conquered, by one without weapons, indeed with help renounced,
wearing the armor of patience, bearing the bow of <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness), stationed at the <s>Bodhi</s> tree, to protect the world. //

children.text: name śītavyañjairlasaddehagehaṃ jane snehavantaṃ vane gehavantam /
children.translated_text: I bow — whose body-abode is radiant with cool marks, compassionate toward people, dwelling in the forest,
endowed with the thirty-two marks called major marks, exceedingly rare, worshipped by the three worlds. //

children.text: name dharmameghāsthitaṃ supratiṣṭhaṃ kalau nāthahīne bhaveyaṃ sanāthaḥ /
children.translated_text: Homage! To him established in the <s>Dharmamegha</s> (Cloud of Dharma) stage, well-established — in the <s>Kali</s> age, bereft of a protector, may I become one with a protector!

children.text: tathā pālituṃ svāṃ pratijñāṃ cakāra janiṃ śākyavaṃśe mahīpāvataṃse //
children.translated_text: Thus, to fulfill his own vow, he took birth in the <s>Śākya</s> lineage, the crest-jewel of earth-protectors. //

children.text: name bhāgyato labhyate darśanaṃ te tathā bhāgyabhājo svayameti buddhiḥ /
children.translated_text: Homage! Your sight is obtained only through fortune; likewise, the fortunate ones' own wisdom comes spontaneously;

children.text: sthito dharmameghe kathaṃ darśanaṃ syād vihīnā na tatrābhigantuṃ praśaktāḥ //
children.translated_text: established in the <s>Dharmamegha</s> [stage], how could there be a vision? The deficient are not capable of reaching there. //
Now, by the mass of dust arisen from your lotus feet, the three worlds are purified;

children.text: tathāsmācchirāṃsi pavitrāṇi satyaṃ cariṣyāmi bodhiṃ bhavacchāsanena //
children.translated_text: likewise, our heads are purified — truly, I shall practice awakening through your teaching. //

children.text: bhujaṅgaprayātaṃ kṛtaṃ mādhavena paṭhed yo jinasyāgratastho hi nityam /
children.translated_text: This <s>Bhujaṅgaprayāta</s> [meter hymn] was composed by <s>Mādhava</s>; whoever, standing before the <s>Jina</s>, recites it daily —

children.text: sadā maṅgalaṃ tasya gehe sudehe prasannāśca rakṣāṃ kariṣyanti buddhāḥ //
children.translated_text: there is always auspiciousness in his home and excellent body, and the <s>Buddhas</s>, being pleased, will grant protection. //

children.text: trijālaṃ ca chitvā sukhāni prabhuktvā tathā dānaśīlādipāraṃgatāśca /
children.translated_text: Having cut through the three nets [of existence] and enjoyed happiness, and having attained the <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections) of generosity, morality, and the rest,
having attained great awakening, the protectors of the world will finally go to the [Pure Land] called <s>Sukhāvatī</s>. //
The <s>Bhujaṅgaprayāta</s> hymn to the glorious <s>Śākyasiṃha</s> (Lion of the Śākyas), composed by <s>Viṣṇu</s>, is complete. //

children.text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 86: Śākyasiṃhastotram yaśodharākṛtam
children.translated_text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 86: <s>Śākyasiṃhastotra</s> (Hymn to the Lion of the Śākyas) composed by <s>Yaśodharā</s>
'This one is your father, the ender of birth, death, and old age;
named <s>Sarvārthasiddha</s> (Accomplisher of All Aims), now [known as] <s>Śākyasiṃha</s> (Lion of the Śākyas), O son!' //
'In whose shade one would become divinely beautiful,
who bears the thirty-two marks — behold your father now!' //
'Having abandoned eighty-four thousand women, free from intoxication,
he who went to the forest of austerities — worship him, the one of great powers!' //
'The seven jewels, the kingdom, and the supreme station of great sovereignty —

children.text: hitvā pravrajito yo 'sau taṃ darśaya jagadgurum //
children.translated_text: having abandoned all, he who went forth as a renunciant — behold him, the guru of the world!' //
'He who was born from the right side of grandmother <s>Māyā</s>,

children.text: lumbinyāmudayāt sūrya iva taṃ pitaraṃ nama //
children.translated_text: in <s>Lumbinī</s>, rising like the sun — bow to that father!' //
'By <s>Abhayā</s>, the noble lady of the clan, at whose lotus feet he bowed —

children.text: traidhātukādhipaṃ devaṃ pitaraṃ tvaṃ sadā nama //
children.translated_text: to that god, the lord of the three realms, your father — always bow!' //
'He who appointed <s>Viśvāmitra</s> as his tutor for proper discipline,
though his soul delighted in the play of childhood — always bow to that father!' //
'Seated beneath the <s>Jambu</s> tree, the five sages, their splendor humbled,

children.text: nirmāninaḥ prābhajan yamenaṃ tātaṃ sadā nama //
children.translated_text: worshipped him, free from pride — always bow to that father!' //
'He who, having awakened his father, made him renounce six portions —
the compassionate one, worshipped by the world — bow to that progenitor, O son!' //
'He who conquered <s>Devadatta</s> and the rest, those proud ones — the all-knowing, the wise,
the learned one who [demonstrated] all fruits — worship that wise progenitor!' //
'On his journey, he who saw the sick, the old, the dead, and the renunciant —

children.text: svayaṃ vijño 'pi papraccha sadā taṃ janakaṃ bhaja //
children.translated_text: though himself already wise, he asked [about them] — always worship that progenitor!' //
'He whose mind was not carried away by the fire of desire while dwelling among beautiful women —

children.text: nirañjanaṃ nirvikalpaṃ suta taṃ janakaṃ bhaja //
children.translated_text: the unstained, the one beyond conceptual construction — O son, worship that progenitor!' //
'Mounting the golden horse <s>Kaṇṭhaka</s>, with <s>Chandaka</s>, he departed
from the land at midnight, praised by the gods — worship him with joy!' //
'He sent back the horse and <s>Chandaka</s> from the forest of austerities,
giving his fine neck-ornament — speak of him, the forest-dweller!' //
'Having approached the river <s>Nairañjanā</s>, he who performed the vow of austerity
for six years for the welfare of the world — worship him, the supreme ascetic!' //
'Seated under the <s>Bodhi</s> tree, having conquered <s>Māra</s>, so difficult to overcome,
he who obtained the jewel of awakening — behold him, the <s>Tathāgata</s>!' //
'Stationed in the Deer Park at <s>Kāśī</s> (Vārāṇasī), turning the wheel of <s>Dharma</s>,
he who was surrounded by <s>Brahmā</s> and others — behold him, the Guru, O son!' //
Having heard the words spoken thus by his mother, <s>Rāhula</s>, greatly amazed,
bowing, looking at his father, attained joy, his face smiling. //
The glorious <s>Śākyasiṃhastotra</s> composed by <s>Yaśodharā</s> is complete. //

children.text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 87: Śāradāṣṭakastotram
children.translated_text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 87: <s>Śāradāṣṭakastotra</s> (Eight-Verse Hymn to Śāradā/Sarasvatī)
Her whose beautiful body resembles a conch, the moon, <s>kunda</s> flowers, and snow, who is seated on a swan, who is most lovely with lotus-leaf [eyes],
whose gentle form is adorned with divine garments and ornaments — to the glorious <s>Bhagavatī Śāradā</s>, I always bow. //
Her who rescues beings drowning in the great ocean of <s>saṃsāra</s>, whose lotus feet are worshipped by gods and men,
whose body is adorned with necklaces, half-necklaces, jeweled earrings — to the glorious <s>Bhagavatī Śāradā</s>, I always bow. //

children.text: yā bhāratīti kathitā jananī ca loke mohāndhakārabharabhagnakṛtāṃ janānām /
children.translated_text: She who is called <s>Bhāratī</s> in the world, the mother of people who are crushed by the mass of the darkness of delusion,

children.text: saṃkīrtitā munibhirastasamastadoṣaiḥ śrīśāradāṃ bhagavatīṃ satataṃ namāmi //
children.translated_text: praised by sages who are free from all faults — to the glorious <s>Bhagavatī Śāradā</s>, I always bow. //
Her who delights in playing the <s>vīṇā</s>, who holds a crystal rosary, who bears a golden book,

children.text: ratnaiḥ śubhaiḥ surucirāṃ kṛtahastapadmāṃ śrīśāradāṃ bhagavatīṃ satataṃ namāmi //
children.translated_text: who is resplendent with auspicious jewels, whose hand is [adorned with] a lotus — to the glorious <s>Bhagavatī Śāradā</s>, I always bow. //

children.text: pūjyā sadaiva jananī parivandanīyā devyā gaṇā manasi saṃparimodanīyāḥ /
children.translated_text: She who is always worshipped, the mother worthy of reverence, whose hosts of goddesses are to be delighted in the mind,

children.text: jīvārthinaḥ phalabhṛto guṇavarṇanā ca śrīśāradāṃ bhagavatīṃ satataṃ namāmi //
children.translated_text: who gives life and fruit, and [whose] virtues are to be described — to the glorious <s>Bhagavatī Śāradā</s>, I always bow. //

children.text: natvā bhajejjagati yo jananīṃ prasiddhāṃ kuryātsadā bhagavatī kilapañcasaukhyam /
children.translated_text: He who, having bowed, worships the renowned mother in the world — the Blessed One bestows upon him the five happinesses:

children.text: saundaryarūpaguṇavittasubhogabhājaṃ śrī śāradāṃ bhagavatīṃ satataṃ namāmi //
children.translated_text: beauty, form, virtue, wealth, and excellent enjoyment — to the glorious <s>Bhagavatī Śāradā</s>, I always bow. //
She who is to be worshipped with offerings, <s>bali</s> oblations, and acts of worship, whose hosts of goddesses have beautiful, charming lotus-faces,

children.text: yaiḥ pūjitā bhagavatī kila jāḍyahantrī śrīśāradāṃ bhagavatīṃ satataṃ namāmi //
children.translated_text: she who, when worshipped, destroys dullness — to the glorious <s>Bhagavatī Śāradā</s>, I always bow. //
By understanding whose grace, the giver of happiness, one becomes equal in radiance to the rising sun of the Lord of the three worlds,

children.text: dharmārthakāmaphaladāmatha mokṣadāṃ ca śrīśāradāṃ bhagavatīṃ satataṃ namāmi //
children.translated_text: she who grants the fruits of <s>dharma</s>, <s>artha</s>, and <s>kāma</s>, and also grants <s>mokṣa</s> — to the glorious <s>Bhagavatī Śāradā</s>, I always bow. //
The glorious <s>Śāradāṣṭakastotra</s> (Eight-Verse Hymn to Śāradā) is complete. //

children.text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 88: Sragdharāpañcakastotram
children.translated_text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 88: <s>Sragdharāpañcakastotra</s> (Five Verses in Sragdharā Meter)
the primordial <s>Buddha</s> of all <s>Buddhas</s>, who has wrought manifold benefit, the abode of radiances,
I worship him whose form is reality, whose existence is stretched and expanded, whose nature is auspicious and worthy of oblation,
formless, unstained, always like the sky, pure, the <s>caitya</s> (shrine) of the mind. //
the embodiment of perfect awakening, resplendent with the three qualities, the sole cause of the five wisdoms,
with vigor, <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation), and <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) as my vessel for crossing the ocean, in the well-born cluster of jewels,
In your luminous form, through unwavering austerity, in the perfections of generosity, morality, patience,

children.text: bodhiṃ prāpto 'smi cāsmin sakalapūravare cākaniṣṭhe mahimni

children.translated_text: I worship you, of universal form, like a crystal jewel displaying various hues. //
I have attained awakening in this supreme, complete <s>Akaniṣṭha</s> heaven —
what then shall I offer, having abandoned kingdoms and other possessions for devotion to you?
Various healing remedies and excellent worship-materials are always offered by all worlds;

children.text: jātau jātau ca jātau kṛtasukṛtacayaṃ kāyavāṅmānasaistai

children.translated_text: all that I shall offer, together with my own body — accept it, O Supremely Wise One! //
In birth after birth after birth, the accumulations of merit made through body, speech, and mind —

children.text: ekaṃ yugmaṃ tṛtīyaṃ yugalayugamatho pañcamaṃ ṣaṣṭhasaṃjñaṃ
saptāṣṭau vai navākhyaṃ daśamamatha tathaikādaśaṃ dvādaśākhyam /
children.translated_text: seventh and eighth, named the ninth, the tenth, and likewise the eleventh, named the twelfth,
One, a pair, a third, a double pair, then a fifth, named the sixth,

children.text: ānantyaṃ svaṃ tadaivaṃ jagadakhilamabhūt tvāṃ name caikarūpam //
children.translated_text: infinity itself — thus the entire world came into being; I bow to you, the one of single form. //
the thirteenth, the fourteenth — and then the arrow-tortoise [cosmology], produced from one side,
the one called <s>Ratnasaṃbhava</s> is the third; the one named <s>Amitābha</s> is the fourth in number;
One is called <s>Vairocana</s>; then the next <s>Jina-Buddha</s> is named <s>Akṣobhya</s>;

children.text: devā daityāśca martyā bhavadavayavajāḥ sarvadā 'haṃ nato 'smi //
children.translated_text: gods, <s>Daityas</s>, and mortals, born from your parts — I am always bowing. //
the fifth is called <s>Amoghasiddhi</s> — and then in the world, the famed hosts of counted and uncounted
The <s>Sragdharāpañcaka</s> (Five Verses in Sragdharā Meter), composed by the glorious <s>Buddha Śākyasiṃha</s>, is complete. //

children.text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 89: Suprabhātastotram śrīharṣadevabhūpativiracitam
children.translated_text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 89: <s>Suprabhātastotra</s> (Morning Hymn) composed by King <s>Śrī Harṣadeva</s>
in heaven and on earth, with wonderfully varied words of praise by lords of ascetics,
Though praised by hosts of gods, <s>Siddhas</s>, <s>Gandharvas</s>, and <s>Yakṣas</s>,

children.text: nabhasi garuḍayāte kiṃ na yānti dvirephāḥ //
children.translated_text: when <s>Garuḍa</s> flies in the sky, do not the bees also fly? //
I too, exerting my power, praise the noble <s>Saṃbuddha</s> (Fully Awakened One) —
whose color is that of molten gold, whose eyes are wide as a full-blown lotus,
You whose wing of sin is destroyed, whose every fault is exhausted,
O <s>Daśabala</s> (One of Ten Powers), may your dawn always be a glorious dawn! //
whose radiant halo is most beautiful, whose glory is the splendid aureole —
who effects the welfare of the three worlds, who tears away the net of the creeper of women,
Of him who conquers the force of <s>Madana</s> (Kāma, god of love), who cuts down the evil path,
O <s>Daśabala</s>, may your dawn always be a glorious dawn! //
who bestows the fruit of equal happiness, who splits the mountain of ignorance —
the one word for the creation of the world in the entire realm of existence —
He who is the first-born, the foremost god of <s>Asuras</s>, gods, and men,
O <s>Daśabala</s>, may your dawn always be a glorious dawn! //
<s>Brahmā</s>, the self-born, of lotus-womb, the creator of men, is still sleeping —
the destroyer of the hosts of darkness, the sole eye of beings —
Standing on the summit of the eastern mountain, copper-red like a cut coral,
O <s>Daśabala</s>, may your dawn always be a glorious dawn! //
even the Sun, languid with pride, is still asleep in every way —
who is like the <s>tilaka</s>-mark of the night, the crest-jewel of all —
White as an elephant's tusk, the cool-rayed Moon,
O <s>Daśabala</s>, may your dawn always be a glorious dawn! //
he too, his passion not departed, is still asleep in every way —
who knows the rules of recitation, the expounder of the <s>Sāma Veda</s> —
Four-armed, with four half-half faces (four faces), the mighty one,
O <s>Daśabala</s>, may your dawn always be a glorious dawn! //
even <s>Brahmā</s>, born of the pure lotus, is asleep —
skilled in burning the three cities, wearing a tiger-skin as his upper garment —
Standing on the peak of the snow-mountain, with a serpent as his sacred thread,
O <s>Daśabala</s>, may your dawn always be a glorious dawn! //
even he, <s>Śiva</s> the trident-bearer, is asleep with the daughter of the mountain —
even <s>Indra</s>, the lord of gods, is bewildered in mind by <s>Śacī's</s> allurements —
Wielding a blazing thunderbolt, unconquerable by demons,
O <s>Daśabala</s>, may your dawn always be a glorious dawn! //
constantly asleep through every night, sunk in the mud of desire —
the destroyer of the strength of the enemies of gods, the creator and form of the universe —
Blue as a <s>kuvalaya</s> (water-lily) petal, with wide lotus-eyes,
O <s>Daśabala</s>, may your dawn always be a glorious dawn! //
even <s>Hari</s> (Viṣṇu) is long asleep, not freed from his dwelling in the womb [of the cosmic ocean] —
the lord of beasts (<s>Paśupati</s>), skilled solely in breaking attachments at the improper time —
With a mass of tawny matted locks, with red, coppery eyes,
O <s>Daśabala</s>, may your dawn always be a glorious dawn! //
even <s>Agni</s> (Fire), his body pierced by the arrows of <s>Kāma</s>, is also asleep —
with stout, hard limbs, bearing a plough and a mace in hand —
White as snow, the moon, and <s>kumuda</s> lilies, with eyes reddened from drinking wine,
O <s>Daśabala</s>, may your dawn always be a glorious dawn! //
<s>Balarāma</s> too lies here, clinging to <s>Revatī's</s> neck —
with <s>mada</s> (ichor) flowing freely, his cheeks swarming with bees —
Elephant-faced, with single tusk, the destroyer of all obstacles everywhere,
O <s>Daśabala</s>, may your dawn always be a glorious dawn! //
even <s>Gaṇapati</s> (Gaṇeśa) is asleep, intoxicated from drinking <s>Vāruṇī</s> liquor —
of beautiful form like a fresh lotus, six-faced, the slayer of <s>Krauñca</s> —
He whose spear is at the tip of his hand, blue as an <s>atasi</s> flower,
O <s>Daśabala</s>, may your dawn always be a glorious dawn! //
even that son of the three-eyed one, <s>Kumāra</s> (Skanda), is eternally sleeping —
enough of all destruction! — with bodies scorched like <s>Pretas</s> (hungry ghosts),
Those devoid of food and clothing, emaciated, deformed,
O <s>Daśabala</s>, may your dawn always be a glorious dawn! //
bereft of both courses, naked, they too are asleep —
<s>Kratu</s>, <s>Pulaha</s>, <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, <s>Vyāsa</s>, <s>Vālmīki</s>, <s>Garga</s> —
The great sages here — <s>Vatsa</s>, <s>Bhṛgu</s>, <s>Aṅgiras</s>, and others,
O <s>Daśabala</s>, may your dawn always be a glorious dawn! //
deluded by the charms of other men's wives, they too are asleep —
in heaven, on earth, or in the sky — the world-protectors and others,
<s>Yama</s>, <s>Varuṇa</s>, <s>Kubera</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Daityas</s>, <s>Uraga</s> (Nāga) lords,
O <s>Daśabala</s> (Ten-Powered One), for you it is always a beautiful dawn, a [true] dawn! //
gazed upon by the coquettish side-glances of maidens — they too are asleep;
Sunk in the ocean of existence, limbs enveloped by the net of delusion, <s>Manu</s>, <s>Kapila</s>, <s>Kaṇāda</s> — led astray, of confused minds,

children.text: samasukhaparihīnā vāliśāste 'pi suptā daśabala tava nityaṃ suprabhātaṃ prabhātam //
children.translated_text: devoid of the happiness of equanimity, those fools too are asleep; O <s>Daśabala</s>, for you it is always a beautiful dawn, a [true] dawn! //
Those who sleep in the darkness of the night of ignorance, on the wide bed of craving, with sense-objects as pillows —

children.text: kāle śubhāśubhaphalaṃ parikīryamāṇe jāgarti yaḥ satatameva namo 'stu tasmai //
children.translated_text: while the fruits of good and evil are being scattered by time, homage to that one who is always awake! //

children.text: tīrtheṣu gokulaśatāni pibanti toyaṃ tṛptiṃ vrajanti na ca tatkṣayamabhyupaiti /
children.translated_text: At the sacred fords, hundreds of herds of cattle drink the water, yet they are not satisfied, nor does [the water] come to an end;

children.text: tadvanmune kaviśatairapi saṃstutasya na kṣīyate guṇanidhirguṇasāgarasya //
children.translated_text: likewise, O sage, the treasure of virtues of one praised by hundreds of poets — the ocean of virtues — is never exhausted. //
The dawn is beautiful for you alone, whose eye is opened by knowledge;
for those blinded by the darkness of ignorance, the sun has forever set. //

children.text: punaḥ prabhātaṃ punarutthito raviḥ punaḥ śaśāṅkaḥ punareva śarvarī /
children.translated_text: Again comes the dawn, again the sun rises, again the moon, again the night;

children.text: mṛtyurjarā janma tathaiva he mune gatāgataṃ mūḍhajano na buddhyate //
children.translated_text: death, old age, birth — likewise, O sage — the deluded person does not understand this coming and going. //
A beautiful dawn, with auspicious stars, welcomed with splendor —

children.text: buddhaṃ dharmaṃ ca saṅghaṃ va praṇamāmi dine dine //
children.translated_text: to the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Dharma</s>, and the <s>Saṅgha</s>, I bow day after day. //
free from pairs [of opposites], with the darkness of passion and hatred destroyed, with senses at peace, free from longing —
Having praised the world-teacher, the best of great sages, the source of the merit of the true <s>Dharma</s>,

children.text: yatpuṇyaṃ samupārjitaṃ khalu mayā tenaiva loko 'khilaṃ

children.translated_text: delighted by the dawn-praise, find supreme faith in the <s>Daśabala</s>! //
whatever merit has been earned by me, by that very [merit] may the entire world,
The <s>Suprabhātastotra</s> (Dawn Hymn) of the <s>Daśabala</s>, composed by King <s>Śrī Harṣadeva</s>, is complete. //

children.text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 90: Svayaṃbhūstavaḥ
children.translated_text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 90: <s>Svayaṃbhūstavaḥ</s>
Homage to you of universal form! Homage to you of luminous form!
Homage always to the Self-Existent One (<s>Svayaṃbhū</s>), for the sake of the world's deliverance! //

children.text: tvaṃ buddhastvaṃ ca dharmo daśabalatanayastvaṃ tathā bodhisattva
stvaṃ bhikṣuḥ śrāvakastvaṃ kuliśavaradharastvaṃ tathā dharmadhātuḥ /
children.translated_text: you are the <s>bhikṣu</s> (monk), you are the <s>śrāvaka</s> (hearer), you are the bearer of the excellent <s>vajra</s>, thus you are the <s>Dharmadhātu</s> (realm of reality);
You are the <s>Buddha</s>, you are the <s>Dharma</s>, you are the son of the <s>Daśabala</s>, thus you are the <s>Bodhisattva</s>,

children.text: tvaṃ brahmā tvaṃ ca viṣṇuḥ pramathagaṇapatistvaṃ mahendro yamastvaṃ
tvaṃ pāśī tvaṃ dhaneśastvamanalapavanau nairṛtastvaṃ maheśaḥ //
children.translated_text: you are the noose-bearer (<s>Varuṇa</s>), you are the lord of wealth (<s>Kubera</s>), you are fire and wind, you are <s>Nairṛta</s>, you are <s>Maheśa</s> (great lord)! //
you are <s>Brahmā</s>, you are <s>Viṣṇu</s>, you are <s>Gaṇapati</s>, lord of the <s>pramatha</s> hosts, you are great <s>Indra</s>, you are <s>Yama</s>,
you are indeed the four types of birth, of the three finest qualities in body, the one form of the five knowledges;
<s>Bhūtas</s> (ghosts), <s>pretas</s> (hungry ghosts), and animals are you; the immortals, <s>Aditi's</s> sons, the oceans are you, and we ourselves;

children.text: annaṃ ratnaṃ ca sarvaṃ matirati mahatī naḥ sadā tvāṃ natāḥ smaḥ //
children.translated_text: food and jewels and everything — [our] great intellect and thought — we are always bowed to you! //
you are the colors, you are time and months, day and also night, the five elements are you indeed,

children.text: pañcajñānena buddhān sṛjasi svayamatho bodhisattvāṃśca pañca

children.translated_text: these elements, the three qualities, <s>Aja</s> (Brahmā), <s>Hari</s> (Viṣṇu), <s>Giriśa</s> (Śiva), and the stationary and moving [beings];
With the five knowledges you yourself create the <s>Buddhas</s> and also the five <s>Bodhisattvas</s>,

children.text: sarveṣāṃ cetasi stho naṭayasi sakalaṃ sarvato rakṣako 'si
tvaṃ bījaṃ cāṅkurastvaṃ phalamapi viṭapī sarvadā tvāṃ natāḥ smaḥ //
children.translated_text: you are the seed, you are the sprout, you are the fruit and the tree — we are always bowed to you! //
you dwell in the minds of all, you perform everything, you are the protector of all from everywhere —

children.text: śreṣṭhaṃ kṣatraṃ tvamasmin prabhavasi bhagavān sarvataḥ sarvadevān

children.translated_text: villages, sacred fords, countries, kings along with people, and all townsfolk too;
You are the best sacred field; O Blessed One, you bring forth all gods everywhere,

children.text: dvīpeṣvanyeṣvapi tvaṃ vibhajasi sakalaṃ jyotiṣāṃ saṃvibhāgam

children.translated_text: you are the one lamp that is the source [of all], pervading the entire world — we bow to you! //
in other continents too, you distribute all the portions of luminaries —
Your radiance, spreading in all directions — white, red, dark, yellow, and crimson —

children.text: dṛṣṭaṃ tataḥ sarvamidaṃ bhavantaṃ manyāmahe tvāṃ praṇatāḥ sma nityam //
children.translated_text: seeing all this, we consider [everything] to be you — we bow to you always! //
Those humans who recite this praise composed by the great kings,
having attained the status of a universal monarch (<s>cakravartin</s>), they indeed shall obtain liberation. //
The <s>Svayaṃbhūstava</s> composed by the four great kings is complete. //

children.text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 91: Svayambhūstotram
children.translated_text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 91: <s>Svayambhūstotram</s>
I bow to the Self-Existent One (<s>Svayaṃbhū</s>), created for the world's sake, without beginning, concealed, imperishable,
the Self-Existent One who is the self of the body's framework! //
I bow to the Self-Existent One — the thousand-petalled lotus, arisen from the beautiful whorl, shining,
the bestower of all desires! //
I bow to the Self-Existent One — delighting a thousand suns, the joy of ten million moons,
worshipped by the worlds of gods and others! //
You alone shine with virtues, established on earth you are resplendent,
you illuminate the three realms — I bow to the Self-Existent One! //

children.text: ayaṃ ka ityayaṃ hṛdā mīmāṃsituṃ na śaktavān /
children.translated_text: "What is this?" — thus the heart is unable to fathom [it],
seen only as a glimpse — I bow to the Self-Existent One! //

children.text: paṭhanti ye narā mudā svayaṃbhuvaḥ stutiṃ sadā /
children.translated_text: Those people who joyfully recite the praise of <s>Svayaṃbhū</s> always,
having attained the accomplishment of the three aims [of life], they obtain that very liberation. //
The <s>Svayambhūstotra</s>, composed by <s>Śikhin</s>, extracted from the great <s>Svayaṃbhūpurāṇa</s>, is complete. //

children.text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 92: Vāgīśvaravarṇanāstotram
children.translated_text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 92: <s>Vāgīśvaravarṇanāstotram</s>

I always bow to <s>Vāgīśvara</s> (Lord of Speech), the teacher of gods, whose body is worshipped by <s>Brahmā</s> and other gods, humans, and <s>Asuras</s>, the abode of all [forms of] knowledge, possessing the kingship of virtues,

children.text: jñānādhipaṃ guṇamayaṃ guṇavṛddhimantaṃ vāgīśvaraṃ suraguruṃ satataṃ namāmi //
children.translated_text: the lord of knowledge, consisting of virtues, endowed with the growth of virtues. //

I always bow to <s>Vāgīśvara</s>, the teacher of gods, who knows the composition of the <s>Vedas</s> and all other <s>śāstras</s> (sciences) and all <s>mantras</s>, whose well-sung words are [celebrated] through hymns, narratives, and the like,

children.text: yaṃ kīryayanti munayo naravāṇyabhijñaṃ vāgīśvaraṃ suraguruṃ satataṃ namāmi //
children.translated_text: whom the sages extol, who is skilled in human speech. //

children.text: jñānapradhānakaśarīramacintyabuddhiṃ vācaspatiṃ divi bhuvi stutakīrtidaṃ tam /
children.translated_text: I always bow to <s>Vāgīśvara</s>, the teacher of gods, whose body is the foremost in knowledge, of inconceivable intelligence, the lord of speech, who gives praised fame in heaven and on earth,

children.text: jñāneśvaraṃ tribhuvaneśacarācaraṃ taṃ vāgīśvaraṃ suraguruṃ satataṃ namāmi //
children.translated_text: the lord of knowledge, [lord of] the moving and unmoving in the three worlds. //
I always bow to <s>Vāgīśvara</s>, the teacher of gods, who is fully known through the fashioning of jewels and other arts, of wondrous and variegated virtues, to be honored by the people,

children.text: sarvajñakārakadharād hṛdi brahmapuñjaṃ vāgīśvaraṃ suraguruṃ satataṃ namāmi //
children.translated_text: from whose heart, the bearer of all-knowing nature, [comes] the mass of <s>Brahma</s>-[knowledge]. //

children.text: caryāvidhau ratipatiṃ sthiradhairyabodhiṃ dhyānādhipaṃ vividhinā sukharañjanīyam /
children.translated_text: I always bow to <s>Vāgīśvara</s>, the teacher of gods, the lord of love in the practice of conduct, of steadfast courage and awakening, the lord of meditation, to be delighted by various means of happiness,

children.text: vidyāpratiṣṭhitaguruṃ bhuvanetipūrṇaṃ vāgīśvaraṃ suraguruṃ satataṃ namāmi //
children.translated_text: the guru established in knowledge, complete in the earth and so on. //

children.text: vāṇīpatiṃ bhujacatuṣṭayabāṇacāpaṃ pustaṃ kṛpāṇamaniśaṃ kramaśo dadhānam /
children.translated_text: I always bow to <s>Vāgīśvara</s>, the teacher of gods, the lord of speech, bearing four arms with a bow and arrow, a book, and a sword, in sequence constantly,

children.text: sarveṣṭadaṃ jagati yaccaṇāravindaṃ vāgīśvaraṃ suraguruṃ satataṃ namāmi //
children.translated_text: the bestower of all desires in the world — that lotus one. //
The <s>Śrī Vāgīśvaravarṇanāstotram</s> (Hymn Describing the Lord of Speech) is complete. //

children.text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 93: Vāgvāṇīstotram
children.translated_text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 93: <s>Vāgvāṇīstotram</s>
I pay homage to <s>Sarasvatī</s>, consciousness dwelling in the heart,
abiding in the throat, of lotus-origin, always fond of the syllable <s>Hrīṃ</s>. //
The giver of intelligence, the granter of boons, the bestower of all desires,
the beloved goddess of <s>Keśava</s> (Viṣṇu), holding a <s>vīṇā</s> (lute), granting boons. //
Fond of the <s>mantras</s> <s>Aiṃ</s> and <s>Hrīṃ</s>, the destroyer of foolish thinking,
self-luminous, without support, the remover of the darkness of ignorance. //
The granter of liberation, eternally auspicious, bestower of excellent boons, fond of purification,
dissolved in the disk of the sun — I bow to her, beloved of the <s>Jina</s>! //
Of the form of knowledge, lamp of the world, the destroyer of the bonds of devotees —

children.text: iti samyak stutā devī vāgīśena mahātmanā //
children.translated_text: thus properly praised, the goddess, by <s>Vāgīśa</s> (Lord of Speech), the great soul, //
showed herself, radiant as the autumn moon.

children.text: sarasvatyuvāca varaṃ vṛṇīṣva bhadanta yatte manasi vartate //
children.translated_text: <s>Sarasvatī</s> said: "Choose a boon, O venerable one, whatever is in your mind." //

children.text: bṛhaspatiruvāca prasannā yadi me devī divyaṃ jñānaṃ pradīyatām /
children.translated_text: <s>Bṛhaspati</s> said: "If you are pleased with me, O Goddess, may divine knowledge be granted!"

children.text: sarasvatyuvāca stotreṇānena ye bhaktyā māṃ stuvanti sadā narāḥ //
children.translated_text: <s>Sarasvatī</s> said: "Those people who praise me always with this hymn, with devotion, //
they obtain supreme knowledge, equal in prowess to me,

children.text: kavitvaṃ matprasādena tathā ca vipulaṃ yaśaḥ //
children.translated_text: and poetic power by my grace, as well as abundant fame. //

children.text: trisandhyaṃ prayato bhūtvā yaḥ stotraṃ paṭhate naraḥ /
children.translated_text: That person who, having become pure, recites this hymn at the three <s>sandhyās</s> (twilight junctions),

children.text: tasya kaṇṭhe sadā vāsaṃ kariṣyāmi na saṃśayaḥ //
children.translated_text: in his throat I shall always dwell — of this there is no doubt." //

children.text:
om aiṃ vāgvādini mama jihvāyāṃ eeṃ hrīṃ mantrasarasvati svāhā /
      bṛhaspatikṛtaṃ śrīvāgvāṇīstotraṃ samāptam //
children.translated_text: <s>Oṃ Aiṃ</s>, O <s>Vāgvādinī</s> (Speaker of Speech), on my tongue, <s>Īṃ Hrīṃ Mantrasarasvatī Svāhā</s>! The <s>Śrī Vāgvāṇīstotram</s>, composed by <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, is complete. //

children.text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 94: Vajradevīstotram ācāryanāgārjunaviracitam
children.translated_text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 94: <s>Vajradevīstotram</s>, composed by Ācārya <s>Nāgārjuna</s>
<s>Oṃ</s>! Homage to the glorious <s>Yoginī</s> Goddess!

children.text: ḍākī yā sarvabuddhā sakalabhayaharā vyāpinī viśvamātā

children.translated_text: one-faced, of red complexion, joyful with three eyes, a sky-goer, of supreme beauty,
The <s>Ḍākinī</s>, who is all <s>Buddhas</s>, the remover of all fears, all-pervading, the Mother of the Universe,
bearing a <s>khaṭvāṅga</s> (skull-staff) in the left hand, holding a skull-cup in the right — of heavenly form! //
blazing with a divine body, with feet established in the sky, two-armed, with loose hair,
the path of liberation for beings, granter of the supreme boon, bestower of the <s>siddhi</s> (accomplishment) of knowledge;
Naked, with a garland on the neck composed of human heads, adorned with the five <s>mudrās</s> (seals),
your feet are lotus-shaped — with bowed head I praise you, O queen of <s>Vidyādharīs</s>! //
O glorious goddess, protector of beings, benefactress of the world, <s>Yoginī</s> of <s>vajra</s>-radiance —
O Blessed Goddess, O great deity — your refuge, O <s>Vajra</s>-one,

children.text: vande pādāmbuje nityaṃ bhajāmi tvāṃ prasīda me //
children.translated_text: I worship your lotus-feet always; I adore you — be gracious to me! //
O Mother of all <s>Buddhas</s>, you yourself are the giver of awakening;
the mother of all <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, the protector and nurturer of welfare. //
The sustainer of all welfare, the purifier of all sins,
shaking the hosts of wicked <s>Māras</s>, the giver of the happiness of great bliss. //
In the zeal of practicing the true <s>Dharma</s>, the bestower of the qualities of strength and valor,
the giver of the happiness of stilled meditation and <s>samādhi</s> (concentration), free from <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions). //
The bestower of the wealth of the great jewel of wisdom-qualities —
taking refuge at the lotus-feet of the Blessed Goddess, I worship! //
I bow to <s>Vajravārāhī</s>, the liberator from all sins,
the goddess who destroys <s>Māra</s>, the bestower of the fruit of <s>Buddhahood</s>. //
I praise the glorious <s>Vajravārāhī</s>, the embodiment of <s>mantras</s>, the sovereign of the <s>Jinas</s>,
the goddess who grants supreme boons, the bestower of excellent <s>ṛddhi</s> (power) and <s>siddhi</s> (accomplishment). //
Born from the family of <s>Vairocana</s>, with loose hair, three-eyed,
with a complexion like twilight vermillion — I worship you, O sovereign of the <s>vajra</s>! //
With a head beautified by the five <s>mudrās</s>, bearing a <s>khaṭvāṅga</s> on the shoulder,
with a <s>vajra</s>-skull-cup in hand — I worship the <s>vajra</s>-enchantress! //
Bearing the five <s>mudrās</s> on the body, adorned with a garland of skulls,
with a lotus-face of playful laughter — I worship the beauty of the three worlds! //
Preceded by <s>Bhairava</s>, with three faces, with <s>carcikā</s> (song) at the neck of prowess,
dense and terrible with hostility — I worship the fearful and terrifying one! //
Between passion and dispassion, transcending existence and non-existence,

children.text: samudbhūtāṃ sadā devīṃ vande tāṃ jñānaḍākinīm //
children.translated_text: always arisen, a goddess — I worship that <s>Jñāna Ḍākinī</s> (Knowledge-Ḍākinī)! //
Drinking the five nectars and liquor, feasting well on the five [types of] rice,
always delighting in song and music — I worship you, worshipped by the gods! //
Always in innate bliss, eternally present, abode of all,
with tinkling anklets on the feet — I worship the one devoted to dance! //
You, the goddess, bestower of <s>siddhis</s>, always delighting in <s>yogācāra</s> (yogic practice),
you, the bestower of <s>Buddha's</s> <s>nirvāṇa</s> — I worship you, the mother of the <s>Buddha</s>! //
Red-bodied <s>Vajravārāhī</s>, embodying a divine form,
goddess of compassion in a striding posture — I bow to <s>Vajrayoginī</s>! //
Resembling a <s>bandhūka</s> flower, of peaceful form, sovereign of the <s>Jinas</s>,
goddess bestowing <s>ṛddhi</s> and <s>siddhi</s> — I bow to <s>Vajrayoginī</s>! //
Endowed with the fullness of twelve years, embodying the nine dances,
goddess pervading the three worlds — I bow to <s>Vajrayoginī</s>! //
The <s>Vajradevīstotram</s>, composed by the venerable Ācārya <s>Śrī Nāgārjuna</s>, is complete. //

children.text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 95: Vajramahākālastotram ācāryanāgārjunakṛtam
children.translated_text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 95: <s>Vajramahākālastotram</s>, composed by Ācārya <s>Nāgārjuna</s>
with <s>Hu Huṃkāra</s> cries on all sides, with faces devouring human flesh, with bodies covered in garlands of blood,
With the sounds of <s>Hāṃ Hāṃ Hāṃkāra</s>, with the tumultuous cries of <s>kili kili</s>, with hosts of <s>Bhūtas</s> and <s>Vetālas</s>,
tawny-eyed, tawny-haired, with locks [adorned with] the fires of corpse-heaps — may the protector of the [cremation] ground protect you! //
with a <s>khaṭvāṅga</s> (skull-staff) and shoulder-hand, bearing human hands, of shape-shifting form, of hideous form,
placing a garland at the throat, with a manifestly fearsome body adorned with ornaments,
With <s>pheṃ pheṃ pheṃ</s>-sounds, with the face of a body pregnant with great fire produced in every direction,

children.text: klīṃ ḍāṃ klīṃ ḍāṃ ninādairvaradahanabhuvi kṣetrapaḥ pātu yuṣmān //
children.translated_text: with <s>klīṃ ḍāṃ klīṃ ḍāṃ</s> sounds — may the <s>Kṣetrapāla</s> (Field-Protector) on the excellent sacrificial ground protect you! //
with slightly reddened lower lip, with a hand holding a garland covering all blood-drops,

children.text: kṣaṃ kṣaṃ kṣaṃ kṣāntimūrtiḥ kalakalakalakṛt kṣāntivṛddhiṃ prakurvan /

children.translated_text: whose universe is trampled and untrampled, speaking <s>kahakahakathana</s>, of dark rain-cloud color,
O <s>kṣaṃ kṣaṃ kṣaṃ</s>, embodiment of patience, making sounds <s>kalakalakalakṛt</s>, promoting the growth of patience,

children.text: hrīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ mantradehaḥ paca paca dahanairjātamantraḥ samantād

children.translated_text: driving away obstacles, may the <s>Kṣetrapāla</s> (Field-Protector) surely pacify enemies! //
whose <s>mantra</s>-body is <s>hrīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ</s>, 'burn, burn' with fires — the <s>mantra</s> born everywhere —
and sinners — destroyer of obstacles, daily attaining the gain of awakening,
With <s>hā hā hā hā</s> bursts of laughter, causing exceeding fear always among the wicked beasts
may the glorious <s>Kṣetrapāla</s> protect [you], bearing the weight of <s>kleśa</s>-limbs in his tawny matted crown! //
filling the cavern of the three worlds with <s>huṃ phaṭ huṃ phaṭ</s> sounds, possessing full power —

children.text: khaṃ khaṃ khaṃ khaṅgapāṇirlalalalalalito rūpato raktapāṇiḥ
raṃ raṃ raṃ raktanetro ru ru rudhirakaraścarcitaścaṇḍavegaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>raṃ raṃ raṃ</s> — with blood-red eyes, <s>ru ru</s> — with blood-streaming hands, smeared, of fierce velocity,
<s>Khaṃ khaṃ khaṃ</s> — sword in hand, gracefully sporting, with blood-red hands,

children.text: kruṃ kruṃ kruṃ krodhadṛṣṭiḥ kuha kuha kuṭilaḥ kuñcitāśeṣaduṣṭaḥ
ḍaṃ ḍaṃ ḍaṃ ḍāmarāṅgo ḍamarukasahito rakṣatāt kṣetrapālaḥ //
children.translated_text: <s>ḍaṃ ḍaṃ ḍaṃ</s> — with <s>ḍāmara</s> body, bearing a <s>ḍamaruka</s> (drum) — may the <s>Kṣetrapāla</s> protect! //
<s>kruṃ kruṃ kruṃ</s> — with wrathful gaze, <s>kuha kuha</s> — crooked, who has crippled all the wicked,

children.text: yaṃ yaṃ yaṃ yāti viśvaṃ yamaniyamayuto yāmino 'yāmino vā
vaṃ vaṃ vaṃ vātavego jhaṭiti karakadhṛt prāptalokopacāraḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>vaṃ vaṃ vaṃ</s> — with the velocity of wind, swiftly holding hailstones, having obtained the service of the world,
<s>Yaṃ yaṃ yaṃ</s> — the universe goes wherever [he goes], endowed with restraint and discipline, whether night-walkers or not,

children.text: bhrūṃ bhrūṃ bhrūṃ bhīṣaṇāṅgo bhṛkuṭikṛtabhayo muktivān sādhakānāṃ
kṣaṃ kṣaṃ kṣaṃ kṣemakārī kṣapayatu duritaṃ rakṣatāt kṣetrapālaḥ //
children.translated_text: <s>kṣaṃ kṣaṃ kṣaṃ</s> — the maker of welfare — may the <s>Kṣetrapāla</s> destroy sins and protect! //
<s>bhrūṃ bhrūṃ bhrūṃ</s> — with terrifying body, creating fear with furrowed brows, granting liberation to practitioners,

children.text: klāṃ klāṃ klāṃ krāntimūrtistribhuvanamaniśaṃ kledayan sarvadā yaḥ
paṃ paṃ paṃ pāśahastaḥ paraśudhṛtakaraḥ pālayan pālanīyān /
children.translated_text: <s>paṃ paṃ paṃ</s> — with a noose in hand, bearing an axe, protecting those who should be protected,
<s>Klāṃ klāṃ klāṃ</s> — embodiment of power, who always moistens the three worlds ceaselessly,
that protector of fields, with a body conquering all — may he protect you with long life! //
the <s>mantra</s>-embodiment of <s>mudrās</s>, granting desired fruits to <s>mantra</s>-practitioners, equal to <s>mantras</s>,

children.text: klīṃ klīṃ klīṃ kṛttivāsā kṛtaripuniyamaḥ kleśitānāṃ sadeśaḥ
kaṃ kaṃ kaṃ kapālamālī kalikaluṣaharaḥ kālavṛndābhakāyaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>kaṃ kaṃ kaṃ</s> — wearing a garland of skulls, remover of the defilements of the Kali age, with a body like a host of death,
<s>Klīṃ klīṃ klīṃ</s> — clad in a hide, who has restrained enemies, the companion of the afflicted,

children.text: caṃ caṃ caṃ caṇḍavegaḥ pracaritasamayāḥ kālabhūtaikalokaḥ
saṃ saṃ saṃ saṃyatātmā samayaśubhaphalaṃ lakṣyatāṃ pātu yuṣmān //
children.translated_text: <s>saṃ saṃ saṃ</s> — self-restrained — may the auspicious fruit of the observance be seen! May he protect you! //
<s>caṃ caṃ caṃ</s> — of fierce velocity, whose observances are proclaimed, the sole world of time-beings,

children.text: ācāryaḥ sādhako vā japati ca niyataṃ puṇyavān jāyate 'sau /
children.translated_text: recites [this hymn to] the <s>mantra</s>-body of <s>mantras</s>, with the radiance of <s>Yama</s>'s discipline — that one surely becomes meritorious.
Whoever, whether <s>ācārya</s> (teacher) or practitioner, on the pure bank of the true path,

children.text: āyuḥ śrīḥ kīrtilakṣmīrdhṛtibalamatulaṃ śāntipuṣṭī prabhā ca
sarvajñatvaṃ ca nityaṃ dinaniśamatulaṃ naśyate vighnajātam //
children.translated_text: and omniscience — always, day and night, incomparably — all classes of obstacles are destroyed. //
Longevity, prosperity, fame, fortune, steadfastness, incomparable strength, peace, nourishment, and radiance,
The glorious <s>Vajra-Mahākāla-stotra</s> is complete. //

children.text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 96: Vajrapāṇināmāṣṭottaraśatastotram
children.translated_text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 96: <s>Vajrapāṇināmāṣṭottaraśatastotram</s>
O <s>Vajrasattva</s>, great being, great vehicle, great-souled one,
O great radiance, great purity, great lord — homage to you! //
O <s>Vajrarāja</s> (Vajra-King), great <s>vajra</s>, <s>Vajra</s> of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>,
great being, great vigor, great skillful means — homage to you! //
O <s>Vajrarāga</s> (Vajra-Passion), great purity, all happiness, great bliss,
supreme bliss without beginning or end, great desire — homage to you! //
O <s>Vajrasādhu</s> (Vajra-Excellent), great satisfaction, proclaimer of 'well done,' delighter,
great joy, great delight, most rejoicing — homage to you! //
O <s>Vajraratna</s> (Vajra-Jewel), great king, self-consecrated, great wise one,
all jewels, greatly resplendent ornament — homage to you! //
O <s>Vajrateja</s> (Vajra-Splendor), great splendor, <s>Vajraprabha</s> (Vajra-Light), great radiance,
<s>Jinaprabha</s> (Jina-Light), great flame, <s>Buddhaprabha</s> (Buddha-Light) — homage to you! //
O <s>Vajraketu</s> (Vajra-Banner), great banner, great flag, bestower of wealth,
banner of the sky, great staff, flag of renunciation — homage to you! //
O <s>Vajrahāsa</s> (Vajra-Laughter), great laughter, who causes great joy and delight,
swiftness of joy, delight in bliss, delight in <s>Dharma</s> — homage to you! //
O <s>Vajradharma</s>, great <s>Dharma</s>, purifier of all <s>dharmas</s>,
<s>Buddha-Dharma</s>, supreme true <s>Dharma</s>, <s>Dharma</s> of passion — homage to you! //
O <s>Vajratīkṣṇa</s> (Vajra-Sharp), great sheath, <s>Prajñā</s>-knowledge, great wise one,
great sword that cuts sin, weapon of the <s>Buddha</s> — homage to you! //
O <s>Vajrahetu</s> (Vajra-Cause), great wheel, <s>Buddha</s>-wheel, great treasure,
supreme <s>Dharma</s> of all <s>maṇḍalas</s>, <s>Dharmacakra</s> — homage to you! //
O <s>Vajrabhāṣa</s> (Vajra-Speech), great speech, free from conceptual elaboration, great syllable,
beyond syllables, great recitation, word of the <s>Buddha</s> — homage to you! //
O <s>Vajrakarma</s> (Vajra-Action), foremost of excellent actions, great action, doer of excellent deeds,
secret worship, great worship, <s>Buddha</s>-worship — homage to you! //
O <s>Vajrarakṣa</s> (Vajra-Protection), great armor, supreme cuirass, greatly firm,
great protection, great essence, <s>Buddha</s>-vigor — homage to you! //
O <s>Vajrayakṣa</s>, great wrath, terrifying to all the wicked,
great skillful means of all <s>Buddhas</s>, foremost <s>Yakṣa</s> — homage to you! //
Great union, great <s>mudrā</s>, great bond of <s>samaya</s> (vow),
great fist, foremost ocean, <s>Vajra</s>-fist — homage to you! //
Worthy of homage, of honor, and of worship, to be revered by <s>Tathāgatas</s> —
since you are called the <s>Bodhicitta</s> (Mind of Awakening) without beginning or end. //
Having relied upon you, all <s>Jinas</s> and heroic <s>Bodhisattvas</s>
have arisen and shall arise, as the chief causes of <s>Buddha</s>-awakening. //
Homage to <s>Vajrasattva</s>! Homage to <s>Vajraratna</s>!
Homage to <s>Vajradharma</s>! Homage to <s>Vajrakarma</s>! //
Having praised you with the foremost names and having bowed with sincere devotion,
whatever merit [is gained] — by that, may everyone attain <s>Buddha</s>-awakening! //
Whoever correctly recites this supreme hundred-and-eight names,
even just once, standing in great devotion — shall attain the state of all <s>Buddhas</s>. //
The glorious <s>Vajrapāṇi</s> One-Hundred-and-Eight Name Hymn is complete. //

children.text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 97: Vajrasattvastotram
children.translated_text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 97: <s>Vajrasattvastotram</s>
I bow to the glorious
the lord of <s>Jinas</s> of various forms, the remover of the fear of darkness, manifested, peaceful as <s>Meru</s>,
<s>Vajrasattva</s>, the supreme teacher of the world, all <s>Buddhas</s>, you,
the sole form of all bliss, consisting of supreme happiness, the cause of liberation for embodied beings. //
the support of the <s>Dharma</s> of sages, the bestower of the auspicious qualities of the <s>Jina</s>, the <s>maṇḍala</s> of <s>Vajradhātu</s> (Vajra-Realm),
A moon-ray dispelling the darkness that wards off the blind darkness of delusion in beings sunk in the ocean of dense ignorance —

children.text: jñānaṃ prakāśya paripūritavīryadhyānaṃ śrīvajrasattvamasamaṃ śirasā namāmi //
children.translated_text: having illuminated knowledge, fulfilled with vigor and meditation — to the incomparable glorious <s>Vajrasattva</s>, I bow with my head! //
He at whose lotus-feet multitudes of gods, <s>Asuras</s>, chiefs of gods, and lords of men have fallen like bees, with their heads —
to the great treasure-trove, the ocean of the accomplishment of <s>siddhis</s> — I go for refuge to the feet of the glorious <s>Lokanātha</s>! //
steadfast, endowed with depth, a treasury of all virtues, anointed as king of <s>Dharma</s>,
The <s>Buddha</s>, lord of the three worlds, bowed to by the best of gods, who has crossed beyond <s>saṃsāra</s>,

children.text: taṃ vande śākyasiṃhaṃ praṇamitaśirasā sarvakālaṃ namāmi //
children.translated_text: to him, <s>Śākyasiṃha</s>, I bow with head inclined — I salute him at all times! //
the darkness of craving and delusion, remover of the defilements of the Kali age, the terminator of desire and greed —
Born from the syllable <s>hrīṃ</s>, the Lord, with a mind moist with compassion,
named <s>Amoghapāśa</s> (Infallible Noose) — to <s>Lokanātha</s> (Lord of the World) I bow! //
<s>Māmakī</s>, <s>Locanā</s>, <s>Tārā</s>, <s>Padminī</s> — for the sake of the <s>Jina</s>-nature,
the abode of all <s>Buddhas</s>, the <s>caitya</s> (shrine), the <s>Dharmadhātu</s> — to that I bow! //
Homage to <s>Tāre</s>! <s>Ture</s>, the heroic! <s>Tuttāre</s>, the destroyer of fear!
<s>Ture</s>, the deliverer from all [afflictions], at all times — I bow to the <s>Svāhā</s>-utterance! //
With eyes [beautiful as] the white lotus of the true <s>Dharma</s>, an ocean of the qualities of the Omniscient One,
the Teacher <s>Samantabhadra</s> — to <s>Śākyasiṃha</s> I bow! //
The glorious <s>Vajrasattvastotra</s> is complete. //

children.text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 98: Vajrasattvastutiḥ
children.translated_text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 98: <s>Vajrasattvastutiḥ</s>

children.text: atha khalu bhagavantaḥ sarvatathāgatāḥ bhagavantaṃ mahāvajrasattvaṃ stuvanti sma-
children.translated_text: Then indeed, all the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, the Blessed Ones, praised the Blessed great <s>Vajrasattva</s> thus:
You whose nature is the <s>vajra</s> of delusion, terrifying to <s>Yama</s>, the enemy, and [his] delight,
pervading all <s>Buddhas</s>, peaceful — O <s>Kāyavajra</s> (Body-Vajra), homage to you! //
You whose nature is the <s>vajra</s> of slander, terrifying to <s>Yama</s>, the enemy, and [his] delight,
resembling the <s>Cittavajra</s> (Mind-Vajra) — O <s>Ratnavajra</s> (Jewel-Vajra), homage to you! //
You whose nature is the <s>vajra</s> of passion, terrifying to <s>Yama</s>, the enemy, and [his] delight,
the supreme foremost of all sounds — O <s>Vāgvajra</s> (Speech-Vajra), homage to you! //
You whose nature is the <s>vajra</s> of envy, terrifying to <s>Yama</s>, the enemy, and [his] delight,
resembling the <s>Kāyavajra</s> (Body-Vajra) — O <s>Saṅgapāṇi</s> (Assembly-Holder), homage to you! //
You whose nature is all <s>Buddhas</s>, the sole aggregate of all <s>Buddhas</s>,
the supreme foremost of all <s>Buddhas</s> — O Lord of the <s>Maṇḍala</s>, homage to you! //
The glorious praise of the great <s>Vajrasattva</s> is complete. //

children.text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 99: Vajravilāsinīstotram mahāpaṇḍitavibhūticandrapādakṛtam
children.translated_text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 99: <s>Vajravilāsinīstotram</s> composed by the great <s>Paṇḍita Vibhūticandrapāda</s>
<s>Oṃ</s>! Homage to the glorious <s>Vajrayoginī</s>!
O you whose feet are worshipped by gods, <s>Asuras</s>, and humans, whose feet are devoted to rescuing those drowning in existence —

children.text: tvayi rodimi nutisavyapadeśaḥ kiṃ paśyasi punaraniśamaśeṣam //
children.translated_text: I weep before you, a pretext for praise — why do you look on forever at the entirety? //

children.text: mātardevi kirasi kaṇamuṣṭiṃ janayad yajñasutaḥ kimatuṣṭim /
children.translated_text: O Mother Goddess, do you scatter a handful of grain? Does the son of sacrifice cause dissatisfaction?

children.text: vajravārāhi narāhisurāṇāṃ tvaṃ śaraṇaṃ tava nāmaparāṇām //
children.translated_text: O <s>Vajravārāhī</s>, you are the refuge of humans, <s>Nāgas</s>, and gods — your name is supreme! //
The fear of <s>Hari</s>, the peafowl-serpent, and the thief does not arise in the mind of one devoted to you;

children.text: mātardevi nibhālaya mahyaṃ kiṃ sahase mama duḥkhamasahyam //
children.translated_text: O Mother Goddess, look upon me — how can you endure my unbearable suffering? //
O bearer of the threatening <s>vajra</s>-skull, pacifier of the wicked, repeller of <s>Māra</s>,
with fresh, tender hands, feet, and limbs, with seven curves of the three folds rising high! //
O one purified from the [duality of] grasped and grasper, with webbed fingers on hands and feet,
with extended long fingers on hands and feet — destroyer of disease, old age, birth, and death! //
With dust rising, body-hair standing upward, abode of the immortal nectar opened through <s>vajra</s>-yoga,
with eyes delighting in the sight of young rays — powerful in removing the suffering of the world! //
Beautiful-browed, slender-waisted, with a delicate middle body, with eyes extending to the ears, with bee-like glances,

children.text: ḍākinye (va hi) viśvamaśeṣaṃ loko vetti na te bahuveṣam //
children.translated_text: O <s>Ḍākinī</s>, all the universe indeed — the world does not know your many forms! //
Effortlessly, the fulfillment of the world's purposes; by mere thought, the accomplishment of the desired [goals] of people;

children.text: mūḍho vetti na duṣkṛtakarma prāvṛṣīva na śilāṅkurajanma //
children.translated_text: the fool does not understand the fruit of evil deeds, like the growth of sprouts on rocks in the rainy season. //
Like a blind man not seeing the sun and moon, the sinful person not experiencing [your] power,

children.text: cintāmaṇimajñā na vidanti prajñe tvasya phalāni phalanti //
children.translated_text: the ignorant not knowing the wish-fulfilling jewel — O wise one, yet the fruits of that one bear fruit! //
O lovely one with wheel-marked hands and feet, whose attachments are burned to ash by the fire of wisdom,
whatever sin was committed by body, speech, and mind, surrounded by passion, hatred, and delusion —

children.text: taddiśāmi tava devi samakṣaṃ yāvadyāmi na durgatipakṣam /
children.translated_text: that I confess before you, O Goddess, directly, so that I may not go to the state of evil destinies.

children.text: manaḥ paramārthaṃ tanustava vedī sa bhavati naiva duritaparikhedī //
children.translated_text: One whose mind knows the ultimate truth, whose body knows you — that one never becomes weary of sin. //
With a body in which all marks are fully present, a vessel for all the minor marks,
a mass [of beauty] intoxicated and languid with fresh youth, with cheeks adorned with a pair of swinging earrings, //
with high hips and heavy full breasts, with necklaces and goad-ornaments hanging at the throat,
with a face like a lotus kissed by the bee of the <s>Saṃvara</s> [embrace], with the heart-lotus embraced by those two arms, //
with eyes undisturbed in intense erotic bliss, with loosened hair and garments [regarded with] indifference,
with a moon-face bitten by <s>Heruka</s>-<s>Rāhu</s>, with a smile producing the <s>hūṃ hūṃ</s> <s>mantra</s>, //
not tolerating the moon standing on the lord's crown — is she stealing the beauty of the sun and moon?
O Mother, your incomparable form [is the form of] the world — contemplate that form of supreme reality! //
The nectar-speech pacifying the burning of <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions), a composition for the purification of those to be disciplined,
<s>Padminī</s> — the stainless fragrance of the lotus, the composition [directed to] the welfare of the world beyond compassion. //
The drinking of the nectar-essence from the divine nectar-holder — that is the treasure of the non-dual awakening of the world.
even the touch of each limb is signless, the mind flooded by the ocean of the innate (<s>sahaja</s>). //

children.text: kiṃ tvaṃ mātaḥ kariṣyasi tābhiḥ ṣaṭtriṃśacchatakoṭyabalābhiḥ /
children.translated_text: What will you do, O Mother, with those thirty-six hundred million powerless ones?

children.text: yadyanyāṃ manute bahutātastadvihāya jhagiti dehi nu mātaḥ //
children.translated_text: If another thinks [there is] abundance, then abandon that and give at once, O Mother! //
<s>Mahāsukha</s> (Great Bliss) <s>Saṃvara</s> —
The obstruction of the <s>nāḍī</s>-<s>cakra</s> (channel-wheel),
O Goddess, you are the hundred-fold modification of conceptual thought, equal to the <s>samādhi</s> of emptiness, the removed [impurity]. //
Through emptiness and compassion, the innate non-dual is liberated — this prostration to <s>Vajra</s> has been divided thus;
pervading existence, non-existence, the entirety, and space — that becomes the unfolding of reality (<s>tattva</s>). //
From that very [source] arise the liberations, the <s>Bodhipakṣa</s> (factors of awakening), and all their antidotes;
the exclusive qualities (<s>āveṇika-dharmas</s>) of the <s>Buddhas</s>, the deeds of ripening the multitude of beings. //
Also, the departure through the three vehicles, and the smoke and other [signs] beyond measure —

children.text: tvadbhaktyā yadalambhi śubhaṃ me bhavatu mano bhavatīparamaṃ me /
children.translated_text: whatever merit I have obtained through devotion to you, may my mind become the supreme of the <s>Bhagavatī</s>,

children.text: sakalakaluṣarahitaṃ guṇasindhustvatparamaṃ hyata eva na bandhuḥ //
children.translated_text: free from all impurities, an ocean of virtues — for there is no kinsman superior to you. //

The glorious <s>Vajravilāsinīstotra</s> (Hymn to the Vajra-Enchantress) in the <s>Guhyasamaya-sādhana-tantra</s> is complete. / This is the composition of the great <s>Paṇḍita Vibhūticandrapāda</s>. //

children.text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 100: Vajravilāsinīsādhanāstavaḥ
