children.translated_text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 100: Vajravilāsinīsādhanāstavaḥ
From the seed-vessel of <s>Saṃvara</s>, which is a powerful hair-essence, a beauty radiant as a blooming sun,
she is marked by the rays of the full new moon shining at the peak of rising and setting. //
Though perceivable through the intoxicating essence of various flowers, the sound — fast, slow, and middle — of buzzing,
the bee, approaching at the midnight festival, drinks [the nectar] — this is the wonder of one whose mind has entered that [state]! //
The moon rises and sets; again from the mountain of rising, the crest —

children.text: ubhayakoṭikalāpinirīkṣaṇe na ca śaśī na vibhāti divākaraḥ //
children.translated_text: when observing the pair at both ends, neither the moon shines nor the sun. //
The sun rises within the petals of the lotus; the moon too dissolves from the peak;

children.text: vrajati cordhvamasau vaḍavānalo gilati rāhuradhaḥ śaśibhāskarau //
children.translated_text: the submarine fire rises upward; <s>Rāhu</s> swallows the moon and sun below. //
The closing and opening of the visible domain of the lotus-seat lotus-eye —
this is the first limb; the closing of the pair of <s>vajra</s>-lotuses is the second and subsequent. //
Immediately, from the friction of the practitioner's seed, the triad ascends to the sky as the fourth;
the innate imperishable radiance, the series of phases (<s>kalā</s>), licking away the dissolution of time. //
If one has attained the realization received from the <s>Guru's</s> mouth regarding the well-trained <s>Vajravilāsinī</s>,
then whoever has that [realization] becomes a seer of reality through the determination of supreme, middling, and inferior. //
The glorious <s>Vajravilāsinīsādhanāstava</s> (Hymn of Practice to the Vajra-Enchantress) is complete. //

children.text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 101: Vajrayoginīpraṇāmaikaviśikā
children.translated_text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 101: Vajrayoginīpraṇāmaikaviśikā
<s>Oṃ</s>! Homage to the glorious <s>Vajrayoginī</s>!
Seated in the form of the syllable <s>Evaṃ</s>, embodying innate bliss (<s>sahajānanda</s>),
abiding in the body of wisdom-consciousness (<s>prajñā-vijñāna</s>) — homage to you, <s>Vajrayoginī</s>! //
Through the various divisions beginning with the first, O bestower of the body of the four blisses,
O one who has attained the perfection of passion (<s>rāga-pāramitā</s>) — homage to you, <s>Vajrayoginī</s>! //
Resembling the full moon of autumn, born from the eightfold yoga of the essence of beings,
arisen from the foremost seed-syllable — homage to you, <s>Vajrayoginī</s>! //
Transcending the duality of existence and non-existence, free from beginning, end, and middle,
liberated from the distinction of self and other — homage to you, <s>Vajrayoginī</s>! //
Mixed between passion and non-passion, free from the three [types of] conceptualization,
O maker of the bliss of great bliss (<s>Mahāsukha</s>) — homage to you, <s>Vajrayoginī</s>! //
Endowed with means of benefiting beings, embodying the nature of the <s>Saṃbhoga</s> (enjoyment) [body],
abiding in a body reddened with compassion — homage to you, <s>Vajrayoginī</s>! //
Having ascended [beyond] existence and <s>Nirvāṇa</s>, resplendent in visible form,
the light of body, speech, and mind — homage to you, <s>Vajrayoginī</s>! //
With a skull-cup and <s>khaṭvāṅga</s> (skull-staff) in the left hand, holding a cleaver (<s>kartī</s>) in the right,
O bearer of emptiness and compassion — homage to you, <s>Vajrayoginī</s>! //
O fierce one, terrible to the <s>Jinas</s>' enemies, destroyer of all <s>Māras</s>,
foremost among all conquered devotions — homage to you, <s>Vajrayoginī</s>! //
Endowed with the garland [of skulls], dwelling in the eight cremation grounds,
endowed with the dramatic flavors of the <s>Buddha's</s> dance — homage to you, <s>Vajrayoginī</s>! //
Creating many forms according to the dispositions of beings,
shining in dark, yellow, and white — homage to you, <s>Vajrayoginī</s>! //
Born from the people of the five <s>Buddhas</s>, having attained the state of the five <s>yoginīs</s>,
and also counted in the number of atoms — homage to you, <s>Vajrayoginī</s>! //

children.text: śaive śaktiriti khyāte tīrthe caṇḍīti kalpite /
children.translated_text: Known as <s>Śakti</s> (Power) in the <s>Śaiva</s> [tradition], conceived as <s>Caṇḍī</s> in the sacred fords,
proclaimed as the <s>Veda</s> in the <s>Vedic</s> [tradition] — homage to you, <s>Vajrayoginī</s>! //
Called <s>Kubjikā</s> in the <s>Kula</s> tradition, known as one who assumes her own disguise,
of universal form, the maker of ritual action — homage to you, <s>Vajrayoginī</s>! //
Not gone [away], O Maker, on account of opposition to the vision of beings,
endowed with the best of all forms — homage to you, <s>Vajrayoginī</s>! //
Accessible only to the vision of the profound yoga of the <s>Nairātmya</s>-<s>dharma</s> (selflessness-teaching),
transcending the conceptualization of being and non-being — homage to you, <s>Vajrayoginī</s>! //
Free from dark, yellow, and other [colors], devoid of both color and colorlessness,
O Mother <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> (Perfection of Wisdom) — homage to you, <s>Vajrayoginī</s>! //
Free from conceptual elaboration, without support, without proliferation, without abode,
pervading space, [embodying] selflessness (<s>Nairātmya</s>) — homage to you, <s>Vajrayoginī</s>! //
O vessel of all those who know jewels, O Mother <s>Vajrayoginī</s> —
homage to you, <s>Vajravārāhī</s>! Homage to you, <s>Vajrayoginī</s>! //
You who have emerged from the lotus-mouth of the true <s>Guru</s>, O one of desired form,
for the destruction of great ignorance — homage to you, <s>Vajrayoginī</s>! //
Thus, having composed twenty-one [verses] to the Mother endowed with virtues,

children.text: puṇyaṃ yadavāptaṃ tena janāḥ santu(labhantu) pūrṇatvam //
children.translated_text: may all beings attain fullness through the merit obtained thereby! //
The glorious <s>Vajrayoginīpraṇāmaikaviṃśikā</s> (Twenty-one Praises to Vajrayoginī) is complete. //

children.text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 102: Vajrayoginyāḥ piṇḍārthastutiḥ siddhācāryavirūpādaviaracitā
children.translated_text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 102: Vajrayoginyāḥ piṇḍārthastutiḥ, composed by <s>Siddhācārya Virūpāda</s>

children.text: om namo vajrayoginyai / om namo buddhadharmasaṃghebhyaḥ / om namo gurubuddhabodhisattvebhyaḥ / om namo locanādidaśavajravilāsinībhyaḥ / namo yamāntakādidaśakroḍha(dha) vīrebhyaḥ / vārāhī śauṇḍinī caiva caṇḍālī ḍombinī tathā /
children.translated_text: <s>Oṃ</s>! Homage to <s>Vajrayoginī</s>! <s>Oṃ</s>! Homage to <s>Buddha</s>, <s>Dharma</s>, and <s>Saṃgha</s>! <s>Oṃ</s>! Homage to the <s>Guru</s>, <s>Buddha</s>, and <s>Bodhisattvas</s>! <s>Oṃ</s>! Homage to <s>Locanā</s> and the ten <s>Vajravilāsinīs</s>! Homage to <s>Yamāntaka</s> and the ten wrathful heroes! <s>Vārāhī</s>, <s>Śauṇḍinī</s>, <s>Caṇḍālī</s>, <s>Ḍombinī</s>,

children.text: naṭanī rajakī brāhmī kapālinī ca sāsa(śāśva) tā //
children.translated_text: <s>Naṭanī</s> (Dancer), <s>Rajakī</s> (Washerwoman), <s>Brāhmī</s>, <s>Kapālinī</s> (Skull-bearer) — and the eternal one, //
<s>Amṛtā</s> (Nectar) and <s>Amṛtakuṇḍalī</s>, the illuminator of the light of wisdom —
this one is the sole great bliss among all the <s>Vīra</s>-goddesses of the directions. //
She is also sung as emptiness (<s>śūnyatā</s>), the supreme power (<s>Śakti</s>), the highest of the highest,
the nectar whose mind flows upward, divine, the skillful means, the ever-flowing one. //
She is a sky-goer (<s>Khecarī</s>), an earth-goer (<s>Bhūcarī</s>), and also a dweller in the netherworld (<s>Pātāla</s>),
the one who establishes and fills perpetually, and who agitates the three worlds. //
The goddess of <s>Bindu</s> (drop), <s>Nāda</s> (sound), and <s>Kalā</s> (phase), she is indeed of the nature of moon and sun;
she is the eternal one, of the <s>Nirmāṇa</s> (transformation) [body], of the <s>Saṃbhoga</s> (enjoyment) [body], and of great bliss. //
Transcending <s>Bindu</s>, <s>Nāda</s>, and <s>Kalā</s>, she is considered the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> (Perfection of Wisdom);
she is indeed the inherent nature of all existences, and yet devoid of all existences. //
Free from dissolution and creation, yet the maker of dissolution and creation;

children.text: śāśvatatvāt sthitā proktā śāśvatena ca varjitā //
children.translated_text: she is said to abide eternally, yet she is free from eternality. //
Profound, embraced, noble, of great meaning, liberated by her own understanding,
free from the threefold emptiness, embodying the luminous nature (<s>prabhāsvara</s>). //
In the form of the single syllable <s>E</s>, united with the syllable <s>Vaṃ</s>,
endowed with the various [moments] beginning with the first, embodying the four blisses. //
Even in the outer <s>maṇḍala</s>-circle, shining forth from the <s>Trikāya</s> (Three Bodies),
in the states of body, speech, and mind, she is the ornament of body, speech, and mind. //
Transcending body, speech, and mind, abiding in the middle through equality,
the goddess embodying selflessness (<s>Nairātmya</s>), established in <s>Tathatā</s> (Suchness). //
Embodying the threefold emptiness, trampled by lotus and <s>vajra</s>,
from the union of <s>Lalanā</s> and <s>Rasanā</s> [channels], the <s>Avadhūtī</s> [central channel] of great bliss. //
She is the one who ferries [beings] across <s>saṃsāra</s>, and she is also born from those conditions;
having obtained this <s>yoginī</s>, one is freed from the bonds of worldly existence. //

children.text: ityeṣā ṛddhidā proktā siddhidā caiva yoginī /
children.translated_text: Thus she is proclaimed as the giver of <s>ṛddhi</s> (supernatural power) and also the giver of <s>siddhi</s> (accomplishment), the <s>yoginī</s>,
and the one supreme in the door to liberation, for those who constantly practice. //

children.text: vajravat kurute dehaṃ rasasiddhiṃ dadāti ca /
children.translated_text: She makes the body [hard as] <s>vajra</s> and grants the <s>siddhi</s> of alchemical essence;
by the grace of the <s>Guru's</s> feet, this <s>Vajrayoginī</s> is obtained. //
By the mere reading of [this hymn to] her, through eagerness in the accumulation of merit,
the <s>yogin</s> constantly attains [her], filled with the accumulation of wisdom. //

children.text:
śrīguhyasamayatantre piṇḍārthāḥ ṣoḍaśaślokāstrikāyavajrayoginyāḥ samāptāḥ /
      kṛtiriyaṃ siddhācāryaśrīvirupādānāmiti //
children.translated_text: The sixteen verses of essential meaning (<s>piṇḍārtha</s>) of the <s>Trikāya Vajrayoginī</s> in the glorious <s>Guhyasamaya-tantra</s> are complete. / This is the composition of <s>Siddhācārya Śrī Virūpāda</s>. //

children.text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 103: Vajrayoginyāḥ stutipraṇidhānam siddhācāryavirūpādaviracitam
children.translated_text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 103: Vajrayoginyāḥ stutipraṇidhānam, composed by <s>Siddhācārya Virūpāda</s>

children.text: om namaḥ śrī vajrayoginyai, namobuddhadharmasaṃghebhyaḥ, namo gurubuddhabodhisattvebhyaḥ, namo locanādidaśavajravilāsinībhyaḥ, namo yamāntakādidaśakrodhavīrebhyaḥ saprajñebhyaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Oṃ</s>! Homage to the glorious <s>Vajrayoginī</s>! Homage to <s>Buddha</s>, <s>Dharma</s>, and <s>Saṃgha</s>! Homage to the <s>Guru</s>, <s>Buddha</s>, and <s>Bodhisattvas</s>! Homage to <s>Locanā</s> and the ten <s>Vajravilāsinīs</s>! Homage to <s>Yamāntaka</s> and the ten wrathful heroes with their consorts!

children.text: om o ā hūṃ iti kāyavākacita indriyavijñānāni, vākacittāni manovijñānāni, paracittajñānābhijñā, parakāyapraveśābhijñā puṇḍarīkeṣu nābhisthe raktasūrya maṇḍalaḥ //
children.translated_text: <s>Oṃ O Ā Hūṃ</s> — thus body, speech, and mind; the sense-consciousnesses; speech and mind; mental consciousness; the superknowledge of others' minds; the superknowledge of entering others' bodies — in the lotuses at the navel, a red sun-<s>maṇḍala</s>. //
The <s>Dharmodayā</s> (source of Dharma), in the middle of the lotus, of vermillion-red form,
three-peaked or triangular, endowed with the four sacred seats (<s>pīṭhas</s>). //
The syllable <s>Hrīṃ</s> in the middle portion of it — its color is proclaimed as yellow;

children.text: tadbhavā pītavarṇā ca avadhūtyā(tī) svayaṃ sthitā //
children.translated_text: born from that, of yellow color, the <s>Avadhūtī</s> (central channel) itself abides. //

children.text: lalanāyāṃ tu suśyāmā rasanāyāṃ ca gaurikā /
children.translated_text: In the <s>Lalanā</s> [left channel], a beautiful dark one; in the <s>Rasanā</s> [right channel], a fair one;
the one in the <s>pratyālīḍha</s> posture, by name, is the yellow, delightful one in the middle. //
The goddess established in the three channels is the <s>Trikāya Vajrayoginī</s>;
she by name is one — the <s>Ḍākinī</s> of all <s>Sambuddhas</s> (Perfectly Awakened Ones). //
Of divine form in the three worlds, the fulfiller of all desires;
with her own cleaver she has severed her own head [held] in the left hand. //
In her right stands the cleaver, the cutter of the world's suffering;

children.text: asyā vāme sthitā śyāmā nāmnā sā varavarṇinī //
children.translated_text: at her left stands the dark one, named <s>Varavarṇinī</s> (Excellent-complexioned). //

children.text: karparaḥ savyahaste ca kartirvāme ca saṃsthitā /
children.translated_text: A skull-cup in the right hand, a cleaver placed in the left;

children.text: dakṣiṇe caiva pītā vai vajravairocanī sthitā //
children.translated_text: and at the right stands the yellow one indeed, <s>Vajrairocanī</s>. //
A cleaver in the right hand, holding a skull-cup in the left,
the goddess in the <s>pratyālīḍha</s> posture, especially naked. //

children.text: karau ca dvau tayoḥ pādau viparītau tathā sthitau /
children.translated_text: The two hands and the two feet of those two are placed in reversed positions;
the one in the middle is the mother of the <s>Buddhas</s>, embodying the Perfectly Awakened One. //

children.text: akṣayā subhagā nityaṃ hantrī ca mṛtyujanmanoḥ /
children.translated_text: Imperishable, ever-fortunate, the destroyer of death and birth,
embodying the great bliss of <s>Dharma</s>, <s>Saṃbhoga</s>, and <s>Nirmāṇa</s> [bodies]. //
This goddess always reigns in the three worlds like the moon;
from the headless trunk through the <s>Avadhūtī</s>, the blood enters into [their] mouths. //
Flowing out through the <s>Lalanā</s> and <s>Rasanā</s> [channels], and at the head,
drinking in the form of compassion-red [blood], for the pacification of all. //
Seeing the suffering of the worlds, the destroyer of the four <s>Māras</s>,

children.text: daurmanasyādi kartyā ca kartantī sarvameva tat //
children.translated_text: and with the cleaver cutting away despondency and the like — she cuts all of that indeed. //
O praised Mother of the <s>Jinas</s>! Be gracious in the ocean of existence;

children.text: svārthaṃ kartuṃ parārthaṃ ca bhavāmyahaṃ yathā kṣamaḥ //
children.translated_text: may I become capable of accomplishing my own purpose and the purpose of others. //
Therefore, O Goddess, you must bestow your grace — cast [it] upon me!
I am a child, of ignorant nature, through faults of body, speech, and mind. //

children.text: gurubhaktiṃ na jāne 'haṃ tvadbhaktiṃ ca viśeṣataḥ /
children.translated_text: I do not know devotion to the <s>Guru</s>, nor devotion to you especially;
therefore understand, O Mistress of the World — may compassion be directed toward me! //

children.text: kāyavākacetasāṃ sāmyaṃ kuru me tvaṃ prasādataḥ /
children.translated_text: Bring about the equality of body, speech, and mind for me, through your grace,

children.text: yena muñcāmi saṃsāraṃ ṣaḍgatiṃ na viśāmyaham //
children.translated_text: by which I may release <s>saṃsāra</s> and not enter the six realms of existence! //
May my body become [hard as] <s>vajra</s>, as long as I am not liberated;

children.text: māraiḥ sarvaiḥ parityakto yathā kāyo bhavenmama //
children.translated_text: may my body become abandoned by all <s>Māras</s>! //
May the shares of <s>siddhi</s> (accomplishment) come playfully, free from obstacles, possessing all <s>siddhis</s>;
may the accomplishment of all practices be [mine], and may the body be undecaying and immortal! //
The terrifying of all <s>Māras</s>, the fulfillment of all desires —

children.text: dehi me tvaṃ varāṃ siddhiṃ hitvā caiva gamāgamam //
children.translated_text: grant me the supreme <s>siddhi</s>, and may I abandon coming and going! //
May the mind dissolve, O Goddess, together with the five senses —
and may there be the accomplishment of <s>Vajrasattva's</s> longevity, youth, health, and true happiness! //
By your grace, may the <s>Mahāmudrā</s> (Great Seal) arise for all;
and may gods, <s>Asuras</s>, and humans, wherever they may abide,
all be happy and attain the fruit of <s>Buddhahood</s>! //

children.text:
śrīguhyasamayatantre trikāyavajrayoginyāḥ stutipraṇidhānaṃ samāptam /
      kṛtiriyaṃ siddhācārya śrīvirūpādānām //
children.translated_text: The praise and aspiration-prayer of <s>Trikāyavajrayoginī</s> from the <s>Śrī Guhyasamaya Tantra</s> is complete. This is the composition of the accomplished master (<s>Siddhācārya</s>) <s>Śrī Virūpāda</s>. //

children.text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 104: Vasantatilakāstutiḥ
children.translated_text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 104: <s>Vasantatilakāstutiḥ</s>
Going through the feet, the secret [center], the anus, the navel, the heart, the head, the <s>dhātu</s>-<s>maṇḍala</s>, and the back of <s>Meru</s>,
passing through the <s>nāḍīs</s> (channels), the <s>samaya</s> (commitment), the <s>vajra</s>, and the lotus — I bow to you, <s>Heruka</s> of the dual mind! //
Abiding in the great space of the five within the pericarp of the secret lotus (<s>guhyakokanada</s>),
the <s>Dharmadhātu</s>-mark, non-dual and beyond duality — I bow to you, <s>Heruka</s> of the innate self (<s>sahajātman</s>)! //
Surpassing the fierce flash of lightning flashing forth from within the mass of dark clouds,
burning both sentient beings and the vessel-world — I bow to you, O Mother of the World, <s>Herukī</s>! //
Born from the assembly of <s>vajra</s>-lotuses arising from the ocean of water in the cavity of the navel-<s>cakra</s>,
greedy for drinking the essence of the palatial nectar — I bow to you whose radiance is the submarine fire (<s>baḍavānala</s>)! //
The glorious <s>Vasantatilakāstuti</s> is complete. //

children.text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 105: Vasudhārānāmadhāraṇīstotram
children.translated_text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 105: <s>Vasudhārānāmadhāraṇīstotram</s>
<s>Oṃ</s>! Homage

children.text: bhagavatyai āryaśrīvasudhārāyai divyarūpī surūpī ca saumyarūpī balapradā /
children.translated_text: to the Blessed Lady <s>Āryaśrīvasudhārā</s>! Of divine form, of beautiful form, of gentle form, bestower of strength,
<s>Vasudharī</s> (Earth-Bearer), <s>Vasudhāraṇī</s> (Wealth-Stream), <s>Vasuśrī</s> (Wealth-Beauty), <s>Śrīkarī</s> (Fortune-Maker), the excellent one. //
<s>Dharaṇī</s> (Earth), <s>Dhāraṇī</s> (Support), <s>Dhātā</s> (Creator), worthy of refuge, affectionate to devotees,
<s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> (Perfection of Wisdom), goddess, <s>Prajñā</s> (Wisdom), <s>Śrībuddhivardhinī</s> (Increaser of Auspicious Intellect). //

children.text: vidyādharī śivā sūkṣmā śāstā sarvatra mātṛkā /
children.translated_text: <s>Vidyādharī</s> (Bearer of Knowledge), <s>Śivā</s> (Auspicious), <s>Sūkṣmā</s> (Subtle), <s>Śāstā</s> (Teacher), universal mother (<s>mātṛkā</s>),
<s>Taruṇī</s> (Youthful), <s>Tāraṇī</s> (Savior), goddess, sovereign of the lords of knowledge-giving. //
<s>Bhūṣitā</s> (Adorned), Mother of Beings (<s>Bhūtamātā</s>), adorned with all ornaments,
terrifier of the wicked, fearsome, fierce, of fierce valor. //
<s>Dānapāramitā</s> (Perfection of Generosity), goddess, rainer [of gifts], of divine form,
the treasury of all auspiciousness, fame, <s>Lakṣmī</s> (fortune), glory, and beauty. //
<s>Dahanī</s> (Burner), <s>Mālinī</s> (Garlanded), <s>Caṇḍī</s> (Fierce), <s>Śabarī</s> (Tribal), Mother of All,
commander of Death, <s>Raudrī</s> (Terrible), <s>Kaumārī</s>, of universal form. //
<s>Vīryapāramitā</s> (Perfection of Vigor), goddess, delighter and illuminator of the world,
<s>Tāpasī</s> (Ascetic), of fierce form, bestower of <s>ṛddhi</s> (power), <s>siddhi</s> (accomplishment), and strength. //
Blessed, meritorious, of great fortune, unconquered, of conquered valor,
the sole benefactress of the world, <s>Vidyā</s> (Knowledge), the auspicious savior in battle. //
<s>Kṣāntipāramitā</s> (Perfection of Patience), goddess, virtuous, devoted to meditation,
<s>Padminī</s> (Lotus-Bearer), lotus-holding, lover of lotuses, seated on a lotus. //
Of pure form, of great radiance, of golden color, maker of light,
<s>Cintāmaṇi</s> (Wish-Fulfilling Gem) great goddess, bearer of the book of wisdom. //
A treasury, ascended to the summit, fond of granaries and wealth,
great throughout the three realms, adorned with divine ornaments. //
Mother of all <s>Buddhas</s>, sovereign of the lords of the <s>Ratnadhātu</s> (Jewel Realm),
<s>Śūnyatā</s> (Emptiness), goddess of contemplation, free from both existence and non-existence. //
Among the trainable, is she not employed? — the cutter of divine afflictions,
the terrifier of all <s>Māras</s>, the shaker of the seven netherworlds. //

children.text: brahmāṇī vedamātā ca guhyā ca guhyavāsinī /
children.translated_text: <s>Brahmāṇī</s>, Mother of the <s>Vedas</s>, secret and dwelling in secrecy,
<s>Sarasvatī</s>, wide-eyed, abiding in the four <s>Brahmavihāras</s> (divine abodes). //
Of the nature of <s>Tathāgata</s>, greatly delightful, bearer of the <s>vajra</s>, upholder of <s>Dharma</s>,
<s>Karmadhāteśvarī</s> (Sovereign of the Action Realm), <s>Vidyā</s> (Knowledge), with a <s>maṇḍala</s> like a universal blaze. //
Awakener of all beings, crowned with the factors of awakening (<s>bodhyaṅga</s>),
<s>Dhyānā</s> (Meditation), wise, endowed with liberation, contemplator of non-duality and duality. //
Accomplisher of all aims, auspicious, of feminine form, of immeasurable valor,
revealer of the paths of the <s>Buddhas</s>, shower of the path to those who have lost their way. //
<s>Vāgīśvarī</s> (Goddess of Speech), of great peace, protector, sustainer, giver of wealth,
bearer of feminine form, accomplished, <s>Yoginī</s>, sovereign of those born of <s>yoga</s>. //
Mind-captivating, of great power, beautiful to behold, of great fortune,
having the compassionate gaze of a caravan-leader, of the nature of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>. //
Homage to you, O great goddess, giver of the welfare of all beings!

children.text: namaste divyarūpī ca vasudhārā namo 'stu te //
children.translated_text: Homage to you, of divine form — to <s>Vasudhārā</s>, homage to you! //

children.text: aṣṭottaraśataṃ nāma trikālaṃ yaṃ paṭhet pumān /
children.translated_text: The person who recites these one hundred and eight names thrice daily
certainly attains accomplishment and the desired aims and wishes. //
Whatever sin committed through ignorance, even the terribly heinous (<s>ānantarya</s>),
all that is swiftly destroyed by merely remembering — everything becomes auspicious. //
Or, endowed with morality, one becomes a rememberer of seven births,
beloved, with authoritative speech, handsome, and pleasant to behold. //
One takes birth in <s>brāhmaṇa</s> or <s>kṣatriya</s> families as an authority,

children.text: ante bhūmīśvaraṃ prāptaḥ paścāt prāpta(ḥ) sukhāvatīm //
children.translated_text: and at the end, having attained lordship of the earth, finally attains <s>Sukhāvatī</s>. //
The <s>Śrī Vasudhārā Nāma Dhāraṇī Stotra</s>, spoken by the Perfectly Awakened One, is complete. //

children.text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 106: Vasudhārāstotram
children.translated_text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 106: <s>Vasudhārāstotram</s>

children.text: yā samyaguktavidhibhiḥ paripathyamānā lakṣmīṃ dadāti vipulāṃ sugatopabhogān /
children.translated_text: She who, when recited with the properly prescribed methods, bestows abundant <s>Lakṣmī</s> (prosperity) and the enjoyments of the <s>Sugata</s> —

children.text: tāṃ dhāraṇīṃ sakalasattvahitaikacittāṃ bhaktyā namāmi satataṃ vasudhārasaṃjñām //
children.translated_text: that <s>dhāraṇī</s> of single-minded devotion to the welfare of all beings, named <s>Vasudhārā</s>, I constantly bow to with devotion. //

children.text: yā saṃsmṛtā sucirasusthataraṃ pravṛddhaṃ dāridrayaduḥkhaduritaṃ śamate narāṇām /
children.translated_text: She who, when remembered, pacifies the long-standing, well-grown sin of the suffering of poverty for people —

children.text: tāṃ kalpavṛkṣasadṛśīṃ vasudhārasaṃjñāṃ nityaṃ namāmi śirasā jagatāṃ hitāya //
children.translated_text: that one named <s>Vasudhārā</s>, like a wish-fulfilling tree, I always bow to with my head, for the welfare of the world. //
A mine of jewels, a treasury and storehouse of gems, raining forth a brilliance of various jewels,

children.text: ratnāvalīṃ ratnamayīṃ vicitrāṃ namāmi cāryāṃ vasudhāradhārām //
children.translated_text: a jewel-garland, made of gems, variegated — I bow to the noble <s>Vasudhārā</s> stream! //
To her who is fruitful with a jewel in hand, who illuminates you, who bears the crest-ornament of generosity and compassion,
whose body is adorned with necklaces, half-necklaces, and dangling earrings — I bow to the noble <s>Vasudhārā</s>, the rainer of wealth, the worthy refuge. //
The <s>Vasudhārā</s> hymn, extracted from the <s>Śrī Vasudhārākalpa</s>, is complete. //

children.text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 107: Vidyākṣarastotram
children.translated_text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 107: <s>Vidyākṣarastotram</s>
Born from the syllable <s>Oṃ</s>, of white radiance, seated on a lion-throne in the center,
endowed with the <s>Bodhi</s> (awakening) <s>mudrā</s> of the three [seals] — we bow to the sage <s>Vairocana</s>! //
Born from the syllable <s>Hūṃ</s>, of blue radiance, seated on an elephant in the east,
endowed with the earth-touching <s>mudrā</s> — we bow to <s>Akṣobhya</s>, <s>Śrīghana</s> (Dense Glory)! //
Born from the syllable <s>Trāṃ</s>, of golden radiance, mounted on a horse in the south,
endowed with the boon-granting <s>mudrā</s> — I bow to <s>Ratnasaṃbhava</s>! //
Born from the syllable <s>Jhiṅ</s>, of red radiance, on a peacock-seat in the west,
bearing the form of meditation — we bow to the lord, the sage <s>Amitābha</s>! //
Born from the syllable <s>Khaṅ</s>, of dark-green radiance, on a <s>Garuḍa</s>-seat in the north,
joined with the <s>abhaya</s> (fearlessness) <s>mudrā</s> — I bow to <s>Amoghasiddhi</s>! //

children.text: rocanā māmakī caiva pāṇḍarā tāraṇī tathā /
children.translated_text: <s>Rocanā</s>, <s>Māmakī</s>, <s>Pāṇḍarā</s>, and <s>Tāraṇī</s> (Tārā) likewise,
established in the corners beginning with <s>Brahmā</s>'s — to the four goddesses, homage, homage! //
Unstained, formless, of the nature of individual light,
the god abiding in the center of the <s>caitya</s> (shrine), <s>Vajrasattva</s> — we bow! //
The <s>Vidyākṣarastotra</s> (Hymn of the Syllables of Knowledge) of the glorious lord <s>Buddha</s> is complete. //

children.text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 108: Advayaparamārthā nāmasaṅgītiḥ
children.translated_text: Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon, Stotra section, text no. 108: <s>Advayaparamārthā Nāmasaṅgītiḥ</s>
<s>Oṃ</s>! Homage to the glorious great lord <s>Mañjunātha</s>!
Then the glorious <s>Vajradhara</s>, supreme tamer of the untamable,
the hero who conquers the three worlds, the king of secrets, the lord of the <s>vajra</s>,
with eyes like awakened white lotuses, with face like a fully blooming lotus,
playfully brandishing the supreme <s>vajra</s> in his own hand again and again,
with the infinite <s>Vajrapāṇis</s>, headed by <s>Bhṛkuṭī</s>-wave and others,
tamers of the untamable, heroes of heroic and terrifying forms,
brandishing in their own hands the sparkling points of <s>vajras</s>,
supreme ones who accomplish the welfare of the world through <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom), <s>upāya</s> (means), and great compassion,
of delighted, satisfied, and joyful dispositions, of wrathful-bodied forms,
lords who perform the activities of the <s>Buddhas</s>, together with those of bowed bodies,
having bowed to the lord, the fully awakened one, the Blessed <s>Tathāgata</s>,
with palms joined in <s>añjali</s>, standing before him, spoke thus:
'For my benefit, for my purpose, out of compassion for me, O all-pervading Lord,
may I obtain [the teaching] as it is, from the <s>Māyājāla</s> (Net of Illusion) Awakening!' //
'For the benefit of all beings sunk in the mire of ignorance, whose minds are troubled by <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions),
for the attainment of the unsurpassed fruit —
may the fully awakened one, the Blessed One, the Teacher, the Guru of the World, reveal it —
the great knower of the reality of the assembly, the supreme knower of the faculties and dispositions!' //
'O Blessed One! Of the knowledge-body, of the great <s>uṣṇīṣa</s> (crown-protuberance), of the Lord of Speech,
of <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, the knowledge-being, the embodiment of knowledge, the self-arisen one —
the <s>Nāmasaṅgīti</s> (Chanting of Names), of profound meaning, of noble meaning, of great meaning, incomparable, auspicious,
beautiful in the beginning, middle, and end, the supreme [chanting of names] —
which was spoken by <s>Buddhas</s> of the past, will be spoken by those of the future,

children.text: pratyutpannāśca saṃbuddhā yāṃ bhāṣante punaḥ punaḥ //
children.translated_text: and is spoken again and again by the fully awakened ones of the present,
which is chanted in this great <s>Māyājāla</s> (Net of Illusion) <s>tantra</s>,
by the joyful great <s>Vajradharas</s>, the immeasurable bearers of <s>mantras</s> —
I too shall hold this, with firm resolve, until final liberation,
so that I, O Lord, may become the holder of the secrets of all fully awakened ones.' //
'I shall reveal it to beings according to the distinctions of their dispositions,
for the complete destruction of all <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions), for the complete elimination of all ignorance.' //
Thus having entreated, the lord of secrets, <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>, [addressed] the <s>Tathāgata</s>,
with palms joined in <s>añjali</s>, body bowed, standing before him. //
Thus end the sixteen verses of the entreaty for knowledge.
Then the Blessed <s>Śākyamuni</s>, the fully awakened one, the supreme among bipeds,
extending his own long, broad, and auspicious tongue from his own mouth,
displaying a smile that purifies the three lower realms of the worlds,
that illuminates the three worlds, that is the teaching that conquers the four <s>Māras</s>,
with a <s>Brāhma</s>-like, sweet voice filling the three worlds,
addressed the lord of secrets, the mighty <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>:

children.text: sādhu vajradhara śrīman sādhu te vajrapāṇaye /
children.translated_text: 'Well done, O glorious <s>Vajradhara</s>! Well done, O <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>!
You who, endowed with great compassion, for the welfare of the world,
are prepared to hear from me the <s>Nāmasaṅgīti</s> (Chanting of Names), of great meaning, pure, destroyer of sin,
of the knowledge-body of <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, the knowledge-being.',
'That being so, I shall well teach this, O lord of the <s>Guhyakas</s> (secret beings)!
Listen with one-pointed mind — that is well, O Blessed One!' //
Thus end the six verses of the response of knowledge.
Then the Blessed <s>Śākyamuni</s>, surveying the entire great <s>mantra</s>-family,
the family of <s>mantra</s>-<s>vidyādharas</s> (knowledge-holders), the three families,
the worldly and supramundane family, the great world-and-beyond family,
the supreme great <s>Mahāmudrā</s> (Great Seal) family, the great <s>Mahā-uṣṇīṣa</s> (Great Crown) family —
thus end the two verses of the knowledge of surveying the six families.
He spoke this verse, combined with the six <s>mantra</s>-kings, the non-dual compassion,
of the nature of non-arising, [the verse] of the Lord of Speech:

children.text: a ā i ī u ū e ai o au aṃ aḥ sthito hṛdi /
children.translated_text: '<s>A Ā I Ī U Ū E AI O AU AṂ AḤ</s> — established in the heart,
I am the embodiment of knowledge, the <s>Buddha</s>, of the <s>Buddhas</s> of the three times.' //
'<s>Oṃ</s>! To the embodiment of the wisdom-knowledge that cuts suffering with the <s>vajra</s>-sharp [sword],
to <s>Arapacana</s>, the lord of speech of the knowledge-body — homage to you!' //
Thus end the three verses of the stages of the <s>Māyājāla</s> Awakening.
Thus the Blessed <s>Buddha</s>, the fully awakened one, born from the syllable <s>A</s> —
the syllable <s>A</s> is the foremost of all syllables, of great meaning, the supreme imperishable. //
The great breath, indeed unborn, free from the nourishment of speech,
the foremost cause of all utterance, supremely luminous in all speech. //
Great festival, great passion (<s>mahārāga</s>), bringing delight to all beings,
great festival, great hatred (<s>mahādveṣa</s>), the great enemy of all <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions). //
Great festival, great delusion (<s>mahāmoha</s>), the destroyer of the delusion of deluded minds,
great festival, great wrath (<s>mahākrodha</s>), the great enemy of great wrath. //
Great festival, great greed (<s>mahālobha</s>), the destroyer of all greed,
great desire (<s>mahākāma</s>), great bliss (<s>mahāsaukhya</s>), great joy (<s>mahāmoda</s>), great delight (<s>mahārati</s>). //
Of great form, of great body, of great color, of great physique,
of great name, of great nobility, of a great and vast <s>maṇḍala</s>. //
The bearer of the great weapon of wisdom, the great goad of afflictions, the foremost one,
of great fame, of great renown, of great radiance, of great brilliance. //
The bearer of great illusion (<s>māyā</s>), the wise one, the accomplisher of the purpose of great illusion,
delighting in the play of great illusion, the great magician of illusion. //
The great lord of generosity, the best, the bearer of great morality, the foremost,
the bearer of great patience, the steadfast, of great heroic valor. //
Established in the great <s>samādhi</s> (concentration) of <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation), the bearer of the body of great wisdom,
of great strength, of great means, with vows, the ocean of knowledge. //
Filled with great loving-kindness, immeasurable, of great compassion, of supreme intellect,
of great wisdom, of great intelligence, of great skillful means, of great deeds. //
Endowed with great supernatural power and strength, of great speed, of great swiftness,
of great supernatural powers, called great lord, of great might and valor. //
The splitter of the great mountain of existence, the bearer of the great <s>vajra</s>, the wealthy one,
the greatly fierce, the greatly terrible, the one who inspires fear of great fear. //
The supreme lord of great <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge), the supreme guru of great <s>mantras</s>,
mounted upon the method of the <s>Mahāyāna</s> (Great Vehicle), the supreme method of the <s>Mahāyāna</s>. //
Thus, the fourteen <s>gāthās</s> (verses) of knowledge of the <s>Vajradhātumaṇḍala</s> (Diamond Realm Maṇḍala).
The great <s>Vairocana Buddha</s>, the great silent one, the great sage,
arisen from the system of great <s>mantras</s>, whose nature is the system of great <s>mantras</s>. //
Who has attained the ten <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections), who relies on the ten <s>pāramitās</s>,
whose purity is the ten <s>pāramitās</s>, whose method is the ten <s>pāramitās</s>. //
The lord of the ten stages (<s>bhūmis</s>), the protector, established on the ten stages,
whose soul is purified by the ten knowledges, the bearer of the purity of the ten knowledges. //
Of ten aspects, whose purpose is the tenfold meaning, the lord of sages, of ten powers, the all-pervading one,
the accomplisher of the welfare of all the universe, the great one who controls the ten aspects. //
Beginningless, whose nature is beyond conceptual elaboration, of pure nature, whose nature is <s>tathatā</s> (suchness),
a speaker of truth, speaking as things are, acting as he speaks, of uncontradictory speech. //
Non-dual yet a teacher of duality, established at the limit of reality (<s>bhūtakoṭi</s>),
one whose lion's roar proclaims non-self, terrifying to the deer-like false ascetics. //
Going everywhere, of unerring course, with a mind swift as a <s>Tathāgata</s>,
a conqueror, whose enemies are conquered, victorious, a universal sovereign (<s>cakravartin</s>), of great strength. //
Chief of assemblies, teacher of assemblies, lord of assemblies, master of assemblies, the sovereign,
of great influence, the leader, not to be led by another, of great method. //
Lord of speech, master of words, the eloquent one, lord of eloquence, of infinite course,
of true speech, a speaker of truth, a teacher of the Four Noble Truths. //
Irreversible, a non-returner, the rhinoceros-horn (<s>khaḍga</s>), the solitary guide,
who has gone forth through various vehicles, the sole cause of the great elements. //
An <s>Arhat</s> (Worthy One), one whose outflows are exhausted, a monk, free from passion, with conquered senses,
one who has attained safety, who has attained fearlessness, who has become cool, who is untroubled. //
Endowed with knowledge and conduct, the <s>Sugata</s> (Well-Gone One), the supreme knower of the world,
without possessiveness, without ego-sense, established in the method of the two truths. //
Standing at the far shore of <s>saṃsāra</s>, with his task accomplished, standing on solid ground,
endowed with the culmination of knowledge of <s>kaivalya</s> (isolation), wielding the weapon of wisdom, the destroyer. //
The true <s>Dharma</s>, the king of <s>Dharma</s>, the radiant one, the maker of light for the world, the supreme,
the lord of <s>Dharma</s>, the king of <s>Dharma</s>, the teacher of the path of the good. //
Of accomplished purpose, of accomplished resolve, free from all resolve,
beyond conceptual construction, inexhaustible, the element, the <s>Dharmadhātu</s> (Dharma-realm), the supreme, the imperishable. //
Meritorious, the accumulation of merit, knowledge, the great mine of knowledge,
the wise one, the knower of the real and unreal, sustained by the two accumulations [of merit and wisdom]. //

children.text: śāśvato viśvarāḍ yogī dhyānaṃ dhyeyo dhiyāṃpatiḥ /
children.translated_text: The eternal, the universal sovereign, the <s>yogī</s>, meditation, the object of meditation, the lord of intellects,
to be known by inner experience, immovable, the supreme primordial one, the bearer of the three bodies (<s>trikāya</s>). //
The <s>Buddha</s> whose nature is the five bodies, the all-pervading one whose nature is the five wisdoms,
whose crown consists of the five <s>Buddhas</s>, the bearer of the five eyes without attachment. //
The father of all <s>Buddhas</s>, the son of the <s>Buddha</s>, the supreme of the supreme,
born from the womb of wisdom, the source, the womb of <s>Dharma</s>, the ender of existence. //
Of dense, single essence, of <s>vajra</s>-nature, newly born, the lord of the world,
born from the sky, self-born, the great fire of wisdom and knowledge. //
<s>Vairocana</s>, of great brilliance, the light of knowledge, the illuminator,
the lamp of the world, the torch of knowledge, of great radiance, luminous. //
The king of <s>vidyās</s> (knowledge-spells), the lord of the foremost <s>mantras</s>, the king of <s>mantras</s>, the accomplisher of great purposes,
of great <s>uṣṇīṣa</s> (crown-protuberance), of wondrous <s>uṣṇīṣa</s>, the seer of all, the lord of the sky. //
The foremost essence of all <s>Buddhas</s>, the eye of joy for the world,

children.text: viśvarupī vidhātā ca pūjyo, mānyo mahāṛṣiḥ //
children.translated_text: of universal form, the creator, the worshipful, the honorable, the great sage. //
The bearer of the three families, the holder of <s>mantras</s>, the bearer of the great <s>samaya</s> (pledge) <s>mantra</s>,
the bearer of the Three Jewels, the best, the supreme teacher of the three vehicles. //
<s>Amoghapāśa</s> (Unerring Noose), the victorious, <s>Vajrapāśa</s> (Vajra-Noose), the great seizer,
<s>Vajrāṅkuśa</s> (Vajra-Hook), the great noose, the terrifier of <s>Vajrabhairava</s>. //
Thus, the twenty-four and three-quarter <s>gāthās</s> of the knowledge of the completely pure <s>Dharmadhātu</s>.

children.text: krodharāṭ ṣaṇmukho bhīmaḥ ṣaṇṇetraḥ ṣaḍbhujo balī /
children.translated_text: The king of wrath, six-faced, the terrible, six-eyed, six-armed, the powerful,
with terrible fangs, a skeleton, <s>Halāhala</s> (poison), hundred-faced. //
<s>Yamāntaka</s> (Destroyer of Death), the king of obstacles, <s>Vajravega</s> (Vajra-Speed), the terrifying,
<s>Vighuṣṭavajra</s> (Vajra-Roar), <s>Hṛdvajra</s> (Heart-Vajra), <s>Māyāvajra</s> (Illusion-Vajra), the great-bellied. //
The lord of the <s>vajra</s>, of <s>vajra</s>-womb, <s>Vajramaṇḍa</s>, like the sky,
<s>Acala</s> (Immovable), with a single mass of matted locks, wearing a wet garment of elephant-hide. //
Making cries of 'Hā Hā,' greatly terrible, making cries of 'Hī Hī,' frightful,
with terrible laughter, with great laughter, with <s>vajra</s>-laughter, with a great roar. //
<s>Vajrasattva</s>, the great being, <s>Vajrarāja</s>, of great bliss,
<s>Vajracaṇḍa</s> (Fierce Vajra), of great delight, <s>Vajra-Hūṃkāra</s>, making the cry of Hūṃ. //
The bearer of the <s>vajra</s>-arrow weapon, <s>Vajrakhaḍga</s> (Vajra-Sword), the cutter,
the bearer of the universal <s>vajra</s>, the <s>vajra</s>-holder, the single <s>vajra</s>-holder, the battle-abandoner. //
With eyes blazing with <s>vajra</s>-flames, with hair ablaze with <s>vajra</s>-flames,
of <s>vajra</s>-possession, of great possession, hundred-eyed, <s>vajra</s>-eyed. //
Whose body sprouts with <s>vajra</s>-hairs, whose body is entirely of <s>vajra</s>-hair,
whose nails begin as <s>vajra</s>-points, whose complexion is dense <s>vajra</s>-essence. //
The wearer of a <s>vajra</s>-garland, the glorious, adorned with <s>vajra</s>-ornaments,
thundering with 'Hā Hā' and terrible laughter, of <s>vajra</s>-voice, of six syllables. //
<s>Mañjughoṣa</s> (Sweet-Voiced), of great sound, whose single voice resounds through the three worlds, the great one,
whose voice extends to the limit of the realm of space, the best among those with voice. //
Thus, the ten and a quarter <s>gāthās</s> of the <s>Ādarśajñāna</s> (Mirror-like Wisdom).
The <s>bhūtakoṭi</s> (limit of reality) of the non-self nature of <s>tathatā</s> (suchness), beyond syllables,
the bull of the proponents of <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness), of deep and noble roar. //
The <s>Dharma</s>-conch, of great sound, the <s>Dharma</s>-bell, of great resonance,
the unestablished <s>Nirvāṇa</s>, the <s>Dharma</s>-drum of the ten directions. //
Formless yet foremost among form-bearers, of many forms, mind-made,
the splendor of the appearance of all forms, the bearer of all reflections without remainder. //
Invincible, called the great lord, the great sovereign of the three realms,
standing on the elevated Noble Path, the <s>Dharma</s>-banner, of great arising. //
Having the youthful body unique in the three worlds, yet the elder, the aged, the lord of creatures (<s>Prajāpati</s>),
the bearer of the thirty-two marks, the beautiful, the most handsome in the three worlds. //
The teacher of the world's knowledge and virtues, the teacher of the world, the confident,
the protector, the savior, the one trusted by the three worlds, the refuge, the guide, the unsurpassed. //
Whose enjoyment is the expanse of the sky, the ocean of omniscient knowledge,
the splitter of the eggshell of ignorance, the breaker of the cage of existence. //
Who has pacified all afflictions without remainder, who has crossed the ocean of <s>saṃsāra</s>,
whose crown is the consecration of knowledge, whose ornament is perfect awakening. //
The pacifier of the three sufferings, the three limits, the infinite, who has reached the three liberations,
freed from all obscurations, who has attained equality with space. //
Who has transcended the stain of all afflictions, who has attained the pathless course through the three times,
the great <s>Nāga</s> (elephant/serpent) of all beings, the crest of the crest of virtues. //
Released from all substrata, well-established on the path of the sky,
the bearer of the great wish-fulfilling jewel, the supreme of all jewels, the all-pervading. //
The great wish-fulfilling tree, abundant, the supreme great auspicious vessel,
the doer of deeds for the welfare of all beings, the well-wisher, loving to beings. //
The knower of good and bad, the knower of time, the knower of pledges, the pledge itself, the all-pervading,
the knower of beings' faculties, the knower of the proper time, skilled in the three liberations. //
Virtuous, the knower of virtues, the knower of <s>Dharma</s>, the renowned, the source of auspiciousness,
the most auspicious of all auspicious things, fame, fortune, renown, the auspicious one. //
The great festival, the great consolation, the great bliss, the great delight,
honor, worship, prosperity, joy, <s>Śrī</s> (glory), the lord of fame. //
The most worthy, the bestower of boons, the best, the refuge-worthy, the supreme refuge,
the enemy of great fear, the most excellent, the destroyer of all fears without remainder. //

children.text: śikhī śikhaṇḍī jaṭilo jaṭī mauṇḍī kirīṭimān /
children.translated_text: The crested one, the one with a crest-tuft, the matted-haired one, the one with matted locks, the shaven-headed one, the crowned one,
five-faced, five-crested, crowned with five bark-garments. //
The bearer of the great vow, the <s>mauñjī</s>-girdle wearer, the celibate, the supreme of vows,
of great austerity, devoted to austerity, the <s>snātaka</s> (graduated student), of the <s>Gautama</s> lineage, the foremost. //
The knower of <s>Brahman</s>, the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, <s>Brahmā</s> himself, who has attained <s>Brahma-Nirvāṇa</s>,
release, liberation, possessed of the limbs of liberation, emancipation, tranquility, auspiciousness. //
<s>Nirvāṇa</s>, cessation, peace, the good, the final departure, the one who has reached the end,
the ender of pleasure and pain, the consummation, dispassion, the exhaustion of substrata. //
Unconquerable, incomparable, unmanifest, without appearance, without stain,
without parts, going everywhere, all-pervading, subtle, the seed without outflows. //
Dustless, free from dust, spotless, with faults expelled, free from disease,
fully awakened, of awakened nature, omniscient, the supreme knower of all. //
Having transcended the nature of consciousness-phenomena, the bearer of non-dual knowledge-form,
beyond conceptual construction, without application, the accomplisher of the work of the <s>Buddhas</s> of the three times. //
Without beginning or end, the <s>Buddha</s>, the primordial <s>Buddha</s> (<s>Ādibuddha</s>), without succession,
whose sole eye is knowledge, the spotless, the embodiment of knowledge, the <s>Tathāgata</s>. //
The lord of speech, the great debater, the king of debaters, the bull of debaters,
the best of speakers, the most excellent, the lion of debaters, the unconquered. //
The all-seeing, the joyful, wreathed in radiance, beautiful to behold,
<s>Śrīvatsa</s> (auspicious mark), of beautiful radiance, brilliance, shining with the splendor of luminous rays. //
The great supreme physician, the best, the extractor of thorns, the unsurpassed,
the tree of all medicines without remainder, the great enemy of the disease of afflictions. //
The <s>tilaka</s>-mark of the three worlds, the beautiful, the glorious, the constellation-circle,
extending to the sky in the ten directions, of great height like the <s>Dharma</s>-banner. //
The sole vast parasol of the world, the circle of loving-kindness and compassion,
the lord of the lotus-dance, the glorious, the jeweled parasol, the greatly all-pervading. //
The great king of all <s>Buddhas</s>, the bearer of the essence of all <s>Buddhas</s>,
the great <s>yoga</s> of all <s>Buddhas</s>, the sole teaching of all <s>Buddhas</s>. //
The glory of the consecration of <s>vajra</s>-jewels, the sovereign lord of all jewels,
the lord and master of all world-lords, the chief of all <s>vajra</s>-holders. //
The great mind of all <s>Buddhas</s>, the mental course of all <s>Buddhas</s>,
the great body of all <s>Buddhas</s>, the <s>Sarasvatī</s> (eloquence) of all <s>Buddhas</s>. //
<s>Vajra</s>-sun, of great light, <s>vajra</s>-moon, of spotless radiance,
of great passion beginning from dispassion, blazing with the radiance of all colors. //
The <s>vajra</s>-seat (<s>paryaṅka</s>) of the <s>Saṃbuddha</s>, the bearer of the <s>Dharma</s> of the <s>Buddha</s>-assembly,
born from the <s>Buddha</s>-lotus, the glorious, the bearer of the treasury of omniscient knowledge. //
The bearer of universal illusion, the king, the great bearer of <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge,
<s>Vajratīkṣṇa</s> (Sharp Vajra), the great sword, the pure, the supreme syllable. //
The great weapon of the <s>vajra-dharma</s>, the great vehicle that cuts suffering,
the <s>Jina</s>-conqueror, of <s>vajra</s>-profundity, of <s>vajra</s>-intellect, the knower of things as they are. //
The fulfiller of all <s>pāramitās</s>, the ornament of all stages (<s>bhūmis</s>),
of the pure <s>dharma</s>-selflessness, whose heart shines with the moon of right knowledge. //
The great exertion of the net of illusion, the supreme master of all <s>tantras</s>,
the complete <s>vajra</s>-seat, the bearer of the complete knowledge-body. //
<s>Samantabhadra</s> (All-Good), <s>Sumati</s> (Good-Minded), <s>Kṣitigarbha</s> (Earth-Treasury), the support of the world,
the great womb of all <s>Buddhas</s>, the seer of the wheel of universal creation. //
The foremost own-nature of all existences, the bearer of the own-nature of all existences,
whose <s>dharma</s> is non-arising, whose purpose is universal, the bearer of the own-nature of all <s>dharmas</s>. //
Of great wisdom in a single instant, the bearer of the comprehension of all <s>dharmas</s>,
the agreement of all <s>dharmas</s>, the sage of the limit of reality, of supreme intellect. //
Serene, of supremely clear nature, the bearer of the awakening of perfect <s>Saṃbuddha</s>,
directly perceptible to all <s>Buddhas</s>, the flame of knowledge, supremely luminous. //
Thus, the forty-two <s>gāthās</s> of the <s>Pratyavekṣaṇajñāna</s> (Individually Discriminating Wisdom).
The supreme accomplisher of desired aims, the purifier of all lower realms,
the supreme lord of all beings, the liberator of all beings. //
The sole hero of the battle with afflictions, the destroyer of the pride of the enemy of ignorance,
Bearer of the <s>rasas</s> (aesthetic sentiments) of intellect and love, glorious, assuming the forms of heroism and repugnance, //
dancing with the sweeping motion of hundreds of arm-staffs and stamping of feet,
dancing in the sky-expanse with the glorious enjoyment of a hundred arms, //
standing on the surface of the great earth trampled by one sole of the foot,
standing on the toenail of the foot that has trampled the summit of the cosmic egg (<s>brahmāṇḍa</s>), //
of singular purpose, whose meaning is the non-dual <s>dharma</s>, the ultimate reality, imperishable,
whose meaning is the forms of various cognitions, the continuum of mind-consciousness, //
delighting in the meaning of all entities, delighting in emptiness (<s>śūnyatā</s>), of supreme intellect,
transcending attachment to existence and the like, the great delight of the three states of existence, //
pure, white as a bright cloud, beautifully radiant as the rays of the autumn moon,
shadowed by the disk of the rising sun, with toenails radiant with great passion, //
with an excellent garment of sapphire (<s>indranīla</s>), bearing the tips of great blue hair,
with the glory of the rays of great jewels, adorned with the <s>nirvāṇa</s> of the <s>Buddhas</s>, //
causing hundreds of world-realms to tremble, of great stride through the bases of supernatural power (<s>ṛddhipāda</s>),
the great bearer of mindfulness, [embodying] reality, the king of the four foundations of mindfulness (<s>smṛtyupasthāna</s>) and <s>samādhi</s>, //
fragrant with the blossoms of the factors of awakening (<s>bodhyaṅga</s>), the ocean of <s>Tathāgata</s>-virtues,
knower of the method of the eightfold path, knower of the path of perfect awakening (<s>samyaksaṃbodhi</s>), //
greatly attached to all beings, [yet] unattached, like the sky,
born in the minds of all beings, swift as the minds of all beings, //
knower of the faculties and objects of all beings, captivating the minds of all beings,
knower of the truth of the meaning of the five aggregates (<s>skandhas</s>), bearer of the purification of the five aggregates, //
standing at the limit of all liberations, skilled in all liberations,
standing on the path of all liberations, the teacher of all liberations, //
having uprooted the twelve links of existence, bearer of the purity of the twelve aspects,
of the form of the method of the four truths, bearer of the realization of the eight knowledges, //
whose meaning is the truth in twelve aspects, knower of reality in sixteen aspects,
whose perfect awakening is in twenty aspects, fully awakened, supreme among all knowers, //
the illuminator of immeasurable millions of <s>Buddha</s>-emanation bodies (<s>nirmāṇakāya</s>),
whose realization [occurs in] every instant, knower of the meaning of every moment of consciousness, //
the illuminator of the world's purpose through the methods of various vehicles,
having gone forth through the three vehicles, established in the fruit of the one vehicle, //
whose self is purified from the realm of <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions), the maker of the exhaustion of the realm of <s>karma</s>,
having crossed the ocean of floods (<s>ogha</s>), having emerged from the wilderness of <s>yoga</s> [bonds], //
having thoroughly abandoned <s>kleśas</s>, secondary <s>kleśas</s>, and defilements, together with their latent impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>),
through wisdom, skillful means, and great compassion, the unfailing accomplisher of the world's purpose, //
whose purpose is the transcendence of all perceptions, whose purpose is consciousness, the maker of cessation,
the object of the minds of all beings, the mental destination of all beings, //
dwelling within the minds of all beings, having attained equality with their minds,
the delighter of the minds of all beings, the delight of the minds of all beings, //
the established conclusion, free from error, devoid of all confusion,
of undoubted understanding, of threefold meaning, of all purposes, of the nature of the three qualities, //
the meaning of the five aggregates, [encompassing] the three times, the illuminator of every moment,
perfectly awakened in a single instant, bearer of the nature of all <s>Buddhas</s>, //
of bodiless body, the foremost of bodies, the illuminator of millions of bodies,
the displayer of all forms, the jewel-banner, the great gem. //
Thus [end] the twenty-four verses of Equality-Knowledge (<s>Samatājñāna</s>).
To be awakened by all perfectly awakened ones, the unsurpassed awakening of the <s>Buddha</s>,
without syllable, the source of <s>mantras</s>, the great <s>mantra</s>, the three families, //
the progenitor of the meaning of all <s>mantras</s>, the great <s>bindu</s> (point), without syllable,
of five syllables, the great void (<s>śūnya</s>), void of <s>bindu</s>, of six syllables, //
of all forms, formless, bearer of the half-half-<s>bindu</s> of sixteen,
without parts, beyond calculation, bearer of the limit of the fourth <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation), //
knower of all the arts of all <s>dhyānas</s>, knower of the family and lineage of <s>samādhis</s>,
of <s>samādhi</s>-body, foremost of bodies, the king of all enjoyment-bodies (<s>saṃbhogakāya</s>), //
the emanation-body (<s>nirmāṇakāya</s>), foremost of bodies, bearer of the lineage of <s>Buddha</s>-emanations,
universally emanating in the ten directions, accomplishing the world's purpose as it truly is, //
the god beyond gods, the lord of gods, the chief of the immortals, the lord of <s>Dānavas</s>,
the lord of the immortals, the teacher of the gods, the tormentor [of enemies], the lord of tormentors, //
having crossed the wilderness of existence, the sole teacher, the guru of the world,
renowned in the worlds of the ten directions, the great lord of the gift of <s>Dharma</s>, //
girded with the armor of loving-kindness (<s>maitrī</s>), clad in the armor of compassion (<s>karuṇā</s>),
with the sword of wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>), with bow and arrow, the destroyer of the battlefield of <s>kleśas</s> and ignorance, //
the enemy of <s>Māra</s>, the hero who conquers <s>Māra</s>, the ender of the fear of the four <s>Māras</s>,
the conqueror of all of <s>Māra's</s> armies, fully equipped, the leader of the world, //
to be worshipped, to be honored, to be saluted, and to be respected always,
the most worthy of worship, to be revered, to be bowed to — the supreme guru. //
Whose stride encompasses the three worlds in one step, whose prowess extends to the edge of space,
possessed of the threefold knowledge, learned in scripture, pure, possessed of the six superknowledges (<s>abhijñā</s>) and six recollections (<s>anusmṛti</s>), //
a <s>Bodhisattva</s>, a great being, transcending the world, of great supernatural power,
established in the Perfection of Wisdom (<s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>), having attained the truth of wisdom, //
knower of the self and of others, universal, the foremost individual in all things,
transcending all comparisons, to be known, the supreme lord of knowledge. //
The best lord of the gift of <s>Dharma</s>, the teacher of the meaning of the four <s>mudrās</s> (seals),
the most worthy of service among the people of the world who travel the three vehicles of liberation, //
of glory purified in the ultimate sense, great, beautiful in the three worlds,
the bringer of all prosperity, the glorious <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, the best among the glorious. //
Thus [end] the fifteen verses of Action-Practice-Knowledge (<s>Kṛtyānuṣṭhānajñāna</s>).
Homage to you, O foremost <s>vajra</s> of boon-granting! Homage to you, O <s>Bhūtakoṭi</s> (Limit of Reality)!
Homage to you, O womb of emptiness! Homage to you, O <s>Buddhabodhi</s> (Buddha-Awakening)! //
Homage to you, O <s>Buddharāga</s> (Buddha-Passion)! Homage, homage to <s>Buddhakāma</s> (Buddha-Desire)!
Homage to you, O <s>Buddhaprīti</s> (Buddha-Joy)! Homage, homage to <s>Buddhamoda</s> (Buddha-Delight)! //
Homage to you, O <s>Buddhasmita</s> (Buddha-Smile)! Homage, homage to <s>Buddhahāsa</s> (Buddha-Laughter)!
Homage to you, O <s>Buddhavāca</s> (Buddha-Speech)! Homage, homage to <s>Buddhabhāva</s> (Buddha-Being)! //
Homage to you, O <s>Abhavodbhava</s> (Born from Non-Existence)! Homage to you, O <s>Buddhasaṃbhava</s> (Buddha-Born)!
Homage to you, O <s>Gaganodbhava</s> (Born from Space)! Homage to you, O <s>Jñānasaṃbhava</s> (Knowledge-Born)! //
Homage to you, O <s>Māyājāla</s> (Net of Illusion)! Homage to you, O <s>Buddhanāṭaka</s> (Buddha-Actor)!
Homage to you, O all of all! Homage to you, O <s>Jñānakāya</s> (Knowledge-Body)! //
